topics.title: 1. Child Development: Growth, Stages & Heredity-Environment
topics.theory:
- **Growth** = quantitative, physical, measurable, stops at maturity; **development** = qualitative + quantitative, lifelong, sequential, continuous. Directions: **cephalocaudal** (head to foot), **proximodistal** (centre to periphery).
- **Piaget:** sensorimotor 0-2 (**object permanence**), preoperational 2-7 (**egocentrism**, animism, no conservation), concrete operational 7-11 (**conservation**, reversibility), formal operational 11+ (abstract/hypothetical reasoning). Terms: schema, **assimilation**, **accommodation**, equilibration.
- **Vygotsky:** sociocultural theory; **ZPD**, scaffolding, MKO, private speech. **Bruner:** enactive, iconic, symbolic modes; spiral curriculum.
- **Erikson:** 8 psychosocial crises - trust vs mistrust (0-1), autonomy vs shame (1-3), initiative vs guilt (3-6), industry vs inferiority (6-12), **identity vs role confusion** (adolescence), intimacy vs isolation, generativity vs stagnation, integrity vs despair.
- **Kohlberg:** preconventional (punishment-obedience, instrumental), conventional (good boy/girl, law and order), **postconventional** (social contract, universal principles; ~13+). Heinz dilemma. Gilligan: ethics of care.
- **Bronfenbrenner:** micro-, meso-, exo- (indirect, e.g. policies/parents' workplace), macro-, chronosystem. **Parten:** 6 play stages (solitary, parallel, associative, cooperative...).
- **Heredity vs environment:** genes set potential, environment shapes expression; both interact (twin studies). Early childhood = 2-6 years; later childhood 6-12; brain highly plastic early.
- **Milestones:** babbling ~6 months, walking/first word ~12 months, two-word sentences 18-24 months; gross motor before fine motor; birth weight doubles ~5 months, triples at 1 year.
- **Adolescence** 12-18: identity formation, peer influence (Marcia statuses), need for emotional guidance.
- **Maturation vs learning:** development depends on both; readiness = maturation + experience.

qs.stem: माता-पिता के समान घुंघराले बाल वाले बच्चों में किस कारक का प्रभाव होता है?
qs.sol: माता-पिता और बच्चों के बालों की बनावट में समानता आनुवंशिकता का सामान्य उदाहरण है। बच्चे अपने माता-पिता से आनुवंशिक रूप प्राप्त करते हैं, जो बालों की संरचना और घुँघरालेपन को प्रभावित कर सकते हैं। वातावरण और सँवारने के तरीके बालों की दिखाई देने वाली दशा बदल सकते हैं, लेकिन प्रश्न पीढ़ियों में समान शारीरिक लक्षण पूछता है। सामाजिक कारक व्यवहार और संबंधों से, आर्थिक कारक संसाधनों से, तथा मनोसामाजिक कारक सामाजिक अनुभव और मानसिक प्रक्रियाओं से जुड़े हैं। इनमें से कोई भी विरासत में मिले शारीरिक साम्य का प्रत्यक्ष कारण नहीं है। इसलिए वंशानुगत कारक प्रश्न के संकेत से मेल खाता है।
qs.rel: Heredity (nature) transmits physical traits via genes, e.g. hair type, eye colour, height. Neighbours: environment (nurture) shapes language, values and skills; twin studies separate the two; 23 chromosome pairs; genes set potential, environment decides expression.

qs.stem: Who introduced the cognitive theory of development during the 1930s?
qs.sol: “Jean Piaget” is correct: Piaget developed a stage-based account of how children’s thinking changes with development. “BF Skinner” fails: Skinner is associated with behaviourism and operant conditioning rather than this cognitive developmental theory.
qs.rel: Piaget's cognitive theory (1930s onward): sensorimotor 0-2, preoperational 2-7, concrete operational 7-11, formal operational 11+. Key terms: schema, assimilation, accommodation, equilibration. Contrast Vygotsky (social), Bruner (modes: enactive, iconic, symbolic).

qs.stem:
Which of the following is an element of effective learning activity?
 I. Spontaneous involvement
 II. Challenging
qs.sol: Effective learning activities should encourage spontaneous involvement and also be challenging enough to engage learners. Therefore both statements are correct.
qs.rel: Types of play: functional/practice, constructive, dramatic/pretend, games with rules. Parten's social play: unoccupied, solitary, onlooker, parallel, associative, cooperative. Piaget linked play to cognitive stage; Vygotsky saw pretend play as creating a ZPD.

qs.stem:
In order to use drama as a linguistic activity, which of the following characteristic(s) need to be included?
 I. Freedom
 II. Enjoyment
qs.sol: Drama as a linguistic activity should include freedom and enjoyment so that learners can express language naturally.
qs.rel: Growth = quantitative, physical, measurable change (height, weight); development = qualitative, overall change including psychological aspects. Neighbours: growth stops at maturity but development is lifelong; development includes growth, and is not always measurable.

qs.stem: NEP 2020 का पूर्ण प्रपत्र क्या है?
qs.sol: NEP का विस्तार National Education Policy है, जिसका हिंदी रूप राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति है। वर्ष 2020 उस नीति दस्तावेज़ के वर्ष को बताता है; वह तीन अक्षरों के विस्तार का हिस्सा नहीं है। N से National, E से Education और P से Policy बनता है। New से आरंभ होने वाले नाम पहले अक्षर का अर्थ बदल देते हैं। आर्थिक कार्यक्रम शिक्षा नीति का नाम भी नहीं है। इसलिए आधिकारिक नाम के तीनों शब्दों को साथ पहचानना आवश्यक है।
qs.rel: Later childhood is 6-12 years (also called the gang age/school age). Infancy 0-2, early childhood 2-6, adolescence 12-18 (puberty onset). Erikson: industry vs inferiority at 6-12; Piaget: concrete operational.

qs.stem: कौन सी आयु सीमा बाद के बचपन से जुड़ी है?
qs.sol: उत्तर बाल्यावस्था की आयु सामान्यतः लगभग 6–12 वर्ष मानी जाती है।
qs.rel: Motor skills: gross (large muscles: running, jumping, hopping) and fine (small muscles: buttoning, writing, drawing). Locomotor skills move the body (walk, run, skip); manipulatory handle objects (throw, catch, kick). Gross develops before fine (cephalocaudal, proximodistal).

qs.stem: वृद्धि और विकास के अनुसार प्रकृति का नियम क्या है?
qs.sol: वृद्धि और विकास में समय के साथ परिवर्तन होना प्रकृति का मूल नियम है। बच्चे के शरीर, व्यवहार, सोच और सामाजिक क्षमताएँ एक ही अवस्था में स्थिर नहीं रहतीं; विकास क्रमिक तथा अनेक आयामों में चलता है। 'समानता' से स्थायी एकरूपता का संकेत मिल सकता है, जबकि विकास में अंतर और नई क्षमताएँ उभरती हैं। 'Alteration' और 'Remodelling' कुछ विशिष्ट बदलावों के शब्द हैं, पर प्रश्न का व्यापक प्राकृतिक सिद्धांत 'Change' है। पूरी जीवन-प्रक्रिया को समेटने वाला सामान्य शब्द चुनना चाहिए, किसी एक प्रकार के रूपांतरण को नहीं।
qs.rel: Law of nature in growth and development is change; development is continuous, sequential, with individual differences. Neighbours: principles of cephalocaudal (head to foot) and proximodistal (centre to periphery) direction, general to specific, and interrelation of domains.

qs.stem: According to NCF 2005, the main goal of Mathematics education in school is......
qs.sol: NCF 2005 emphasizes the mathematization of children's thinking, meaning the development of mathematical ways of reasoning rather than only memorizing formulae.
qs.rel: Early brain plasticity: huge synapse formation, 'use it or lose it' pruning, critical periods for language and vision. Brain reaches about 90% of adult size by age 5. Neighbours: enriched environment, early stimulation, responsive caregiving.

qs.stem:
“It is not always possible to bring real objects to the classroom”. Which of the following is/are the reason(s) behind the given statement?
 I. Size of the object
 II. Safety
 III. Cost
qs.sol: Real objects may be difficult to bring to class because of their size, safety concerns or cost. All three reasons are valid.
qs.rel: Constructivist/Rousseau-style view: children come to school with curiosity, prior knowledge and desire to know. Link: NCF 2005 treats the child as a constructor of knowledge; neighbours: prior knowledge, naturalism, child-centred education.

qs.stem: What is neural plasticity in early childhood?

opts.B: The brain's ability to change and adapt
opts.C: The process of learning to walk

qs.sol: Neural plasticity is the brain’s capacity to change and adapt in response to experience. “The process of learning to walk” may be influenced by plasticity, but it is one learned ability rather than the brain’s general capacity to adapt.
qs.rel: Neural plasticity: brain's capacity to rewire through experience; highest in early childhood. Neighbours: synaptogenesis, synaptic pruning, myelination, sensitive/critical periods, importance of early childhood care and education.

qs.stem: Which of the following age range is known as early childhood?
qs.sol: “2-6 years” is supported because early childhood commonly spans roughly ages two through six in the cited developmental classification. “1-6 years” begins in infancy, outside the usual early-childhood interval used by the board.
qs.rel: Early childhood is 2-6 years (preschool years; ICDS/ECCE covers 3-6). Neighbours: infancy birth-2, later childhood 6-12; NEP 2020 foundational stage 3-8 years (5+3+3+4 structure); Piaget preoperational 2-7.

qs.stem: ________ mode includes two teaching media, viz. a video recorder and a computer in an integrated way, which makes learning highly interactive.
qs.sol: “V-CAL” refers to video-assisted computer learning that integrates a video recorder with a computer for interactive instruction. “Simulation” can model a situation on a computer, but it does not by itself specify this video-and-computer arrangement.
qs.rel: Language and speech are most sensitive up to about six years; NEP 2020 stresses ECCE up to age 8 and 85% of brain growth by age 6. Neighbours: babbling at ~6 months, first word ~12 months, two-word sentences ~18-24 months.

qs.stem: किसी व्यक्ति की वृद्धि और विकास को प्रभावित करने वाले आंतरिक कारक _________ हैं। I. बुद्धि मत्ता II. आनुवंशिकता कारक III. सामाजिक प्रकृति
qs.sol: विकास के आंतरिक प्रभावों में वंशानुगत गुण, बुद्धि और व्यक्ति की अपनी सामाजिक प्रवृत्ति शामिल हो सकती है। ये अनुभवों पर व्यक्ति की प्रतिक्रिया बदलते हैं। परिवार, विद्यालय और समुदाय जैसे बाहरी प्रभाव इनके साथ काम करते हैं, पर प्रश्न में बताए गुण व्यक्ति के अपने लक्षण हैं। बुद्धि भी आंतरिक लक्षण है और छूटती है। व्यक्ति की सामाजिक प्रवृत्ति भी इस सूची में शामिल है। तीनों को व्यक्ति के अपने गुण के रूप में लिया गया है। केवल सामाजिक प्रवृत्ति में बुद्धि और वंशानुक्रम छूटते हैं।
qs.rel: Internal (endogenous) factors: heredity, intelligence, hormones/endocrine glands, health, emotional makeup. External factors: family, school, peers, nutrition, culture, socio-economic status. Neighbours: nature-nurture interaction and maturation.

qs.stem: What does the listening mode focus on?
qs.sol: Listening is a receptive language mode: learners interpret spoken words and meaning from oral input. It does not require producing a text.
qs.rel: Characteristics of development: continuous, sequential, qualitative, has predictable pattern, individual differences, lifelong, results from maturation and learning. Neighbours: growth is mostly quantitative and stops after maturity; development is holistic.

qs.stem: Vygotsky presented the ___________ theory.
qs.sol: Vygotsky emphasised the social origins of learning and development through interaction with others. “Social learning” names Bandura’s observational-learning account, while the intended label here is social development.
qs.rel: Vygotsky: sociocultural theory. Key terms: ZPD, scaffolding, MKO (more knowledgeable other), private speech, language as tool of thought, cultural mediation. Contrast Piaget (stages, individual discovery) and Bruner (spiral curriculum, discovery learning).

qs.stem: Discussion method aims at____ .
qs.sol: Discussion brings participants' contributions together and integrates their work toward a shared understanding.
qs.rel: Piaget preoperational stage (2-7): symbolic thought, egocentrism, animism, centration, lack of conservation, irreversibility. Substages: preconceptual 2-4, intuitive 4-7. Neighbours: sensorimotor stage ends with object permanence.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन से बच्चे जन्म से महसूस कर सकते हैं तथा चेहरे और शरीर की मुद्रा के माध्यम से इन्हें व्यक्त कर सकते हैं? I. रुचि II. संकट III. ख़ुशी
qs.sol: शिशु जन्म के आसपास से ही चेहरे के भाव और शरीर की मुद्रा के द्वारा कई मूल भावनाएं प्रकट कर सकता है। रुचि किसी वस्तु की ओर देखने और ध्यान देने से दिखाई दे सकती है। संकट रोने और तनावपूर्ण मुद्रा में तथा खुशी मुस्कान जैसे भावों में दिखाई देती है। प्रश्न तीनों अवस्थाओं के बारे में पूछता है, इसलिए किसी एक या दो तक उत्तर सीमित करने से शिशु की अभिव्यक्ति का एक वास्तविक पहलू छूट जाता है।
qs.rel: Newborns show basic emotions through facial expressions (interest, distress, disgust, then joy/anger/fear later). Bridges' and Watson's emotion differentiation; emotions appear in order: distress/pleasure first, then others. Neighbours: social smile ~6 weeks, stranger anxiety ~8 months.

qs.stem: What is the primary purpose of assessing scanning abilities in AAC users?

opts.A: To facilitate communication through indirect selection methods
opts.B: To enhance the user's musical skills
opts.C: To determine the user's preference for visual arts
opts.D: To assess the user's mathematical abilities

qs.sol: “To facilitate communication through indirect selection methods” is the reason to assess scanning: the user can select a message as choices are presented in sequence. “To determine the user's preference for visual arts” would assess an interest, not the access method needed for AAC selection.
qs.rel: Piaget: understanding of natural/physical laws and conservation matures by about 12 (formal operations), with gradual growth through concrete stage. Neighbours: conservation of number ~6-7, volume ~11-12; hypothetical-deductive reasoning appears at formal stage.

qs.stem: Relationships and interaction between boys and girls in school is called:
qs.sol: The correct term for relationships and interactions between boys and girls in school is "gender dynamics". This concept specifically refers to the social patterns, power relations, and behaviors observed between genders within an educational context. Other options may refer to attitudes or prejudices rather than the mutual interactions themselves.
qs.rel: Imaginary fears of childhood (monsters, darkness) fade by about 12 as cognitive development and reality testing improve. Neighbours: fears in infancy are of loud sounds/strangers; phobias; the role of conditioning (Watson's Little Albert).

qs.stem: इनमें से कौन मूल्यांकन की विशेषता नहीं है?

opts.C: यह कक्षागृह तक ही सीमित नहीं है
opts.D: इसमें केवल अकादमिक विषय शामिल हैं

qs.sol: मूल्यांकन शैक्षिक और अशैक्षिक विकास दोनों को देखता है; यह केवल शैक्षिक विषयों तक सीमित नहीं है।
qs.rel: Milestones: birth weight doubles by about 4-5 months and triples by about 12 months; height grows 50% by one year. Neighbours: pincer grasp ~9 months, sitting ~6 months, walking ~12 months, first words ~12 months.

qs.stem:
The syllabus of Environment Studies for class III to V is woven around the 6 interconnected themes. Which of the following is/are among those themes?
 Statements:
 I. Shelter
 II. Water
 III. Food
qs.sol:
Concept: The EVS syllabus for classes III to V is not split into separate subjects; NCF 2005 organises it as a web of six interconnected themes that widen year on year from the child's immediate world outward.

Application: The six official themes are Family and Friends, Food, Shelter, Water, Travel, and Things We Make and Do. Checking each statement against this list:

Statement I names Shelter, which is one of the six listed themes.

Statement II names Water, which is one of the six listed themes.

Statement III names Food, which is one of the six listed themes. …
qs.rel: Kicking/throwing a football = gross motor skill (large muscles). Fine motor = small muscle control (buttoning, drawing). Neighbours: hopping on one foot ~4 years, tying shoelaces ~5-6, locomotor vs manipulative skills.

qs.stem: Piaget divided which of the following domain of development into four stages: The Sensorimotor Stage, The Pre-Operational Stage, Concrete Operational Stage and The Formal Operational Stage?
qs.sol: Piaget's four stages--sensorimotor, pre-operational, concrete operational, and formal operational--describe cognitive development.
qs.rel: Piaget's four stages describe cognitive development: sensorimotor, preoperational, concrete operational, formal operational. Neighbours: Erikson has 8 psychosocial stages; Kohlberg 3 levels/6 stages for moral development; Freud 5 psychosexual stages.

qs.stem: वृद्धि के बारे में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही नहीं है?

opts.B: वृद्धि परिपक्वता के साथ रूक जाती है
opts.C: वृद्धि पूरी तरह से अवलोकन योग्य और मापन योग्य नहीं है
opts.D: वृद्धि, विकास का एक अंग है

qs.sol: वृद्धि का सामान्य अर्थ शरीर के आकार, भार या अन्य परिमाण में बदलाव है। ऐसे बदलाव सामान्यतः देखे और मापे जा सकते हैं। परिपक्वता पर शारीरिक वृद्धि की सीमा आती है और विकास की व्यापक प्रक्रिया में वृद्धि एक भाग है। इसीलिए यह दावा कि वृद्धि पूरी तरह अवलोकनीय और मापनीय नहीं है, पूछे गए गलत कथन के रूप में चुना जाता है।
qs.rel: Growth is quantitative, observable and measurable and stops at maturity; it is not the whole of development. Neighbours: development is qualitative and lifelong; growth is a part of development; both are affected by heredity and environment.

qs.stem: What preschool limitation prevents seeing others' viewpoints?
qs.sol: Egocentrism is the preschool limitation in which a child has difficulty seeing from another person's viewpoint.
qs.rel: Egocentrism (preoperational): inability to take another's viewpoint; shown in the three-mountains task. Neighbours: animism, centration, irreversibility; decentration develops in concrete operational stage; Vygotsky saw egocentric speech as private speech.

qs.sol: एरिक्सन के अनुसार आत्मीय संबंध बनाने बनाम अलगाव की मनोसामाजिक चुनौती “युवावस्था के प्रारंभिक वर्षो में” से जुड़ी है। “किशोरावस्था” में पहचान बनाम भूमिका भ्रम की चुनौती अधिक प्रमुख मानी जाती है।
qs.rel: Erikson's stages: trust vs mistrust (0-1), autonomy vs shame (1-3), initiative vs guilt (3-6), industry vs inferiority (6-12), identity vs role confusion (adolescence), intimacy vs isolation (young adult), generativity vs stagnation, integrity vs despair.

qs.stem: According to Piaget’s theory, in which stage does object permanence develop?
qs.sol: According to Jean Piaget's theory of cognitive development, object permanence is a fundamental milestone that emerges during the Sensorimotor stage. This period spans from birth to approximately two years of age, where infants learn that objects continue to exist even when they cannot be seen.
qs.rel: Object permanence: awareness that objects exist when out of sight, develops in the sensorimotor stage (about 8-12 months, mastered by 18-24 months). Neighbours: substages (primary circular reactions etc.), A-not-B error, deferred imitation.

qs.stem: According to Kohlberg's Moral Development Theory, ethical principles are internalized and judgments are made in the age group of:
qs.sol: Kohlberg's Moral Development Theory outlines three levels of moral reasoning: Pre-conventional, Conventional, and Post-conventional. The question specifically asks about the internalization of ethical principles, which characterizes the Post-conventional level. This highest stage involves reasoning based on universal ethical principles and individual conscience rather than societal rules or laws. Research indicates that this advanced form of moral reasoning typically emerges during adolescence and continues into adulthood, generally starting around age 13. Therefore, the correct answer is Option C (13 and above). …
qs.rel: Kohlberg: postconventional level (stage 5 social contract, stage 6 universal ethical principles) appears from about 13 and above and not all reach it. Preconventional: punishment-obedience, instrumental exchange; conventional: good boy/girl, law and order. Gilligan criticised it for gender bias.

qs.stem: In which stage of cognitive development of Piaget’s theory, a child understands and carry out calculations involving proportions?
qs.sol: Piaget's Formal Operational stage begins around age eleven and is marked by the ability to think abstractly. Children at this stage can handle hypothetical-deductive reasoning and understand complex proportional relationships without concrete objects.
qs.rel: Formal operational stage (11+): abstract thinking, proportional and hypothetical-deductive reasoning, combinatorial logic. Neighbours: concrete operational stage handles conservation, classification, seriation; Inhelder's pendulum and balance-scale tasks.

qs.sol: “9 months” is the usual approximate age for emergence of a thumb-and-forefinger pincer grasp in developmental milestone accounts. “11 months” is plausible for a more refined pincer grasp, but the question asks when this grasp first becomes possible.
qs.rel: Pincer grasp (thumb and forefinger) emerges about 9 months; grasping reflex earlier; walking alone at 12-15 months. Neighbours: sits unaided ~6 months, crawls ~8-9 months, stranger anxiety, object permanence ~8 months.

qs.stem: 'अहं केंद्रित विचार' पियाजे के संज्ञानात्मक विकास के चरणों के किस चरण की एक प्रमुख विशेषता है?
qs.sol: पियाजे के सिद्धांत में पूर्वसंक्रिय अवस्था लगभग 2 से 7 वर्ष तक रहती है। इस अवस्था में बच्चे प्रतीकों और भाषा का प्रयोग कर सकते हैं, पर उनका चिंतन अहं केंद्रित होता है: उन्हें दूसरे व्यक्ति के दृष्टिकोण से चीज़ें देखने में कठिनाई होती है, जैसा पियाजे ने तीन पहाड़ों वाले प्रयोग में दिखाया। जीववाद, केंद्रीकरण और संरक्षण की कमी इसकी अन्य विशेषताएँ हैं। संवेदी-गत्यात्मक अवस्था (0-2 वर्ष) में शिशु इंद्रियों और क्रियाओं से सीखते हैं और वस्तु स्थायित्व विकसित करते हैं। स्थूल संक्रिय अवस्था (7-11) में बच्चे मूर्त वस्तुओं के बारे में तार्किक सोचते हैं, और औपचारिक संक्रिया अवस्था (11 वर्ष और आगे) में अमूर्त तर्क करते हैं। अतः उत्तर पूर्वसंक्रिय है।
qs.rel: Egocentric thought is key feature of the preoperational stage (2-7 years). Neighbours: animism, centration, lack of conservation, symbolic play and language explosion; contrast with concrete operations (decentration, reversibility).

qs.sol: पियाजे के अनुसार मूर्त संक्रियात्मक अवस्था में बच्चा मात्रा के संरक्षण को समझने लगता है, इसलिए “मूर्त संक्रियात्मक अवस्था (Concrete operational stage)” सही है। “पूर्व-संक्रियात्मक अवस्था (Preoperational stage)” में बाहरी रूप बदलने पर बच्चा सामान्यतः मात्रा बदलने का अनुमान लगा लेता है।
qs.rel: Concrete operational stage (7-11): conservation, reversibility, classification, seriation, decentration, but needs concrete objects. Neighbours: conservation of number comes before volume; formal stage brings abstract reasoning.

qs.stem: The transition from one Piagetian stage to another is best described as:
qs.sol: Piaget's theory states that cognitive development stages follow a fixed, invariant sequence for all individuals. While the order remains constant across cultures, the timing of transitions varies based on maturation and environment.
qs.rel: Piaget: stages are universal and sequential, but timing varies across children and cultures; transitions are gradual, not abrupt. Neighbours: no skipping of stages, qualitative differences, disequilibrium drives progress; critics note underestimation of infants.

qs.stem: A preschool teacher notices that Riya can button her shirt but struggles to hop on one foot. What does this indicate?

opts.A: Fine motor skills are more developed than gross motor skills
opts.B: Delay in cognitive sequencing abilities affecting motor coordination
opts.C: Underdeveloped sensory integration leading to bilateral confusion
opts.D: Inadequate maturation of language-mediated motor planning

qs.sol: Buttoning a shirt needs fine motor control, while hopping on one foot needs gross motor control. Riya can button but struggles to hop, so fine motor skills are more developed than gross motor skills.
qs.rel: Fine motor (buttoning) usually matures differently from gross motor (hopping); hopping on one foot appears about 4-5 years. Neighbours: motor development follows cephalocaudal and proximodistal laws; skills uneven across children; practice and readiness matter.

qs.stem: जीन पियाजे के संज्ञानात्मक विकास के सिद्धांत में चार चरण शामिल हैं। किस चरण में बच्चा संरक्षण की अवधारणा को समझना शुरू करता है—अर्थात, आकृति या स्वरूप में परिवर्तन के बावजूद मात्रा समान रहती है?
qs.sol:
पियाजे का संज्ञानात्मक विकास सिद्धांत बच्चों के मानसिक विकास को चार क्रमबद्ध चरणों में बांटता है, जिनमें से प्रत्येक चरण बच्चे की वस्तुओं और विचारों पर मानसिक संक्रियाएं (operations) करने की क्षमता से परिभाषित होता है।

संरक्षण (conservation) — यह समझ कि किसी वस्तु की मात्रा (संख्या, द्रव्यमान, आयतन, लंबाई) उसके भौतिक स्वरूप या व्यवस्था में परिवर्तन के बावजूद समान रहती है — विशेष रूप से मूर्त संक्रियात्मक चरण (लगभग 7 से 11 वर्ष) में विकसित होती है। इस चरण में बच्चे "संक्रियात्मक" चिंतन प्राप्त कर लेते हैं: वे किसी परिवर्तन को मानसिक रूप से उलट सकते हैं (उत्क्रमणीयता/reversibility) और एक साथ एक से अधिक आयामों पर ध्यान दे सकते हैं (बहु-आयामी ध्यान/decentration), इसलिए वे केवल वस्तु के दिखने के …
qs.rel: Conservation begins in the concrete operational stage (about 7 years); liquid, number and mass conservation tasks. Neighbours: preoperational children centre on one dimension; reversibility and compensation explain conservation; volume conservation at ~11.

qs.stem: When a learner encounters new information that cannot be readily incorporated into their existing mental frameworks, and must therefore adjust their current understanding, what cognitive process is primarily at play?
qs.sol:
Piaget described cognitive development as adaptation through two complementary processes acting on mental schemas. Assimilation fits new experience into an existing schema without changing it, while accommodation modifies an existing schema, or builds a new one, when the incoming experience does not fit. Equilibration is the broader self-regulating drive that moves a learner between these two processes to restore a stable, coherent understanding.

The stem describes new information that cannot be readily incorporated into the learner's existing framework, so the learner must adjust their current understanding. …
qs.rel: Accommodation = altering schemas to fit new information; assimilation = fitting new information into existing schemas; equilibration balances them. Neighbours: schema, disequilibrium, adaptation (assimilation + accommodation), organisation.

qs.stem:
Choose the correct answer from the options to complete the sentence.

Development of an individual is a collective outcome of:
qs.sol: Development combines biological maturation with learning from experience. Neither biological growth alone nor schooling alone covers the whole process.
qs.rel: Development is the collective outcome of maturity and learning. Neighbours: heredity and environment, readiness.

qs.sol: “बाल्यावस्था से वयस्कता की ओर संक्रमण।” के दौरान किशोर नई सामाजिक भूमिकाएँ और अपनी पहचान तलाशते हैं, जिससे पहचान संबंधी उलझन हो सकती है। “किशोरों की जन्म से ही निश्चित पहचान होती है।” पहचान को जन्म से स्थिर मानता है, जबकि किशोरावस्था में पहचान का अन्वेषण जारी रहता है।
qs.rel: Adolescence (12-18) is a transition from childhood to adulthood: identity formation (Erikson: identity vs role confusion), storm and stress (G. Stanley Hall), Marcia's identity statuses. Neighbours: puberty, formal operations, peer influence.

qs.sol: Growth and development are related but distinct ideas in the study of children. Growth refers to quantitative, measurable changes in the physical body — increases in height, weight, and overall size — that occur mainly during the years leading up to physical maturity. Development refers to a broader process of change across the child's cognitive, social, and emotional capacities, continuing throughout life even once physical growth has slowed or stopped. …
qs.rel: Growth is quantitative and measurable (height, weight); development is qualitative and includes growth plus maturation and learning. Neighbours: growth stops, development continues; development is multidimensional; both interact.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements best explains the interaction between heredity and environment in human development?

opts.A: Heredity sets the potential, and environment influences its realisation.
opts.B: Heredity has a greater influence than environment in all cases.
opts.C: Environment determines heredity during prenatal stages.
opts.D: Environment determines physical structure; heredity determines behaviour.

qs.sol: Development is shaped by both heredity and environment acting together, not by either factor alone. Heredity refers to the genetic material an individual inherits at conception; it fixes a range of potential for physical, cognitive, and behavioural traits. Environment refers to every external influence during and after development — nutrition, stimulation, learning opportunities, family, and culture — that acts on this inherited potential and decides how much of it is actually expressed. …
qs.rel: Heredity sets potential (range) and environment determines how far it is realised; both interact continuously (e.g. height needs nutrition). Neighbours: nature-nurture controversy, twin and adoption studies, Vygotsky and Bronfenbrenner emphasising environment.

qs.stem: What is an effective way to assess the impact of pretend play on language development?
qs.sol: Pretend play supports language development through interaction, narration and role-based conversation. Observing group storytelling is therefore an effective way to assess its language impact.
qs.rel: Pretend play supports language, narrative skill, symbolic thinking and social perspective; observing group storytelling and role talk reveals vocabulary and syntax use. Neighbours: Vygotsky's view of play as leading development; Parten's stages; Piaget's symbolic play.

qs.stem: Which psychological theory best explains the process of self-concept development through stages of autonomy and emotional regulation?
qs.sol: “Erikson’s Psychosocial Development Theory” is correct: Erikson describes psychosocial stages in which autonomy, initiative and later identity contribute to the developing sense of self. “Piaget’s Cognitive Development Theory” fails: Piaget focuses on changes in thinking and reasoning rather than these psychosocial tasks.
qs.rel: Erikson's psychosocial theory: autonomy vs shame and doubt (1-3 years) builds self-control and self-concept. Neighbours: trust vs mistrust, initiative vs guilt, industry vs inferiority; each stage has a crisis and virtue (hope, will, purpose, competence).

qs.sol:
अवधारणा

व्यवहार और विकास को आनुवंशिकता (प्रकृति) तथा परिवेश और अनुभव (पोषण) दोनों प्रभावित करते हैं। इन दोनों प्रभावों के सापेक्ष योगदान पर होने वाली बहस को मनोविज्ञान में “प्रकृति बनाम पोषण” कहा जाता है।

अनुप्रयोग

प्रश्न में पहला पक्ष आनुवंशिकता है, इसलिए वह प्रकृति से मेल खाता है। दूसरा पक्ष परिवेश है, इसलिए वह पोषण से मेल खाता है। अतः दिए गए युग्म में आनुवंशिकता और परिवेश के प्रभावों का मानक नाम “पोषण बनाम प्रकृति” है।

तुलना

“जीन बनाम शिक्षा” में परिवेश को केवल औपचारिक शिक्षा तक सीमित किया गया है।

“मस्तिष्क बनाम मानसिक वाद-विवाद” आनुवंशिकता और परिवेश की श्रेणियों का युग्म नहीं है।

“आनुवंशिकता बनाम मनोविज्ञान” में दूसरा शब्द एक अध्ययन-विषय है, परिवेश का नाम नहीं।

इसलिए उत्तर: पोषण  …
qs.rel: Behaviour and development are shaped jointly by heredity (nature) and environment/experience (nurture); the relative contribution is the nature-nurture debate. Neighbours: twin studies, adoption studies, interaction view as accepted position.

qs.stem: A secondary school student begins questioning family beliefs after discussions with friends and gradually changes some of their views. Which concept of socialization does this scenario best represent?

opts.B: Influence of peer group in middle childhood
opts.C: Dominance of group games during adolescence
opts.D: Development of moral values in childhood

qs.sol:
Concept

Socialization is the lifelong process through which a person absorbs the norms, values and beliefs of their social groups. The family is the first (primary) agent of socialization, but the peer group is a powerful secondary agent: as a child grows, age-mates become a key point of reference, and discussion with them can lead a person to re-examine and revise beliefs that were first learned at home.

Application

In this scenario the student begins questioning family beliefs after talking with friends and adjusts some views because of the peer group. The source of the change is the age-mate group and the outcome is a reshaping of previously held attitudes. …
qs.rel: Peer group influence increases from middle childhood through adolescence; peers shape attitudes, values and conformity. Neighbours: Erikson's identity vs role confusion, Kohlberg's conventional level, Bronfenbrenner's microsystem.

qs.stem: Which of the following comes under socio-emotional development of play?

opts.A: Playing helps to develop memory, and the ability to analyse
opts.C: Play provides opportunity for children to demonstrate their abilities and skills
opts.D: By play children learn or develop the ability to keep their mind on task at hand

qs.sol: When children play, they test their limits, master new challenges (like building a tall tower or winning a game), and showcase what they can do. This directly builds self-esteem, confidence, and a sense of identity, which are core pillars of emotional and social growth.
qs.rel: Play offers socio-emotional benefits: cooperation, turn-taking, empathy, expression of feelings, self-regulation. Neighbours: Parten's social play stages, Erikson's initiative vs guilt in the play age, Vygotsky's role of pretend play.

qs.stem: At which stage, the child not only detects your voice, discriminates between things that are the same or different, but begins to understand exactly what he is hearing?
qs.sol: “Comprehension” is the stage at which the child understands the meaning of what is heard, beyond merely noticing or distinguishing sounds. “Discrimination” means telling sounds apart as the same or different, without necessarily understanding their message.
qs.rel: Receptive language/comprehension stage: infant recognises voice, discriminates sounds and begins understanding words before speaking. Neighbours: language milestones: cooing 2-3 months, babbling ~6 months, first word ~12 months, two-word stage ~2 years.

qs.stem: While human development generally follows predictable patterns, educators consistently observe that no two students, even those of the same age, learn or behave identically. This core concept, acknowledging the unique combination of physical, intellectual, emotional and social attributes in each person, is known as:
qs.sol: Concept: Educational psychology describes growth along two complementary axes. The universal axis covers what every learner shares — the common sequence, direction and principles that development follows. The individual axis covers how the physical, intellectual, emotional and social attributes of one learner are organised into a single characteristic whole. The technical name for that organised whole is personality; Allport (1937) defined it as the dynamic organisation within the individual of those psychophysical systems that determine the person's characteristic behaviour and thought. …
qs.rel: Individual differences: development follows common patterns but personality, rate and style differ even among same-age children. Neighbours: heredity-environment interaction, Gardner's multiple intelligences, differentiated instruction.

qs.stem:
The process in which new and different ways of understanding and thinking emerge at different times is called _____.

Choose the correct answer from the options below:
qs.sol:
Modified from the official paper: the marked Hindi निरंतर सीखना is aligned to असतत सीखना, translating the printed English Discontinuous learning.

New, qualitatively different ways of thinking emerge at distinct times or stages.

That is discontinuous change; gradual change without distinct stages is continuous.

The described process is discontinuous learning.
qs.rel: Stage-based theories propose discontinuous development with qualitative shifts at different times, versus continuous (gradual) change. Neighbours: Piaget, Erikson, Kohlberg are stage (discontinuous) theorists; Bandura/learning theories emphasise continuity.

qs.stem: विकास परिपक्वता और अधिगम दोनों पर निर्भर करता है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही नहीं है? I. अधिगम समय के परिणामस्वरूप मांसपेशियों और तंत्रिका तंत्र में परिवर्तन को संदर्भित करता है। II. परिपक्वता व्यक्ति पर कार्य करने वाली उपयुक्त पर्यावरणीय शक्तियों की कार्रवाई को संदर्भित करती है।

opts.D: ना ही I ना ही II

qs.sol: विकास दो प्रक्रियाओं से होता है। परिपक्वता वंशानुगत क्षमताओं का प्रस्फुटन है: समय और आयु के साथ मांसपेशियों, तंत्रिका तंत्र और शरीर की अन्य संरचनाओं में होने वाले परिवर्तन, जो प्रशिक्षण पर बहुत कम निर्भर होते हैं। अधिगम अनुभव, अभ्यास और व्यक्ति पर उपयुक्त पर्यावरणीय शक्तियों की कार्रवाई से व्यवहार में होने वाला परिवर्तन है। कथन I अधिगम के नाम से परिपक्वता की परिभाषा देता है, और कथन II परिपक्वता के नाम से अधिगम की परिभाषा देता है। अतः दोनों कथन सही नहीं हैं।
qs.rel: Development depends on both maturation (biological readiness) and learning (experience); neither alone suffices, e.g. walking and writing need readiness. Neighbours: critical periods, readiness principle (Thorndike), Gesell's maturation theory.

qs.stem: A first-year college student, facing pressure to conform to peer norms, often exhibits denial about academic challenges. Which conceptual factor most likely contributes to the persistence of this defence mechanism in the sociocultural context?

opts.A: Influence of peer acceptance on defence mechanism selection
opts.D: Level of personal motivation affecting learning strategies

qs.sol:
Concept

Defence mechanisms (such as denial) are unconscious strategies used to manage anxiety. In educational psychology, why a defence mechanism persists is explained not only by intrapsychic factors but also by sociocultural reinforcement: during late adolescence and early adulthood, the peer group becomes a powerful reference group, and any behaviour — including a coping or defence response — that earns peer acceptance tends to be reinforced and sustained, while behaviour that risks peer rejection is avoided.

Application

The stem specifies that the student faces pressure to conform to peer norms, which is a peer-group-level (sociocultural) pressure. …
qs.rel: Adolescent peer pressure produces conformity and defence mechanisms like denial; peer acceptance matters. Neighbours: other defence mechanisms (repression, projection, rationalisation, regression, sublimation); Erikson's identity crisis.

qs.stem: इनमें से कौन सा सही नहीं है?

opts.A: जन्म पूर्व और जन्म पश्चात मानव सत्ता का विकास एक प्रतिमान या एक सामान्य क्रम का अनुकरण करता है |
opts.B: विकास की दिशा 'शीर्षपाद-पुच्छीय' के साथ साथ 'समीपस्थ' दिशा में भी है |
opts.C: विकास की प्रक्रिया गर्भाधान से लेकर जन्म से परिपक्वता तक निरंतर चलती रहती है।
opts.D: लड़कियां लड़कों की तुलना में पहले परिपक्व हो जाती हैं।

qs.sol:
अवधारणा: मानव विकास क्रमबद्ध और दिशात्मक प्रक्रिया है; यह गर्भाधान से शुरू होकर जीवनभर चलती रहती है। विकास में शीर्षपाद-पुच्छीय तथा समीप-दूरस्थ दिशाएँ और सामान्य परिपक्वता-भेद शामिल होते हैं।

अनुप्रयोग: पहले कथनों में विकास के सामान्य सिद्धान्त मिलते हैं। विकास का क्रम एक प्रतिमान का अनुसरण करता है; शरीर का विकास सिर से पैर की ओर और केंद्र से बाहर की ओर बढ़ता है; तथा लड़कियाँ सामान्यतः लड़कों से पहले परिपक्व होती हैं।

प्रतिपरीक्षण: विकास की परिभाषा इसे परिपक्वता पर समाप्त नहीं करती। गर्भाधान से परिपक्वता तक की अवधि उसका केवल एक चरण है, इसलिए जीवन के बाद के चरण भी विकास की निरंतरता में आते हैं।

निष्कर्ष: परिपक्वता तक ही विकास चलने का कथन विकास की आजीवन निरंतरता को सीमित करता है, इसलिए सही  …
qs.rel: Development begins at conception and continues through life. Neighbours: prenatal stages - germinal, embryonic, fetal.

qs.stem: A preschool teacher recorded a four-year-old child saying "I runned fast," while the child was correctly saying "She brought the flowers." What does this consistent grammatical error primarily indicate about the process the child is engaged in?
qs.sol:
Concept: Overgeneralization (also called overregularization) is a well-documented stage in child grammatical development. Once a child extracts a productive rule from the language they hear — such as the pattern of attaching a tense-marking morpheme to a verb stem — the child begins applying that rule broadly across verbs in the same category, including verbs whose past-tense form is actually irregular and does not follow the rule.

Application: Here, the child produces "runned" by attaching the regular past-tense morpheme "-ed" to the irregular verb "run," a form no adult models. …
qs.rel: Overregularisation ('runned') shows children learning productive morphological rules; it indicates rule-based language learning, not imitation. Neighbours: Chomsky's LAD, Brown's stages, telegraphic speech, holophrases.

qs.stem: “School Readiness” which is an important component in the ICDS Early Childhood Care and Education initiative, hold its roots in the Law of Readiness proposed by which of the following learning theories?
qs.sol: Thorndike stated a Law of Readiness among his laws of learning: readiness to act makes learning more satisfying and effective.
qs.rel: School readiness links to Thorndike's Law of Readiness (learning is effective when learner is ready) and maturation. Neighbours: laws of exercise and effect, ICDS ECCE for 3-6 years, Gesell's readiness; NEP 2020 Balvatika/foundational stage.

qs.stem: अकादमिक जरूरतों के अलावा किशोरावस्था के छात्रों के लिए निम्नलिखित में से क्या आवश्यक है?

opts.A: भावनात्मक और प्रेरक आवश्यकताओं को संबोधित करना
opts.C: नवीनतम शिक्षण गैजेट के साथ लैस करना

qs.sol: किशोरों को पढ़ाई के साथ भावनात्मक और प्रेरक सहारा चाहिए।
qs.rel: Adolescents need emotional, motivational and social support besides academics: guidance and counselling, life skills, healthy peer relationships. Neighbours: identity formation, storm and stress, Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya programme, adolescence education.

qs.stem:
Choose the most appropriate option from the following.

Development and behavior of individuals is by and large influenced by:
qs.sol: Development reflects the interaction of inherited traits with circumstances; neither factor acts in isolation.
qs.rel: Development and behaviour are shaped by interplay of heredity and environment. Neighbours: nature vs nurture, epigenetics.

qs.stem: ब्रौंफेनब्रनर के विकास के सिद्धांत के अनुसार, सरकारी नीतियों और सांस्कृतिक परिवर्तनों में व्यक्ति के पारिस्थितिक तंत्र की कौन सी परत शामिल है?
qs.sol: आधिकारिक उत्तर पर टिप्पणी: पुस्तिका में एक्सोसिस्टम अंकित है। सरकारी नीति बाहरी संस्थाओं के माध्यम से व्यक्ति को अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से प्रभावित कर सकती है, इसलिए यह व्याख्या संभव है। व्यापक सांस्कृतिक मूल्य सामान्यतः मैक्रोसिस्टम से जुड़े होते हैं, इसलिए प्रश्न की शब्दावली एक से अधिक पारिस्थितिक परतों को समेटती है।
qs.rel: Bronfenbrenner's ecological systems: microsystem (family, school), mesosystem (links among microsystems), exosystem (indirect settings, e.g. parents' workplace, government policies), macrosystem (culture, laws), chronosystem (time/historical change).

qs.sol: “विकासात्मक प्रतिफल का समर्थन करना और भविष्य में अधिगम कठिनाइयों को कम करना” प्रारंभिक सहायता से विकासात्मक कौशल बढ़ाने और आगे की सीखने की कठिनाइयाँ कम करने का लक्ष्य बताता है। “शारीरिक अशक्तता का शीघ्र निदान करना” मूल्यांकन का उपयोगी कदम हो सकता है, पर हस्तक्षेप का समग्र विकासात्मक उद्देश्य नहीं है।
qs.rel: Early intervention supports developmental outcomes and reduces later learning difficulties. Neighbours: critical periods, plasticity, screening and identification, early stimulation, IFSP/IEP concepts.

qs.sol: भोजन के बाद रोना सामान्य शिशु व्यवहार हो सकता है; अन्य व्यवहार सामाजिक संचार से जुड़े प्रारंभिक संकेत हैं। “अपना नाम सुनकर जवाब न देना” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि नाम पुकारने पर प्रतिक्रिया न देना संभावित प्रारंभिक संकेत है।
qs.rel: Crying after feeding is normal infant behaviour; red flags for autism are not responding to name, poor eye contact and delayed joint attention (by 12 months). Neighbours: M-CHAT and Q-CHAT screening, social communication deficits.

topics.deep:
- **Growth vs development:** growth = quantitative, physical, measurable, stops at maturity; development = qualitative + quantitative, psychological, lifelong, sequential, continuous, follows cephalocaudal (head to foot) and proximodistal (centre to periphery) directions, general to specific, with individual differences. Maturation = biological unfolding (Gesell); **readiness** = maturation plus experience.
- **Age bands:** infancy 0-2, early childhood 2-6 (preschool; ICDS/ECCE 3-6), later childhood 6-12, adolescence 12-18 (puberty, "storm and stress" - G. S. Hall), adulthood 18+. NEP 2020 foundational stage = 3-8 years.
- **Piaget's cognitive stages:**

| Stage | Age | Key features |
|---|---|---|
| Sensorimotor | 0-2 | reflexes to goal-directed action, **object permanence** (~8-12 months), A-not-B error |
| Preoperational | 2-7 | symbolic play, **egocentrism**, animism, centration, no conservation, irreversibility |
| Concrete operational | 7-11 | **conservation**, reversibility, classification, seriation, decentration - needs concrete objects |
| Formal operational | 11+ | abstract, hypothetical-deductive and proportional reasoning |

- **Piaget's terms:** schema, **assimilation** (fit new into old), **accommodation** (change schema), **equilibration**, adaptation, organisation, disequilibrium. Stages are universal and sequential but timing varies. Critics: underestimated infants, ignored culture.
- **Vygotsky:** sociocultural; **ZPD** (gap between independent and assisted performance), scaffolding (Wood-Bruner), MKO, private speech becomes inner speech, language as tool of thought. Bruner: enactive, iconic, symbolic modes; spiral curriculum.
- **Erikson (psychosocial):**

| Crisis | Approx. age | Virtue |
|---|---|---|
| Trust vs mistrust | 0-1 | hope |
| Autonomy vs shame/doubt | 1-3 | will |
| Initiative vs guilt | 3-6 | purpose |
| Industry vs inferiority | 6-12 | competence |
| Identity vs role confusion | 12-18 | fidelity |
| Intimacy vs isolation | young adult | love |
| Generativity vs stagnation | middle adult | care |
| Integrity vs despair | old age | wisdom |

- **Kohlberg's moral development:** Preconventional (stage 1 punishment-obedience, stage 2 instrumental exchange) -> Conventional (stage 3 good boy/girl, stage 4 law and order) -> Postconventional (stage 5 social contract, stage 6 universal ethical principles; ~13+ and not everyone). Method: Heinz dilemma. Piaget's moral stages: heteronomous (before ~7) then autonomous. Gilligan: ethics of care critique.
- **Freud (psychosexual):** oral, anal, phallic, latency, genital. **Bronfenbrenner:** microsystem, mesosystem, exosystem (indirect settings, policies), macrosystem (culture), chronosystem (time). **Bowlby/Ainsworth:** attachment (secure, avoidant, ambivalent). **Parten:** unoccupied, solitary, onlooker, parallel, associative, cooperative play.
- **Heredity vs environment:** genes set the potential (range), environment decides expression; twin and adoption studies; internal factors = heredity, intelligence, hormones; external = family, school, nutrition, culture. Critical/sensitive periods; early brain is highly plastic (synaptogenesis then pruning, myelination).
- **Milestones:** social smile ~6 weeks, sits ~6 months, babbling ~6 months, pincer grasp ~9 months, walks ~12 months, first word ~12 months, two-word sentences 18-24 months, vocabulary ~2000-2500 words at 5-6 years; birth weight doubles by ~5 months and triples by 1 year; gross motor precedes fine motor.
- **Adolescence:** Marcia's identity statuses (diffusion, foreclosure, moratorium, achievement), peer influence, emotional lability, need for guidance and counselling, Elkind's imaginary audience.

**Likely question angles:**
- Match theorist with theory (Piaget, Vygotsky, Erikson, Kohlberg, Bruner, Bronfenbrenner, Bowlby).
- Age ranges of Erikson's, Piaget's or Kohlberg's stages and crises.
- Conservation of number/mass/volume ages and which stage lacks reversibility.
- Differences between growth and development, maturation and learning.
- Principles of development (cephalocaudal, proximodistal, general to specific).
- Zone of proximal development vs scaffolding and who coined each.
- Identify Bronfenbrenner system from an example (parents' workplace = exosystem).
- Motor milestone at a given age; gross vs fine motor.
- Types of play (Parten) and their ages.
- Heredity-environment interaction statements; twin studies.

topics.title: 2. Learning Theories & Psychology of Learning
topics.theory:
- **Learning** = relatively permanent change in behaviour due to experience (not maturation/fatigue). It is active, purposive, continuous, transferable.
- **Classical conditioning** (Pavlov): UCS-UCR, CS-CR; extinction, spontaneous recovery, generalisation. **Operant** (Skinner): reinforcement (positive/negative) vs punishment, shaping, schedules; variable ratio most extinction-resistant.
- **Thorndike (trial and error, connectionism):** laws of **readiness, exercise, effect**; cat puzzle box (published 1898-1913).
- **Gestalt** (Wertheimer, Koffka, Kohler): insight learning, whole > parts, figure-ground, closure, proximity. **Tolman:** latent learning, cognitive maps.
- **Bandura (social learning):** attention, retention, reproduction, motivation; Bobo doll; **self-efficacy**; vicarious reinforcement.
- **Constructivism** (Piaget, Vygotsky, Bruner): learners construct knowledge; 5E model; teacher = facilitator; NCF 2005 stance.
- **Kolb:** concrete experience -> reflective observation -> abstract conceptualisation -> active experimentation. Dewey: learning by doing.
- **Transfer of learning:** positive/negative/zero; lateral vs vertical; theories - identical elements (Thorndike), generalisation (Judd).
- **Learning styles** (VARK): visual, auditory, read/write, kinaesthetic; recency/primacy effects; Ebbinghaus forgetting curve.
- Teacher-centred = memorising, extrinsic motivation; learner-centred = interaction, intrinsic motivation.

qs.stem:
Which factors affect learning?

1. Maturation

2. Readiness to learn

3. Learning environment

Choose the correct code.
qs.sol: Maturation, readiness and the learning environment all influence learning.
qs.rel: Factors affecting learning: maturation, readiness, motivation, learning environment, intelligence, teacher method, fatigue, health. Neighbours: Thorndike's Law of Readiness, individual differences, transfer of training.

qs.stem: बच्चे अपनी प्रथम भाषा मुख्यतः किस प्रकार अर्जित करते हैं?
qs.sol:
अवधारणा

प्रथम-भाषा अर्जन मुख्यतः अंतर्निहित भाषा-विकास है: बच्चे सुलभ और सार्थक भाषायी संपर्क तथा सामाजिक अंतःक्रिया से प्रतिरूपों, अर्थों और प्रयोग का अनुमान लगाते हैं। मौखिक भाषा के संदर्भ में इसमें सामान्यतः सुनना और सांकेतिक भाषा के संदर्भ में दृश्य अंतःक्रिया शामिल होती है। यह प्रत्यक्ष भाषा-शिक्षण से भिन्न है, जिसमें नियमों या पाठों की योजना बनाकर उन्हें क्रमबद्ध किया जाता है।

अनुप्रयोग

परिवेश से अर्जन इसी अंतर्निहित प्रक्रिया को दर्शाता है: बच्चा वास्तविक उद्देश्यों के लिए प्रयुक्त सुलभ भाषा से संपर्क करता है, भाषायी रूपों को अर्थों से जोड़ता है और औपचारिक व्याकरण-पाठ्यक्रम की आवश्यकता के बिना धीरे-धीरे उसका प्रयोग करने लगता है।

तुलना

औपचारिक कक्षा-शिक्षण नियोजित संस्थागत अनुदेशन …
qs.rel: Constructivism: learners actively construct knowledge from experience and prior knowledge (Piaget, Vygotsky, Bruner). Neighbours: 5E model, discovery learning, ZPD, NCF 2005 stress on constructing knowledge, teacher as facilitator.

qs.stem:
Learning can be considered as ______.

I. the relatively permanent modification of behaviour

II. the relatively permanent change in personality
qs.sol:
Note on the answer key: DSSSB published only a provisional answer key for this paper, and no final key. The provisional key marks “Both I and II”. The defensible answer is “Only I”, because learning is normally defined by relatively lasting behavioural change, while personality change is only a possible consequence. This question is graded by the provisional key, as in the actual exam.

Including the second statement in the definition is disputed. The standard learning definition centres on a relatively permanent behavioural change from experience; the scope of the second statement is disputed.
qs.rel: Learning = relatively permanent change in behaviour (or behaviour potential) due to experience or practice. Neighbours: not due to maturation, fatigue or drugs; Kimble's definition; includes knowledge, skills and attitudes.

qs.stem: _________ अधिगम का प्रमुख साधन है।
qs.sol: प्रत्यक्ष अनुभव क्रिया को चिंतन से जोड़ता है और यहाँ इसे अधिगम का प्रमुख साधन माना गया है।
qs.rel: Experience (especially direct, first-hand) is the chief means of learning; Dewey's learning by doing and Kolb's experiential cycle (concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualisation, active experimentation). Neighbours: Edgar Dale's cone of experience.

qs.stem: LCMS stands for __________.
qs.sol: “learning content management system” is the expansion of LCMS, a system for creating, organising and delivering learning content. “learning content module system” sounds similar but substitutes “module” for the established term “management.”
qs.rel: 'Cognition' derives from Latin cognoscere (to know); it covers thinking, remembering, perceiving, problem-solving. Neighbours: Piaget's cognitive development, Bloom's cognitive domain, metacognition (Flavell).

qs.stem: The National Academy of Agricultural Research Management is located in:
qs.sol:
Identify NAARM, the ICAR academy for agricultural research management.

Its campus is at Rajendranagar in Hyderabad.
qs.rel: Thorndike: trial and error (connectionism, S-R bonds) with laws of readiness, exercise and effect; experiment with cat in puzzle box. Neighbours: Skinner (operant), Pavlov (classical), Kohler (insight, apes).

qs.stem: Which of the following methods emphasises the active participation of learners and is based on the principle of learning by doing?
qs.sol:
Concept

Teaching methods differ chiefly in where they place the primary source of learning — the teacher’s spoken exposition, a general rule supplied in advance, a sudden inner insight, or the learner’s own activity.

Experiential learning, developed by John Dewey and David Kolb, rests on the principle that knowledge is constructed from the learner’s own concrete experience and from reflection on that experience. This principle is what is meant by “learning by doing”, and it is precisely what makes the learner’s participation necessarily active. …
qs.rel: Learning is purposive, active, continuous, goal-directed, transferable and results from experience; it is never unintentional-only or passive. Neighbours: learning vs maturation, learning is individual and social, relatively permanent.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a step in the Scientific method of solving a problem?

opts.C: Memorizing the steps to solve the problem

qs.sol: The scientific method of problem solving proceeds through steps such as sensing (recognising) the problem, defining and analysing it, collecting relevant data, forming hypotheses, testing them and drawing conclusions. Memorising the steps to solve a problem is rote learning, not a step of the scientific method.
qs.rel: Trial-and-error theory belongs to E. L. Thorndike (S-R bond, connectionism), published 1898-1913. Neighbours: laws of readiness, exercise (use and disuse) and effect; secondary laws; cat in puzzle box.

qs.stem: कौन सी जोड़ी प्रतिभागियों को पारस्परिक कौशल, आत्मविश्वास, संचार और मुखरता विकसित करने में मदद करते हैं?
qs.sol: मिश्रित लिंग की जोड़ी में अलग लैंगिक अनुभव वाले प्रतिभागी साझा कार्य करते हैं। सहायक वातावरण में इससे संवाद, आत्मविश्वास और अपनी बात स्पष्ट रखने का अभ्यास हो सकता है। बाकी शब्द किसी एक लिंग या पहचान को बताते हैं, जोड़ी की मिश्रित बनावट नहीं। प्रश्न किसी लिंग की क्षमता का मूल्यांकन नहीं, सहभागियों की व्यवस्था पूछता है। पुरुष एक लिंग बताता है, मिश्रित जोड़ी की संरचना नहीं। महिला भी एक लिंग बताता है, दो समूहों का मिश्रण नहीं। मिश्रित लिंग की जोड़ी विविध सहभागिता देती है। ट्रांसजेंडर एक पहचान है, अपने आप जोड़ी की संरचना नहीं।
qs.rel: Thorndike's trial-and-error work is associated with the 1913 publication (Educational Psychology). Neighbours: doctoral research on animal intelligence 1898; Pavlov's classical conditioning 1900s; Skinner's operant box 1930s.

qs.stem: What is neural plasticity in early childhood?

opts.B: The brain's ability to change and adapt
opts.C: The process of learning to walk

qs.sol: Neural plasticity is the brain’s capacity to change and adapt in response to experience. “The process of learning to walk” may be influenced by plasticity, but it is one learned ability rather than the brain’s general capacity to adapt.
qs.rel: Learning produces relatively permanent change in behaviour due to experience; it is not temporary change from fatigue or drugs. Neighbours: learning vs maturation, learning curve, plateau.

qs.stem: How students learn and develop in school?
qs.sol: Students learn through exchanges with teachers, peers, tasks, and the classroom environment. They discuss ideas, ask questions, receive feedback, and build on what others say. Interaction names this social process directly and explains both learning and development in school. Intellectual describes a domain of development rather than a way students engage with others. Coordination can support activities, and motivation can encourage participation, but neither alone states the process of learning with people in a school setting.
qs.rel: School learning and development occur through interaction among learner, peers, teacher and environment (social constructivism). Neighbours: Vygotsky's social interaction, collaborative learning, ZPD, scaffolding.

qs.stem: Financial resources in a school refer to:

opts.C: grants and allocations to the school

qs.sol:
A school's resources are conventionally grouped into three broad categories: human resources (the people who teach and learn), physical or material resources (the infrastructure, equipment, and facilities used for teaching and learning), and financial resources (the money available to run and sustain the school, including its budget, grants, and other monetary allocations).

The question asks specifically what financial resources refers to. …
qs.rel: Kolb's experiential learning cycle has four stages: concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualisation, active experimentation. Neighbours: learner types: diverger, assimilator, converger, accommodator; Gibbs' reflective cycle has six stages.

qs.stem: 'अधिगम शैलियों (learning styles)' की अवधारणा के अनुसार,

opts.A: प्रभावी शिक्षण के लिए अधिगम शैलियाँ अप्रासंगिक होती हैं
opts.B: अलग-अलग छात्रों के अधिगम के अधिमानित तरीके होते हैं जैसे दृश्य, श्रव्य या गत्यात्मक
opts.C: सभी विद्यार्थी, अपनी वरीयताओं की परवाह किए बिना एक ही तरीके से सीखते हैं
opts.D: अधिगम के लिए केवल दृश्य और श्रव्य शैलियाँ ही प्रभावी होती हैं

qs.sol:
अवधारणा

अधिगम शैलियाँ (Learning Styles) की अवधारणा के अनुसार, प्रत्येक शिक्षार्थी की सूचना ग्रहण करने और संसाधित करने की एक अधिमानित (preferred) विधि होती है। इसे सामान्यतः तीन प्रमुख श्रेणियों में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है — दृश्य (Visual), श्रव्य (Auditory), और गत्यात्मक/स्पर्शनीय (Kinesthetic) — जिन्हें संक्षेप में VAK मॉडल कहा जाता है (नील फ्लेमिंग के VARK मॉडल में पठन-लेखन शैली भी जोड़ी गई है)। इस अवधारणा का मूल सिद्धांत यह है कि शिक्षार्थियों के बीच सीखने के माध्यम को लेकर व्यक्तिगत भिन्नता (individual variability) पाई जाती है, न कि एकरूपता।

अनुप्रयोग

प्रश्न में दिए गए चार कथनों में से केवल एक कथन इस केंद्रीय सिद्धांत — अर्थात शिक्षार्थियों के बीच अधिगम माध्यम की विविधता — को सही ढंग से …
qs.rel: Learning styles: learners prefer different modes (visual, auditory, kinaesthetic - VARK/Fleming); teachers use varied methods to match. Neighbours: Kolb's styles, Gardner's multiple intelligences; research evidence for 'matching' is weak.

qs.stem: Which skill is essential when cross collating information from different sources?

opts.C: Evaluating the credibility and relevance of each source
opts.D: Accepting all information as true without evaluation

qs.sol: “Evaluating the credibility and relevance of each source” is correct: Cross-checking sources requires judging whether each source is trustworthy and relevant to the question. “Accepting all information as true without evaluation” fails: Accepting every claim without evaluation prevents errors or conflicting evidence from being identified.
qs.rel: Learning brings mental (cognitive) growth: knowledge, understanding and skills, besides emotional and social change. Neighbours: learning vs growth, domains: cognitive, affective, psychomotor (Bloom).

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन कम दृष्टि वाले बच्चों के लिए सहायक उपकरण नहीं है?
qs.sol:
उत्तर-कुंजी पर टिप्पणी: DSSSB ने इस प्रश्नपत्र की केवल अनंतिम उत्तर-कुंजी जारी की थी, अंतिम कुंजी नहीं। अनंतिम कुंजी “स्पीच सिंथेसाइज़र” को सही मानती है। तर्कसंगत उत्तर “ब्रेल” है, क्योंकि ब्रेल मुख्यतः अंधत्व में स्पर्श से पढ़ने का साधन है, पर अल्प दृष्टि वाले विद्यार्थी को भी सहायता दे सकता है। इस प्रश्न का मूल्यांकन अनंतिम कुंजी के अनुसार किया गया है, जैसा वास्तविक परीक्षा में हुआ।

स्क्रीन पाठ को आवाज में बदलना अल्प दृष्टि वाले विद्यार्थी की मदद कर सकता है। ब्रेल मुख्यतः अंधत्व में स्पर्श से पढ़ने के लिए है; आवर्धक और चश्मा बची दृष्टि को सहारा देते हैं और वाणी संश्लेषण भी सहायक हो सकता है।
qs.rel: Bandura's observational learning has four processes: attention, retention, reproduction (motor), motivation (reinforcement). Neighbours: Bobo doll experiment, vicarious reinforcement, modelling, self-efficacy, reciprocal determinism.

qs.stem: जब विद्यालय में विभिन्न प्रकार की सामग्री का उपयोग किया जाता है, तो उसे क्या कहा जाता हैं?
qs.sol:
उत्तर-कुंजी पर टिप्पणी: DSSSB ने इस प्रश्नपत्र की केवल अनंतिम उत्तर-कुंजी जारी की थी, अंतिम कुंजी नहीं। अनंतिम कुंजी “सामग्री अनुकूलन” को सही मानती है। तर्कसंगत उत्तर “सामग्री विस्तार” है, क्योंकि अधिक प्रकार की सामग्री का उपयोग शाब्दिक रूप से सामग्री विस्तार है, पर इसे अनुकूलन भी माना जा सकता है। इस प्रश्न का मूल्यांकन अनंतिम कुंजी के अनुसार किया गया है, जैसा वास्तविक परीक्षा में हुआ।

अनुकूलन सामग्री को शिक्षार्थियों के अनुसार बदलता है और विविध सामग्री के उपयोग को भी शामिल कर सकता है। अधिक प्रकार की सामग्री उपलब्ध सामग्री का विस्तार करती है।
qs.rel: Visual learners prefer images, maps and graphic organisers; auditory prefer listening/discussion; kinaesthetic prefer doing. Neighbours: VARK model, Gardner's spatial intelligence, multisensory teaching.

qs.stem: In enhancing physical climate of the classroom, what is the role of a teacher? I. Draw attention of the school authorities for regular maintenance of the school building II. Place a dust bin in the classroom for systematic disposal of garbage of the classroom
qs.sol: A teacher can improve the physical classroom climate by informing school authorities about needed building maintenance and by providing a dustbin for orderly waste disposal. Structural repair requires institutional action, while daily cleanliness also needs classroom routines. Both actions support a safer, cleaner learning space. A dustbin and disposal routine also improve the space. Reporting maintenance needs is also part of responsible care. Maintenance advocacy and waste disposal both help the physical climate. Both practical teacher actions contradict denying the statements.
qs.rel: Behaviourism: learning is S-R association shaped by conditioning and reinforcement (Watson, Pavlov, Thorndike, Skinner). Neighbours: mind seen as black box, cognitivists reject this; observable behaviour is unit of study.

qs.stem: The step ‘Generalization’ in the Herbartian model aims at which of the following?
qs.sol:
Concept: In the Herbartian lesson sequence, generalization moves from particular examples to a principle that applies beyond those examples. Comparison or association first identifies shared features; generalization then expresses the shared rule.

Application: The prompt asks for the aim of the Generalization step. After comparing lesson examples, learners formulate a general rule that can be used in further cases. This makes ‘Formulating universal rules’ the matching activity.

Repeating the entire lesson revisits content; it does not abstract a rule from the examples.

Providing entertainment seeks engagement rather than a general principle. …
qs.rel: Experiential learning is learning through experience plus reflection (Kolb, Dewey). Neighbours: 4-stage cycle, project and field-based learning, 'learning by doing'; Edgar Dale's cone of experience.

qs.stem: Which of the following statement characterize the nature of social sciences? I. Social science are those aspect of knowledge which have direct bearing on man’s activities in different sociocultural fields. II. Social science seek to find out truths about human relationships which ultimately contribute to the social utility and advancement of knowledge.
qs.sol: Social sciences study human beings in society, their economic, political, social and cultural activities, so they are the branches of knowledge with a direct bearing on man's activities in different sociocultural fields. They also seek truths about human relationships that contribute to social welfare and to the advancement of knowledge. Both statements characterise the nature of social sciences.
qs.rel: Empiricism: knowledge comes from sensory experience and observation (Locke, Hume), as against rationalism (reason, Descartes). Neighbours: scientific method, a posteriori knowledge, Locke's tabula rasa, intuition and authority as other sources.

qs.stem: शैक्षिक यथार्थवाद एक विचार है कि हमें छात्रों को वास्तविकता का बोध होने और समझने के लिए सिखाने के लिए ___________, आलोचनात्मक चिंतन और वैज्ञानिक पद्धति का अध्ययन करना चाहिए।
qs.sol: शैक्षिक यथार्थवाद तर्क, आलोचनात्मक चिंतन और संसार के वैज्ञानिक अध्ययन पर बल देता है।
qs.rel: Classical conditioning is Ivan Pavlov's (dog salivation): UCS, UCR, CS, CR; processes: acquisition, extinction, spontaneous recovery, generalisation, discrimination. Neighbours: Watson's Little Albert, Skinner's operant conditioning.

qs.stem: बच्चों में आमतौर पर किस उम्र तक प्रारंभिक कल्पनात्मक भय गायब हो जाते हैं?
qs.sol: बाल विकास साहित्य (जैसे हरलॉक) बताता है कि प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था के भय प्रायः काल्पनिक होते हैं: भूत, राक्षस, अंधेरे और अकेले रहने का भय। तर्क और वास्तविकता की समझ बढ़ने के साथ ये काल्पनिक भय घटते हैं और सामान्यतः लगभग 12 वर्ष की आयु (उत्तर बाल्यावस्था के अंत) तक गायब हो जाते हैं; बाद के भय अधिक सामाजिक और यथार्थपरक होते हैं। प्रश्नपत्र की कुंजी भी 12 वर्ष देती है।
qs.rel: Characteristics of learning: it is transferable, purposive, continuous, active and experience-based; learning that cannot be transferred is not true learning. Neighbours: transfer of learning (positive, negative, zero), Thorndike's identical elements theory.

qs.stem: Which scheme was specifically revised in 1992 to promote education of children with disabilities in mainstream schools?
qs.sol: The Integrated Education for Disabled Children scheme was revised in 1992 to support children with disabilities in regular schools. The other named programs date from different education initiatives.
qs.rel: Repeated attempts until success = trial and error (Thorndike). Neighbours: insight learning (Kohler's Sultan, sudden solution), Skinner's shaping, the law of effect and learning curve.

qs.stem: A student tries many ways to build a stable tower by arranging blocks. After several unsuccessful attempts, the child finally manages to build a balanced structure. This illustrates __________.
qs.sol:
Concept: Thorndike's theory of trial and error learning (connectionism) states that when an organism faces a new problem, it tries out several different responses more or less at random. A response that produces a satisfying outcome is gradually strengthened (Thorndike's law of effect), while unsuccessful responses are gradually abandoned, until through repeated practice the successful response is performed reliably.

Application: In the scenario, the child tries several different arrangements of the blocks, and each unsuccessful attempt is followed by another attempt with a different arrangement. …
qs.rel: Transfer of learning: applying learning from one situation to another; types: positive, negative, zero; lateral, vertical; near and far. Neighbours: Thorndike's identical elements, Judd's generalisation theory, Gestalt transposition.

qs.stem: Why is early auditory stimulation crucial during a child's development?

opts.A: Because the brain's plasticity decreases with age, making early stimulation ineffective.
opts.B: Because the brain's plasticity is highest during early years, facilitating rapid development of listening and language skills.
opts.C: Because auditory skills are innate and do not require external stimulation.
opts.D: Because language development is solely dependent on visual cues.

qs.sol: “Because the brain's plasticity is highest during early years, facilitating rapid development of listening and language skills.” explains why early access to sound and responsive interaction supports auditory learning. “Because auditory skills are innate and do not require external stimulation.” overlooks the experience needed to develop useful listening and language abilities.
qs.rel: Principle of recency: most recent learning is remembered best (primacy = first learnt is remembered best). Neighbours: serial position effect, laws of exercise and effect, spaced practice, Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve.

qs.stem: Which of the following best exemplifies the 'Integrated' principle in curriculum development for children with mental retardation?

opts.A: Teaching mathematical operations in isolation without real-life application
opts.B: Emphasising rote memorisation of isolated facts
opts.D: Organising activities that combine language, art, and daily living skills

qs.sol:
An integrated curriculum connects several areas in one meaningful activity instead of teaching each skill in isolation.

Combining language, art and daily living gives practice across domains within the same learning experience.
qs.rel: Self-efficacy (Bandura): belief in one's ability to succeed; higher self-efficacy gives greater effort, persistence and motivation. Neighbours: sources: mastery experience, vicarious experience, verbal persuasion, emotional state; reciprocal determinism.

qs.stem: Perceiving the Great Bear constellation can be based on which of these theories?
qs.sol:
A constellation is perceived by grouping separate stars into a meaningful whole.

Gestalt theory explains this organization of parts into a unified pattern.
qs.rel: Gestalt theory: perception of wholes ('whole is greater than the sum of its parts'); principles: proximity, similarity, closure, continuity, figure-ground. Neighbours: Wertheimer, Kohler, Koffka; insight learning.

qs.stem: In the context of social cognitive theory, what role does self-efficacy play in learning and motivation?

opts.A: Higher self-efficacy leads to greater motivation, persistence, and resilience in the face of challenges.
opts.B: Self-efficacy is irrelevant to learning; only external rewards and punishments are significant motivators.
opts.C: Low self-efficacy enhances performance by motivating individuals to seek help and guidance.
opts.D: Self-efficacy is a static trait that does not change over time and does not impact learning outcomes.

qs.sol:
Concept: Self-efficacy is a person’s own judgement of their capability to organise and execute the courses of action required to reach a designated level of performance (Albert Bandura, social cognitive theory). It is not a general personality trait but a domain-specific and changeable belief. Four sources are identified for it:

Mastery experiences — one’s own direct record of success or failure, the strongest source of all.

Vicarious experience — watching a comparable other perform the task.

Verbal persuasion — credible encouragement or feedback from others.

Physiological and affective states — felt stress, fatigue, or arousal, and how it is interpreted. …
qs.rel: Self-efficacy (Bandura, social cognitive theory): confidence in one's capability affects choice of tasks, effort and persistence. Neighbours: observational learning, modelling, reciprocal determinism, locus of control (Rotter).

qs.stem: Which of the following emphasizes the role of rewards and punishment in learning?
qs.sol:
Thorndike’s law of effect connects a response’s consequences with its future strength.

Satisfying outcomes strengthen the response, while unpleasant outcomes weaken it in the classical account.
qs.rel: Law of effect (Thorndike): responses followed by satisfying consequences are strengthened; those followed by annoying ones weaken. Neighbours: Skinner's positive/negative reinforcement and punishment, reinforcement schedules.

qs.stem:
Which of the following does not define learning?

Learning can be defined as _____.

opts.B: Change achieved through practice and experience

qs.sol:
Learning is a relatively lasting change arising from practice or experience.

It can improve or worsen behaviour, and its effects can be assessed.

The claim that its change is not measurable therefore fails the intended definition.
qs.rel: Learning is a measurable, relatively permanent change in behaviour; change that is not measurable or not permanent is not learning. Neighbours: learning vs performance, fatigue/drug-induced change excluded.

qs.stem: What do we call it when learning of higher behavioural levels are facilitated by lower behavioural levels?
qs.sol:
Lower-level abilities become prerequisites supporting higher-level abilities.

Transfer moving upward through this hierarchy is called vertical transfer.
qs.rel: Vertical transfer: lower-level learning facilitates higher-level learning (e.g. addition helps multiplication); lateral transfer applies similar-level skill to a new setting. Neighbours: positive, negative, zero transfer; Gagné's hierarchy of learning.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a type of experience where a sudden, flash-like conviction of certainty strikes us?
qs.sol:
Intuition is an immediate apprehension or conviction that appears without a consciously articulated chain of reasoning.

Its sudden flash-like certainty distinguishes it from sensory disturbances and deliberate imaginative construction.
qs.rel: Intuition: sudden, insight-like conviction without conscious reasoning. Neighbours: insight learning (Kohler), 'aha' experience, Bruner on intuitive thinking, creativity stages (preparation, incubation, illumination, verification).

qs.stem:
The process of augmenting the same type of skills from that were to begin with is called:

Choose the correct response from the option below.
qs.sol:
Modified from the official paper: the Hindi निरंतर सीखना is changed to असतत सीखना to align with Discontinuous learning.

Augmenting the same type of skills is gradual quantitative development, retaining the skill’s underlying kind.

This is continuous learning; a discontinuous pattern involves qualitative change or reorganization.
qs.rel: Continuous/cumulative learning builds the same type of skills from earlier ones. Neighbours: spiral curriculum (Bruner), vertical and lateral transfer, practice and revision.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a process by which children learn? 1. Imitation 2. Observation Choose the correct code.
qs.sol: “Neither 1 nor 2”: Imitation and observation are both established ways children learn, so neither is excluded. “Only 1”: Declaring either process non-learning contradicts everyday observational learning.
qs.rel: Children learn through imitation, observation, trial and error, instruction and play, so both are valid processes. Neighbours: Bandura's modelling, Thorndike, Skinner's shaping, Vygotsky's social interaction.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a characteristic of learning process?

opts.C: Learning is the outcome of the interaction of the individual with the environment.

qs.sol: “Learning is a passive process.” is not a characteristic of learning because learners actively interact with experience and their environment. “Learning is goal-directed.” can describe purposeful learning, so it does not fit the negative prompt.
qs.rel: Learning is an active process: learner engagement is essential, so 'passive' is not a characteristic. Neighbours: constructivist active learning, goal-directed, transferable, lifelong.

qs.stem: दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही कथन का चयन करें।

opts.A: एडवर्ड थॉर्नडाइक (Edward Thorndike) को व्यवहारवाद के जनक के रूप में जाना जाता है।
opts.B: प्रयास एवं त्रुटि द्वारा अधिगम इवान पावलोव (Ivan Pavlov) द्वारा प्रतिपादित किया गया था।
opts.C: क्रियाप्रसूत अनुकूलन सिद्धांत बी. एफ. स्किनर (B. F. Skinner) द्वारा प्रतिपादित किया गया था।
opts.D: जॉन बी. वॉटसन (John B. Watson) ने शास्त्रीय अनुकूलन सिद्धांत प्रतिपादित किया था।

qs.sol:
संकल्पना

अधिगम सिद्धांत व्यवहार को परिवर्तित करने वाली प्रक्रिया के आधार पर शास्त्रीय अनुकूलन, क्रियाप्रसूत अनुकूलन और प्रयास एवं त्रुटि अधिगम में भेद करते हैं।

क्रियाप्रसूत अनुकूलन में किसी अनुक्रिया के बाद आने वाले परिणाम उस अनुक्रिया की भावी संभाव्यता को परिवर्तित करते हैं: पुनर्बलन इसे बढ़ाता है, जबकि दंड इसे घटाता है।

अनुप्रयोग

क्रियाप्रसूत अनुकूलन के सिद्धांत का प्रतिपादन बी. एफ. स्किनर द्वारा किए जाने वाला कथन इस भेद के अनुरूप है। स्किनर ने थॉर्नडाइक के प्रभाव के नियम के आधार पर क्रियाप्रसूत व्यवहार का प्रायोगिक विश्लेषण विकसित किया।

विरोधी विकल्पों का अंतर

एडवर्ड थॉर्नडाइक का संबंध संबंधवाद, प्रभाव के नियम तथा प्रयास एवं त्रुटि अधिगम से है; जॉन बी. …
qs.rel: Operant (instrumental) conditioning: Skinner, reinforcement shapes behaviour. Neighbours: classical conditioning (Pavlov), positive vs negative reinforcement.

qs.stem: What is the key method of learning in the behavioristic approach?
qs.sol: Behaviorist learning explains behavior change through stimulus-response associations and reinforcement. Conditioning is the process used to establish those associations.
qs.rel: Behaviourism's key method is conditioning: classical (Pavlov), operant (Skinner), connectionism (Thorndike). Neighbours: reinforcement, shaping, extinction, programmed instruction, token economy.

qs.sol: व्यवहार विश्लेषण की दो प्रमुख शाखाएँ प्रायोगिक और अनुप्रयुक्त व्यवहार विश्लेषण हैं। “प्रायोगिक और परिणामी (Experimental and Consequential)” में परिणामी को शाखा कहा गया है, जबकि मान्य शाखा अनुप्रयुक्त व्यवहार विश्लेषण है।
qs.rel: Behaviour analysis (Skinner) has two branches: experimental analysis of behaviour (basic research) and applied behaviour analysis (ABA, used in autism intervention). Neighbours: ABC model, DTT, reinforcement.

qs.sol: A stronger conditioned stimulus can make a conditioned response develop faster. “Random presentation of conditioned stimulus and un-conditioned stimulus” weakens their predictable association and tends to slow acquisition.
qs.rel: Classical conditioning is stronger when CS precedes UCS closely and is intense; random pairing weakens learning; extinction follows CS without UCS. Neighbours: forward vs backward conditioning, higher-order conditioning.

qs.stem: बच्चे जो देखते हैं उसका अनुकरण और आंतरिककरण क्यों करते हैं और फिर उन पैटर्न को अपने जीवन में दोहराते हैं?

opts.A: क्योंकि उन्हें सिखाया गया था कि कु छ लक्षण या गतिविधियाँ उनके लिए संलग्न होने के लिए उपयुक्त या अनुपयुक्त हैं
opts.B: क्योंकि वे माता-पिता की पीढ़ियों से बहुत प्रभावित हैं।
opts.C: क्योंकि बच्चे अपने प्राथमिक देखभालकर्ता को जो कु छ करते देखते हैं, उसके अवलोकन और अनुकरण के माध्यम से अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से सीखते हैं
opts.D: क्योंकि वे समकक्ष व्यक्ति की तुलना में उन भूमिकाओं को वयस्कों के रूप में खुद ही लेने की अधिक संभावना रखते हैं, जिनके माता-पिता कम रूढ़िवादी थे।

qs.sol: बच्चे देखभालकर्ताओं को देखकर और उनका अनुकरण करके अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से सीखते हैं।
