qs.rel: Children imitate and internalise caregivers' behaviour through observational learning (Bandura's social learning theory) and identification. Neighbours: modelling, vicarious reinforcement, gender-role socialisation, Bobo doll.

qs.stem: सामाजिक शिक्षा सिद्धांत समाजीकरण सिद्धांतों के तहत वर्गीकृत सिद्धांतों में से एक है। यह ____ के साथ सबसे निकट से जुड़ा हुआ है।
qs.sol: सामाजिक अधिगम सिद्धांत अल्बर्ट बंडूरा से जुड़ा है; इसमें दूसरों का अवलोकन और अनुकरण करके सीखना शामिल है।
qs.rel: Social learning theory is Albert Bandura's: learning by observing and imitating models, with attention, retention, reproduction and motivation. Neighbours: Bobo doll study, self-efficacy, socialisation theories, Mead's symbolic interactionism.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन अधिगम और शिक्षण के लिए शिक्षक-केंद्रित उपागम के बारे में सही नहीं है?

opts.A: एक मार्गीय संचालन किया जाता है; छात्र निष्क्रिय रूप से बैठते हैं और शिक्षक को सुनते हैं।
opts.B: छात्र परियोजना कार्य से परिचित होते हैं।
opts.C: पाठ्य प्रश्नों के उत्तर दिए जाते हैं और रटकर सीखे जाते हैं।
opts.D: शिक्षक का दृष्टिकोण पाठ्यक्रम को समय पर पूरा करना होता है।

qs.sol: शिक्षक-केंद्रित उपागम में शिक्षक मुख्य सूचना देता है और विद्यार्थी प्रायः सुनते हैं। पाठ्यपुस्तक के प्रश्नों को याद करना तथा समय पर पाठ्यक्रम पूरा करना भी ऐसे संचालन से मेल खाता है। परियोजना कार्य में विद्यार्थी खोज, योजना और कार्यान्वयन में अधिक सक्रिय होते हैं; यह विद्यार्थी-केंद्रित गतिविधि का उदाहरण है। प्रश्न असंगत कथन पूछता है, इसलिए परियोजना कार्य वाली बात को चुनना चाहिए।
qs.rel: Teacher-centred approach: teacher is authority, lecture/rote learning, passive students, exams; project work belongs to learner-centred approach. Neighbours: learner-centred vs teacher-centred contrasts, constructivist classroom.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are not correct?
 Statements:
 I. Conditioning of elicited behaviours defines classical conditioning.
 II. Conditioning of emitted behaviours defines operant conditioning.
qs.sol: Classical conditioning concerns elicited behaviours, while operant conditioning concerns emitted behaviours. Since both statements are correct, neither is not correct.
qs.rel: Classical conditioning concerns involuntary/elicited (reflex) responses; operant conditioning concerns voluntary behaviour shaped by consequences. Neighbours: respondent vs operant behaviour, Skinner box, Pavlov.

qs.stem: Which of the following best differentiates classical conditioning from operant conditioning?

opts.A: Classical conditioning involves learning through consequences; operant conditioning involves association between stimuli.
opts.B: Classical conditioning is based on reinforcement schedules; operant conditioning is based on pairing stimuli.
opts.C: Operant conditioning involves voluntary behaviours; classical conditioning involves involuntary reflexive responses.
opts.D: Operant conditioning occurs without consequences; classical conditioning requires punishment.

qs.sol: “Operant conditioning involves voluntary behaviours; classical conditioning involves involuntary reflexive responses.” is correct: Operant conditioning changes voluntary actions through their consequences, whereas classical conditioning links stimuli to elicit reflexive responses. “Classical conditioning involves learning through consequences; operant conditioning involves association between stimuli.” fails: The alternative reverses those mechanisms by assigning consequences to classical conditioning and stimulus pairing to operant conditioning.
qs.rel: Classical = association of stimuli, involuntary responses; operant = voluntary behaviour controlled by reinforcement or punishment. Neighbours: positive/negative reinforcement vs punishment, schedules (fixed/variable ratio and interval).

qs.stem: Fearing of authority and trying to avoid punishment comes under:
qs.sol: Avoiding punishment is the early, authority-oriented stage of moral development.
qs.rel: Avoiding punishment and obeying authority is Kohlberg's preconventional level, stage 1 (punishment-obedience orientation) of moral development. Neighbours: stage 2 instrumental exchange, conventional level, Piaget's heteronomous morality.

qs.stem:
Choose the best option from the following.
When a child applies the knowledge of addition learnt through beads on addition with sticks the learning transferred to as referred to as:
qs.sol: The child applies the same addition concept to a different material at a similar level of complexity. Transfer across parallel contexts is lateral transfer.
qs.rel: Lateral transfer: using learned knowledge in a similar situation at the same level (beads to sticks in addition). Neighbours: vertical transfer, positive/negative/zero transfer, Gagné's hierarchy.

qs.stem: “Repetitions in learning can strengthen the connections and disuse can weaken the connections” is a classroom implication of which of the following theories?
qs.sol: Thorndike’s law of exercise says use strengthens stimulus-response bonds and disuse weakens them; it belongs to trial-and-error learning.
qs.rel: Repetition strengthens and disuse weakens connections = Thorndike's Law of Exercise (use and disuse) in trial and error learning. Neighbours: law of readiness and effect; classroom use: drill and revision.

qs.stem: Methods and theories of learning are dealt with under which of the following disciplines?
qs.sol: Educational psychology studies how people learn and the theories and methods of learning.
qs.rel: Educational psychology deals with learning theories and methods in education (Skinner defined it as psychology applied to education). Neighbours: developmental psychology, pedagogy, philosophy of education, sociology of education.

topics.deep:
- **Learning** = relatively permanent change in behaviour (or behaviour potential) due to experience/practice, not maturation, fatigue or drugs. Characteristics: purposive/goal-directed, active, continuous, transferable, individual and social, based on experience.
- **Behaviourist theories:**

| Theorist | Theory | Key ideas |
|---|---|---|
| Pavlov | Classical conditioning | UCS, UCR, CS, CR; acquisition, extinction, spontaneous recovery, generalisation, discrimination |
| Watson | Behaviourism | emotional conditioning (Little Albert); psychology = study of behaviour |
| Thorndike | Connectionism / trial and error | puzzle box (cat); laws: **readiness, exercise (use/disuse), effect** |
| Skinner | Operant conditioning | reinforcement (positive/negative), punishment, shaping, schedules, Skinner box, programmed instruction |
| Hull | Drive reduction | need reduction reinforces |

- **Reinforcement schedules:** continuous, fixed ratio, variable ratio (highest, most extinction-resistant), fixed interval, variable interval. Negative reinforcement removes an aversive stimulus (not punishment). Thorndike's secondary laws: multiple response, set/attitude, prepotency, response by analogy, associative shifting.
- **Cognitive / insight theories:** **Gestalt** (Wertheimer, Koffka, Kohler): whole > sum of parts, insight learning (Sultan the chimp), laws of proximity, similarity, closure, continuity, figure-ground. **Tolman:** latent learning, cognitive maps, sign-gestalt. **Bruner:** discovery learning, spiral curriculum. **Ausubel:** meaningful reception learning, advance organisers. **Gagne:** 8 types of learning, 9 events of instruction.
- **Social learning (Bandura):** observational learning = attention, retention, reproduction, motivation; Bobo doll; vicarious reinforcement; self-efficacy; reciprocal determinism.
- **Constructivism:** learners build knowledge from experience and prior knowledge (Piaget cognitive constructivism, Vygotsky social constructivism); 5E model (engage, explore, explain, elaborate, evaluate); NCF 2005 encourages it; teacher is facilitator; knowledge is constructed not transmitted.
- **Humanistic:** Rogers (facilitation of significant learning, unconditional positive regard), Maslow.
- **Experiential learning (Kolb):** concrete experience -> reflective observation -> abstract conceptualisation -> active experimentation; learner types diverger, assimilator, converger, accommodator. Dewey: learning by doing; Dale's cone of experience (direct purposeful experiences at base).
- **Learning styles:** VARK (visual, auditory, read/write, kinaesthetic), Honey-Mumford; evidence for matching teaching to style is weak but varied modalities help.
- **Transfer of learning:** positive, negative, zero; lateral vs vertical; near vs far. Theories: **identical elements** (Thorndike), **generalisation** (Judd), transposition (Gestalt). Ebbinghaus: forgetting curve; spacing effect; primacy and recency effects.
- **Memory:** Atkinson-Shiffrin (sensory, short-term, long-term); working memory ~7 +/- 2 (Miller); proactive and retroactive interference; mnemonics.
- **Approaches:** teacher-centred (lecture, rote, extrinsic motivation) vs learner-centred (peer interaction, intrinsic motivation, inquiry).
- **Educational psychology** applies psychology to education (Skinner); learning theories belong there; methods: introspection, observation, experiment, case study, survey.

**Likely question angles:**
- Match theory with proponent (Pavlov, Thorndike, Skinner, Bandura, Kohler, Tolman, Kolb).
- Identify law (readiness, exercise, effect, primacy, recency) from a classroom example.
- Positive vs negative reinforcement vs punishment scenarios.
- Which schedule of reinforcement is most resistant to extinction.
- Steps of observational learning and Bandura's concept of self-efficacy.
- Gestalt principles from visual examples.
- Types of transfer from examples (lateral, vertical, negative).
- Stages of Kolb's cycle or the 5E model in order.
- Characteristics of learning (which is not a characteristic).
- Differences between classical and operant conditioning.

topics.title: 3. Motivation, Personality, Intelligence & Emotions
topics.theory:
- **Maslow's hierarchy:** physiological, safety, belonging, esteem, **self-actualisation**; D-needs vs B-needs. **Intrinsic** vs **extrinsic** motivation; self-determination (Deci-Ryan): autonomy, competence, relatedness; Weiner's attribution; Dweck's growth mindset.
- **Intelligence:** Binet-Simon (1905); **IQ = MA/CA x 100** (Stern); Wechsler scales; Raven's non-verbal test. Spearman g and s; Thurstone 7 PMA; Guilford SI (120 factors); Cattell fluid/crystallised; Sternberg triarchic.
- **Gardner's 8 MI:** linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, bodily-kinaesthetic, musical, interpersonal, intrapersonal, naturalist. **Emotional intelligence** is Goleman/Salovey-Mayer - not one of Gardner's eight.
- **Personality** (Allport): dynamic organisation of psychophysical systems. Type (Sheldon, Jung, Kretschmer); **trait** (Allport, Cattell 16PF, Eysenck PEN); **Big Five = OCEAN**; Freud: id-ego-superego.
- **Projective techniques:** Rorschach, TAT, sentence completion, word association, draw-a-person; aptitude test is not projective.
- **Emotions:** Goleman's EI components; catharsis = release of pent-up emotion; defence mechanisms (repression, projection, rationalisation, regression, sublimation).
- **Creativity:** fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration (Guilford, Torrance); divergent thinking; Wallas's four stages.
- **Attitude** = predisposition (cognitive, affective, behavioural); measured by Likert scale.
- Mindfulness (MBSR, Jon Kabat-Zinn) improves emotional regulation and reduces stress; counselling can be directive/non-directive.
- Wisdom = knowledge + experience (judgement).

qs.stem:
______ is the type of assessment.

I. Formative assessment 

II. Summative assessment
qs.sol: Both I. Formative assessment and II. Summative assessment are major types of assessment. Therefore, the correct option is "Both I and II"
qs.rel: Personality is the total pattern of characteristic ways of thinking, feeling and acting (Allport: dynamic organisation of psychophysical systems). Neighbours: trait, type, psychoanalytic and humanistic approaches; the Big Five.

qs.stem:
Which of the following are the strategies to enhance the motivation level of the learners?
I. Build on strengths first
II. Offer choices
III. Facilitate creativity
IV. Provide a secure environment
qs.sol: Motivation grows when teachers begin with learners' strengths, allow meaningful choices, support creative work and provide a secure classroom. Strength based success builds confidence; choice gives ownership; creativity encourages expression; safety makes participation less threatening. None of the four strategies in the question undermines motivation, so the inclusive combination is justified. All four supports, including strength building and creativity, can increase motivation. Excluding statements I and III ignores the motivating effect of early success and creative work. Leaving out strengths ignores the confidence gained from early success. …
qs.rel: Motivation strategies: build on strengths, offer choice, set achievable goals, give feedback and recognition, relevance to life. Neighbours: intrinsic vs extrinsic motivation, Maslow, Bandura's self-efficacy, Weiner's attribution.

qs.stem:
Children’s _____ towards learning language play an important role in language acquisition.
 I. Motivation
 II. Self confidence
 III. Curiosity
qs.sol: Motivation, self-confidence and curiosity all influence children's language acquisition.
qs.rel: Self-observation develops self-awareness: knowing strengths and weaknesses, which supports reflection and regulation. Neighbours: metacognition, reflective journals, Johari window, self-concept and self-esteem.

qs.stem: Deductive reasoning is essentially a
qs.sol:
No official answer key was published for this paper; the answer is worked out from the question.

Deduction starts from general premises or a rule and applies them to a particular case.

The standard name for that general-to-specific direction is top-down reasoning.
qs.rel: Maslow's hierarchy (1943): physiological, safety, love/belonging, esteem, self-actualisation; later cognitive, aesthetic and transcendence. Neighbours: deficiency vs growth needs, humanistic psychology, Rogers.

qs.stem: Which of the following combination is correct? I. Intrinsic Motivation – Preparing any project in science/mathematics may give pleasure to the pupil as a result of which he/she is motivated to undertake similar activities on his/her own. II. Extrinsic Motivation – Rewards like money and grades.
qs.sol: Intrinsic motivation comes from within the learner: the activity is rewarding in itself. A pupil who enjoys preparing a science or mathematics project and therefore takes up similar activities on her own is intrinsically motivated, so pair I is correct. Extrinsic motivation comes from outside the activity, in the form of rewards or to avoid punishment, such as money, grades, prizes or praise, so pair II is correct. Both combinations are correct.
qs.rel: Intrinsic motivation comes from internal satisfaction (interest, project enjoyment); extrinsic from rewards, grades, praise. Neighbours: self-determination theory (Deci and Ryan), Hull's drive reduction, Maslow, overjustification effect.

qs.stem: नए (beginner) शिक्षकों के लिए पाठ योजना (lesson plan) का मुख्य कार्य क्या है?

opts.A: यह सैद्धांतिक ज्ञान की आवश्यकता को समाप्त करती है।
opts.B: यह दैनिक कार्ययोजना प्रदान करती है।
opts.C: यह विद्यार्थियों की ग्रेडिंग करने में सहायता करती है।
opts.D: यह प्रशासनिक निर्देश प्रदान करती है।

qs.sol:
पाठ योजना शिक्षण-अधिगम प्रक्रिया के लिए शिक्षक द्वारा पहले से तैयार की गई एक संरचित रूपरेखा होती है, जिसमें शिक्षण उद्देश्यों, विषय-वस्तु के प्रस्तुतीकरण के चरणों, शिक्षण विधियों-गतिविधियों और मूल्यांकन बिंदुओं को क्रमबद्ध ढंग से लिखा जाता है। यह विशेष रूप से अनुभवहीन (beginner) शिक्षकों के लिए एक व्यावहारिक कार्य-मार्गदर्शिका का काम करती है, क्योंकि उनके पास कक्षा-प्रबंधन का पूर्व अनुभव नहीं होता।

चूँकि नए शिक्षकों के पास तात्कालिक निर्णय लेने का अनुभव नहीं होता, इसलिए पाठ योजना उन्हें बताती है कि कक्षा में किस क्रम में क्या पढ़ाना है, किन गतिविधियों-साधनों का प्रयोग करना है, और समय का बँटवारा कैसे करना है — अर्थात् यह एक ठोस दैनिक कार्ययोजना प्रदान करती है, जिसे शिक्षक कक्षा में चरण-दर-चर …
qs.rel: Observing oneself reveals patterns in behaviour and reactions, supporting self-awareness and self-regulation. Neighbours: self-reflection, reflective practice, emotional intelligence (Goleman).

qs.stem: Rohan, a 5-year-old boy, is playing with a football. Which motor skill is being displayed in this context?
qs.sol: Playing football mainly uses large body muscles and whole-body movement. This is a gross motor skill.
qs.rel: Emotions influence adjustment, attitudes, learning and health of children; positive emotions help and prolonged negative ones harm. Neighbours: Goleman's emotional intelligence, catharsis, Bridges' emotional development.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are those medium(s) by which value education can be provided to the students?
 Statements:
 I. Skits and Dramas
 II. Morning Assembly
 III. Compulsory Subject
qs.sol: Value education can be provided through skits/dramas, morning assembly and compulsory subjects. All three are possible media.
qs.rel: Attitude (मनोवृत्ति) is a mental state of predisposition showing likes and dislikes. Neighbours: components: cognitive, affective, behavioural; Likert scale measures it; interest and aptitude differ.

qs.stem: The _______ technique takes the form of tears, also may include expressions of anger and rage.
qs.sol: “catharsis” is correct: Catharsis refers to the expression or release of strong emotion, which may include crying or anger. “clarification” fails: Clarification seeks to make thoughts or meanings clearer rather than describing emotional release.
qs.rel: Catharsis: release of pent-up emotions (tears, anger) to relieve tension (Freud, Aristotle in drama). Neighbours: defence mechanisms (sublimation, repression), play therapy, role play for emotional release.

qs.stem: After observing recurring incidents of bullying, a school counselor introduces activities rooted in empathy-building and self-control, drawing on Buddhist and Islamic traditions. Which dimension of peace education is being emphasized?

opts.A: Moral and spiritual development for inner harmony

qs.sol: Empathy-building and self-control for inner harmony emphasize the moral and spiritual dimension of peace education.
qs.rel: Empathy-building and self-control activities support moral and social-emotional development, an approach to bullying. Neighbours: Kohlberg's moral stages, SEL, peer mediation, anti-bullying policy.

qs.stem: In a classroom, Rehan consistently completes assignments on time and organizes his work meticulously. Applying the Big Five model, which personality dimension best explains Rehan's behavior?
qs.sol: In the Big Five model, being organized, careful, punctual and responsible reflects high conscientiousness.
qs.rel: Big Five (OCEAN): openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, neuroticism. Meticulous, on-time work shows high conscientiousness. Neighbours: Costa and McCrae, trait theories (Allport, Cattell, Eysenck).

qs.stem: Who out of the following is not one of the chief exponents of the trait theory of personality?
qs.sol: “Pritchett” is supported because allport, Cattell and Eysenck are trait theorists; Pritchett is not counted among the chief exponents. “G.W. Allport” is a principal trait theorist, so he does not meet the question's exclusion.
qs.rel: Trait theorists: Allport, Cattell (16PF), Eysenck (extraversion, neuroticism, psychoticism). Type theorists: Sheldon, Kretschmer, Jung. Neighbours: Freud is psychoanalytic, Rogers humanistic.

qs.stem: इनमें से कौन मास्लो का आवश्यकता पदानुक्रम नहीं है?
qs.sol: मास्लो के आवश्यकता पदानुक्रम के स्तर हैं: शारीरिक (फ़िज़ियोलॉजिकल) आवश्यकताएँ, सुरक्षा आवश्यकताएँ, प्रेम/अपनापन की आवश्यकताएँ, सम्मान आवश्यकताएँ (जिन्हें अनेक पाठ्यपुस्तकें प्रतिष्ठा या अहं आवश्यकताएँ भी कहती हैं) और आत्मसाक्षात्कार। सुरक्षा स्वयं एक स्तर है और प्रतिष्ठा आवश्यकताएँ सम्मान स्तर का ही दूसरा नाम हैं। ‘‘Phycological needs’’ वाला विकल्प अंग्रेज़ी में ‘‘Phycological’’ (physiological की वर्तनी-त्रुटि) और हिन्दी में ‘‘मनोवैज्ञानिक’’ छपा है; दोनों पढ़तों में यह पदानुक्रम का हिस्सा है, क्योंकि शारीरिक आवश्यकताएँ आधार स्तर हैं और मनोवैज्ञानिक आवश्यकताएँ (अपनापन और सम्मान) मास्लो के समूहन में आती हैं। आश्रय केवल शारीरिक आवश्यकताओं का एक उदाहरण है, किसी स्तर का नाम नहीं; अतः यही पदानुक्र …
qs.rel: Maslow's needs: physiological (food, shelter, clothing), safety, belongingness, esteem, self-actualisation. Neighbours: D-needs vs B-needs; hierarchy ordered prepotent; criticisms of cultural rigidity.

qs.stem: What distinguishes personality from other characteristics in psychological studies?

opts.A: The interplay between organic and psychological events

qs.sol: Personality is distinguished by the organized interplay between organic and psychological events, not merely appearance or group dynamics.
qs.rel: Personality is distinct: it integrates organic (physical) and psychological systems into a unique whole (Allport). Neighbours: temperament vs character, heredity and environment shaping personality.

qs.stem: A teacher notices that a student who was previously confident in group work has recently become withdrawn after repeated negative interactions with classmates. Based on the scenario, which social factor is most likely influencing the student's personality development?
qs.sol: Concept: Personality development is shaped by several categories of factors: biological or hereditary factors present from birth (such as inborn temperament), family-based factors (such as parenting style or relationships with siblings), and social factors arising from a person's ongoing interactions with others outside the immediate family, such as peers, teachers, and the wider community. Repeated peer interactions, whether supportive or negative, are a well-documented social influence on a student's self-concept, confidence, and social behaviour during the school years. …
qs.rel: Peer rejection can lead to withdrawal and lower self-esteem; teacher support and cooperative tasks help. Neighbours: socio-metric techniques (Moreno), bullying, social-emotional learning.

qs.stem: According to Howard Gardner’s theory, which of the following intelligences is NOT a component of multiple intelligences?
qs.sol: Gardner’s multiple intelligences include bodily-kinesthetic, logical-mathematical, and musical abilities. Emotional intelligence is a distinct framework and not one of the standard Gardner categories.
qs.rel: Gardner's multiple intelligences: linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, bodily-kinaesthetic, musical, interpersonal, intrapersonal, naturalist (existential proposed). Emotional intelligence is Goleman/Salovey-Mayer, not Gardner's.

qs.stem: व्यक्ति त्व के लक्षण (ट्रेट) सिद्धांत के प्रमुख प्रतिपादक कौन हैं? I. आर.बी. कैटेल II. एच.जे. ईसनक III. सिगमंड फ्रॉयड
qs.sol: आर. बी. कैटेल और एच. जे. आइजेंक व्यक्तित्व के गुण सिद्धांत के प्रमुख व्याख्याता हैं। कैटेल ने कारक विश्लेषण से मूल गुण खोजे और आइजेंक ने व्यापक व्यक्तित्व आयाम दिए। सिगमंड फ्रायड मुख्यतः मनोविश्लेषण से जुड़े हैं, गुण सिद्धांत से नहीं। इसलिए पहले दो नाम सही हैं। फ्रायड मनोविश्लेषण से हैं, इसलिए यह समूह अधिक शामिल करता है। फ्रायड जुड़ते और आइजेंक गलत ढंग से छूटते हैं। कैटेल भी प्रमुख गुण सिद्धांतकार हैं। कैटेल और आइजेंक दोनों ने गुण आधारित विचार दिए।
qs.rel: Trait theory exponents: R. B. Cattell, H. J. Eysenck, G. W. Allport; Freud is psychoanalytic. Neighbours: Cattell's 16 source traits, Eysenck's PEN, Allport's cardinal, central, secondary traits.

qs.stem:
“Preparing any project in science/mathematics may give pleasure to the pupil as result of which he/she is motivated to undertake similar activities on his/her own.”
 This given statement describes which of the following type(s) of motivation?
 Statements:
 I. Intrinsic Motivation
 II. Extrinsic Motivation
qs.sol: When a project gives pleasure and motivates the pupil to do similar activities independently, the motivation comes from interest and satisfaction in the activity itself. This is intrinsic motivation.
qs.rel: Pleasure in doing a project motivates further work: intrinsic motivation. Neighbours: extrinsic motivation, Hull's drive, Murray's need for achievement, McClelland's n-Ach.

qs.sol: “अंतर्भूत अभिप्रेरण का समर्थन करना” विद्यार्थी को अपनी रुचि, प्रयास और प्रगति से उपलब्धि का अनुभव दिलाता है, जिससे आत्म-सम्मान मजबूत हो सकता है। “विद्यार्थियों की अविशिष्ट सराहना करना” उपयोगी प्रतिपुष्टि के बिना सामान्य प्रशंसा है, इसलिए वह वास्तविक प्रगति का बोध कम कराती है।
qs.rel: Supporting intrinsic motivation through interest, effort and progress strengthens self-esteem. Neighbours: autonomy, competence, relatedness (Deci and Ryan), mastery goals, praise for effort (Dweck's growth mindset).

qs.stem: Which of the following doesn't belong to the Projective Techniques of methods of assessing personality?
qs.sol: “Aptitude Test” is supported because an aptitude test measures capacity or potential and is not a projective personality technique. “Children Apperception Test” uses story interpretation to reveal personality indirectly, so it is a projective assessment rather than a capacity test.
qs.rel: Projective techniques: Rorschach inkblot, TAT, sentence completion, word association, draw-a-person. An aptitude test is not projective; it is a psychometric test. Neighbours: inventories (MMPI), rating scales, interview.

qs.stem: Which foundational mindfulness program was developed to help people take responsibility for their well-being through paying attention and understanding their experiences?
qs.sol: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction is the foundational programme developed to help people take responsibility for well-being through mindful attention and awareness.
qs.rel: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) was developed by Jon Kabat-Zinn (1979). Neighbours: mindfulness-based cognitive therapy, emotion regulation, teacher well-being, yoga and meditation in NEP 2020.

qs.stem: A study on Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) among secondary teachers showed a significant reduction in stress. To transform emotional responses, which component of MBSR is most important?
qs.sol:
Contemporary process-based models of mindfulness training (for example, Holzel et al.'s neurocognitive framework) describe MBSR's effects through several distinguishable component mechanisms: attention regulation, body awareness, emotion regulation, and a change in perspective on the self. Each mechanism is cultivated by a different practice and produces a different kind of outcome.

In this framework, emotion regulation is the mechanism that directly governs how an emotional reaction to a stressor is generated, modulated, or changed, through processes such as reappraisal and the extinction of a learned reaction. …
qs.rel: Mindfulness training (MBSR) reduces stress by improving emotional regulation and attention. Neighbours: teacher burnout, SEL, breathing practices, resilience.

qs.stem: The individual who has unique traits and characteristics is called ________________.
qs.sol: An exceptional individual has distinctive traits or characteristics relative to typical development.
qs.rel: Exceptional individuals deviate from the average in traits (gifted or disabled); every individual is unique. Neighbours: individual differences, gifted/talented, differently-abled, Terman's gifted study (IQ 130+).

qs.stem: Motivational levels and abilities can be identified by awareness of which of the following?
qs.sol: Educational psychology studies learning, motivation and learner differences, so it helps identify these levels and abilities.
qs.rel: Educational psychology helps identify learners' motivation, abilities and needs. Neighbours: aptitude vs achievement tests, individual differences, guidance and counselling.

qs.sol: “परामर्शदाता” को अपनी प्रतिक्रियाओं और सेवार्थी की जरूरतों को समझकर निष्पक्ष मूल्यांकन तथा ईमानदार संबंध बनाए रखने का प्रशिक्षण दिया जाता है। “विद्यार्थी” सेवा पाने की भूमिका बताता है, पेशेवर परामर्श और मूल्यांकन की जिम्मेदारी नहीं।
qs.rel: A counsellor is trained to be objective and genuine, understanding client needs (Rogers' unconditional positive regard, empathy, congruence). Neighbours: directive vs non-directive counselling, guidance vs counselling, confidentiality.

qs.sol: “अभिप्रेरण की कमी” सीखने में भागीदारी को प्रभावित कर सकती है, पर विशिष्ट अधिगम अक्षमता का प्राथमिक न्यूरोविकासात्मक कारण नहीं मानी जाती। “संवेदी क्षीणता” भी अधिगम में कठिनाई ला सकती है, पर संवेदनात्मक हानि से उत्पन्न कठिनाई को विशिष्ट अधिगम अक्षमता से अलग पहचानना चाहिए।
qs.rel: Lack of motivation affects participation but is not the neurodevelopmental cause of specific learning disability (SLD). Neighbours: dyslexia, dysgraphia, dyscalculia; SLD causes are neurological.

qs.stem: Wisdom can be defined as a combination of:
qs.sol:
Knowledge supplies information, while experience develops judgment about its use.

Combining knowledge with experience yields wisdom in the stated definition.
qs.rel: Wisdom combines knowledge and experience (sound judgement). Neighbours: data, information, knowledge, wisdom hierarchy (DIKW); tacit vs explicit knowledge; Sternberg's wisdom-intelligence-creativity synthesis.

topics.deep:
- **Motivation** = internal state energising and directing behaviour. Intrinsic (interest, enjoyment) vs extrinsic (grades, praise, rewards); overjustification effect can reduce intrinsic motivation. Classroom strategies: build on strengths, choice, relevant tasks, achievable goals, feedback, recognition, curiosity, cooperative work.
- **Maslow's hierarchy (1943):** physiological -> safety -> love/belonging -> esteem -> self-actualisation (later cognitive, aesthetic, transcendence). Deficiency (D) needs vs growth (B) needs. Humanistic psychology: Rogers (self, unconditional positive regard).
- **Other motivation theories:**

| Theory | Proponent | Core idea |
|---|---|---|
| Drive reduction | Hull | biological need reduction |
| Need for achievement | McClelland / Atkinson | n-Ach, n-Aff, n-Power |
| Attribution | Weiner | ability, effort, task difficulty, luck; stable/unstable, internal/external |
| Self-determination | Deci and Ryan | autonomy, competence, relatedness |
| Two-factor | Herzberg | hygiene vs motivators |
| Self-efficacy | Bandura | belief in own capability |
| Growth mindset | Dweck | intelligence malleable |
| Locus of control | Rotter | internal vs external |

- **Intelligence:** Binet-Simon (1905) first test; Stern coined IQ = (MA/CA) x 100; Terman's Stanford-Binet; Wechsler (WISC, WAIS, verbal and performance); Raven's progressive matrices (non-verbal); Alpha and Beta (army tests). Classification: genius 140+, gifted 130+, average 90-110, borderline 70-85, intellectual disability below 70.
- **Theories of intelligence:**

| Theorist | Theory |
|---|---|
| Spearman | two-factor: g and s |
| Thurstone | seven primary mental abilities |
| Guilford | Structure of Intellect (operations, content, products; 120 factors) |
| Cattell | fluid vs crystallised |
| Gardner | 8 multiple intelligences: linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, bodily-kinaesthetic, musical, interpersonal, intrapersonal, naturalist |
| Sternberg | triarchic: analytical, creative, practical |
| Goleman / Salovey-Mayer | emotional intelligence (not part of Gardner's eight) |

- **Personality** (Allport: dynamic organisation of psychophysical systems that determine unique adjustment). Approaches: **type** (Sheldon: endomorph, mesomorph, ectomorph; Jung: introvert/extrovert; Kretschmer), **trait** (Allport cardinal/central/secondary; Cattell 16PF; Eysenck PEN; **Big Five/OCEAN** - Costa and McCrae), psychoanalytic (Freud: id, ego, superego), humanistic (Rogers, Maslow), social learning (Bandura).
- **Assessment of personality:** inventories (MMPI, 16PF), rating scales, interviews, **projective techniques** - Rorschach inkblot (10 cards), TAT (Murray and Morgan), sentence completion, word association (Jung), draw-a-person. Aptitude tests are not projective.
- **Emotions:** Goleman's five components (self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, social skills); catharsis; Bridges' emotional differentiation; emotions affect adjustment and learning. **Defence mechanisms:** repression, denial, projection, rationalisation, regression, sublimation, reaction formation, displacement.
- **Creativity (Guilford, Torrance):** fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration; divergent thinking; stages preparation, incubation, illumination, verification (Wallas). Attitude = predisposition with cognitive, affective, behavioural components (Likert scale); interest and aptitude differ.
- **Mental health and guidance:** counselling (directive, non-directive, eclectic), mindfulness (Jon Kabat-Zinn's MBSR), stress management, anti-bullying through empathy and SEL. Exceptional individuals include gifted and disabled.

**Likely question angles:**
- Level of Maslow's hierarchy for a described need; which is not part of it.
- Name the eight intelligences and identify the example (musician = musical).
- Match psychologist with intelligence theory (Spearman g, Thurstone, Guilford).
- Formula and computation of IQ; classification bands.
- Trait vs type exponents; Big Five letters.
- Which technique is projective vs non-projective.
- Intrinsic vs extrinsic motivation from classroom examples.
- Attribution style (effort vs ability) and Dweck's mindsets.
- Defence mechanism identification from a scenario.
- Dimensions of creativity (fluency, flexibility, originality).

topics.title: 4. Inclusive Education: Concepts, Policies & Practice
topics.theory:
- **Integration** (child adapts to school; medical model; IEDC 1974) vs **inclusion** (system adapts; social/rights model). Inclusive class = disabled and non-disabled learn together with support; essence = embracing diversity.
- **Salamanca Statement 1994** (UNESCO): inclusive schools, enrol children in neighbourhood regular schools. **UNCRPD 2006** (Art. 24; India ratified 2007). Warnock Report 1978 coined "special educational needs".
- **RPwD Act 2016:** **21 disabilities**, 4% job reservation, 5% in higher education, free education 6-18 yrs for benchmark disability (40%+); replaced PWD Act 1995 (7 disabilities).
- **RTE 2009:** ages 6-14, Article 21A; 25% reservation (Sec 12); children with disabilities counted as disadvantaged group (2012 amendment). National Trust Act 1999; RCI Act 1992.
- **Schemes:** IEDC (1974, revised 1992), IEDSS (2009, secondary), DPEP, SSA, **Samagra Shiksha 2018**; NEP 2020 stresses barrier-free access and special educators.
- **Barriers:** attitudinal, physical (ramps/elevators = accessibility), curricular, institutional. **UDL:** multiple means of engagement, representation, expression. Differentiated instruction: content, process, product.
- **Models:** medical, social, charity, rights-based; impairment vs disability vs handicap (WHO). CBR (WHO 1978) empowers persons with disabilities in community; CBVT = vocational training.
- **IEP** team: parents, teachers, therapists; accommodations vs modifications; remedial vs enrichment education.
- Learners with impairments are heterogeneous; family involvement and peer sensitisation raise success.
- Types of exclusion: economic, social, political, cultural; intersectionality (Crenshaw).

qs.stem: जिस विद्यालय में सभी छात्र एक छत के नीचे पढ़ सकते हैं उसे ___________ कहा जाता है।
qs.sol: समावेशी विद्यालय वह है जहाँ अलग-अलग क्षमताओं, आवश्यकताओं और पृष्ठभूमि वाले विद्यार्थी एक साथ सीख सकें। आवश्यक सहयोग और अनुकूलन देकर सभी के लिए एक ही शैक्षिक समुदाय बनाना इसका लक्ष्य है। प्रश्न का 'एक छत के नीचे' संकेत इसी साथ पढ़ने की व्यवस्था की ओर है। 'विशेष' (Exclusive) विद्यालय विद्यार्थियों को अलग रखने वाली व्यवस्था है, और 'विशेषज्ञता' विद्यालय किसी खास क्षेत्र या समूह पर केंद्रित होता है। 'सामान्य' शब्द सभी विद्यार्थियों की भागीदारी सुनिश्चित करने वाले सिद्धांत को स्पष्ट नहीं करता। इसलिए समावेशी विद्यालय का नाम उपयुक्त है।
qs.rel: A school where all learners study together, with appropriate support, is an inclusive school. Neighbours: special school (segregated), integrated school, mainstream; Salamanca Statement 1994.

qs.stem: Which of the following methods is best suited for teaching science?
qs.sol:
DSSSB's official key marks "Deduction" (the Hindi print reads "अनुमान", which means inference) and the board credits it. The answer shown is "Activities", because activity-based learning is the standard recommendation for teaching science.

Science is fundamentally an empirical, hands-on discipline: concepts such as chemical reactions, forces, and biological processes are grasped most durably when learners directly manipulate materials, observe outcomes, and construct understanding through first-hand experience, rather than through verbal exchange or abstract logical reasoning alone. …
qs.rel: Inclusive class = general education class where disabled and non-disabled students learn together with supports. Neighbours: integration (child adapts) vs inclusion (system adapts); RPwD Act 2016; NEP 2020.

qs.stem: A standard language becomes the language of ______. I. media II. administration III. judiciary
qs.sol: A standard language is the codified variety widely used for public communication. It commonly appears in mass media, government administration, and judicial proceedings, where shared conventions and intelligibility matter. Other varieties continue in everyday life, but the question asks about institutional domains of the standard variety. Each of the three listed domains is included.
qs.rel: Universal Design for Learning (CAST): multiple means of engagement, representation, and action/expression to make learning accessible to all. Neighbours: differentiated instruction, barrier-free access, early childhood UDL.

qs.stem: What is the one important role of a family in supporting adults with special needs?

opts.B: Making all decisions without involving the individual
opts.C: Providing emotional support and advocating for their needs

qs.sol: “Providing emotional support and advocating for their needs” helps adults with special needs participate and access appropriate services while respecting their choices. “Making all decisions without involving the individual” undermines the adult’s autonomy even if family members intend to help.
qs.rel: Inclusive classroom: heterogeneous class with disabled and non-disabled students learning together. Neighbours: principles - diversity valued, participation, accessibility; Index for Inclusion; peer support.

qs.stem: What are the benefits of drama and art in education ?
qs.sol: Drama and art give students active ways to represent ideas, communicate, observe, and reflect. In an educational setting these activities can deepen understanding and participation across subjects, so becoming a better learner is the direct curricular benefit. Acting or artistic technique may improve for some students, but training performers is not the central aim of using arts in general education. Becoming a better person is a broad possible aspiration; it is less specific to the learning outcome asked for in this question.
qs.rel: Family provides emotional support and advocacy for persons with special needs. Neighbours: family-centred intervention, parent counselling, self-help groups, community-based rehabilitation.

qs.stem: What should be the first guide in the selection of learning resources?
qs.sol:
Concept:

A learning resource is a means to learning, not an end in itself. In learner-centred pedagogy — the position taken by the National Curriculum Framework (NCF) and reaffirmed by NEP 2020 — the educational worth of any resource is decided by how well it connects with the learner: what the learner already knows, what engages the learner, and what the learner meets in everyday life. The first criterion applied while selecting a learning resource is therefore the learner profile; practical constraints such as budget, infrastructure and teacher familiarity are filters applied afterwards, to settle the final choice among resources that already meet that criterion. …
qs.rel: Factors affecting inclusive education: assessment system, teacher preparation, attitudes, diversity, resources. Neighbours: attitudinal barrier, infrastructural barrier, support services, curricular flexibility.

qs.stem: पाठ्यचर्या में, भाषा के संबंध में शिक्षक की क्या भूमिका है?

opts.A: प्रत्येक विषय में सभी व्याकरणिक त्रुटियों को ठीक करना
opts.B: प्रत्येक कक्षा के बाद एक पृथक भाषा के पीरियड में पढ़ाना
opts.C: विषय-विशिष्ट भाषा और संप्रेषण कौशल विकसित करने में सहायता करना
opts.D: भाषा की चिंता किए बिना अपने विषय पर फोकस करना

qs.sol:
संकल्पना

पाठ्यचर्या में भाषा केवल भाषा-विषय की सामग्री नहीं, बल्कि ज्ञान सीखने और व्यक्त करने का माध्यम भी है। प्रत्येक विषय अपनी शब्दावली, वाक्य-विन्यास, व्याख्या और तर्क-पद्धति का उपयोग करता है; इसलिए भाषा-विकास विषय-अध्यापन के भीतर भी होता है।

अनुप्रयोग

यहाँ शिक्षक की भूमिका विद्यार्थियों को विषय की अवधारणाएँ समझने के साथ उस विषय की शब्दावली, व्याख्या, चर्चा और अभिव्यक्ति का उपयोग करना सिखाना है। इस कारण “विषय-विशिष्ट भाषा और संप्रेषण कौशल विकसित करने में सहायता करना” पाठ्यचर्या में भाषा की समेकित भूमिका को व्यक्त करता है।

विकल्पों का अंतर

“प्रत्येक विषय में सभी व्याकरणिक त्रुटियों को ठीक करना” भाषा को मुख्यतः शुद्धता-सुधार तक सीमित करता है; विषय-बोध के लिए शब्दावली और संप्रेषण का वि …
qs.rel: RTE Act 2009 gives free and compulsory education to all children 6-14 years including children with special needs (amended 2012 to include disabled in disadvantaged group). Neighbours: Article 21A (86th Amendment 2002), 25% reservation (Section 12).

qs.stem: The period from birth to ______ of age (early childhood) is critical for development of language and speech.
qs.sol: Early childhood is commonly taken here as the period from birth through six years, when speech and language develop rapidly. “Five years” stops short of that stated span, although substantial language development occurs before age five.
qs.rel: Developmental approach to inclusion considers each child's cognitive, emotional, physical and social developmental level. Neighbours: individualised education, differentiated instruction, Vygotsky ZPD.

qs.stem: What does the scope of Social Studies primarily include?

opts.A: Studying history, geography, civics, economics, culture.
opts.C: Learning concepts from maths and science subjects.
opts.D: Focusing mainly on memorising dates and names.

qs.sol: Social Studies covers society through history, geography, civics, economics and culture, rather than only political events or memorized dates.
qs.rel: CBR (WHO 1978) aims to empower persons with disabilities within their communities; five components: health, education, livelihood, social, empowerment. Neighbours: DPEP-IED, RCI, CBRDTC.

qs.stem: Symbols used in alternative and augmentative communication can represent:
qs.sol: AAC symbols can stand for objects, actions, abstract concepts and emotions, enabling a broad range of messages. “only objects and actions” does not fit: objects and actions omit abstract ideas and feelings.
qs.rel: Inclusive education rejects segregated special schools and classes that separate disabled children. Neighbours: integrated education, mainstreaming, resource room, itinerant teacher.

qs.stem: Which evaluation method is considered most comprehensive for assessing both the social communication skills and repetitive behaviours characteristic of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)?

opts.C: Direct observation combined with structured diagnostic tools like ADOS and ADI-R

qs.sol: “Direct observation combined with structured diagnostic tools like ADOS and ADI-R” draws on observed behaviour and structured information about social communication and repetitive behaviour. “Parent questionnaires without classroom observation” can add useful history but alone miss direct evidence across settings.
qs.rel: Ramps, elevators and infrastructure changes are accessibility (physical access) factors. Neighbours: barrier-free environment, Accessible India Campaign 2015, RPwD Act 2016, Universal design.

qs.stem:
Choose from the options given below.

Performing arts helps in:
qs.sol: Performing arts connect expression and experience with ideas, supporting meaningful learning.
qs.rel: Disability-inclusive electoral reforms (polling stations, information, participation) are examples of inclusion in civic life. Neighbours: accessibility, RPwD Act 2016, Election Commission accessible features.

qs.stem: शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009 की निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी धारा पाठ्यक्रम और मूल्यांकन प्रक्रिया का प्रावधान करती है?
qs.sol: निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 29 पाठ्यक्रम और मूल्यांकन प्रक्रिया से संबंधित है: सरकार द्वारा अधिसूचित शैक्षिक प्राधिकरण प्रारंभिक शिक्षा का पाठ्यक्रम और मूल्यांकन प्रक्रिया निर्धारित करता है, जो संवैधानिक मूल्यों, सर्वांगीण विकास, गतिविधि व खोज द्वारा अधिगम और सतत एवं व्यापक मूल्यांकन के अनुरूप हो। धारा 31 बाल अधिकारों की निगरानी, धारा 33 राष्ट्रीय सलाहकार परिषद, और धारा 35 निर्देश जारी करने की शक्ति से संबंधित है।
qs.rel: Disability policy goals: raise public awareness, inclusion, equal opportunities, rights and participation. Neighbours: PWD Act 1995, RPwD Act 2016 (21 disabilities), UNCRPD 2006.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a primary goal of development policies related to disability?

opts.A: To promote public awareness and inclusion
opts.B: To restrict access to public transportation
opts.C: To increase taxation on assistive devices
opts.D: To limit educational opportunities for persons with disabilities

qs.sol: “To promote public awareness and inclusion” supports equal participation by addressing barriers and attitudes toward disability. “To restrict access to public transportation” would create another barrier to participation, contrary to that goal.
qs.rel: Inclusive school principle: all students learn together, valued and supported. Neighbours: UNESCO's Salamanca Statement, Index for Inclusion, whole-school approach, collaboration.

qs.stem:
While giving written feedback in Assessment for Learning, which of the following point(s) need to be taken care of?
 I. Don’t jump straight to errors. Praise first.
 II. Encourage the student to make corrections. Don’t simply write the correct answers, spellings and so on.
qs.sol: Assessment for Learning (AfL) treats feedback as a tool to improve future performance, not just to judge past performance. Two research-based guidelines govern effective written AfL feedback: open with what the student did well before addressing errors, so the student stays receptive rather than defensive; and prompt the student to locate and fix their own mistakes (spelling, computation, expression) rather than the teacher simply supplying the correct version, so the student practises self-correction. …
qs.rel: A system lacking flexibility for diverse learners cannot be inclusive; flexible curriculum and pedagogy are needed. Neighbours: curricular adaptation, differentiated instruction, UDL.

qs.stem: Essence of Inclusion lies in _____.
qs.sol:
Inclusion recognises and values differences among learners.

Resources, admission and infrastructure support it but do not exhaust its meaning.

Its essence is embracing diversity.
qs.rel: Essence of inclusion: embracing diversity and valuing every learner. Neighbours: accessibility, participation, achievement; difference between integration and inclusion.

qs.stem: Why is literature considered an essential source of learning for children in the early years?

opts.A: It replaces all other classroom activities
opts.B: Elicits spontaneity and integrated language learning
opts.C: It focuses solely on memorization of stories
opts.D: It teaches only vocabulary and grammar

qs.sol: Literature supports early learning because it naturally encourages spontaneity, imagination and integrated language development.
qs.rel: 'Special needs' emphasises modifications in the education system to meet individual needs, not defects in the child. Neighbours: CWSN, IEP, adaptations, social model of disability.

qs.stem: What is a key activity recommended for developing middle-order expressive skills in the Indian Sign Language (ISL)?

opts.A: Using repetitive single signs in isolation
opts.C: Limiting communication to finger spelling only
opts.D: Expressing feelings and narratives through natural signing in conversation

qs.sol: Natural signed conversation that expresses feelings and narratives builds connected, expressive use of Indian Sign Language. “Memorising the ISL dictionary” does not fit: memorising a dictionary does not practise expression in interaction.
qs.rel: Youth with disabilities face extra barriers in developing self-determination (choice-making, goal setting, self-advocacy). Neighbours: transition planning, vocational training, self-advocacy.

qs.stem: What is the main objective of educational leadership in schools?

opts.A: Supervising administrative staff without involvement in classroom teaching
opts.B: Managing school finances and maintaining physical infrastructure only
opts.C: Improving teaching methods and effectively enhancing students' learning outcomes
opts.D: Organizing school programs and extra-curricular activities specifically

qs.sol:
Instructional leadership theory frames a school leader's core mandate as strengthening the teaching-learning process itself: setting clear instructional goals, supporting teachers' pedagogical growth, and improving students' learning outcomes, rather than any single administrative, financial, or event-management task.

Applying this principle to the given options, the objective centred on refining teaching methods and enhancing students' learning outcomes is the one that instructional-leadership theory identifies as the school leader's core objective. …
qs.rel: IEDC (1974, revised 1992) promoted education of disabled children in regular schools; later IEDSS (2009) for secondary level; Samagra Shiksha 2018 covers inclusive education. Neighbours: PIED 1987, DPEP 1994, SSA 2001.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a key goal of Community-Based Employment programmes for persons with disabilities?

opts.A: Limiting access to higher education opportunities
opts.C: Encouraging complete dependence on government aid
opts.D: Facilitating gainful employment within the local community

qs.sol: Community-based employment supports paid work and participation in the person’s local community. “Encouraging complete dependence on government aid” does not fit: complete aid dependence conflicts with earning through work.
qs.rel: Community-based employment aims at gainful employment within the local community. Neighbours: sheltered employment, supported employment, vocational rehabilitation, 4% reservation under RPwD Act.

qs.stem: Who has said, “Scientific method consists of systematic observation, classification and interpretation of data”?
qs.sol: “Lundberg” is supported: Lundberg defined scientific method in terms of systematic observation, classification and interpretation of data. By contrast, “Pearson” pearson is known for statistics but not this quoted definition.
qs.rel: Learners with impairments are heterogeneous: types, severity, onset and needs differ. Neighbours: individual differences, individualised education, labelling dangers.

qs.stem:
One of the important aims of teaching mathematics to children is to comprehend mathematical language. Which of the

following consists entirely of standard elementary mathematical symbols?
qs.sol:
Modified from the official paper: both stems now ask for a set entirely of standard elementary mathematical symbols; the original negation contradicted the marked set.

The less-than sign, braces, addition sign and equals sign all have standard elementary mathematical functions.

Every other set includes a hash, ampersand, semicolon or question mark used as punctuation or context-dependent notation.
qs.rel: Individualisation tailors learning to a child's needs and current level. Neighbours: IEP, differentiated instruction, personalised learning, programmed instruction.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a major content area in the Primary level Environmental Studies curriculum?

opts.A: Understanding plants, animals, water, air, and the surrounding environment
opts.B: Studying only historical events unrelated to the environment or nature
opts.C: Focusing solely on advanced scientific theories and laboratory experiments
opts.D: Memorizing definitions and terms without observing the natural world

qs.sol: Primary EVS includes understanding the immediate environment, including plants, animals, water, air and surroundings. It is not limited to rote definitions or unrelated history.
qs.rel: Inclusive education addresses specific socio-emotional and academic needs of each learner. Neighbours: counselling, SEL, learning support, resource teachers.

qs.stem: परियोजना-आधारित अधिगम (PBL) में, अधिगम अनुभव की सफलता के लिए कौन-सा पहलू सबसे महत्वपूर्ण है?

opts.A: विद्यार्थियों को वास्तविक दुनिया की जटिल परियोजनाओं में शामिल करना, जिसमें लंबे समय तक आलोचनात्मक चिंतन करने, सहयोग करने और समस्या-समाधान करने की आवश्यकता होती है।
opts.B: परियोजना विषय से संबंधित तथ्यों को रटकर स्मरण करने पर बल देना।
opts.C: सहयोगात्मक परियोजनाओं के बजाय केवल व्यक्तिगत असाइनमेंट (assignments) और परीक्षणों पर केंद्रित होना।
opts.D: निर्देशों का एक विस्तृत सेट प्रदान करना और विद्यार्थियों से अपेक्षा करना कि वे बिना किसी विचलन के उनका अनुसरण करें।

qs.sol:
अवधारणा

परियोजना-आधारित अधिगम एक विद्यार्थी-केंद्रित शिक्षण-पद्धति है, जो प्रामाणिक एवं जटिल समस्याओं के सतत अन्वेषण के आधार पर व्यवस्थित की जाती है। इसकी आवश्यक विशेषताओं में विद्यार्थी की स्वायत्त सक्रियता, सहयोग, आलोचनात्मक चिंतन, समस्या-समाधान तथा एक सार्थक उत्पाद का निर्माण शामिल हैं।

अनुप्रयोग

यहाँ वास्तविक जीवन की एक जटिल परियोजना के इर्द-गिर्द निर्मित और दीर्घ अवधि तक चलने वाला उपागम अन्वेषण, आलोचनात्मक चिंतन, सहयोग तथा समस्या-समाधान को प्रत्यक्ष रूप से संयोजित करता है। ये प्रक्रियाएँ परियोजना को वह माध्यम बनाती हैं, जिसके द्वारा विद्यार्थी ज्ञान का निर्माण और अनुप्रयोग करते हैं।

तुलना

रटकर याद करना अधिगम को सतत अन्वेषण और ज्ञान के अनुप्रयोग के स्थान पर अलग-अलग तथ्यों के स्मरण प …
qs.rel: Early inclusive citizenship education fosters acceptance of diversity from a young age. Neighbours: national integration, values education, multicultural education, peace education.

qs.stem: The Grammar Translation Method (GTM) was originally based on:

opts.A: Classical language teaching of Latin and Greek.

qs.sol: The Grammar Translation Method originated from classical language teaching, especially Latin and Greek, where grammar rules and translation were central.
qs.rel: Individual attention within a group, with a collaborative approach, is part of inclusive teaching. Neighbours: cooperative learning, peer tutoring, team teaching, co-teaching.

qs.stem: When facilities like extra time, modified seating arrangements, and appropriate assistive devices are provided to students with disabilities, what does this practice reflect?
qs.sol: Inclusive education means adapting teaching methods, learning materials, and the classroom environment so that a student with a disability can access the same curriculum and activities as classmates, in the same classroom, without being separated out. The specific instructional and assessment adjustments used to make this happen — for example extra time, seating changes, or assistive technology — are called reasonable accommodations, and delivering them through teaching practice is what is meant by pedagogical inclusion. …
qs.rel: Providing extra time, seating arrangement and assistive devices is pedagogical (instructional) inclusion; curricular and physical inclusion differ. Neighbours: accommodations vs modifications, assistive technology.

qs.stem: इनमें से कौन विकलांगता का मॉडल नहीं है?
qs.sol: चैरिटी, सामाजिक और पुनर्वास मान्यता प्राप्त दिव्यांगता मॉडल हैं; मेंटल मॉडल यहाँ मानक नामित मॉडल नहीं है।
qs.rel: Models of disability: medical, social, charity, rights-based, economic; 'mental model' is not one. Neighbours: ICF (WHO 2001), medical vs social model, UNCRPD rights-based approach.

qs.stem: ___________ is a strategy for enhancing the quality of life of persons with special needs.
qs.sol: “Community-based rehabilitation” is correct: Community-based rehabilitation coordinates local participation and supports to improve inclusion and daily life. “Community-based recreation” fails: Community-based recreation can contribute to wellbeing, but it is only one activity, not the broader support strategy asked for.
qs.rel: Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR) enhances quality of life for persons with special needs. Neighbours: CBR matrix (WHO), NIEPID, RCI, home-based training.

qs.stem: Which of the following is an example of an attitudinal barrier in inclusive education?

opts.A: Negative beliefs about students with disabilities
opts.B: Lack of ramps for wheelchair users
opts.D: Unavailability of learning materials in accessible formats

qs.sol: Negative beliefs about students with disabilities are attitudes that obstruct inclusion. “Lack of ramps for wheelchair users” is a physical access barrier, whereas an attitudinal barrier lies in people’s beliefs and expectations.
qs.rel: Attitudinal barriers: negative beliefs, stereotypes and low expectations about disability. Neighbours: environmental/physical barriers, institutional/policy barriers, sensitisation.

qs.sol: “Physical disabilities” is outside the traditional ASD triad, which concerns social interaction, communication, and restricted or repetitive patterns of behaviour. “Communication challenges” belongs to that traditional triad, even though current diagnostic descriptions group social and communication features together.
qs.rel: Autism triad concerns social interaction, communication and restricted/repetitive behaviour; physical disability is outside it. Neighbours: DSM-5 two domains, spectrum, comorbidity.

qs.stem: Which of the following does not entirely drive effective implementation of inclusion?
qs.sol:
Resources are necessary, but inclusive practice also requires acceptance, understanding and an inclusive outlook.

Funding by itself cannot ensure effective inclusion.
qs.rel: Effective inclusion depends on attitudes, training, collaboration and philosophy; funding alone does not drive it. Neighbours: leadership, curriculum adaptation, parental involvement.

qs.stem: The full form of CBRDTC is __________.

opts.A: Community Based Rehabilitation Development and Teaching Centre
opts.B: Community Based Rehabilitation Development and Training Centre
opts.C: Community Based Rehabilitation Department and Training Centre
opts.D: Community Based Rehabilitation Department and Teaching Centre

qs.sol: “Community Based Rehabilitation Development and Training Centre” is correct: The expansion names a community-based rehabilitation centre focused on development and training. “Community Based Rehabilitation Development and Teaching Centre” fails: Teaching sounds related but does not reproduce the training component of the stated acronym.
qs.rel: CBRDTC = Community Based Rehabilitation Development and Training Centre (under RCI context). Neighbours: Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI Act 1992), NIEPMD, NIVH, AYJNISHD.

qs.stem: Which of the following best describes economic exclusion?

opts.A: Exclusion due to alienation from political processes and inequality before the law.
opts.B: Exclusion based on the distribution of resources, wealth, and access to markets.
opts.C: Exclusion resulting from lack of citizenship status and deprivation of basic rights.
opts.D: Exclusion due to lack of political rights, freedom of expression, and political participation.

qs.sol: Economic exclusion concerns unequal access to resources, wealth and markets. Political exclusion and citizenship deprivation are different forms of exclusion.
qs.rel: Economic exclusion = exclusion based on distribution of resources/means of livelihood. Neighbours: social exclusion, political exclusion, cultural exclusion; Sen's capability approach.

qs.stem: The Standard of denying inclusive education to a student is:
qs.sol:
Inclusive education presumes that learners should have access to education with suitable support.

Exclusion therefore requires an exceptionally demanding justification rather than a routine threshold.

The intended standard for denying access is very high.
qs.rel: The standard for denying inclusive education should be very high: education in mainstream is the default, denial only in exceptional cases. Neighbours: least restrictive environment, right to education of CWSN.

qs.stem: UN Women has supported the promotion of inclusive electoral processes and the political participation of women with disabilities. This support includes:

opts.A: national coordination mechanisms on disability matters
opts.C: fewer women lead organisations of persons with disabilities
opts.D: capacity-building and sensitisation of security forces to ensure the needs of persons with disabilities are met, especially those of women

qs.sol: Capacity-building and sensitisation of security forces can help make elections accessible to women with disabilities. “systemic marginalisation and structural barriers” describes obstacles to participation, whereas sensitising security forces is a support measure.
qs.rel: Capacity-building and sensitisation of officials and stakeholders enables disability-inclusive political participation. Neighbours: UN Women, CEDAW, SDG 5 and 10.

qs.stem: कौन समावेशी शिक्षा का पहलू नहीं है?
qs.sol:
उत्तर-कुंजी पर टिप्पणी: DSSSB ने इस प्रश्नपत्र की केवल अनंतिम उत्तर-कुंजी जारी की थी, अंतिम कुंजी नहीं। अनंतिम कुंजी “समाज सेवा” को सही मानती है, और यहाँ मूल्यांकन इसी के अनुसार होता है। “परिधीय सेवा” भी तर्कसंगत है, क्योंकि परिधीय सेवाओं को कक्षा में समावेशन का आंतरिक पक्ष नहीं, बाहरी सहायक व्यवस्था भी माना जा सकता है।

आवश्यक और सहयोग सेवाएँ समावेशी शिक्षा से जुड़ी व्यवस्थाएँ हैं। संकीर्ण सेवा-वर्गीकरण में समाज सेवा को अलग रखा गया है। लेकिन “पहलू” की सीमा बताए बिना परिधीय सेवा को भी कक्षा के समावेशन से बाहर की सहायक व्यवस्था माना जा सकता है।
qs.rel: Inclusive education involves access, participation, support and diversity; 'social service' is not an aspect. Neighbours: pillars: presence, participation, achievement.

qs.stem: According to the Salamanca Statement (1994), what is considered as the most effective way to promote inclusion for disabled children?

opts.A: Enrolling disabled children in neighbourhood regular schools
opts.B: Establishing special schools for disabled children
opts.C: Providing separate classrooms within regular schools
opts.D: Offering homeschooling options for disabled children

qs.sol: The Salamanca Statement supports neighbourhood regular schools as a means of inclusive education. “Providing separate classrooms within regular schools” retains segregation inside a school and therefore falls short of learning together in neighbourhood classes.
qs.rel: Salamanca Statement 1994 (UNESCO): enrol children with disabilities in neighbourhood regular schools as the most effective way to promote inclusion. Neighbours: 'Education for All', Dakar 2000, UNCRPD 2006.

qs.stem:
Choose the most appropriate option.
Inclusive Schools are more effective when:
qs.sol:
Inclusive education works when the whole school (management, teachers, students and parents) accepts that every child belongs, and adapts its culture, policy and practice accordingly.

This shared inclusive philosophy is the foundation. Special educators, counsellors and competent teachers are resources that work well only within it.

Hence the most appropriate option is: it has inclusive philosophy.
qs.rel: Inclusive schools work best with an inclusive philosophy supported by pedagogy and leadership. Neighbours: whole-school approach, collaborative culture, flexible curriculum.

qs.sol: An impairment is a condition or loss affecting a body function or structure. Disability describes the resulting limitation in activity or participation. “Disability” does not fit: disability refers to activity or participation restrictions, rather than the underlying bodily condition.
qs.rel: Impairment = loss/abnormality of body structure or function; disability = resulting activity limitation; handicap = social disadvantage (WHO ICIDH). Neighbours: ICF 2001.

qs.stem:
When students with special education needs are made to fit into the pre-existing school structure, is called:

Choose the right answer from the options below.
qs.sol:
Integration places learners with special needs into an existing mainstream structure and expects adaptation to that structure.

Thus the described arrangement is integrated education.
qs.rel: Integrated education = child with special needs fits into existing school structure; inclusive education = system adapts to child. Neighbours: mainstreaming, segregated education.

qs.stem: शिक्षा की दृष्टि से समावेशी शिक्षा की क्या आवश्यकता है? I. शोध से पता चलता है कि बच्चे समावेशी समायोजन में अकादमिक और सामाजिक रूप से बेहतर प्रदर्शन करते हैं। II. समावेशन में भय को कम करने और मित्रता बनाने की क्षमता है

opts.D: ना ही I ना ही II

qs.sol: समावेशी शिक्षा के व्यापक रूप से उद्धृत कारण तीन शीर्षकों में बाँटे जाते हैं: मानव अधिकार, अच्छी शिक्षा और सामाजिक समझ। अच्छी शिक्षा के अंतर्गत शोध बताता है कि बच्चे समावेशी परिवेश में शैक्षिक और सामाजिक दोनों रूप से बेहतर करते हैं। यह दावा कि समावेशन में भय कम करने और मित्रता, सम्मान तथा समझ विकसित करने की क्षमता है, सामाजिक समझ के अंतर्गत आता है, शिक्षा के दृष्टिकोण के अंतर्गत नहीं। अतः शिक्षा के दृष्टिकोण से समावेशी शिक्षा की आवश्यकता का उत्तर केवल कथन I देता है।
qs.rel: Inclusive education benefits all learners: social skills, acceptance, academic outcomes. Neighbours: research evidence, peer learning, reduction of stigma.

qs.sol: “अशक्तता व्यक्तियों के लिए सहायक तकनीकों के अनुसंधान और उपयोग को बढ़ावा देना” सही है, क्योंकि अनुच्छेद 4 राज्यों से दिव्यांग व्यक्तियों के लिए सहायक प्रौद्योगिकी के अनुसंधान, विकास और उपलब्धता को बढ़ावा देने की अपेक्षा करता है। “शैक्षणिक संस्थानों तक केवल वास्तविक पहुँच सुनिश्चित करना” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि शैक्षणिक भवन तक भौतिक पहुँच महत्त्वपूर्ण है, पर केवल उसी तक दायित्व सीमित करने से सहायक तकनीक का दायित्व पूरा नहीं होता।
qs.rel: Assistive technology research and use is promoted for persons with disabilities (RPwD Act 2016). Neighbours: ADIP scheme, accessible ICT, screen readers.

qs.stem: The goal of the CBVT program is to:

opts.A: promote advanced academic research in virtual technologies
opts.C: increase self-awareness about career interests and abilities

qs.sol: “increase self-awareness about career interests and abilities” fits a career-based vocational training programme because informed choices depend on recognising personal strengths and preferences. “conduct research in behavioural sciences” is an academic research activity rather than the learner-focused career goal described here.
qs.rel: CBVT (community-based vocational training) aims to build career interest awareness and employability. Neighbours: vocational rehabilitation, NHFDC, sheltered workshops.

qs.stem: The concept of integrated education in India emerged during the mid 1950s. It is based on the ____________ of disability and it emphasises placement of children with disabilities in mainstream schools.
qs.sol: “Medical model” is correct: Integration places a child in a mainstream setting while treating disability chiefly as an individual condition requiring support or remediation. “Inclusive model” fails: The inclusive model instead calls for adapting the school system to learner diversity, which is a different approach.
qs.rel: Integrated education in India (1950s-70s) was based on the medical model, where the child adapts to the system. Neighbours: social model, rights-based model, IEDC 1974, Kothari Commission.

qs.sol: UDL के अनुसार शिक्षण वातावरण लचीला होना चाहिए ताकि व्यक्तिगत अधिगम अंतर के अनुसार भागीदारी संभव हो। “समरूपता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए सभी के लिए एक जैसा पाठ्यक्रम तैयार करना” व्यक्तिगत भिन्नताओं को अनदेखा करता है, जबकि लचीला शिक्षण वातावरण विभिन्न जरूरतों के अनुसार पहुँच देता है।
qs.rel: UDL requires flexible teaching environment to accommodate individual learning differences. Neighbours: multiple means of representation, expression and engagement.

qs.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.

In certain cases of special attention or special needs, art form in teaching is also used as a technique for:
qs.sol: Art activities can provide a therapeutic means of expression and support for learners with special needs.
qs.rel: Art can serve as therapy for children with special needs (art therapy, music therapy, play therapy). Neighbours: occupational therapy, speech therapy, remedial teaching.

qs.sol: “गैर-अनुकू लित खेल के मैदान के उपकरण” सही है: बिना अनुकूलन के बने खेल उपकरण प्रमस्तिष्क घात वाले विद्यार्थी की पहुँच या नियंत्रण संबंधी जरूरतों के अनुरूप नहीं होते, इसलिए वे सहायक प्रौद्योगिकी नहीं हैं। “संवर्द्धक और वैकल्पिक संचार उपकरण और सॉफ्टवेयर” सही नहीं है: संवर्द्धक और वैकल्पिक संचार उपकरण तथा सॉफ्टवेयर संप्रेषण और अधिगम में वास्तविक सहायता दे सकते हैं।
qs.rel: Unadapted playground equipment excludes children with disabilities; adapted equipment ensures participation. Neighbours: universal design, accessible play, barrier-free environment.

qs.stem:
"विशेष आवश्यकता वाले बच्चों की ज़रूरतें अलग-अलग बच्चों में अलग-अलग होंगी जोकि उनकी दिव्यँग पर निर्भर करती है।" इस दिए गए कथन के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है?

I. मानसिक मंद बच्चे को एक संकल्पना को समझने के लिए ठोस सामग्री की आवश्यकता नहीं होगी, लेकिन पुनरावृत्त निर्देशों की आवश्यकता होगी।

II. मोटर विकलांग बच्चे को आवश्यकता के आधार पर शारीरिक सहायता की आवश्यकता होगी।

opts.D: ना ही I ना ही II

qs.sol: बौद्धिक अक्षमता वाले बच्चे ठोस, प्रत्यक्ष सामग्री, छोटे-छोटे चरणों और बार-बार दिए गए निर्देशों से सबसे अच्छा सीखते हैं, क्योंकि अमूर्त विचार समझना उनके लिए कठिन होता है। कथन I गलत है, क्योंकि यह कहता है कि ऐसे बच्चे को ठोस सामग्री की आवश्यकता नहीं होगी। गामक या चलन-संबंधी अक्षमता वाले बच्चों को उनकी स्थिति के अनुसार शारीरिक सहायता चाहिए, जैसे सहायक उपकरण, रैंप, अनुकूलित बैठने की व्यवस्था या चलने में मदद; इसलिए कथन II सही है। उद्धृत सिद्धांत यही है कि सहायता हर बच्चे की विशेष अक्षमता के अनुरूप हो।
qs.rel: Special needs of children vary individually; needs assessment guides IEP. Neighbours: categories of CWSN, identification and screening, resource support.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा संयोजन सही है? I. अतिरिक्त सहायता के लिए बच्चे को संसाधन कक्ष में रखा जाता है। - समावेशी शिक्षा II. नियमित कक्षा में छात्रों को सभी आवश्यक सहायता उपलब्ध कराई जाएगी - एकीकृत शिक्षा

opts.D: ना ही I ना ही II

qs.sol: दिए गए दोनों कथनों में एकीकरण और समावेशन के नाम उलट गए हैं। संसाधन कक्ष में अलग अतिरिक्त सहायता देना प्रायः एकीकृत व्यवस्था से जुड़ता है। समावेशी शिक्षा का लक्ष्य नियमित कक्षा के भीतर आवश्यक सहायता और सहभागिता उपलब्ध कराना है। केवल विद्यालय में प्रवेश पर्याप्त नहीं होता; वातावरण भी शिक्षार्थी की जरूरतों के अनुसार बदलना चाहिए। इसलिए किसी भी कथन में दिया गया नाम उसके वर्णन से ठीक मेल नहीं खाता।
qs.rel: Providing extra support resources is part of inclusive classrooms (resource room, peer help). Neighbours: remedial teaching, resource teacher, itinerant model.

qs.stem:
An effective inclusive environment is beneficial to the larger group without disabilities as it develops many attributes.

Which of these is not the benefit of inclusion to the non-disabled group?
qs.sol:
The marked key distinguishes personal attitudes from the composition of a group.

Tolerance, acceptance and compassion are attitudes; diversity describes differences among the group’s members.

Note on the official key: diversity is also a defensible educational benefit of inclusion. The printed question asks about benefits and gives no personal-attitude restriction. The board marks diversity using that narrower classification; the ambiguity remains.
qs.rel: Inclusive environment develops diversity acceptance, empathy and cooperation among all students. Neighbours: sensitisation, peer tutoring, shared learning.

qs.stem: The concept of inclusive education is that:

opts.A: Every child in society should be valued equally
opts.B: A special child must be included in every child
opts.C: Only special children should be educated in schools
opts.D: All students must respect a special child

qs.sol: Inclusive education values every child equally and provides access for all.
qs.rel: Inclusive education: every child is valued equally and learns together. Neighbours: right to education, non-discrimination, Article 21A, UNCRPD Article 24.

qs.stem: An inclusive learning environment is the one that is designed typically for:

opts.C: That grade and age group of learners
opts.D: The students with special educational needs

qs.sol: An inclusive classroom is designed for the full age or grade cohort, with access and support for diverse learners within it. It is not restricted to one disability or subgroup.
qs.rel: An inclusive environment is designed for all learners in a grade/age group, not just specified target groups. Neighbours: universal design, heterogeneous classroom.

qs.stem: What is the main Role and responsibility of head master of inclusive school?

opts.A: Recognizing that all students benefit from inclusion
opts.B: Special children must get special attention

qs.sol: In an inclusive school the head teacher's main role is to lead a whole-school belief that inclusion benefits all students, and to shape attitudes, policies and practices around it. Special attention, infrastructure and special teachers are supporting measures, not the core responsibility.
qs.rel: The headmaster of an inclusive school must recognise that all students benefit from inclusion and lead supportive policy. Neighbours: whole-school approach, teacher training, resource mobilisation.

qs.stem:
Integrated Education for Disabled Children (IEDC) was established with an objective to _____.
Complete the statement with the right option from the following.

opts.A: Providing educational opportunities to all children with disabilities under the general school system
opts.B: Providing guidance to all children with special education needs
opts.C: Providing educational opportunities only to children to physical disabilities
opts.D: Providing educational opportunities for children with mental disabilities

qs.sol: IEDC aims to include children with disabilities in the general school system, rather than restrict provision to a single disability type.
qs.rel: IEDC (1974) provided educational opportunities for disabled children in regular schools with assistance for books, aids, and special teachers. Neighbours: revised 1992, IEDSS 2009, Samagra Shiksha.

qs.stem: Institutional initiative for inclusive education can be evidenced when _____.

opts.A: School has undifferentiated material for all students
opts.B: Teachers plan common assessments for all students
opts.C: Time is provided for teams of teachers and paraprofessionals to plan together
opts.D: School conducts entry level tests to enroll able students

qs.sol: Providing joint planning time lets teachers and support professionals coordinate accommodations for diverse learners, showing an institutional commitment to inclusion.
qs.rel: Institutional initiative for inclusion: time for teachers and parents to plan and collaborate. Neighbours: school inclusion policy, teacher training, resource centres.

qs.sol: समावेशन सभी को संसाधनों तथा भागीदारी के अवसरों तक पहुँच देता है।
qs.rel: Inclusion gives access to resources and opportunities to participate. Neighbours: equity, accessibility, participation, differentiation.

qs.sol: छात्रों की अलग आवश्यकताओं के अनुसार शिक्षण बदलना विभेदन है।
qs.rel: Differentiation = adapting teaching to students' different needs (content, process, product). Neighbours: Tomlinson's model, readiness/interest/learning profile, flexible grouping.

qs.sol: समावेशी वातावरण की शुरुआत शिक्षार्थियों की विविधता को स्वीकार करने से होती है।
qs.rel: Inclusive environment begins by accepting learner diversity. Neighbours: sensitisation, positive attitudes, welcoming school culture.

qs.stem:
Choose the most appropriate option to complete the sentence.

Inclusive environment stems from:

opts.D: Pairing of philosophy and pedagogical practices

qs.sol: An inclusive environment grows when an inclusive philosophy is put into consistent pedagogical practice.
qs.rel: Inclusive environment stems from pairing philosophy with pedagogical practice. Neighbours: belief + practice, leadership, collaborative teaching.

qs.stem:
सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प चुनें।

संवेदीकरण सहकर्मी एक समावेशी स्कूल में ______ को कम करने के तरीकों में से एक है।
qs.sol: सहकर्मियों को संवेदनशील बनाना सम्मान बढ़ाता है और समावेशी विद्यालय में विद्यार्थियों को धमकाना घटाता है।
qs.rel: Sensitisation of peers reduces prejudice and negative attitudes in inclusive schools. Neighbours: peer tutoring, circle of friends, disability awareness programmes.

qs.sol: “नवागंतुकों को नए परिवेश, उसके नियमों और अवसरों से परिचित कराना ताकि उन्हें समायोजित होने में सहायता मिल सके” सही है: अभिविन्यासी समूह निर्देशन नवागंतुकों को संस्था, नियम और उपलब्ध अवसर समझाकर नए परिवेश में समायोजन में मदद करता है। “व्यक्तिगत मनोवैज्ञानिक आकलन करना” सही नहीं है: व्यक्तिगत मनोवैज्ञानिक आकलन किसी एक व्यक्ति की जाँच है, समूह को नए परिवेश से परिचित कराने का उद्देश्य नहीं।
qs.rel: Orientation of newcomers to environment, rules and opportunities helps them settle: school orientation/induction. Neighbours: transition support, peer buddy, mobility training for visually impaired.

qs.sol: “माध्यमिक स्तर पर दिव्याङ्ग के लिए समावेशी शिक्षा (IEDSS)” का लक्ष्य माध्यमिक स्तर पर दिव्यांग विद्यार्थियों की समावेशी शिक्षा को सहायता देना है। “राष्ट्रीय माध्यमिक विद्यालय शिक्षा अभियान (RMSA)” माध्यमिक शिक्षा का व्यापक अभियान है; उसका नाम इस विशिष्ट दिव्यांगता-केंद्रित कार्यक्रम को नहीं बताता।
qs.rel: IEDSS (Inclusive Education of Disabled at Secondary Stage, 2009) aims to enable disabled students to complete 4 years of secondary schooling in an inclusive environment. Neighbours: IEDC, Samagra Shiksha.

qs.sol: “अधिगम वातावरण से बाधाओं को दूर करना” विविध विद्यार्थियों के लिए सीखने की सामग्री, सहभागिता और अभिव्यक्ति को सुलभ बनाने का व्यापक लक्ष्य है। “भौतिक वातावरण से बाधाओं को हटाना” भी पहुँच से जुड़ा है, पर वह केवल भौतिक स्थान की बाधाओं तक सीमित है।
qs.rel: Removing barriers in learning environment (physical, attitudinal, curricular) enables participation of diverse learners. Neighbours: UDL, reasonable accommodation, universal access.

qs.sol: समूह में “सकारात्मक समकक्षी प्रभाव और सामाजिक कौशल के व्यापकीकरण को बढ़ावा देना” से सहपाठियों के साथ सीखे व्यवहार का अभ्यास और अलग परिस्थितियों में उसका उपयोग बढ़ सकता है। “केवल शैक्षिक निष्पादन पर ध्यान केंद्रित करना” समूह से मिलने वाले सामाजिक अधिगम को छोड़ देता है, इसलिए लाभ को बहुत संकुचित कर देता है।
qs.rel: Positive peer influence and generalisation of social skills are supported by group-based, peer-mediated interventions. Neighbours: social skills training, circle of friends, peer buddy.

qs.sol: पारिवारिक सहायता समूह का उद्देश्य भरोसा और क्षमता बढ़ाना है, इसलिए “आत्मविश्वास स्तर को कम करना” उसका काम नहीं हो सकता। “उनकी जरूरतों की पहचान करना” परिवार की स्थिति समझकर उपयुक्त सहायता तय करने में मदद करता है।
qs.rel: Family support groups raise trust, confidence and coping capacity of families. Neighbours: parent training, self-help groups, family-centred intervention.

qs.sol: “दो या अधिक अशक्तताओं का एक साथ होना जिसके परिणामस्वरूप सार्थक शैक्षिक आवश्यकताएँ होती हैं” सहवर्ती अशक्तताओं से पैदा होने वाली संयुक्त शैक्षिक जरूरतों को दर्शाता है। “दो या अधिक जीर्ण रोग होना” रोगों की संख्या बताता है, पर बहु-अशक्तता और उससे उत्पन्न शिक्षा-संबंधी जरूरत को नहीं परिभाषित करता।
qs.rel: Multiple disabilities: two or more disabilities co-occurring requiring significant educational support. Neighbours: deaf-blindness, RPwD Act 2016 lists multiple disabilities including deaf-blindness.
