qs.stem: According to NCERT and Samagra Shiksha guidelines in India, which of the following is a key skill or competency for a teacher acting as a counselor?

opts.A: Conducting active listening, empathy, and effective communication during counseling
opts.D: Managing school financial budgets and accounts

qs.sol: Active listening, empathy and effective communication are central skills in school counseling. “Managing school financial budgets and accounts” is an administrative responsibility, not the interpersonal competency used while counseling a learner.
qs.rel: Teachers in inclusive classrooms need active listening, empathy and effective communication per NCERT/Samagra Shiksha guidelines. Neighbours: collaboration, differentiated instruction, positive behaviour support.

qs.stem: A key benefit of family involvement in inclusive education is:

opts.A: improved student success regardless of socio-economic status
opts.C: reduction in financial burden on schools

qs.sol: Family participation supports student learning and inclusion across socioeconomic backgrounds. “increased dependency on special educators” does not fit: family involvement should support autonomy and collaboration, not dependency.
qs.rel: Family involvement improves student success irrespective of socio-economic background; parent-teacher partnership matters. Neighbours: parental participation, SMC under RTE, home-school link.

qs.stem:
Special attention given to students with or without special needs is called _____.

Choose the right option.
qs.sol:
Remedial education identifies learning gaps and provides targeted help.

Such help can be given to any learner, whether or not formally identified with special needs.

That matches the emphasis on special attention in the printed stem.
qs.rel: Remedial education: special attention to learners with or without special needs who need extra help. Neighbours: enrichment education, compensatory education, diagnostic teaching.

topics.deep:
- **Concepts:** Special education (segregated special schools) -> **integration/mainstreaming** (child fits into existing school; medical model) -> **inclusion** (system adapts; social/rights-based model). Exclusion = denial of access; segregation = separate schools. Inclusive education values diversity, ensures presence, participation and achievement of all learners; "special needs" refers to the modifications the system must make (CWSN = children with special needs).
- **Models of disability:** medical (deficit in the person), social (barriers in society), charity, rights-based, economic, biopsychosocial (ICF 2001). Terms: **impairment** (loss of structure/function), **disability** (activity limitation), **handicap** (social disadvantage) - WHO ICIDH.
- **International milestones:**

| Year | Document | Point |
|---|---|---|
| 1948 | UDHR | right to education |
| 1960 | UNESCO Convention against Discrimination in Education | equality of educational opportunity |
| 1978 | Warnock Report (UK) | coined "special educational needs" |
| 1990 | Jomtien - Education for All | EFA |
| 1994 | **Salamanca Statement** (UNESCO) | inclusive schools, neighbourhood regular schools |
| 2000 | Dakar Framework | EFA goals |
| 2006 | **UNCRPD** | Article 24 inclusive education; India ratified 2007 |
| 2015 | SDG 4 | inclusive, equitable quality education |

- **Indian legislation and schemes:**

| Item | Key fact |
|---|---|
| IEDC 1974 | integrated education; revised 1992; **IEDSS 2009** at secondary stage |
| RCI Act 1992 | Rehabilitation Council of India regulates special-educator training |
| PWD Act 1995 | 7 disabilities; 3% reservation |
| National Trust Act 1999 | autism, cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, multiple disabilities |
| **RPwD Act 2016** | **21 disabilities**; 4% reservation in government jobs, 5% in higher-education seats; free education 6-18 years for benchmark disability (40%+); replaced PWD Act 1995 |
| RTE Act 2009 | 6-14 years; 25% reservation (Section 12); disabled children included in "disadvantaged group" (2012 amendment) |
| Samagra Shiksha 2018 | merges SSA, RMSA, TE; includes inclusive education (IE) component |
| NEP 2020 | inclusive, barrier-free access, resource centres, special educators, ISL |
| DPEP 1994, SSA 2001 | community mobilisation, IED component |
| ADIP scheme | aids and appliances; Accessible India (Sugamya Bharat) Campaign 2015 |

- **National institutes:** NIEPMD (Chennai; intellectual and multiple disabilities, formerly NIMH), NIEPVD (Dehradun; visual, earlier NIVH), AYJNISHD (Mumbai; hearing), NILD (Kolkata; locomotor), NIEPID, NIEPA (planning and administration).
- **Barriers:** attitudinal (negative beliefs, low expectations), physical/infrastructural (stairs, toilets), curricular (rigid syllabus, exams), institutional/policy, communication barriers. Accessibility features: ramps, elevators, tactile paths, signage.
- **Strategies:** UDL (CAST: multiple means of engagement, representation, action/expression), differentiated instruction (Tomlinson: content, process, product), IEP (present level, goals, services, review), resource room, itinerant teacher, co-teaching, peer tutoring, circle of friends, accommodations (extra time, scribe) vs modifications (changed content), Index for Inclusion (Booth and Ainscow), sensitisation of peers, family involvement.
- **CBR (WHO 1978):** community-based rehabilitation matrix - health, education, livelihood, social, empowerment. **CBVT** = community-based vocational training; supported and sheltered employment.
- **Other exclusion types:** economic, social, political, cultural; **intersectionality** (Crenshaw). Multicultural education (James Banks): content integration, knowledge construction, prejudice reduction, equity pedagogy, empowering school culture. Gifted and talented also need special provision; remedial vs enrichment education.

**Likely question angles:**
- Integration vs inclusion difference statements.
- Year/article of Salamanca, UNCRPD, RPwD Act and number of disabilities.
- Percentage reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities.
- Which scheme/centre: IEDC, IEDSS, SSA, Samagra Shiksha.
- Identify type of barrier from a scenario.
- UDL principles and examples of accommodation vs modification.
- Full forms: CBR, CWSN, IEP, UDL, RCI, NIEPMD.
- Models of disability matching.
- Role of headmaster/teacher/family in inclusive school.
- Examples of exclusion (economic, political, social).

topics.title: 5. Developmental & Learning Disabilities (ASD, ADHD, ID, SLD)
topics.theory:
- **Intellectual disability:** IQ below ~70 + deficits in adaptive behaviour before 18 yrs. Bands: mild 50-69, moderate 35-49, severe 20-34, profound <20. Old labels: moron, imbecile, idiot. Teach with real/concrete objects first, task analysis, repetition.
- **Assessment:** **Vineland Social Maturity Scale** (Doll 1935) - 89 items, 8 domains, gives SA/SQ; **BASIC-MR** (NIMH Secunderabad) guides IEP; IQ tests (Binet, Wechsler).
- **Autism:** term coined by **Eugen Bleuler** (1911); Kanner 1943; Asperger 1944. **DSM-5** merged autistic disorder, Asperger's and PDD-NOS into **ASD** (social communication deficits + restricted/repetitive behaviours).
- **ASD screening:** M-CHAT, **Q-CHAT**, Infant-Toddler Checklist; diagnosis: ADOS, CARS. Interventions: **ABA**, **DTT** (cue-response-consequence-pause), **TEACCH**, PECS, visual supports, social stories.
- **ADHD:** inattention + hyperactivity-impulsivity (onset before 12 years). **SLD:** dyslexia (reading), dysgraphia (writing), dyscalculia (maths); multisensory structured language teaching.
- **Hyperlexia:** advanced decoding with poor comprehension in ASD; NVLD: weak visual-spatial, good verbal skills.
- **Behaviour modification:** ABC model (antecedent-behaviour-consequence), reinforcement, shaping, token economy, **response cost**, time-out, extinction, prompt fading.
- **Causes:** Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Fragile X, PKU, prenatal infections; delayed speech may be due to ID, hearing loss, behavioural disorder.
- **IEP team:** parents, special/general teachers, therapists; a librarian is not a core member.
- Expressive language disorder = difficulty sharing thoughts; receptive = difficulty understanding.

qs.stem: Constructivist theory in education is based on ___

opts.A: the idea that learn from the society
opts.C: the idea that people actively construct or make their own knowledge
opts.D: the knowledge from the book they learn

qs.sol: Constructivism holds that learners actively build knowledge through experience and reflection.
qs.rel: Causes of delayed speech: intellectual disability, hearing impairment, behavioural/emotional disorders, lack of stimulation, autism. Neighbours: speech vs language delay, expressive vs receptive disorders, early hearing screening.

qs.stem: Which tool is commonly used to assess intellectual disability in children?
qs.sol: “Standardised intelligence tests” is correct: Standardised intelligence tests help assess intellectual functioning as one component of an intellectual-disability evaluation. “Hearing test” fails: A hearing test checks auditory function and cannot determine intellectual functioning.
qs.rel: Intellectual disability is assessed with standardised intelligence tests (Binet, Wechsler) plus adaptive behaviour scales. Neighbours: IQ below ~70, onset before 18 years, Vineland, BASIC-MR, AAMR classification.

qs.stem: Which of the following best describes hyperlexia in children with autism spectrum disorders?

opts.D: Difficulty understanding and using social language despite strong decoding skills

qs.sol: Hyperlexia may involve advanced word decoding alongside difficulty with comprehension and social use of language. “Complete absence of verbal communication” does not fit: complete absence of speech is not required for this reading profile.
qs.rel: Hyperlexia: advanced word-decoding ability with poor comprehension and social language use, seen in some autistic children. Neighbours: echolalia, literal language, pragmatic language deficits.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a feature of sex?

opts.D: It changes from time to time

qs.sol: “It changes from time to time”: The paper treats biological sex as a biological classification rather than a social attribute that varies with time. “It is nature-made.”: The nature-made description fits the paper’s biological framing.
qs.rel: BASIC-MR (NIMH Secunderabad) assesses basic skills in persons with intellectual disability; results guide IEP and group teaching plans. Neighbours: sections - Part A (basic skills) and Part B (behaviour); Vineland social maturity scale.

qs.stem: LAC विद्यालय और महाविद्यालय के पाठ्यक्रमों के लिए शब्द है जो छात्रों को विदेशी भाषा का अध्ययन करने की अनुमति देता है। LAC का अर्थ ___________ है।
qs.sol: LAC का विस्तार 'Language across the curriculum' है। इसका आशय यह है कि भाषा का उपयोग और विकास केवल भाषा-विषय की कक्षा तक सीमित नहीं; विज्ञान, गणित, इतिहास आदि विषयों में पढ़ना, चर्चा करना और लिखना भी भाषिक अधिगम का हिस्सा है। प्रश्न का विदेशी भाषा संबंधी परिचय संकीर्ण है, पर संक्षेप के अक्षर और स्थापित शैक्षिक अवधारणा स्पष्ट हैं। 'Content' या 'class' पूरे पाठ्यक्रम में भाषा की भूमिका को नहीं दर्शाते, जबकि 'coaching' निजी प्रशिक्षण का संदर्भ देता है। सभी विषयों में भाषा की उपस्थिति पहचानना निर्णायक है।
qs.rel: Expressive language disorder: difficulty conveying thoughts and feelings in speech; receptive disorder: difficulty understanding. Neighbours: aphasia, stuttering (fluency), articulation (speech sound) disorders.

qs.stem: Which of the following social science subject may not be categorized under the ‘Pure social sciences’ branch?
qs.sol: Anthropology, history, and public administration study human societies and institutions, so they fit branches of social science in this classroom classification. Medicine primarily studies health, disease, and treatment and is usually grouped with medical or health sciences. It is the exception the question seeks. Anthropology studies human culture and society. History examines human societies through past events. Public administration studies institutions and governance. Medicine belongs primarily to health sciences.
qs.rel: Eugen Bleuler (1911) coined 'autism'; Leo Kanner (1943) described early infantile autism; Hans Asperger (1944) described Asperger's. Neighbours: DSM-5 spectrum (2013), Lorna Wing's triad.

qs.stem: What is the collaboration that teacher need to build among students?
qs.sol:
Classroom collaboration should advance a shared learning task through purposeful interaction.

Students contribute ideas, explain their reasoning and learn from one another.

This is meaningful collaboration rather than cooperation without a defined learning purpose.
qs.rel: VSMS (Edgar Doll, 1935; India: Malin's adaptation) measures social maturity across 8 domains: self-help general, eating, dressing, locomotion, occupation, communication, self-direction, socialisation. Neighbours: 89 items; gives SA and SQ.

qs.stem: What is the primary reason for using a blindfold during Orientation and Mobility training?

opts.A: To protect the eyes from sunlight
opts.B: To simulate the experience of total blindness for training purposes
opts.C: To help students memorise routes visually

qs.sol: “To simulate the experience of total blindness for training purposes” allows a sighted trainee to practise attending to nonvisual orientation and mobility cues under supervision. “To help students memorise routes visually” conflicts with the blindfold’s purpose because it blocks visual route cues.
qs.rel: ASD students struggle with changes in routine, sensory overload and transitions; use visual schedules and predictability. Neighbours: TEACCH structured teaching, social stories, sensory breaks.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
 I. Multilingualism is an integral part of the Indian linguistic heritage.
 II. The culture and attitude towards language has a prominent role to play in a country being monolingual or multilingual.
qs.sol: Multilingualism is part of India's linguistic heritage, and social culture and attitudes toward language influence whether a country is monolingual or multilingual. Both statements are correct.
qs.rel: Screening identifies those at risk; diagnosis confirms a condition. Neighbours: M-CHAT, Q-CHAT, developmental surveillance, multidisciplinary evaluation.

qs.sol: “पसंदीदा रं ग (Favourite colour)” सही है, क्योंकि पसंदीदा रंग सामान्यतः संदेश के भेजने, सुनने या समझने की प्रक्रिया में बाधा नहीं डालता। “भौतिक दूरी (Physical distance)” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि भौतिक दूरी आवाज की स्पष्टता और दृश्य संकेतों की उपलब्धता घटा सकती है, इसलिए वह संचार को प्रभावित करती है।
qs.rel: Messages may depend on context, such as favourite colour as a preference rather than a communicative message. Neighbours: AAC, functional communication, preference assessment.

qs.stem: Problems in sharing our thoughts, ideas and feelings are known as ____________ disorder.
qs.sol: “expressive language” disorder affects putting thoughts, ideas and feelings into words or other language forms for others. “receptive language” disorder primarily affects understanding language that comes in, rather than expressing a message.
qs.rel: Most comprehensive ASD assessment combines direct observation with structured diagnostic tools (ADOS, ADI-R). Neighbours: CARS, ISAA (India), screening vs diagnosis.

qs.stem: Which of this is not a level of language?
qs.sol: Levels of linguistic analysis describe different aspects of a language. Phonetics studies speech sounds, morphology studies the structure and formation of words, and syntax studies how words combine into sentences. English is a particular language on which those kinds of analysis can be performed. It is therefore an object of study, not one of the analytical levels. The question contrasts categories such as sounds, word form, and sentence structure with the name of a language. This distinction applies regardless of whether the language being studied is English, Hindi, or Sanskrit.
qs.rel: Assessing basic curricular skills identifies learning needs and guides instruction for students with LD. Neighbours: curriculum-based assessment, error analysis, IEP goals, dyslexia, dysgraphia, dyscalculia.

qs.stem: While teaching a children how to read, which of the following things need to be kept in mind? I. The material used must be meaningful and of the level of the child. II. The material should be in a language that the child is familiar with.
qs.sol: Reading material should match the child's level and use familiar language. Both points support early reading instruction.
qs.rel: Behaviour modification (Skinner-based) aims to increase adaptive and decrease maladaptive behaviour using reinforcement, shaping, token economy. Neighbours: ABC analysis, extinction, time-out, response cost.

qs.stem: Which of the following stage is used for child cognition development at the age from 2 years to 7 years?
qs.sol: In Piaget's theory, the pre-operational stage covers approximately ages 2 to 7 years.
qs.rel: ADHD core features: inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity; types: predominantly inattentive, hyperactive-impulsive, combined. Neighbours: DSM-5 onset before 12 years; management: behaviour therapy, structured routine.

qs.stem:
सामाजिक विज्ञान में पाठ्यचर्या घटकों में निम्नलिखित में से कौन से शामिल है?
I. भूगोल में प्रमुख प्रक्रियाएं
II. व्यक्तियों, पर्यावरण और संसाधनों के बीच अंतर्संबंध
III. ऐतिहासिक निर्वचन कौशल
IV. संविधान पर आधारित मूल्य
qs.sol: सामाजिक विज्ञान का पाठ्यक्रम भूगोल, इतिहास और नागरिक शास्त्र को जोड़ता है। विद्यार्थी भौगोलिक प्रक्रियाएं तथा व्यक्ति, पर्यावरण और संसाधन संबंध पढ़ते हैं; वे ऐतिहासिक प्रमाणों की व्याख्या करते और संवैधानिक मूल्यों पर चर्चा करते हैं। ये परस्पर पूरक घटक हैं, प्रतिस्पर्धी सूचियां नहीं। इसलिए चारों तत्व समेकित पाठ्यक्रम में शामिल होते हैं। इसमें भौगोलिक प्रक्रियाएं छूटती हैं, जो विषय का महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा हैं। भूगोल, ऐतिहासिक व्याख्या और संवैधानिक मूल्य सभी पाठ्यक्रम में हैं। इसमें व्यक्ति पर्यावरण संबंध और नागरिक मूल्य छूटते हैं। इस चयन में व्यापक सूची से ऐतिहासिक व्याख्या कौशल हट जाता है।
qs.rel: For intellectual disability, start teaching with real/concrete objects, then models and pictures, then abstract symbols. Neighbours: task analysis, repetition, concrete-to-abstract, multisensory teaching.

qs.stem: Which of the following best represents Susan Stryker's view of transgender identity?

opts.B: It is limited to those who undergo surgery.
opts.C: It includes all identities that challenge gender boundaries.

qs.sol:
Trans studies scholarship distinguishes a broad, umbrella definition of transgender identity from narrower single-criterion definitions built around one fixed trait, a surgical procedure, or an internal mental state alone. Susan Stryker, a foundational historian of transgender studies, defines "transgender" as an umbrella term covering the many identities and practices that cross, move between, or otherwise challenge socially constructed gender boundaries — not any one fixed category, pathway, or internal state.

Applying this framing to the four options offered here:

It is a fixed category — an umbrella definition rejects treating the identity as one fixed, unchanging category. …
qs.rel: IEP team: parents, special and general teachers, therapists, school psychologist, the child where appropriate; a librarian is not a core member. Neighbours: IEP contents (present level, goals, services, review).

qs.stem: The process of acquiring knowledge through observation and experiences is called _________.
qs.sol: Empiricism grounds knowledge in sensory observation and experience. The other methods rely on repeated belief, an authority, or a claimed disclosure instead.
qs.rel: ABC model: Antecedent (trigger), Behaviour, Consequence. Neighbours: functional behaviour analysis, positive behaviour support, reinforcement.

qs.stem: Gender, as a concept in socialisation, primarily refers to what type of characteristics?
qs.sol:
In sociology, sex refers to the biological attributes a person is born with (chromosomes, anatomy, hormones), while gender is the set of roles, behaviours, and traits that a society assigns to being male or female. Gender attributes are learned through socialisation — through family, peer groups, schooling, and media — so they vary across cultures and historical periods rather than being fixed by biology.

In the question, the phrase “as a concept in socialisation” points directly to this learned, socially transmitted dimension of gender rather than to biology. …
qs.rel: VSMS has 89 items arranged by age; scored to give Social Age (SA) and Social Quotient (SQ = SA/CA x 100). Neighbours: 8 categories, Edgar Doll 1935.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a critical factor in ensuring the accuracy of differential assessment in Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD)?

opts.A: Relying solely on parental reports without observational data
opts.B: Use of a single standardised test without clinical judgment
opts.C: Ignoring co-occurring conditions during the assessment process
opts.D: Comprehensive training of assessors in ASD-specific diagnostic tools and protocols

qs.sol: Differential assessment depends on assessors trained to use ASD-specific tools and protocols alongside clinical judgment. “Use of a single standardised test without clinical judgment” does not fit: one test without judgment cannot establish a careful differential assessment.
qs.rel: ABA (Lovaas) is a commonly recommended evidence-based approach for ASD communication and behaviour. Neighbours: DTT, PRT, TEACCH, PECS, social stories, speech therapy.

qs.stem: Proper application of content knowledge is evident when the teacher:

opts.A: gives a lot of home assignments
opts.C: transforms the subject matter in such a way that it reaches the students

qs.sol:
Concept: Effective teaching requires more than possessing subject-matter (content) knowledge alone — it requires Pedagogical Content Knowledge (PCK): the ability to transform that content, through analogies, representations, examples, and sequencing, into a form that is accessible and meaningful to learners at their level of understanding (Shulman, 1987).

Application: The stem asks which teacher behaviour demonstrates "proper application of content knowledge" in practice. The option stating that the teacher "transforms the subject matter in such a way that it reaches the students" directly describes this act of reshaping content for learner accessibility — the defining feature of PCK. …
qs.rel: Children with intellectual disability benefit from rich language models, encouragement and multisensory practice. Neighbours: repetition, visual supports, functional vocabulary.

qs.stem:
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given.

The concept of “quality” is:

opts.D: As per norms of the society

qs.sol: Quality is an evaluative perception and can differ between individuals. It is not an invariant property shared by all observers.
qs.rel: Differential assessment in ASD needs trained assessors and multi-source evidence. Neighbours: differentiating from intellectual disability, language disorder, hearing loss.

qs.stem: Which of the following thing(s) a teacher should do consciously to avoid gender bias and to promote gender equality? I. They must use gender-neutral language and encourage children also to do so. II. Teacher may avoid assigning gendered jobs.
qs.sol: Using gender-neutral language avoids stereotyping pupils through words. Avoiding gender-assigned classroom jobs prevents role expectations from restricting participation. Both teacher actions promote equity.
qs.rel: Perceptual-motor assessment covers visual perception and visual-motor integration, body awareness, balance. Neighbours: Beery VMI, Frostig test, Bender-Gestalt.

qs.stem: Which of the following is an essential area to consider when assessing perceptual motor skills?

opts.A: Visual perception and visual motor integration
opts.D: Ability in music and sound patterns

qs.sol: “Visual perception and visual motor integration” covers how a learner interprets visual input and coordinates it with movement, both central to perceptual motor assessment. “Ability in music and sound patterns” concerns auditory or musical processing rather than this visual-motor coordination.
qs.rel: Multisensory structured language instruction (Orton-Gillingham) is effective for reading difficulties like dyslexia. Neighbours: phonics, fluency practice, assistive text-to-speech.

qs.stem: ‘Make room for shared experiences.’ Which of the following statement is correct regarding the given statement? I. They are an invaluable source of language work. II. They create an atmosphere of involvement and togetherness.
qs.sol: Invaluable means extremely valuable or useful; it does not mean valueless. Shared experiences give learners common events to describe, question and discuss, providing rich material for language work. Shared events also encourage participation, involvement and togetherness. Thus both I and II apply.
qs.rel: Visual aids and structured visual supports are strongly recommended for ASD. Neighbours: TEACCH, PECS, visual schedules, social stories, routine.

qs.sol: In the older classification used by this question, an educable child was assigned the IQ band 50 to 70. “20 to 49” belongs to a lower historical IQ band and therefore does not fit the paper’s educable category.
qs.rel: Older classification of intellectual disability: educable children had IQ about 50-70, trainable about 30-50 (some texts 20-49), custodial below that. Neighbours: ICD-10 mild 50-69, moderate 35-49; AAIDD support-based model; Binet-Simon.

qs.stem: 'Imbecile' is/was the term that was used for people with mental disabilities in:
qs.sol: 'Imbecile' is an obsolete and offensive historical label that was used in older classifications for people with intellectual or mental disabilities. In the given exam context, it is associated with the late 18th-century period, not with present-day respectful terminology. Hence the correct option is late 18th century.
qs.rel: 'Imbecile' was a historical clinical term (late 18th-19th century onward) for moderate mental deficiency; others: idiot (profound), moron (mild). Neighbours: now intellectual disability; IQ bands.

qs.sol: “ध्वन्यात्मक जागरूकता और शब्दावली का सीमित संपर्क” सही है, क्योंकि श्रवण संकेतों तक सीमित पहुँच कुछ विद्यार्थियों के लिए ध्वन्यात्मक जागरूकता और नई शब्दावली सीखने के अवसर घटा सकती है। “सांके तिक भाषा अधिगम में कठिनाई” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि सांकेतिक भाषा सीखने में कठिनाई श्रवण क्षति का अनिवार्य परिणाम नहीं है और बताई गई साक्षरता चुनौती को सीधे नहीं समझाती।
qs.rel: Limited exposure to phonological awareness and vocabulary hampers early reading, an indicator in dyslexia risk. Neighbours: phonemic awareness, decoding, rapid naming.

qs.stem: What is the main objective of craft activities for persons with mental retardation in special education centres?

opts.C: Keep them busy in recreational activity

qs.sol: Craft activities can keep learners engaged in recreation and give them opportunities to practise practical skills. “Train them in modern technologies” is a narrower specialised training goal than ordinary craft engagement.
qs.rel: Craft activities for persons with ID build fine motor, vocational and recreational skills and keep them engaged. Neighbours: sheltered workshops, pre-vocational training.

qs.stem: When assessing basic curricular skills (e.g., literacy/numeracy) for students with disabilities, which practice is most essential?

opts.A: Providing individualised accommodations (e.g., extra time, assistive tools or alternative formats)
opts.B: Exempting students with disabilities from assessments to reduce stress
opts.C: Using the same standardised test for all students to ensure fairness
opts.D: Focusing only on non-academic skills like social behaviour

qs.sol: “Providing individualised accommodations (e.g., extra time, assistive tools or alternative formats)” helps students show their literacy or numeracy skills through an accessible assessment. “Using the same standardised test for all students to ensure fairness” may measure access barriers instead of the intended skill when necessary accommodations are withheld.
qs.rel: Individualised accommodations are essential when assessing basic skills of students with disabilities. Neighbours: extra time, scribes, alternative formats, CBSE concessions.

qs.stem: What is the primary purpose of the Infant-Toddler Checklist in autism spectrum disorder assessment?

opts.A: To screen for early communication and social delays

qs.sol: The Infant-Toddler Checklist is a screening tool for early communication and social delays, not a definitive autism diagnosis. “To diagnose autism definitively” does not fit: a screening checklist cannot establish a definitive diagnosis.
qs.rel: Infant-Toddler Checklist (CSBS) screens early communication and social behaviour for ASD. Neighbours: M-CHAT-R (16-30 months), Q-CHAT, ADOS.

qs.sol: “Fragile X syndrome” is an inherited condition often associated with intellectual and learning difficulties, matching the developmental and cognitive effects in the question. “Turner syndrome” is also genetic, but it is not the condition chiefly identified here by this pattern of cognitive impairment.
qs.rel: Fragile X syndrome is an inherited (X-linked) cause of intellectual disability and autism features. Neighbours: Down syndrome (trisomy 21), PKU, Rett syndrome, Prader-Willi.

qs.stem: In designing a prosthetic classroom environment for children with multiple disabilities, which of the following best describes the use of a standing frame?

opts.A: A tool for upper limb therapy and writing practice
opts.B: An aid to reduce muscle tone and promote engagement in classroom activities
opts.C: A safety device to prevent falls during recess
opts.D: A support for napping during breaks

qs.sol: A standing frame supports upright positioning, helps manage muscle tone and allows classroom participation. “A tool for upper limb therapy and writing practice” does not describe a frame that positions the body upright for participation.
qs.rel: For multiple disabilities, positioning/adaptive aids reduce muscle tone and promote engagement. Neighbours: occupational and physiotherapy, adaptive seating, AAC.

qs.sol: “autism” is correct: TEACCH is a structured support model developed for autistic people and their needs across ages. “mild ID” fails: Mild intellectual disability may coexist with autism, but it is not the defining population named by TEACCH.
qs.rel: TEACCH (Division TEACCH, University of North Carolina) is a structured teaching programme for autism. Neighbours: visual structure, work systems, physical organisation, routines.

qs.sol: इस चेकलिस्ट के दिए गए डोमेन में सामाजिक, मनोरंजनात्मक और व्यक्तिगत क्षेत्र आते हैं; संवेगात्मक क्षेत्र अलग पाँचवाँ डोमेन नहीं है। “सामाजिक (Social)” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि सामाजिक व्यवहार मूल्यांकन का एक क्षेत्र है।
qs.rel: Adaptive behaviour checklists assess social, recreational and personal domains. Neighbours: Vineland, AAMR adaptive behaviour scale, functional assessment.

qs.stem: In DSM-5, which of the following disorders were merged under the single term autism spectrum disorder?

opts.A: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, Asperger’s, Rett syndrome
opts.C: Asperger’s, Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, Communication disorder
opts.D: Autistic disorder, Asperger’s disorder, PDD-NOS, Childhood disintegrative disorder

qs.sol: DSM-5 brought autistic disorder, Asperger’s disorder, PDD-NOS and childhood disintegrative disorder under autism spectrum disorder. “Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, Asperger’s, Rett syndrome” does not fit: aDHD and Rett syndrome are not both included in the DSM-5 autism spectrum grouping.
qs.rel: DSM-5 (2013) merged autistic disorder, Asperger's disorder and PDD-NOS into ASD, with two domains: social communication, and restricted repetitive behaviours. Neighbours: severity levels 1-3.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a cognitive implication often observed in children with multiple disabilities, as related to functional limitations?

opts.A: Need for footrests in corner sitting
opts.D: Tendency to forget skills through disuse

qs.sol: A cognitive effect of limited practice is forgetting a skill through disuse. “Presence of primitive reflexes” is a neurological or motor sign, not the cognitive loss of a skill from insufficient use.
qs.rel: Children with multiple disabilities may forget skills through disuse and need repeated practice. Neighbours: functional curriculum, generalisation difficulties, routines.

qs.stem: Frequent use of gestures and delayed speech may indicate an issue related to which of the following?
qs.sol:
Concept: In early-childhood developmental screening, different sensory and cognitive impairments produce characteristic — and different — combinations of behavioural signs. Identifying the likely area of concern means matching the exact combination of signs described to the domain whose typical presentation best fits it.

Application: Here, the child shows two signs together — increased use of gestures and delayed onset of speech. …
qs.rel: Gesturing with delayed speech may indicate a hearing problem (or language/ASD concern). Neighbours: audiometry, OAE, BERA, early identification.

qs.stem:
Identify from the given list the correct option.

Which of the following is a behavioural characteristic of mentally retarded individual?
qs.sol: The keyed behavioural characteristic is difficulty showing age-appropriate social behaviour across situations. The paper uses dated terminology, retained in the printed stem.
qs.rel: Mental retardation is characterised by immaturity in social situations and limited adaptive behaviour. Neighbours: AAIDD, Vineland, IQ bands.

qs.sol: “ADHD/ADD से पीड़ित बच्चों में अक्सर अर्थक्रियात्मक भाषायी न्यूनता होती है, जिसमें वार्तालाप के दौरान बारी-बारी से बोलने और टॉपिक में सुसंगतता बनाए रखने में कठिनाई होती है।” सही है, क्योंकि ध्यान और आत्मनियमन की कठिनाइयाँ बातचीत में बारी लेने तथा विषय पर बने रहने जैसे व्यावहारिक भाषा कौशल को प्रभावित कर सकती हैं। “ADHD/ADD केवल शारीरिक अतिसक्रियता को प्रभावित करता है, न कि संचार को।” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि केवल शारीरिक अतिसक्रियता तक प्रभाव सीमित मानना गलत है, क्योंकि संचार में ध्यान और सामाजिक उपयोग भी शामिल हैं।
qs.rel: ADHD/ADD children often show functional language deficits in organisation and pragmatics. Neighbours: executive function, inattention, working memory.

qs.sol: “Q-CHAT” सही है, क्योंकि Q-CHAT में ऑटिस्टिक विशेषताओं की आवृत्ति या तीव्रता पर आधारित अंकन से मात्रात्मक स्कोर बनाया जाता है। “M-CHAT” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि M-CHAT का मूल ढाँचा हाँ/नहीं प्रतिक्रियाओं वाली स्क्रीनिंग है, इसलिए वह यहाँ अपेक्षित क्रमिक अंकन का उदाहरण नहीं है।
qs.rel: Q-CHAT (Quantitative Checklist for Autism in Toddlers) measures frequency/intensity of autistic traits. Neighbours: M-CHAT, CHAT, screening age 18-24 months.

qs.sol:
अवधारणा

अशाब्दिक अधिगम नि:शक्तता (NVLD) में भाषा-आधारित क्षमता के साथ दृश्य-स्थानिक प्रसंस्करण, मोटर समन्वय और गैर-मौखिक सामाजिक संकेतों की समझ में कठिनाई का पैटर्न देखा जाता है। यह अवधारणा किसी एक अलग लक्षण के बजाय इन क्षेत्रों के संयुक्त प्रभाव पर आधारित है।

अनुप्रयोग

दिए गए वर्णन में दृश्य-स्थानिक कठिनाइयाँ, मोटर समन्वय में समस्या और शारीरिक भाषा समझने में परेशानी तीनों एक साथ हैं। इसलिए यह NVLD के संयुक्त गैर-मौखिक प्रोफ़ाइल का वर्णन करता है।

तुलना

आलंकारिक भाषा और सामाजिक सूक्ष्मभेद: सामाजिक-भाषिक कठिनाई का संकेत देता है, पर दृश्य-स्थानिक और मोटर घटक नहीं बताता।

ध्वनिपरक प्रसंस्करण और डिकोडिंग: पढ़ने से जुड़े ध्वनि-भाषिक कौशल पर केंद्रित है।

संगीत और लय की श्रवण स्मृति: श्रवण स्म …
qs.rel: NVLD: strong verbal skills with deficits in visual-spatial, motor and social perception. Neighbours: dyslexia (language-based LD), dyscalculia, dysgraphia.

qs.sol: “पर्वेसिव डेवलपमेंटल डिसऑर्डर नॉट अदरवाइज़ स्पेसिफाइड (Pervasive developmental disorder not otherwise specified - PDD-NOS)” सही है, क्योंकि PDD-NOS पूर्व निदान श्रेणी थी जिसे DSM-5 के व्यापक ऑटिज़्म स्पेक्ट्रम विकार निदान में समाहित किया गया। “बाइपोलर डिसऑर्डर (Bipolar disorder)” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि बाइपोलर डिसऑर्डर मनोदशा से जुड़ी अलग नैदानिक श्रेणी है, उसे ऑटिज़्म स्पेक्ट्रम में समाहित नहीं किया गया।
qs.rel: PDD-NOS (pervasive developmental disorder not otherwise specified) was an older category folded into ASD in DSM-5. Neighbours: Rett disorder, childhood disintegrative disorder.

qs.sol: “तीव्रता के स्तरों में भिन्नता” सही है, क्योंकि ऑटिज़्म स्पेक्ट्रम में सहायता की आवश्यकताएँ और कठिनाइयों की तीव्रता व्यक्ति-व्यक्ति में बदलती हैं, इसलिए संज्ञानात्मक क्षमता भी एक जैसी मानना उचित नहीं है। “केवल संचार समस्या” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि इसे केवल संचार समस्या कहना व्यवहार, संवेदनात्मक अनुभव और व्यक्ति की भिन्न क्षमताओं की पूरी तस्वीर नहीं देता।
qs.rel: Autism is a spectrum: variation in severity and intensity of symptoms. Neighbours: levels 1-3 of support, Asperger's as high-functioning, early signs.

qs.sol: “ये संदर्भ-विशिष्ट व्यवहारों और पर्यावरणीय कारकों की उपेक्षा कर सकते हैं।” सही है, क्योंकि केवल मानकीकृत परीक्षण लेने से बच्चे का अलग-अलग परिस्थितियों में व्यवहार तथा परिवेश का प्रभाव छूट सकता है। “ये सूक्ष्म सामाजिक व्यवहारों को प्रभावी ढंग से ग्रहण करते हैं।” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि यह कहना कि ऐसे परीक्षण सूक्ष्म सामाजिक व्यवहारों को प्रभावी ढंग से पकड़ते हैं, प्रत्यक्ष अवलोकन और संदर्भ-आधारित जानकारी की जरूरत को अनदेखा करता है।
qs.rel: Reducing behaviour to a single cause ignores context-specific behaviours and environment; functional analysis considers setting. Neighbours: ABC chart, positive behaviour supports.

qs.sol: “व्यापक विकासात्मक और कार्यात्मक निर्धारण” सही है, क्योंकि व्यापक विकासात्मक और कार्यात्मक आकलन बच्चे के विकास-इतिहास, व्यवहार और दैनिक कामकाज को कई संदर्भों में देखता है। “कक्षा शिक्षक द्वारा किया गया नैदानिक परीक्षण” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि कक्षा शिक्षक का अवलोकन उपयोगी सूचना दे सकता है, पर उसके द्वारा अकेले किया गया नैदानिक परीक्षण पूर्ण मूल्यांकन नहीं है।
qs.rel: Comprehensive developmental and functional assessment evaluates all domains. Neighbours: multidisciplinary team, ISAA, adaptive behaviour, IEP planning.

qs.sol: “खाने के कौशल” सही है, क्योंकि प्लेट से भोजन उठाकर मुँह तक ले जाने में नेत्र-हाथ समन्वय स्वयं भोजन करने की क्रिया का हिस्सा है। “खाद्य तैयारी के कौशल” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि खाद्य तैयारी के कौशल भोजन बनाने से संबंधित हैं, तैयार भोजन खाने की इस क्रिया से नहीं।
qs.rel: Self-feeding skills (picking food from plate to mouth) depend on fine motor, eye-hand coordination; part of daily living skills training. Neighbours: dressing, toileting, task analysis.

qs.sol: “प्रबल स्मृति प्रतिधारण” न्यूनतम मस्तिष्क दुष्क्रिया से सामान्यतः जुड़ी कठिनाई का संकेत नहीं है। “अतिसक्रियता” जैसी गतिविधि और व्यवहार-नियमन की कठिनाई इससे जुड़ सकती है, इसलिए वह यहाँ अपवाद नहीं है।
qs.rel: Strong memory retention is not typical of minimal brain dysfunction; it presents with attention, perceptual and learning problems. Neighbours: ADHD, hyperactivity, soft neurological signs.

qs.sol: “स्पष्टीकरण और भावमूलक अभिव्यक्ति के साथ समूह सस्वर पाठ” में उच्चारण और लय से छंद सुनाई देता है तथा भावपूर्ण प्रस्तुति और स्पष्टीकरण से रस समझने में सहायता मिलती है। “विद्यार्थियों द्वारा मौन पठन” अर्थ ग्रहण में उपयोगी हो सकता है, पर केवल मौन पढ़ने से लय और सामूहिक भावाभिव्यक्ति का अनुभव सीमित रहता है।
qs.rel: Group choral reading with clarification and expressive emotion builds speech clarity and confidence for children with speech difficulties. Neighbours: articulation therapy, fluency, voice.

qs.sol: “वाक् , सामाजिक अंतःक्रिया और प्रतिबंधित व्यवहार में विलंब” सामाजिक संचार और अंतःक्रिया की कठिनाइयों के साथ सीमित या दोहराव वाले व्यवहार की ओर संकेत करता है। “मोटर समन्वय संबंधी समस्याओं” कुछ बच्चों में साथ हो सकता है, लेकिन अपने आप में ऑटिज़्म स्पेक्ट्रम का मुख्य पहचान-लक्षण नहीं है।
qs.rel: Delays in speech, social interaction and restricted behaviours define ASD triad. Neighbours: Wing's triad, DSM-5 two domains, early signs by 12-18 months.

qs.sol: प्रतिक्रिया लागत में “चेतावनी देना, परेशान करना या धमकी देना” बच्चे के लिए अपमानजनक या भय पैदा करने वाला हो सकता है और सीखने के लक्ष्य से ध्यान हटाता है। “नियमों का सुसंगत प्रवर्तन” नियमों को पूर्वानुमेय बनाता है, इसलिए उचित और शांत ढंग से लागू होने पर उपयोगी है।
qs.rel: Response cost removes a reinforcer (tokens/privileges) for misbehaviour; warning or threatening is not response cost. Neighbours: time-out, extinction, token economy, differential reinforcement.

qs.sol: “शाब्दिक संकेतों से शुरू करना और ज़रूरत पड़ने पर सहायता बढ़ाना” कम सहायता वाले संकेत से शुरू कर जरूरत के अनुसार अधिक प्रत्यक्ष सहायता देने की क्रमिक विधि बताता है। “पहले शारीरिक सहायता का उपयोग करना और फिर हावभावों में मंद होना (fading)” पहले अधिकतम शारीरिक सहायता देकर उसे घटाता है, जो विपरीत दिशा का क्रम है।
qs.rel: Least-to-most prompting begins with verbal cues and increases help as needed (prompt hierarchy). Neighbours: most-to-least prompting, fading, errorless learning, chaining.

qs.sol: DTT के चार चरण संकेत, प्रतिक्रिया, परिणाम और विराम हैं; इस क्रम में प्रत्येक छोटे लक्ष्य पर अभ्यास किया जाता है। “संकेत (cue) → प्रतिक्रिया (response) → विराम (pause) → परिणाम (consequence)” में विराम को परिणाम से पहले रखा गया है, जबकि प्रतिक्रिया के बाद परिणाम देकर फिर विराम आता है।
qs.rel: DTT (discrete trial training) has four steps: cue/antecedent, response, consequence, pause (inter-trial interval). Neighbours: ABA, Lovaas, reinforcement, prompting.

qs.stem: Which of the following curricular adaptations is most effective in addressing the sensory processing challenges faced by children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in inclusive classrooms?

opts.A: Eliminating social interaction activities to avoid overstimulation
opts.B: Replacing all group activities with independent seatwork
opts.C: Reducing academic content to the lowest grade level available
opts.D: Providing sensory breaks and using multi-sensory instructional methods

qs.sol: Sensory breaks and multisensory teaching can reduce overload while preserving access to learning. “Replacing all group activities with independent seatwork” does not fit: replacing every group activity removes inclusive opportunities.
qs.rel: Sensory breaks and multisensory approaches address sensory processing challenges in ASD. Neighbours: sensory integration therapy, noise reduction, quiet corner.

qs.stem: Which of the following conditions is most accurately associated with both genetic and prenatal etiological factors contributing to developmental disabilities?
qs.sol: Down syndrome is associated with chromosomal factors; prenatal factors such as maternal age affect risk. “Fetal Alcohol Syndrome” does not fit: fetal alcohol syndrome is linked to prenatal alcohol exposure but is not a genetic chromosomal condition.
qs.rel: Down syndrome (trisomy 21) shows genetic origin with prenatal contributions to intellectual disability. Neighbours: Fragile X, PKU, maternal rubella, fetal alcohol, anoxia at birth.

qs.stem: Which assessment method is most effective for evaluating a child’s functional communication skills in everyday settings?

opts.D: Parent and teacher interviews combined with naturalistic observation

qs.sol: Functional communication assessment draws on family and teacher interviews together with naturalistic observation in everyday settings. “Standardised language tests only” does not fit: a standardised language test alone misses everyday use in context.
qs.rel: Functional communication is best assessed through parent and teacher interviews plus natural observation. Neighbours: ecological assessment, checklists, language sample.

qs.stem:
Match the following Classification Of Cognitive Disability (Mental Retardation) with their range of intelligence quotient (IQ).

Severity Levels

	

Range of IQ
qs.sol: The standard IQ ranges in the given list are: profound mental retardation below 20, mild mental retardation 50-75, and severe mental retardation 20-34. Therefore the matching is I-2, II-3, III-1.
qs.rel: Classification of ID by IQ: mild 50-69, moderate 35-49, severe 20-34, profound below 20 (ICD-10); older: moron/imbecile/idiot. Neighbours: borderline 70-85, AAIDD support-based model.

topics.deep:
- **Intellectual disability (ID):** significant limitations in intellectual functioning (IQ below ~70) and adaptive behaviour with onset before 18 years (AAIDD). ICD-10 bands: mild 50-69 (educable), moderate 35-49 (trainable), severe 20-34, profound below 20. Older labels - moron (mild), imbecile (moderate), idiot (profound) - are obsolete. Causes: Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Fragile X, PKU, Rubella, anoxia, malnutrition, lead, fetal alcohol. Teaching: real/concrete objects first, task analysis, repetition, multisensory, functional curriculum, prompting and fading, vocational training.
- **Assessment tools in India:** Vineland Social Maturity Scale (Doll 1935; Indian adaptation Malin) - **89 items, 8 domains** (self-help general, eating, dressing, locomotion, occupation, communication, self-direction, socialisation), gives SA and SQ; **BASIC-MR** (NIMH Secunderabad) - Part A basic skills, Part B behaviour; Binet and Wechsler IQ tests; Seguin form board, Bhatia battery; ISAA (autism).
- **Autism spectrum disorder (ASD):** Bleuler coined "autism" (1911); **Kanner** (1943) early infantile autism; Asperger (1944). **DSM-5 (2013)** merged autistic disorder, Asperger's and PDD-NOS into ASD with two domains: persistent social communication deficits and restricted/repetitive behaviours (levels 1-3 support). Wing's triad: social interaction, communication, imagination. Features: echolalia, hyperlexia, poor eye contact, joint-attention deficit, sensory issues, routine rigidity. Screening: **M-CHAT-R/F, Q-CHAT**, CSBS Infant-Toddler Checklist; diagnosis: ADOS, ADI-R, CARS. Interventions: **ABA** (Lovaas), **DTT** (cue, response, consequence, pause), PRT, **TEACCH** (structured teaching, visual schedules), PECS, social stories, sensory integration, speech therapy.
- **ADHD:** inattention + hyperactivity-impulsivity, onset before 12 years, types: predominantly inattentive, hyperactive-impulsive, combined. Management: behaviour therapy, structured routine, short tasks, medication under doctors; executive-function deficits.
- **Specific learning disability (SLD):** neurodevelopmental, average IQ with difficulty in reading (**dyslexia**), writing (**dysgraphia**), maths (**dyscalculia**), motor coordination (dyspraxia); NVLD = good verbal skills, weak visual-spatial/social perception. Teaching: multisensory structured language instruction (Orton-Gillingham), phonics, assistive tech, accommodations (extra time, reader/scribe - CBSE concessions). Lack of motivation is not a cause. RPwD Act lists SLD among benchmark disabilities.
- **Speech and language disorders:** receptive vs expressive language disorder; articulation (speech-sound) disorders, fluency (stuttering), voice disorders, aphasia. Delay in speech may result from hearing loss, ID, emotional/behavioural disorder, deprivation, autism.
- **Behaviour modification (Skinner-based):** ABC model (antecedent-behaviour-consequence), positive/negative reinforcement, shaping, chaining, token economy, **response cost** (removing a privilege/token), time-out, extinction, differential reinforcement, prompt hierarchy (most-to-least, least-to-most), fading, generalisation, functional behaviour analysis. Aim: increase adaptive, decrease maladaptive behaviour.
- **IEP team:** parents, special educator, general teacher, therapists, psychologist, school head; a librarian is not core. IEP content: present level, annual goals, short-term objectives, services, timeline, review.
- **Multiple disabilities and deaf-blindness:** two or more disabilities; need functional curriculum, routines, tactile cues, adaptive positioning; skills may be forgotten through disuse. Perceptual-motor assessment: visual perception, visual-motor integration, body awareness (Frostig, Bender-Gestalt, Beery VMI).
- **Screening vs diagnosis; differential assessment** needs trained assessors; curricular-skills assessment identifies learning needs; functional communication assessed via parent/teacher interviews and observation.

**Likely question angles:**
- Number of items/domains in Vineland; what BASIC-MR measures.
- IQ ranges for mild, moderate, severe, profound ID.
- Who coined "autism"; DSM-5 spectrum merger; early signs.
- Which therapy for which condition (ABA, TEACCH, PECS, OT, speech).
- Dyslexia vs dysgraphia vs dyscalculia definitions.
- Two core features of ADHD.
- Identify ABC component, reinforcement type or response cost example.
- Causes: genetic vs prenatal vs perinatal syndromes (Down, Fragile X, PKU).
- Members of IEP team.
- Teaching strategy for ID (concrete first, task analysis).

topics.title: 6. Sensory & Physical Disabilities, Braille, Sign Language & Assistive Tech
topics.theory:
- **Visual impairment:** blindness (acuity below 3/60 or field below 10 deg) vs low vision (6/18 to 3/60); Snellen chart. **Braille** (Louis Braille, 1829): 6-dot cell, 64 patterns (63 usable); Grade 2 contractions save space; slate and stylus, Perkins brailler, embosser, abacus (Cranmer), Taylor frame.
- **O&M:** long white cane (protects from obstacles, detects surface changes), sighted-guide technique (hold above elbow, guide steps ahead), upper/lower body protection. Hearing aid is not a VI device.
- **Low-vision aids:** magnifiers, telescopes, large print, reading stand, typoscope (reading guide), contrast and lighting.
- **Hearing:** RPwD Act - deaf = 70 dB or more, hard of hearing = 60-70 dB. 26-40 dB mild, 41-55 moderate, 56-70 moderately severe, 71-90 severe, 91+ profound. **OAE/BERA** test infants.
- **Communication approaches:** **oralism** (speech + lip-reading), manualism (sign), **total communication**, bilingual; **Simcom** = simultaneous communication of speech and sign. **ISL** (ISLRTC) is a natural language; ISS is manually coded Indian language.
- **Deaf-blindness** = combined hearing + vision loss; use routines, tactile cues, object calendars.
- **Cerebral palsy:** spastic/athetoid/ataxic; hemiplegia (one side), diplegia (legs), quadriplegia; orthotics, pommel, adaptive seating, avoid W-sitting; botulinum toxin + physiotherapy for spasticity.
- **AAC** (Augmentative and Alternative Communication): symbols represent objects, actions, concepts, emotions; scanning access; team = user, family, SLP, teacher.
- Assistive-technology planning starts with **need assessment**; e-classrooms need captions/sign interpretation.
- Astigmatism = uneven focusing; orthosis supports, prosthesis replaces.

qs.sol: शिक्षार्थी-केंद्रित पाठ्यचर्या विद्यार्थियों की वर्तमान जीवन आवश्यकताओं और विकासात्मक चरणों के अनुसार अनुभव चुनती है। “भविष्य की परीक्षाओं की तैयारी” एक सीमित परीक्षा लक्ष्य है, इसलिए वह इसका सबसे सीधा आधार नहीं है।
qs.rel: Adjustable reading stand positions print comfortably for children with low vision or physical disability, improving access to print. Neighbours: magnifiers, large print, closed-circuit TV (CCTV), good lighting.

qs.stem:
लैंगिक भेदभाव परिवार से शुरू होता है और विभिन्न स्थानों तक फैलता है। निम्नलिखित में से वे स्थान कौन-से हैं?

I. पुलिस स्टेशन

II. नौकरी के लिए नियुक्ति

III. कार्यस्थल
qs.sol: लैंगिक भेदभाव सबसे पहले परिवार में बेटों और बेटियों के साथ असमान व्यवहार से सीखा जाता है और फिर सार्वजनिक संस्थाओं तक पहुँचता है। पुलिस स्टेशनों में महिलाओं को अक्सर पक्षपात झेलना पड़ता है, जहाँ उत्पीड़न या घरेलू हिंसा की शिकायतों की अनदेखी या असंवेदनशील व्यवहार हो सकता है। नौकरी की नियुक्ति में उन्हें नज़रअंदाज़ किया जा सकता है या कम वेतन दिया जा सकता है। कार्यस्थल पर उन्हें असमान वेतन, उत्पीड़न और पदोन्नति रोकने वाली अदृश्य बाधा का सामना करना पड़ सकता है। इसलिए बताए गए तीनों स्थान ऐसे भेदभाव के क्षेत्र हैं।
qs.rel: Braille embosser prints Braille hard copy from digital text; transcribers convert print to Braille. Neighbours: Perkins brailler, Braille slate and stylus, refreshable Braille display, Louis Braille 1829.

qs.stem:
Art education is the area of learning that is based upon which of the following?
I. The visual, tangible art
II. The performing arts
qs.sol: Art education includes both visual/tangible arts and performing arts. Therefore both statements I and II are correct. Printed order: Only I; Only II; Both I and II; Neither I nor II. The stored option order stays fixed because this question has test usage.
qs.rel: Deafness = profound, congenital/irreversible hearing loss (above 90 dB); hard of hearing = partial. Neighbours: RPwD Act 2016: deaf = 70 dB or more, hard of hearing = 60-70 dB; audiometry.

qs.stem: How can a teacher use the results from the BASIC-MR scale?

opts.D: To design an IEP and group teaching plans

qs.sol: BASIC-MR results identify strengths and needs that a teacher can use to design an individual education plan and group teaching. “To measure IQ levels only” does not fit: the scale informs adaptive and educational planning, not IQ measurement alone.
qs.rel: Closed captions and sign language interpretation make e-classrooms accessible to learners with hearing impairment. Neighbours: transcripts, visual alerts, WCAG accessibility, ISL.

qs.stem: How can a teacher use the results from the BASIC-MR scale?

opts.D: To design an IEP and group teaching plans

qs.sol: BASIC-MR results identify strengths and needs that a teacher can use to design an individual education plan and group teaching. “To measure IQ levels only” does not fit: the scale informs adaptive and educational planning, not IQ measurement alone.
qs.rel: Deaf-blindness = combined hearing and vision impairment (e.g. Helen Keller); needs tactile communication and routine. Neighbours: tactile sign, calendars, object cues, Sense International India.

qs.stem: Why is early identification important for children with visual impairment?

opts.A: It delays the start of intervention
opts.B: It helps provide timely support and intervention
opts.C: It only focuses on medical treatment
opts.D: It reduces the need for any assistance later

qs.sol: Early identification allows timely intervention and support for a child with visual impairment. “It only focuses on medical treatment” is too narrow because early identification also enables educational and developmental intervention.
qs.rel: Early identification of visual impairment enables timely intervention, aids and development support. Neighbours: screening, low-vision assessment, early intervention up to 6 years.

qs.stem: किस रंग को पौरुष माना जाता है?
qs.sol: प्रश्न में मानी गई पारंपरिक लैंगिक रूढ़ि में नीले रंग को पौरुष से जोड़ा जाता है।
qs.rel: American Sign Language (ASL) is a natural language with grammar; ISL is the Indian sign language (ISLRTC set up 2015). Neighbours: BSL, Auslan, finger spelling.

qs.stem:
Which of the following are the strategies to enhance the motivation level of the learners?
I. Build on strengths first
II. Offer choices
III. Facilitate creativity
IV. Provide a secure environment
qs.sol: Motivation grows when teachers begin with learners' strengths, allow meaningful choices, support creative work and provide a secure classroom. Strength based success builds confidence; choice gives ownership; creativity encourages expression; safety makes participation less threatening. None of the four strategies in the question undermines motivation, so the inclusive combination is justified. All four supports, including strength building and creativity, can increase motivation. Excluding statements I and III ignores the motivating effect of early success and creative work. Leaving out strengths ignores the confidence gained from early success. …
qs.rel: Reading guide (typoscope) helps low-vision readers track lines. Neighbours: magnifier, hand-held vs stand, large print, contrast.

qs.stem: RTE अधिनियम विशेष आवश्यकता वाले बच्चों सहित ____ वर्ष आयु वर्ग के बच्चों को मुफ्त और अनिवार्य शिक्षा के बच्चों के अधिकार का प्रावधान करता है।
qs.sol: RTE अधिनियम विशेष आवश्यकता वाले बच्चों सहित 6 से 14 वर्ष आयु को कवर करता है।
qs.rel: Hearing loss levels: 26-40 dB mild, 41-55 moderate, 56-70 moderately severe, 71-90 severe, 91+ profound. Neighbours: audiometer, pure tone audiometry, hearing aid candidacy.

qs.stem: In which year was EDUSAT launched?
qs.sol: “2004” is supported: EDUSAT, India’s dedicated educational satellite, was launched in 2004. By contrast, “2001” 2001 predates the EDUSAT launch.
qs.rel: Augmentative communication devices help students select symbols or generate speech when speech is difficult. Neighbours: low-tech (boards), high-tech (SGDs), PECS.

qs.stem: Which of the following combination is correct? I. Intrinsic Motivation – Preparing any project in science/mathematics may give pleasure to the pupil as a result of which he/she is motivated to undertake similar activities on his/her own. II. Extrinsic Motivation – Rewards like money and grades.
qs.sol: Intrinsic motivation comes from within the learner: the activity is rewarding in itself. A pupil who enjoys preparing a science or mathematics project and therefore takes up similar activities on her own is intrinsically motivated, so pair I is correct. Extrinsic motivation comes from outside the activity, in the form of rewards or to avoid punishment, such as money, grades, prizes or praise, so pair II is correct. Both combinations are correct.
qs.rel: AAC symbols can represent objects, actions, concepts and emotions (e.g. Blissymbols, PCS). Neighbours: unaided (gestures) vs aided (boards), scanning access.

qs.stem:
_____ is the first step for learning a language.
 I. Speaking
 II. Listening
qs.sol:
Concept — A language is made up of four skills that develop in a fixed order: Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing (the L-S-R-W sequence proposed by J. A. Bright). Listening and reading are receptive skills, used to take language in; speaking and writing are productive skills, used to send language out. Acquisition is input-driven, so a receptive skill must always be established before the matching productive skill can appear.

Application — The stem offers two of those four skills: Speaking, the productive oral skill, and Listening, the receptive aural skill. In the L-S-R-W sequence Listening occupies position 1 and Speaking position 2. …
qs.rel: A blindfold simulates total blindness in O&M training so that sighted trainers or low-vision learners use non-visual cues. Neighbours: cane techniques, sighted guide, orientation vs mobility.

qs.stem: कार्यभार का मुख्य उद्देश्य _____ का मूल्यांकन करना है।
qs.sol: कार्यभार मुख्यतः यह जाँचता है कि छात्र विषयवस्तु को कितना समझता और लागू करता है।
qs.rel: ISL/ISS in the classroom improves conceptual understanding for deaf learners. Neighbours: ISL has own grammar, ISS is manually coded Indian languages, bilingual-bicultural approach.

qs.stem: Linguistic diversity in Indian classrooms can be addressed effectively by:

opts.A: Enforcing a single language of instruction strictly.

qs.sol: Linguistic diversity is best addressed through multilingual strategies that value and use learners' languages instead of suppressing them.
qs.rel: Braille contractions (grade 2) save space and increase reading speed. Neighbours: Grade 1 uncontracted, six-dot cell, 63 combinations, Nemeth code for maths.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन संकलनात्मक निर्धारण की एक विशेषता है?

opts.A: इसे पाठ्यक्रम के अंतिम चरण में उपयोग किया जाता है।
opts.B: ग्रेड की ज्यादा महत्त्व नहीं हैं।
opts.D: यह छात्रों की आवश्यकताओं के अनुसार लचीला हो सकता है।

qs.sol: संकलनात्मक निर्धारण 'अधिगम का आकलन' है: इसे पाठ्यक्रम, इकाई या सत्र के अंत (अंतिम चरण) में उपलब्धि आँकने और प्रमाणित करने हेतु किया जाता है, प्रायः ग्रेड या अंकों के रूप में जिनका महत्त्व अधिक होता है। प्रक्रिया-उन्मुख होना और विद्यार्थियों की चलती आवश्यकताओं के अनुसार लचीला होना रचनात्मक निर्धारण की विशेषताएँ हैं।
qs.rel: AAC includes tools and strategies supplementing or replacing speech. Neighbours: aided/unaided, symbol-based, scanning, speech-generating devices.

qs.stem: शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009 का कौन सा अध्याय बच्चों के अधिकार के संरक्षण का प्रावधान करता है?
qs.sol: निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009 का अध्याय VI बाल अधिकार के संरक्षण से संबंधित है।
qs.rel: Low vision: remaining vision can be trained for efficient use (functional vision, optical aids). Neighbours: visual acuity 6/18-6/60, field of vision, RPwD Act defines low vision as <40%.

qs.stem: While teaching a children how to read, which of the following things need to be kept in mind? I. The material used must be meaningful and of the level of the child. II. The material should be in a language that the child is familiar with.
qs.sol: Reading material should match the child's level and use familiar language. Both points support early reading instruction.
qs.rel: Braille is for blind, not a low-vision aid; low-vision aids include magnifiers, large print, telescopes. Neighbours: screen magnifiers, tinted glasses, contrast sheets.

qs.stem: What is the main objective of cooperative discipline in the classroom?

opts.A: Helping students understand each other’s cooperation
opts.C: Students listening passively to the teacher

qs.sol: Cooperative discipline is a classroom-management model (most associated with Linda Albert's work building on Rudolf Dreikurs) in which teachers and students share responsibility for behaviour: rules and consequences are worked out together, and students are guided toward self-discipline through mutual respect and cooperation rather than through one-way control or compliance. …
qs.rel: Lip reading/watching facial cues is used in oral approach to supplement hearing. Neighbours: speechreading, cued speech, auditory-verbal therapy.

qs.stem: What is the first step in planning for assistive technology for a student with special needs?

opts.A: Asking the student’s friends for recommendations
opts.C: Conducting a need assessment to understand the student’s strengths and challenges
opts.D: Sending the student to a special school

qs.sol: Assistive technology planning begins by assessing the student’s abilities, needs and learning context before selecting a device. “Purchasing available devices” does not fit: buying first risks selecting a device that does not suit the learner.
qs.rel: The long cane protects from obstacles and detects surface changes in path. Neighbours: sighted guide technique, upper-body and lower-body protection, white cane day.

qs.stem: सीखना और अध्यापन के पाठ्यक्रम में सीखने के किन दृष्टिकोणों पर चर्चा की गई है?
qs.sol: सीखने और अध्यापन को समझने के लिए मनोवैज्ञानिक तथा सामाजिक-सांस्कृतिक, दोनों दृष्टिकोण उपयोगी हैं। पहला ध्यान, स्मृति, प्रेरणा और संज्ञानात्मक विकास जैसे व्यक्ति के भीतर होने वाले परिवर्तनों को देखता है। दूसरा भाषा, परिवार, साथियों और संस्कृति के साथ सहभागिता को महत्व देता है। पाठ्यक्रम में सीखना केवल किसी एक अध्यापन विधि या सक्रियता का नाम नहीं है। भौतिक विज्ञान एक विषय है, सीखने का समग्र दृष्टिकोण नहीं। प्रश्न बहुवचन 'किन दृष्टिकोणों' में दो पूरक विचारधाराओं का संयुक्त उत्तर माँगता है।
qs.rel: Simcom = simultaneous communication of speech and sign in total communication. Neighbours: total communication, oralism, manualism, bilingual approach.

qs.stem:
Which of the following pre-number concepts can be developed in children during the pre-school years?
 Statements:
 I. Matching
 II. Sorting
 III. Comparing
qs.sol: Matching, sorting and comparing are pre-number concepts that can be developed during the preschool years.
qs.rel: Braille cell: 6 dots in 2 columns and 3 rows; 63 combinations. Neighbours: Perkins brailler, slate and stylus, Grade 2.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is a key principle in creating an inclusive school for children

with special needs?

opts.A: Keeping children with special needs in separate classrooms
opts.C: Fostering an environment where all students learn together
opts.D: Providing special services only outside of school hours

qs.sol:
Concept: Inclusive education, as defined under India's Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (Section 2(m)) and by frameworks such as UNICEF, is an education system in which children with and without disabilities are educated together in the same classrooms and schools, with teaching, curriculum, and support adapted to the full range of learner needs, rather than separating students by ability or disability status.

Application: The option describing a shared environment where all students learn together directly reflects this principle: it centers the school's design on joint participation and common instructional spaces rather than on separation by need. …
qs.rel: First step in planning assistive technology is need assessment of the student, environment and tasks. Neighbours: SETT framework, trial use, training, review.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी अधिगम शैली, नई जानकारी को समझने के लिए छवियों, मानचित्रों और ग्राफिक ऑर्गनाइज़रों को प्राथमिकता देती है?
qs.sol:
अवधारणा: शिक्षा मनोविज्ञान में प्रचलित VARK मॉडल के अनुसार अधिगम शैलियों (learning styles) को चार व्यापक श्रेणियों में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है — श्रवणात्मक (Auditory: बोली और सुनी गई जानकारी, चर्चा एवं व्याख्यान), दृश्य (Visual: चित्र, आरेख, ग्राफ एवं स्थानिक निरूपण-प्रणालियाँ), वाचन/लेखन वरीयता (Reading/Writing: लिखित शब्द, सूचियाँ एवं पाठ्य-सामग्री), और गतिसंवेदी (Kinesthetic: प्रत्यक्ष अनुभव, गतिविधि एवं व्यावहारिक अभ्यास)। प्रत्येक शैली सूचना ग्रहण करने और समझने की भिन्न वरीयता को दर्शाती है।

अनुप्रयोग: प्रश्न में वर्णित विशेषता — नई जानकारी को समझने के लिए छवियों, मानचित्रों और ग्राफिक ऑर्गनाइज़रों को प्राथमिकता देना — ठीक दृश्य (Visual) अधिगम शैली की परिभाषित पहचान है, क्योंकि यह शैली स …
qs.rel: ISL is a natural language with own grammar; ISS is a manually coded form of spoken Indian languages. Neighbours: ISLRTC, bilingual education, fingerspelling.

qs.stem: Which of the following phases of teaching includes ‘Selection of appropriate methods of teaching’ ?
qs.sol:
No official answer key was published for this paper; the answer is worked out from the question.

Selection of methods occurs before the lesson is carried out.

It is part of the pre-active or planning phase, alongside selecting objectives, content and teaching aids.
qs.rel: Oralism relies on speech and visual cues such as lip reading plus amplification; manualism uses sign. Neighbours: Alexander Graham Bell (oral), Abbe de l'Epee (sign), Milan Congress 1880.

qs.stem:
Scientific argument involves three components. Which of the following are these components?
 Statements:
 I. Hypothesis
 II. Predictions
 III. The evidence
qs.sol: A scientific argument uses a hypothesis, predictions and evidence. All three listed components are part of scientific argumentation.
qs.rel: Scanning access lets AAC users select items by switch via indirect selection (linear, row-column). Neighbours: direct selection, switch access, eye-gaze.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
 I. Discrimination disregards individual need, merit and potential.
 II. Providing separate toilets for boys and girls does not tantamount to discrimination.
qs.sol: Discrimination ignores individual need, merit and potential. Separate toilets for boys and girls are a reasonable facility and do not by themselves constitute discrimination. Both statements are correct.
qs.rel: Low-vision adaptations: magnifiers, large print, good lighting, high contrast. Neighbours: not small font; Braille for blind; CCTV, screen readers.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are the role(s) of teachers in the Theme Based Integrated Early Childhood and Care Education Programme?
 Statements:
 I. Observe children to identify their interests, needs and capabilities and the pace of their development
 II. Create nurturing and positive relationships.
qs.sol: In theme-based integrated ECCE, teachers observe children to understand their interests and needs, and create nurturing positive relationships.
qs.rel: Oral motor therapy improves muscle tone and control of tongue, lips and jaw for speech and feeding. Neighbours: speech-language therapy, cerebral palsy management, feeding skills.

qs.sol: A librarian is not typically a core member of an individualised education programme team. “Parents” participate in planning goals and supports for their child, so they belong in the IEP discussion unlike the keyed occupational role.
qs.rel: Speech-generating devices produce synthesised speech for non-speaking users. Neighbours: AAC types, eye-gaze systems, text-to-speech.

qs.stem: Which of the following tests is commonly used to assess the hearing sensitivity of infants and young children who cannot respond behaviourally?
qs.sol: “Otoacoustic emissions (OAE) test” records a cochlear response to sound without requiring an infant to give a behavioural answer. “Pure-tone audiometry” ordinarily depends on a reliable response to heard tones, so it is less suitable for a child who cannot respond behaviourally.
qs.rel: OAE (otoacoustic emissions) and BERA screen infants who cannot respond behaviourally. Neighbours: pure tone audiometry (older children), play audiometry, tympanometry.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a key goal of Community-Based Employment programmes for persons with disabilities?

opts.A: Limiting access to higher education opportunities
opts.C: Encouraging complete dependence on government aid
opts.D: Facilitating gainful employment within the local community

qs.sol: Community-based employment supports paid work and participation in the person’s local community. “Encouraging complete dependence on government aid” does not fit: complete aid dependence conflicts with earning through work.
qs.rel: Middle-order expressive skills in ISL include expressing feelings and narratives. Neighbours: ISL levels, facial expression and non-manual features, signing space.

qs.stem: Which of the following co-curricular activities is not related to the motor development of students?
qs.sol: “Newspaper reading” mainly exercises reading and cognition, not bodily motor skills. “Clay modelling” develops hand and finger coordination.
qs.rel: Visual acuity = clarity of detail (6/6 normal); visual field = extent of area seen. Neighbours: Snellen chart, legal blindness 6/60, field below 10 degrees.

qs.stem: किस प्रक्रिया में समय की अवधि में छात्र के प्रदर्शन, अधिगम और समझने के प्रति व्यवहार के साक्ष्य की जांच करके निर्देशात्मक निर्णय सावधानी से किए जाते हैं? I. मूल्यांकन II. आकलन

opts.D: ना ही I ना ही II

qs.sol:
उत्तर-कुंजी पर टिप्पणी: DSSSB ने इस प्रश्नपत्र की केवल अनंतिम उत्तर-कुंजी जारी की थी, अंतिम कुंजी नहीं। अनंतिम कुंजी “I तथा II दोनों” को सही मानती है। तर्कसंगत उत्तर “केवल II” है, क्योंकि शिक्षण को दिशा देने वाला सतत साक्ष्य आकलन है, हालांकि मूल्यांकन भी उसका उपयोग कर सकता है। इस प्रश्न का मूल्यांकन अनंतिम कुंजी के अनुसार किया गया है, जैसा वास्तविक परीक्षा में हुआ।

दोनों प्रक्रियाएँ शिक्षण में मदद कर सकती हैं. यहाँ अधिगम का सतत प्रमाण जुटाना केंद्रीय है, यद्यपि मूल्यांकन भी इसका उपयोग कर सकता है।
qs.rel: Early auditory stimulation is crucial because brain plasticity is highest early, critical for language. Neighbours: early hearing detection, cochlear implant timing, aural habilitation.

qs.stem:
Choose the best option from the following.

Text books contain information about human rights, values and social norms. Thus we can call text books as:
qs.sol:
Teaching human rights, values and social norms can shape how learners act towards other people.

The official key therefore emphasizes textbooks as tools for social change.

Note on the official key: Source of information is also a defensible literal description of the printed premise. The request for the best description lets the board prefer the broader social purpose, rather than mere factual provision.
qs.rel: Voice modulation, character speech and pauses make dramatisation and reading aloud effective. Neighbours: speech therapy techniques, expression, role-play.

qs.sol: “इसमें पथ प्रदर्शक की बांह को कोहनी के ठीक ऊपर पकड़ना और एक कदम पीछे रहना शामिल है।” सही है: इस तकनीक में दृष्टिबाधित व्यक्ति मार्गदर्शक की बाँह को कोहनी के ऊपर पकड़कर उससे थोड़ा पीछे चलता है, ताकि दिशा और गति के संकेत मिलें। “इसमें मार्गदर्शन हेतु पथ प्रदर्शक कु त्ते का उपयोग किया जाता है।” सही नहीं है: पथ प्रदर्शक कुत्ते का उपयोग अलग गतिशीलता विधि है; उसमें व्यक्ति मानव मार्गदर्शक की बाँह नहीं पकड़ता।
qs.rel: Sighted guide technique: hold guide's arm above the elbow and walk one step behind. Neighbours: narrow-space technique, seating, doors.

qs.stem: If the individual has vision less than _____ after maximum correction, they are called visually impaired.
qs.sol:
Note on the answer key: DSSSB published only a provisional answer key for this paper, and no final key. The provisional key marks “6/60”, which is the graded answer here. “6/24” is also defensible, because a broader low-vision definition can count people below 6/24 as visually impaired.

The question gives no classification scheme. A visual-acuity threshold of 6/60 is used in one classification, while other schemes include less severe acuity loss within visual impairment.
qs.rel: Visual impairment: visual acuity worse than 6/18 after correction (low vision) and blindness below 3/60 (RPwD Act); the question uses 6/60. Neighbours: Snellen, field of vision, RPwD Act 2016.

qs.sol: “हस्ताकृति (Handshape)” सही है, क्योंकि हस्ताकृति हाथ की बनावट बताती है और संकेत के मैनुअल घटकों में आती है। “भौहें हिलाना (Eyebrow movement)” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि भौहें हिलाना चेहरे की अभिव्यक्ति है, इसलिए इसे गैर-मैनुअल घटक माना जाता है।
qs.rel: Handshape is a sign parameter along with location, movement, palm orientation and non-manual signals. Neighbours: ISL, Stokoe's parameters.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not an assistive device used for children with Visual Impairment?
qs.sol: Braille, arithmetic frames and abacus can support visually impaired learners. A hearing aid supports hearing impairment, not visual impairment.
qs.rel: Hearing aid is for hearing impairment, not vision. Neighbours: aids for VI: Braille writer, slate, abacus, talking books, screen readers (JAWS, NVDA).

qs.stem: Which term refers specifically to the quantification of a person's inability to hear?
qs.sol: “Hearing loss” refers to a reduction in hearing sensitivity that can be quantified through hearing assessment. “Deafness” describes a more severe hearing status but is not the general term for measuring the degree of reduced hearing.
qs.rel: Hearing loss quantifies reduced hearing (in dB); deafness is profound loss. Neighbours: hard of hearing, audiogram, hearing threshold.

qs.stem: Which term refers specifically to the quantification of a person's inability to hear?
qs.sol: “Hearing loss” refers to a reduction in hearing sensitivity that can be quantified through hearing assessment. “Deafness” describes a more severe hearing status but is not the general term for measuring the degree of reduced hearing.
qs.rel: Hearing loss is the measured inability to hear (dB HL). Neighbours: conductive, sensorineural, mixed types; congenital vs acquired.

qs.sol: A long cane detects obstacles and surface changes during independent travel by a person with visual impairment. “Spectacles” does not fit: spectacles may improve vision but are not the standard mobility aid described.
qs.rel: Long cane detects obstacles and surface changes; spectacles do not. Neighbours: Hoover cane technique, touch and slide, cane length.

qs.sol: Upper-arm and forearm protective techniques shield the upper body and head from obstacles at those heights. “the middle parts” does not fit: the middle body does not match the chest-and-head examples in this protective technique.
qs.rel: Upper-body protective technique (arm across chest) shields from obstacles at upper level; lower-body technique protects legs. Neighbours: trailing, squaring off.

qs.sol: “Using vision to identify food colours” is correct: Using sight to judge food colours is not a reliable core skill for a person with visual impairment; independent living training uses accessible cues and routines. “Developing personal grooming routines” fails: Personal grooming routines are practical daily living skills and are commonly taught.
qs.rel: Judging food colours by sight is not core for visually impaired; tactile and auditory skills used. Neighbours: self-help skills, orientation and mobility, daily living skills.

qs.stem: In braille, a new paragraph should begin at which braille cell on a new line?
qs.sol: “Third” names the braille cell where a new paragraph is conventionally indented on its new line. “First” would start flush with the margin and would not show the paragraph indentation.
qs.rel: In Braille, a new paragraph begins at the third cell on a new line (indented two cells). Neighbours: line spacing, margins, six-dot cell.

qs.sol: A pommel separates and positions the legs of a child with tightness between them. “pelvic strap” secures the pelvis to a seat but does not provide the between-leg positioning supplied by a pommel.
qs.rel: Pommel (abductor wedge) positions legs apart for children with scissoring/tightness; pelvic strap secures pelvis. Neighbours: adaptive seating for cerebral palsy.

qs.sol: “Head: Leaning over desk” is correct: Leaning the head over a desk strains the neck and undermines supported alignment, so it will not reduce postural fatigue. “Spine: Symmetrical with normal curves preserved” fails: Keeping the spine symmetrical with its normal curves supports posture and can reduce fatigue.
qs.rel: Leaning over desk strains posture; correct seating keeps head upright with supported alignment. Neighbours: adaptive furniture, foot support, CP posture management.

qs.sol: Prolonged W sitting can interfere with healthy hip and knee joint development. “It promotes excessive flexibility in the ankle.” points to a different joint and does not state the hip and knee concern of sustained W sitting.
qs.rel: Prolonged W-sitting stresses hip and knee joints and affects posture development. Neighbours: tailor sitting, tripod, posture, tightness.

qs.sol: “Botulinum toxin injections combined with physiotherapy” is correct: For focal spasticity, botulinum toxin may reduce overactive muscle activity while physiotherapy supports movement, stretching and function. “Solely occupational therapy without medical treatment” fails: Occupational therapy can help function, but using it alone does not directly address spastic muscle overactivity in the way this combined intervention can.
qs.rel: Botulinum toxin plus physiotherapy manages focal spasticity. Neighbours: orthoses, selective dorsal rhizotomy, baclofen, types of CP: spastic, athetoid, ataxic.

qs.sol: “hemiplegia” is correct: Hemiplegia affects one side of the body, matching weakness of an arm and hand on that side. “quadriplegia” fails: Quadriplegia affects all four limbs rather than just one side.
qs.rel: Hemiplegia = paralysis of one side of the body; diplegia: legs; quadriplegia: all four limbs. Neighbours: monoplegia, paraplegia, spastic CP.

qs.stem: Who are minimal essential members of an AAC team?

opts.A: The individual with the disability and their key communication partners
opts.D: The individual with the communication disability and speech-language pathologists

qs.sol: “The individual with the disability and their key communication partners” are essential because AAC choices must work for the person using them in real interactions. “The individual with the communication disability and speech-language pathologists” includes a valuable specialist, but leaves out the everyday partners who help make communication functional.
qs.rel: Minimal AAC team: the individual and their communication partners/family, plus speech-language pathologist and teacher. Neighbours: assessment, device selection, training.
