qs.sol: “वार्तालाप के दौरान वक्ता का मुख ढकना” सही है, क्योंकि वार्तालाप में वक्ता का मुख ढकने से होंठों को देखकर अर्थ निकालने का संकेत घटता है और उपलब्ध श्रवण संकेत पर ध्यान जाता है। “अतिरंजित ओष्ठ पठन का उपयोग” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि अतिरंजित ओष्ठ पठन बच्चे को दृश्य संकेतों पर अधिक निर्भर बनाता है, इसलिए वह श्रवण-केंद्रित अभ्यास के विपरीत है।
qs.rel: Covering the mouth while speaking blocks lip reading for hearing impaired students. Neighbours: face the class, good lighting, visual alerts.

qs.stem: Moving your guiding elbow towards the midline of your back is a technique used __________.
qs.sol: “in narrow spaces” is correct because the guide moves the guiding elbow toward the middle of the back so the traveller can move behind them in single file. “in doorways” may also involve a confined passage, but the elbow movement described is the general narrow-space technique rather than a doorway-specific step.
qs.rel: In narrow spaces the guide moves their elbow towards the midline of the back so the traveller follows single-file. Neighbours: sighted guide, doors, stairs.

qs.sol: “नयन संपर्क” सही है, क्योंकि नयन संपर्क सामने वाले का ध्यान और संवाद में भाग लेने की तत्परता दिखाने वाला दृश्य सामाजिक संकेत है। “वाक्य संरचना” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि वाक्य संरचना भाषायी गठन से संबंधित है, गैर-मौखिक सामाजिक संकेत से नहीं।
qs.rel: Eye contact draws attention and supports communication, especially with children with hearing impairment/ASD. Neighbours: joint attention, visual attention, gaze.

qs.sol: “दृष्टिबाधित लोगों के बीच साक्षरता के लिए भी ब्रेल आवश्यक है।” सही है, क्योंकि ब्रेल के माध्यम से दृष्टिबाधित व्यक्ति स्पर्श से स्वयं पढ़ और लिख सकता है; इस कारण वह साक्षरता का आज भी महत्त्वपूर्ण साधन है। “ऑडियो सामग्री ने ब्रेल का पूर्णतः स्थान ले लिया है।” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि ऑडियो सामग्री सुनने में मदद करती है, पर वह वर्तनी और लिखित पाठ से प्रत्यक्ष जुड़ाव सहित ब्रेल के सभी काम नहीं कर सकती।
qs.rel: Braille is essential for literacy among visually impaired people; audio alone does not replace literacy. Neighbours: Louis Braille, Braille Day 4 January.

qs.sol: “कार्यात्मक स्वतंत्रता को बढ़ाना” सही है, क्योंकि अंगोच्छेदन के बाद पुनर्वास में रोजमर्रा के काम सुरक्षित और यथासंभव स्वतंत्र रूप से कर पाना प्रमुख लक्ष्य है। “केवल सौंदर्यात्मक प्रकटन में सुधार करना” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि केवल बाहरी रूप सुधारने पर ध्यान देने से गतिशीलता और दैनिक कार्यों में भागीदारी की जरूरत पूरी नहीं होती।
qs.rel: Prosthetics and rehabilitation after amputation aim at functional independence. Neighbours: orthotics vs prosthetics, loco-motor disability in RPwD Act.

qs.sol: “यह संवेगात्मक और स्पष्ट संचार का समर्थन करता है।” सही है, क्योंकि प्राकृतिक संकेत और चेहरे के भाव संवेग को दृश्य रूप में स्पष्ट करते हैं, जिससे बधिर शिक्षार्थी सहज संवाद कर सकते हैं। “यह औपचारिक संकेतों को बढ़ावा देने के लिए संवेगात्मक संकेतों के उपयोग को कम करता है।” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि संवेगात्मक संकेतों का उपयोग कम करना भावों की अभिव्यक्ति घटाएगा, जबकि उद्देश्य उसे मजबूत करना है।
qs.rel: Supports emotional and clear communication, e.g. expressive facial and body language for hearing impaired. Neighbours: total communication, visual cues.

qs.stem: _________ is a tool that allows children with CP to use letters, words and phrases on a screen to verbally express their thoughts and emotions.

opts.B: Electronic communication device without an on-screen letter or word display

qs.sol: “Electronic communication board” is correct: An electronic communication board can display selectable letters, words and phrases and produce spoken output for a child with cerebral palsy. “Electronic communication device” fails: An electronic communication device is a broader category; the board describes the specific pictured or screen-based tool, though the terms can overlap.
qs.rel: Electronic communication board lets CP children select letters, words and phrases verbally via screen. Neighbours: low-tech boards, eye-gaze, switches, AAC.

qs.sol: “Otoacoustic Emissions” is correct: Otoacoustic emissions assess inner-ear response and are used in hearing evaluation. “Visual Discrimination” fails: Visual discrimination is a relevant visual skill that a functional vision assessment may examine.
qs.rel: OAE tests inner-ear (cochlear outer hair cell) function. Neighbours: BERA, tympanometry, audiometry.

qs.stem: In the organisational framework for Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC), which type of communication is characterised by the user’s ability to generate novel messages independently of immediate situational context, often involving creative language use?
qs.sol: Independent communication means the person can construct new messages without depending on the immediate situation. “Context-dependent communication” does not fit: context-dependent messages rely on the immediate situation for meaning.
qs.rel: AAC independent communication = user communicates without partner help; dependent/partner-assisted communication needs support. Neighbours: aided/unaided, symbols.

qs.stem: जिसे दृश्य और श्रवण हानि हो ऐसा बच्चा किस श्रेणी के अंतर्गत आता है?
qs.sol: दृश्य और श्रवण, दोनों प्रकार की हानि वाले बच्चे को शैक्षिक सहायता की दृष्टि से “विशेष बच्चा” कहा जा सकता है। “विकलांग बच्चा” व्यापक पुराना शब्द है, जो कई प्रकार की हानि को समेटता है और संयुक्त संवेदी जरूरत को उतनी स्पष्टता से नहीं बताता।
qs.rel: A child with both visual and hearing impairment is deaf-blind and comes under multiple disabilities/special category. Neighbours: RPwD Act 2016 listing, tactile communication.

qs.sol: “स्थानिक लेआउट और नेविगेशन का वर्णन करने हेतु मौखिक या ऑडियो अनुसंकेतों का उपयोग करने वाला इलेक्ट्रॉनिक सिस्टम” सही है, क्योंकि श्रवण मानचित्र स्थान और मार्ग की जानकारी आवाज या अन्य श्रव्य संकेतों में देता है, जिससे उपयोगकर्ता परिवेश का मानसिक नक्शा बना सके। “कंपन अनुसंकेतों वाला स्मार्टफ़ोन GPS ऐप” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि कंपन वाला जीपीएस ऐप मुख्यतः स्पर्श संकेत देता है; केवल कंपन उसे श्रवण मानचित्र नहीं बनाता।
qs.rel: Verbal or audio cues describing spatial layout help blind learners with navigation. Neighbours: tactile maps, landmarks, orientation.

qs.sol: “ब्रेल स्टाइलस और स्लेट (Braille Stylus and Slate)” सही है, क्योंकि ब्रेल स्टाइलस और स्लेट से कागज पर बिंदु दबाकर लिखना ब्रेल लेखन की पारंपरिक हाथ से की जाने वाली विधि है। “पर्किन्स ब्रेलर (Perkins Brailler)” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि पर्किन्स ब्रेलर भी ब्रेल लिख सकता है, लेकिन वह यांत्रिक लेखन उपकरण है, पारंपरिक स्लेट-स्टाइलस जोड़ी नहीं।
qs.rel: Braille stylus and slate are manual writing tools for blind persons. Neighbours: Perkins brailler, Taylor frame, abacus (Cranmer).

qs.sol: “श्रवण फ़िगर-ग्राउंड समस्याएं, श्रवण एकीकरण समस्याएं, श्रवण ध्यान समस्याएं” में शोर के बीच लक्षित ध्वनि अलग न कर पाने को श्रवण फ़िगर-ग्राउंड, उच्च स्तरीय कार्य को श्रवण एकीकरण और लंबे समय तक सुनने को श्रवण ध्यान से जोड़ा गया है। “श्रवण ध्यान समस्याएं, श्रवण एकीकरण समस्याएं, श्रवण फ़िगर-ग्राउंड समस्याएं” शोर में ध्वनि अलग करने की कठिनाई को केवल ध्यान से जोड़ता है और निरंतर सुनने की कठिनाई को फ़िगर-ग्राउंड से, इसलिए उसका मिलान ठीक नहीं है।
qs.rel: Auditory processing disorders involve figure-ground, integration and attention problems. Neighbours: central auditory processing, listening in noise, dyslexia overlap.

qs.sol: “जीवन में दिनचर्या” से बधिर-दृष्टिहीन व्यक्ति को घटनाओं का अनुमान लगाने और दैनिक गतिविधियों में अपेक्षित क्रम समझने में मदद मिलती है। “गंध का बोध” एक सहायक संवेदी संकेत हो सकता है, पर वह नियमित, पूर्वानुमेय गतिविधि-क्रम का स्थान नहीं लेता।
qs.rel: Daily routines help deaf-blind people anticipate events (calendar systems, object cues). Neighbours: touch cues, tactile signing, anticipation.

qs.sol: “सहायक उपकरणों और परिवार-केंद्रित हस्तक्षेप तक शीघ्र पहुंच प्रदान करना” से बच्चे को आरंभ में ही उपयुक्त संचार साधन मिलते हैं और परिवार दैनिक बातचीत में उनका अभ्यास करा सकता है। “दृश्य या स्पर्श सहायता के बिना केवल मौखिक निर्देशों पर निर्भर रहना” संचार के दृश्य या स्पर्श मार्गों को हटाता है, जो कई बच्चों के लिए आवश्यक पहुँच देते हैं।
qs.rel: Early access to assistive devices and family-centred intervention improves outcomes for hearing impairment. Neighbours: hearing aids, cochlear implants, auditory-verbal therapy.

qs.sol: “वास्तविक वस्तुओं और उत्थित आरेखों जैसे ठोस और स्पर्शनीय साधनों का उपयोग करें” दृष्टिबाधित विद्यार्थी को आकार, संख्या और संबंधों को स्पर्श करके समझने का अवसर देता है। “सभी अवधारणाओं के लिए केवल मौखिक तरीकों का उपयोग करें” श्रव्य जानकारी दे सकता है, पर सभी गणितीय अवधारणाओं के लिए ठोस स्पर्श अनुभव का पूरा विकल्प नहीं है।
qs.rel: Real objects and raised diagrams (tactile aids) support concept learning in blind students. Neighbours: concrete experiences, tactile graphics, models.

qs.sol: “बहरा-अंधा व्यक्ति” में दृष्टि और श्रवण दोनों की हानि से आसपास की दृश्य और ध्वन्यात्मक जानकारी तक पहुँच सीमित हो सकती है। “अंधा व्यक्ति” में दृष्टि बाधित होती है, पर श्रवण उपलब्ध होने पर ध्वनियों से जानकारी मिल सकती है।
qs.rel: Deaf-blind persons have combined vision and hearing loss that limits sensory input. Neighbours: Helen Keller, Anne Sullivan, tactile sign.

qs.sol: “हेडफ़ोन” ध्वनि सुनने का उपकरण है, चलने-फिरने में शारीरिक सहारा देने वाला साधन नहीं। “स्कूटर” चलते समय भार सँभालने और संतुलन में सहायता देता है, इसलिए गतिशीलता सहायक उपकरण है।
qs.rel: Headphones are hearing devices, not mobility aids (walker, crutches, wheelchair). Neighbours: assistive listening devices, FM systems, loop systems.

qs.sol: “श्रवण यंत्र” ध्वनि को बढ़ाकर या संसाधित करके सुनने तक पहुँच देने वाला तकनीकी उपकरण है। “ओष्ठ पठन” संचार में सहायक सीखा हुआ कौशल है, उपकरण-आधारित तकनीकी सहायता नहीं।
qs.rel: Hearing aid amplifies/processes sound; cochlear implant stimulates auditory nerve electrically. Neighbours: BTE, ITE types, FM systems, earmoulds.

qs.sol: स्पास्टिक डिप्लेजिया में कूल्हों और घुटनों का अत्यधिक मुड़ा रहना “क्राउच चाल (crouch gait)” से मेल खाता है। “स्टेपपेज चाल (steppage gait)” मुख्यतः पैर उठाने की कमजोरी से जुड़ी चाल है, इसलिए यहाँ कम उपयुक्त है।
qs.rel: Spastic diplegia: legs more affected, hips and knees flexed (crouch gait), scissoring. Neighbours: hemiplegia, quadriplegia, athetoid, ataxic CP.

qs.sol: “ध्वनि की उपस्थिति या अनुपस्थिति को पहचानना” संसूचन का आधार है: श्रोता पहले यह बताता है कि ध्वनि आई या नहीं। “वार्तालाप में विशिष्ट शब्दों को पहचानना” में ध्वनि पहचानना पड़ता है, जो केवल उसकी उपस्थिति जानने से आगे का श्रवण कौशल है।
qs.rel: Detection is the first level of auditory skills: awareness of sound presence or absence; then discrimination, identification, comprehension. Neighbours: Erber's hierarchy.

qs.sol: “शरीर की तुलना में थोड़ा चौड़ा चाप (arc) बनाते हुए केन को एक तरफ से दूसरी तरफ प्रदोलित करना” में छड़ी को रास्ते की चौड़ाई में दोनों ओर चलाकर आगे की सतह और बाधाओं की जानकारी ली जाती है। “पृष्ठ की बनावट को महसूस करने के लिए केन को एक तरफ से ड्रैग करना” सतह की बनावट का संकेत दे सकता है, पर वह दोनों ओर स्पर्श करने वाली मानक चाप-गतिविधि का वर्णन नहीं है।
qs.rel: Arc technique: the cane swings slightly wider than the body in a side-to-side arc in tandem with steps. Neighbours: two-point touch, touch-and-drag, cane grip.

qs.sol: इंटरप्रेटर शिक्षक के कथन को सांकेतिक भाषा में बदलता है और बधिर विद्यार्थी के सांकेतिक उत्तर को बोलकर प्रस्तुत कर सकता है। “लिप स्पीकर (lip speaker)” स्पष्ट मुख-गतियों से बोलता है; वह शिक्षक की बात का सांकेतिक अनुवाद और विद्यार्थी के संकेतों का वॉयस-ओवर दोनों नहीं करता।
qs.rel: Educational interpreter converts teacher's speech to sign for deaf students. Neighbours: ISL interpreter, role of captioning, note-taker.

qs.sol: Astigmatism results from uneven focusing of light on the retina and causes blurred vision. “Myopia” focuses distant images in front of the retina, a different refractive error from the uneven focusing described in the stem.
qs.rel: Astigmatism arises from uneven corneal/lens curvature causing blurred vision; myopia: image before retina; hypermetropia: behind retina. Neighbours: cylindrical lens correction.

qs.sol: Robotic exoskeletons are wearable devices that augment or assist human movement. “Wheelchairs” support mobility by carrying a seated user, whereas an exoskeleton augments movement through a wearable mechanical structure.
qs.rel: Robotic exoskeletons are wearable devices assisting walking in paralysis. Neighbours: orthotics, prosthetics, wheelchairs, assistive technology.

qs.sol: Orthotic devices are external braces that support alignment and mobility for students with cerebral palsy. “Prosthetic devices” replace a missing body part, whereas orthoses are external braces that support an existing limb or joint.
qs.rel: Orthotic devices (braces, splints, AFOs) support alignment and mobility in cerebral palsy; prosthetics replace missing limbs. Neighbours: callipers.

qs.sol: Six Braille dot positions permit 64 patterns; excluding the blank leaves 63 dot combinations. “26” counts letters in the English alphabet, not the nonblank patterns made from six independently raised or unraised Braille dots.
qs.rel: Six dots permit 64 patterns including blank; 63 combinations used. Neighbours: Louis Braille (1824-1829), grade 1/2, Nemeth code.

qs.sol: A slate and stylus are tools for writing Braille by embossing dots on paper. “reading” is done by feeling Braille dots, while the slate and stylus physically emboss those dots onto paper.
qs.rel: Slate and stylus emboss Braille dots by hand; the Perkins brailler is a mechanical writer. Neighbours: Braille display, reading from right to left when writing.

qs.sol: An abacus is a portable frame with movable beads used for arithmetic. “Taylor frame” uses movable type pieces rather than the beads specified in this description of a portable calculating device.
qs.rel: Abacus (Cranmer abacus) is a counting frame used by blind children for arithmetic. Neighbours: Taylor frame, talking calculator, Nemeth code.

qs.sol: A rigid one-piece aluminium cane is a white long cane rather than a folding cane. “Folding cane” has sections that collapse for storage, so it cannot be the rigid one-piece construction specified in the question.
qs.rel: A rigid one-piece aluminium white cane is a long cane; folding canes collapse; support canes provide balance. Neighbours: identification canes, length.

qs.sol: Braille represents written characters through raised dots read by touch by visually impaired persons. “hearing impaired” concerns difficulty hearing sound; it does not by itself create the need to read raised dots by touch.
qs.rel: Braille is a tactile system of raised dots read by visually impaired persons. Neighbours: Louis Braille, 6-dot cell, refreshable displays.

qs.sol: Hearing supplies distant environmental cues, such as traffic and voices, that help orientation and mobility. “It is the only sense used in navigation.” does not fit: navigation uses several senses and mobility skills, not hearing alone.
qs.rel: Hearing gives distant environmental cues (traffic, voices) crucial for orientation and mobility. Neighbours: vision, touch, olfaction as other cues.

qs.sol: प्रारंभिक श्रवण उद्दीपन सुनने से जुड़े तंत्रिका मार्गों तथा वाक् और भाषा के अधिग्रहण को सहारा देता है। “यह किसी भी सहायक श्रवण डिवाइसों की आवश्यकता को रोकता है।” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि श्रवण उद्दीपन सहायक श्रवण यंत्र की आवश्यकता समाप्त नहीं करता।
qs.rel: Early auditory stimulation develops neural pathways for speech and language. Neighbours: critical period, early intervention, aural rehabilitation.

topics.deep:
- **Visual impairment (VI):** RPwD Act 2016 - **blindness** (visual acuity below 3/60 in better eye with best correction, or field of vision below 10 degrees) and **low vision** (acuity 6/18 to 3/60, i.e. 6/18-6/60 range; education-based "low vision" can use residual sight). Terms: visual acuity (Snellen chart; 6/6 normal) vs visual field. Conditions: myopia (image before retina), hypermetropia, **astigmatism** (uneven curvature -> blurred vision), cataract, glaucoma, retinitis pigmentosa, nystagmus.
- **Braille:** invented by Louis Braille (1824, published 1829); six-dot cell (2 columns x 3 rows) gives 64 patterns, 63 usable; Grade 1 uncontracted, Grade 2 contracted (saves space, speeds reading); Nemeth code for maths; Perkins brailler; **slate and stylus** (right to left writing); Taylor frame, **Cranmer abacus**; embosser prints Braille; refreshable Braille display; screen readers (JAWS, NVDA); Daisy talking books. New paragraph in Braille begins at the third cell. Braille Day: 4 January. Low-vision aids: magnifiers, telescopes, large print, reading stand, typoscope (reading guide), CCTV, contrast and lighting.
- **Orientation and Mobility (O&M):** sighted guide technique (hold above elbow, guide one step ahead; narrow space - guide's arm moved to midline of back), **long white cane** (touch-and-slide/two-point touch, arc slightly wider than shoulders), upper/lower body protection, trailing, squaring off, landmarks, blindfold training for low-vision learners. Early identification and early intervention are crucial.
- **Hearing impairment (HI):** RPwD Act - **deaf**: 70 dB or more in better ear; **hard of hearing**: 60-70 dB. Common bands: 26-40 mild, 41-55 moderate, 56-70 moderately severe, 71-90 severe, 91+ profound. Types: conductive, sensorineural, mixed; prelingual vs postlingual. Tests: pure-tone audiometry, play audiometry, **OAE and BERA** for infants, tympanometry. Auditory skill hierarchy (Erber): detection, discrimination, identification, comprehension. Aids: hearing aids (BTE, ITE), cochlear implants, FM systems, loop systems.
- **Communication approaches:** **oralism** (speech, lip/speech reading, amplification; A. G. Bell; Milan Congress 1880), **manualism** (sign; Abbe de l'Epee, Gallaudet), **total communication** (all modes), bilingual-bicultural (sign as L1, written language as L2), cued speech, Simcom (simultaneous communication of speech and sign), auditory-verbal therapy. **ISL** (ISLRTC, Delhi, set up 2015) is a natural language with own grammar; ISS is manually coded form of spoken Indian language. Sign parameters: handshape, location, movement, palm orientation, non-manual signals. Classroom: face the class, don't cover the mouth, captions, visual alerts, interpreter.
- **Deaf-blindness:** combined vision and hearing loss (Helen Keller, Anne Sullivan); tactile signing, object cues, calendar systems, routines to anticipate events.
- **Locomotor / cerebral palsy:** CP = non-progressive brain damage; types spastic, athetoid, ataxic, mixed; hemiplegia (one side), diplegia (legs), quadriplegia (all four), monoplegia, paraplegia. Management: physiotherapy, orthotics (braces, AFOs), **pommel** (abducts legs), adaptive seating, standing frames, botulinum toxin for focal spasticity, oral-motor therapy; avoid prolonged W-sitting. Prosthetics replace limbs; exoskeletons assist walking.
- **AAC (Augmentative and Alternative Communication):** unaided (gesture, sign) vs aided (boards, devices); low-tech (picture boards, PECS) to high-tech (speech-generating devices, electronic communication boards, eye-gaze); direct selection vs scanning (switch); symbols represent objects, actions, concepts, emotions; communicative competence = linguistic, operational, social, strategic; minimal AAC team = user, communication partners/family, speech-language pathologist, teacher.
- **Assistive technology planning:** need assessment first (SETT framework: student, environment, tasks, tools), trial, training, review; ICT must be accessible (WCAG, closed captions for e-classrooms).

**Likely question angles:**
- Number of dots/combinations in Braille; who invented it; slate and stylus usage.
- Acuity thresholds and difference between blind and low vision.
- Hearing-loss decibel bands; deaf vs hard of hearing; test for infants.
- Oralism vs manualism vs total communication; full form of Simcom.
- Which device is assistive for VI vs HI vs CP (hearing aid, cane, orthosis).
- Types of cerebral palsy and plegias.
- Sighted guide and cane techniques.
- AAC symbol types and team membership.
- Inappropriate classroom practice (covering mouth, W-sitting).
- ISL vs ISS; ISLRTC.

topics.title: 7. Gender, Society & Education
topics.theory:
- **Sex** = biological, fixed; **gender** = socially/culturally constructed roles that vary by time and culture. Gender identity, expression, sexual orientation are distinct; intersex = variation in sex characteristics.
- **Patriarchy** = male domination; matriarchy = female domination; gender stereotype = fixed belief about roles; **hidden curriculum** = unstated norms in school that teach gender roles.
- **Gender equality** (equal rights/opportunity) vs equity (fairness) vs parity (numerical). **Gender-neutral policy** makes no distinction; gender-sensitive recognises differences.
- **Socialisation agents:** family, school, peers, media, community - **heredity is not an agent**. Mead (symbolic interactionism), Bandura (modelling), Kohlberg (gender constancy), Bem (gender schema), Butler (performativity).
- **Census 2011:** sex ratio 943 (option ~940), **child sex ratio (0-6) 914**; Kerala highest. Sex-selective abortion via amniocentesis/ultrasound -> **PCPNDT Act 1994**.
- Laws: Dowry Prohibition 1961, Equal Remuneration 1976, Domestic Violence Act 2005, **POSH 2013**, Transgender Persons Act 2019, NALSA 2014, Women's Reservation Act 2023.
- **Education schemes:** **KGBV 2004** (residential girls' schools), NPEGEL 2003, Mahila Samakhya 1988, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao 2015; NPE 1986/POA 1992 stress textbook revision and gender sensitisation.
- Sources of discrimination: unequal division of labour at home, education and job bias, laws/policies, media; Devadasi system (South India) dedicates girls to temples.
- **Teacher strategies:** mixed-gender pairs, turn-taking, gender-balanced visuals, reviewing biased textbooks, equal expectations.
- Blue as 'masculine' is a social stereotype; intersectionality (Crenshaw) links gender with disability, caste, class.

qs.stem:
Choose the appropriate option to complete the sentence. 

“______ is what feelings sound like”.
qs.sol:
The phrase asks for an art form that expresses feelings through sound.

Music uses organised sound to convey emotion, completing the sentence.
qs.rel: Gender equality in schools means equal access, opportunities and treatment for all genders, not separate classrooms. Neighbours: gender equity (fairness), gender parity (numerical equality), gender-neutral vs gender-sensitive policy; Article 15 and 21A.

qs.stem: Which among the following is NOT considered as the agent of socialization?
qs.sol: Family, school and community are agents of socialization. Heredity is biological inheritance, not a socialization agent.
qs.rel: Agents of socialisation: family, school, peer group, community, media, religion. Heredity is biological, not an agent. Neighbours: primary vs secondary socialisation, hidden curriculum, Mead and Cooley's looking-glass self.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is an element of effective learning activity?
 I. Spontaneous involvement
 II. Challenging
qs.sol: Effective learning activities should encourage spontaneous involvement and also be challenging enough to engage learners. Therefore both statements are correct.
qs.rel: Sources of gender discrimination: unequal division of labour at home, bias in hiring and promotion, discriminatory laws and customs, media and textbooks. Neighbours: son preference, glass ceiling, unpaid care work.

qs.stem: Who out of the following had developed the theory of trial and error learning?
qs.sol: “E.L.Thorndike” is supported: E. L. Thorndike developed trial-and-error learning through puzzle-box experiments with cats. By contrast, “B. F. Skinner” skinner is associated with operant conditioning.
qs.rel: Gender discrimination is socially constructed and culturally influenced, not natural or biological. Neighbours: sex vs gender, socialisation, stereotypes, Simone de Beauvoir ('one is not born a woman').

qs.stem: What happens after the hypothesis is verified?
qs.sol: Verifying a hypothesis can establish new knowledge from the investigation. “Students memorise the result” describes recall of a finding, not the knowledge gained when a hypothesis is tested and supported.
qs.rel: Government policies and family/parental attitudes both can be sources of gender discrimination. Neighbours: intra-household discrimination, schooling of girls, dowry, preference for sons, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao.

qs.stem:
Ideas for dramas may come from which of the following sources?
 Statements:
 I. The imagination
 II. The environment
 III. History/Literature
 IV. Movies
qs.sol: Creative and classroom drama draws its raw material from several distinct, non-overlapping modes of experience: what a person invents purely from imagination, what they directly observe in their surrounding environment, narrative already recorded in history or literature, and narrative already realised in another medium such as film. Standard drama-teaching method treats all of these as legitimate starting points for a dramatic idea, not just one or two of them. …
qs.rel: Gender bias begins in the family and extends to school, workplace, media, police station and courts. Neighbours: institutional sexism, hidden curriculum, patriarchy, Vishakha guidelines/POSH Act 2013.

qs.stem: Who is the chief exponent of the Theory of Trail and Error ?
qs.sol:
No official answer key was published for this paper; the answer is worked out from the question.

Thorndike’s puzzle-box experiments demonstrated learning through trial and error.

Successful responses are strengthened through their consequences, forming the basis of his connectionist account.
qs.rel: Sex is biological, fixed, universal, nature-made; gender is socially constructed, varies with time and culture. So 'changes from time to time' describes gender, not sex. Neighbours: gender roles, stereotypes, gender identity.

qs.stem: What should be the first guide in the selection of learning resources?
qs.sol:
Concept:

A learning resource is a means to learning, not an end in itself. In learner-centred pedagogy — the position taken by the National Curriculum Framework (NCF) and reaffirmed by NEP 2020 — the educational worth of any resource is decided by how well it connects with the learner: what the learner already knows, what engages the learner, and what the learner meets in everyday life. The first criterion applied while selecting a learning resource is therefore the learner profile; practical constraints such as budget, infrastructure and teacher familiarity are filters applied afterwards, to settle the final choice among resources that already meet that criterion. …
qs.rel: Blue as masculine and pink as feminine is a social stereotype, not biological. Neighbours: gender stereotypes in toys, occupations, textbooks; socialisation theories; gender roles are learned.

qs.stem: What is the full-form of CCE?
qs.sol: “Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation” is supported: CCE expands to Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation, covering ongoing assessment across learning domains. By contrast, “Continuous and Cumulative Education” cumulative Education substitutes both the scope and activity named by CCE.
qs.rel: Patriarchy = male-dominated social structure; matriarchy = female-dominated; androgyny = mix of traits; egalitarian = equal. Neighbours: patrilineal/patrilocal practices, Kate Millett, feminism waves.

qs.stem: Which of the following is/are the source(s) of gender discrimination? I. Educational opportunities II. Government policies III. Family and parents
qs.sol: Unequal educational opportunities, discriminatory policy design, and family expectations can each create or sustain gender discrimination. The printed list therefore includes all three sources.
qs.rel: Educational opportunities, government policies and family attitudes are sources of gender discrimination. Neighbours: school dropout of girls, safety, early marriage, wage gap, gender budgeting.

qs.stem: What societal structure is characterized by male domination over women?
qs.sol:
Societal structures are classified by which gender holds the dominant institutional power. A patriarchy is a social order in which men occupy the primary positions of authority, leadership, and property control, while women are structurally subordinate to that authority; a matriarchy is the mirror-image structure with women in dominant positions; androgyny and egalitarianism describe gender-trait blending and equal-status arrangements respectively, not male-over-female dominance.

The stem asks specifically for the structure defined by male domination over women. …
qs.rel: Misuse of amniocentesis and ultrasonography for sex-selective abortion skews the sex ratio; controlled by PCPNDT Act 1994. Neighbours: female foeticide, declining child sex ratio (914 in 2011), Beti Bachao Beti Padhao 2015.

qs.stem: 2011 की जनगणना के अनुसार हमारे देश में लिंगानुपात कितना है?
qs.sol: प्रश्नपत्र में 2011 जनगणना का प्रारंभिक लिंगानुपात प्रति 1,000 पुरुषों पर 940 महिलाएँ दिया है।
qs.rel: Census 2011: sex ratio 943 females per 1000 males (the nearest option, 940, is the key); Kerala highest (1084), Daman and Diu lowest (618). Neighbours: child sex ratio 0-6 = 914; Census 2001 sex ratio 933 and child 927.

qs.stem: During early childhood, a child’s brain is described as:
qs.sol: “highly plastic and responsive” is correct: Neural plasticity in early childhood lets experience and teaching strongly shape developing abilities. “fully developed” fails: The brain is still developing at this stage and is not already mature.
qs.rel: Mixed-gender pairs/groups build interpersonal skills, confidence, communication and assertiveness and reduce stereotypes. Neighbours: cooperative learning, co-education, gender-sensitive pedagogy, peer learning.

qs.stem: Which of the following is/are the characteristic(s) of an effective method of teaching and learning? I. Provides a scope for peer learning II. Encourages students to think independently and construct knowledge of their own
qs.sol: Peer learning lets pupils explain ideas to one another. Independent thinking asks them to build and test their own understanding. Both are features of an effective learning method.
qs.rel: KGBV (2004, SSA component) provides residential upper-primary schools for girls from SC/ST/OBC/minority and BPL families in educationally backward blocks. Neighbours: NPEGEL, Mahila Samakhya, Sukanya Samriddhi, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao.

qs.stem: समावेशी शिक्षा किन विद्यालय और कक्षाओं के उपयोग को अस्वीकार करती है?
qs.sol: समावेशी शिक्षा उपयुक्त सहायता और अनुकूलन के साथ विद्यार्थियों को सामान्य कक्षा में साथ पढ़ाने पर बल देती है। प्रश्न के पारंपरिक विरोध में अलग विशेष विद्यालय या पृथक विशेष कक्षा को नियमित व्यवस्था के रूप में अस्वीकार किया जाता है। निजी और सरकारी शब्द विद्यालय के संचालन का प्रकार बताते हैं; दोनों समावेशी हो सकते हैं। सहकारी व्यवस्था भी अपने-आप पृथक्करण नहीं बताती। मुख्य अंतर विद्यार्थियों को दिव्यांगता या सहायता की आवश्यकता के आधार पर अलग करने का है, संस्थान के स्वामित्व का नहीं। इस उत्तर का अर्थ विशेष सेवाओं की आवश्यकता का पूर्ण निषेध नहीं, बल्कि नियमित पृथक शिक्षण के स्थान पर साझा कक्षा को प्राथमिकता देना है।
qs.rel: Language teaching should promote gender equality: mixed-gender group work, non-sexist language and inclusive texts. Neighbours: gender-sensitive textbooks, hidden curriculum, sexist language.

qs.stem: कौन सी नीति लिंग के बीच कोई अंतर नहीं करती है?
qs.sol: जो नीति लिंग के आधार पर कोई भेद नहीं करती और सभी पर एक समान नियम लागू करती है, उसे लिंग-तटस्थ नीति कहते हैं; वह लिंग को प्रासंगिक श्रेणी नहीं मानती। लिंग-जागरूक नीति लिंग से जुड़ी परिस्थितियों को स्पष्ट रूप से पहचानती है। लिंग-समानता नीति समान अवसर या परिणाम के लक्ष्य से चलती है और इसके लिए असमान प्रारम्भिक स्थितियों को पहचानकर अलग उपाय भी कर सकती है, इसलिए उसका अर्थ ‘‘कोई अंतर न करना’’ नहीं है। लिंग-विशिष्ट नीति किसी एक लिंग या अलग-अलग लिंगों के लिए अलग उपाय बनाती है। अतः ‘‘कोई अंतर नहीं करती’’ का संकेत लिंग-तटस्थ नीति की ओर है।
qs.rel: Gender-neutral policy makes no distinction between sexes; gender-aware/sensitive recognises differences; gender-equality/transformative seeks to change relations. Neighbours: Moser's framework, gender mainstreaming.

qs.stem: Who first used the term 'autism'?
qs.sol: Eugen Bleuler first used the term autism in psychiatric writing. “Sigmund Freud” developed psychoanalytic theory, but he is not credited with the first use of the term in this question.
qs.rel: Mixed-gender pairs help develop interpersonal skills, confidence, communication and assertiveness. Neighbours: single-sex vs co-educational schools, peer group, collaborative learning, gender sensitivity.

qs.stem: 21वीं सदी के लिए शिक्षा के चार स्तंभ _______ हैं।

opts.A: जानने के लिए सीखना, करने के लिए सीखना, जीने के लिए सीखना और बनने के लिए सीखना।
opts.B: जाना सीखना, काम करना सीखना, लिखने के लिए सीखना, पढ़ने के लिए सीखना
opts.C: पुस्तक के लिए सीखना, लिखने के लिए सीखना, जीने के लिए सीखना और करने के लिए सीखना
opts.D: सीखने के लिए सीखना, बनने के लिए सीखना, सिखाने के लिए सीखना, करने के लिए सीखना

qs.sol: डेलोर के चार स्तंभ हैं: जानना सीखना, करना सीखना, साथ रहना सीखना और होना सीखना। “जीने के लिए सीखना” इस पत्र में अभिप्रेत निकटतम शब्दांकन है।
qs.rel: Gender-equitable curriculum for marginalised girls includes content reflecting their lives, literacy instruction building empowerment, and removal of stereotypes. Neighbours: intersectionality, NCF 2005 gender position paper, inclusive textbooks.

qs.stem: Gender-balanced visuals in textbooks are important because they help to:
qs.sol: Gender-balanced visuals help challenge stereotypical roles by showing all genders in varied activities and responsibilities.
qs.rel: Gender-balanced visuals challenge stereotypical roles and show both genders in varied roles. Neighbours: hidden curriculum, textbook audits, NCERT gender-sensitive guidelines, role models.

qs.stem: Why is it important to state objectives in terms of pupils’ expected behavioural outcomes?

opts.C: To clearly define the change in student behaviour due to learning

qs.sol:
Behavioural outcomes describe an observable change in a learner after instruction.

Stating the expected change makes the intended learning result explicit and lets a teacher check whether it occurred.
qs.rel: Sex is biological, gender is socially/culturally constructed. Neighbours: gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation; Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019; NALSA v. Union of India 2014.

qs.stem: Which of the following is an adaptation useful for students with low vision?
qs.sol:
Low vision students benefit when visual information is enlarged and made easier to resolve.

A magnifier increases the apparent size of print or objects while preserving the student’s available vision.
qs.rel: Child sex ratio (0-6 years) Census 2011 = 914 girls per 1000 boys (2001: 927); lowest in Haryana, Punjab. Neighbours: overall sex ratio 940, PCPNDT Act, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao.

qs.stem: According to behaviourist perspective, learning is primarily based on:
qs.sol:
Behaviourism (associated with Watson, Pavlov, and Skinner) explains learning as an observable, measurable change in behaviour that results when a stimulus becomes linked to a response — through classical conditioning (a neutral stimulus paired repeatedly with another stimulus until it comes to trigger a response on its own) or operant conditioning (a response is strengthened or weakened by the reinforcement or punishment that follows it). This view deliberately leaves out unobservable internal mental processes as the mechanism of learning.

The question asks what behaviourists treat as the primary basis of learning. …
qs.rel: Discrimination disregards individual need, merit and potential; providing equal opportunities is the remedy. Neighbours: equality vs equity, Article 14-16, affirmative action, reservation policy.

qs.stem: The concept of 'special needs' most accurately emphasises:

opts.A: modifications in the education system for inclusive access
opts.B: equal punishment policies for all students
opts.D: assigning more homework to slower learners

qs.sol: In inclusive education, the term 'special needs' refers to learners who require additional or different support to access the same curriculum, environment, and opportunities as their peers. The guiding principle — reflected in frameworks such as India's Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities — is that the education system itself must adapt (through curriculum design, teaching methods, assessment, and physical access) so that no learner is excluded from the general classroom. …
qs.rel: Gender dynamics = relationships and interaction between boys and girls (and others) in school. Neighbours: gender roles, gender relations, gender sensitivity, classroom participation patterns.

qs.stem: _____ में अन्य छात्रों को उनके काम की गुणवत्ता पर प्रतिक्रिया प्रदान करने वाले छात्र शामिल हैं।
qs.sol: समकक्ष आकलन में छात्र अन्य छात्रों के काम पर प्रतिक्रिया देते हैं।
qs.rel: Susan Stryker: transgender is an umbrella term for all identities that cross or challenge gender norms. Neighbours: Judith Butler (gender as performativity), cisgender, intersex, NALSA 2014, Transgender Persons Act 2019.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is the most crucial consideration when selecting learning

resources for an inclusive classroom?

opts.A: The resource's appeal to the majority group in the class
opts.B: The teacher's familiarity with the resource
opts.D: The resource’s ability to meet diverse learning needs and abilities

qs.sol: Concept: Inclusive education requires that learning resources be selected primarily for their capacity to accommodate the full range of learner diversity — different abilities, paces, and support needs — rather than for convenience, popularity, or budget. This is the core principle behind Universal Design for Learning (UDL): a resource is judged by whether every learner can actually access and engage with it. …
qs.rel: Gender is the socially and culturally constructed roles, behaviours and attributes for men and women, as distinct from biological sex. Neighbours: Ann Oakley, gender roles, gender identity.

qs.stem: Subjects are generally limited to:
qs.sol: Curriculum theory draws a specific distinction between a "subject" and a "discipline". A subject is a fixed, simplified unit of knowledge (such as Mathematics, Science, or Language) organised into a timetable for teaching and learning at the school stage. A discipline, by contrast, is a specialised, research-oriented body of knowledge pursued by a community of scholars, and it is this term that describes organised study at the college/university level. …
qs.rel: Gender in socialisation refers to culturally constructed characteristics. Neighbours: gender typing, stereotype, internalisation, family, media, school as agents.

qs.stem: Which of the following intervention strategies is most effective in improving reading comprehension skills in students with learning disabilities?

opts.A: Allowing students to read silently without guidance
opts.B: Focusing solely on oral reading fluency drills
opts.D: Use of multisensory structured language instruction (MSL) that integrates visual, auditory and kinesthetic modalities

qs.sol: “Use of multisensory structured language instruction (MSL) that integrates visual, auditory and kinesthetic modalities” gives learners explicit, connected ways to work with print and language, supporting the decoding and language knowledge needed for comprehension. “Focusing solely on oral reading fluency drills” may improve reading rate, but fluency practice alone does not directly teach meaning-making strategies or address all underlying language needs.
qs.rel: Teachers avoid gender bias by equal expectations, mixed groups, non-stereotyped examples and fair opportunities. Neighbours: hidden curriculum, call patterns, gender audit of materials.

qs.stem: 6 साल के बच्चे के शब्दावली में औसतन कितने शब्द संचित होते हैं?
qs.sol: अंतर्निहित पूर्वावलोकन कुंजी छह वर्ष के बच्चे की औसत शब्दावली लगभग 2560 शब्द बताती है।
qs.rel: Classroom gender discrimination in India includes boys prioritised in participation, separate seating and gender-typed tasks. Neighbours: dropout of girls, hidden curriculum, gender bias in textbooks.

qs.stem: What is Learning in one context and applying it to another called technically?
qs.sol:
A skill or principle learned in one situation may influence performance in another.

Carrying that learning between contexts is technically called transfer of learning.
qs.rel: Judith Butler: gender is performative, repeatedly enacted through acts and speech rather than an inner essence (Gender Trouble, 1990). Neighbours: queer theory, Simone de Beauvoir, social constructionism.

qs.stem:
Continuous education process, involvement of students and teacher is the characteristic of which type of education 

system?
qs.sol:
The intended system has a regular, organised teaching-learning process with defined teacher and student roles.

This is the formal education model represented by the board key.
qs.rel: Nutritional requirements of boys and girls are similar until adolescence (about 7-9 years or puberty), after which they diverge. Neighbours: Mid-Day Meal scheme, anaemia in adolescent girls, IFA supplementation.

qs.stem:
Which of the following can help a teacher to make teaching–learning process participatory in social science?
 Statements:
 I. By arranging debate, discussions on emerging social issues for example: dowry, population growth etc.
 II. By teaching students that how to cooperate with each other.
qs.sol: Debates and discussions on social issues, along with cooperation among students, make social-science teaching participatory.
qs.rel: George Herbert Mead's symbolic interactionism: self and society arise through social interaction using symbols and language (looking-glass self by Cooley). Neighbours: role-taking, 'I' and 'me', gender socialisation.

qs.sol: “युवा अवस्था से ही समावेशी नागरिक शिक्षा प्रदान करना” सही है, क्योंकि कम उम्र से नागरिक अधिकारों और निर्णय प्रक्रियाओं की समावेशी शिक्षा भागीदारी तथा नेतृत्व का आधार बनाती है। “सभी निर्णयों के लिए संरक्षकता सौंपना” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि सभी निर्णय किसी संरक्षक को सौंपना लड़कियों की अपनी राजनीतिक आवाज और स्वायत्तता सीमित करता है।
qs.rel: Gender socialisation is the process by which children learn gender norms from family, school, peers and media. Neighbours: gender typing, Bandura's social learning, Kohlberg's cognitive developmental gender constancy, Bem's gender schema.

qs.sol:
अवधारणा

जेंडर समाजीकरण वह प्रक्रिया है जिसमें बच्चे सामाजिक संस्थाओं और संबंधों से जेंडर से जुड़े मूल्य, मानदंड और अपेक्षाएँ सीखते हैं। विद्यालय इस प्रक्रिया का औपचारिक और अनौपचारिक परिवेश प्रदान करते हैं।

अनुप्रयोग

स्कूल में शिक्षक निर्देश और अपेक्षाएँ व्यक्त करते हैं, सहपाठी पारस्परिक व्यवहार के जरिए मानदंड साझा करते हैं और पाठ्यचर्या चयनित उदाहरणों व भूमिकाओं को प्रस्तुत करती है। इन तीनों माध्यमों से बच्चों तक जेंडर-संबंधी सामाजिक संकेत पहुँचते हैं।

तुलना

केवल शैक्षणिक उपलब्धि पर ध्यान उपलब्धि-केंद्रित लक्ष्य बताता है, सामाजिक संप्रेषण की पूरी प्रक्रिया नहीं।

सभी जेंडर मानदंडों को समाप्त करना समाजीकरण के माध्यमों का वर्णन नहीं करता।

जेंडर-तटस्थ अधिगम एक शैक्षिक लक्ष्य का नाम देता ह …
qs.rel: Gender socialisation teaches children to accept gender roles via institutions and interaction. Neighbours: primary and secondary socialisation, toys, language, hidden curriculum.

qs.stem: ‘समाज सोचता है कि कुछ प्रकार के कार्य केवल पुरुषों द्वारा और कुछ महिलाओं द्वारा किए जाने के लिए होते हैं।’ निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन इस दिए गए कथन को संतुष्ट करता है? I. हम शायद ही कभी महिलाओं को हल से जमीन जोतते हुए देखते हैं। II. हम शायद ही कभी पुरुषों को बच्चों और परिवार के अन्य सदस्यों के कपड़े धोते हुए देखते हैं।

opts.D: ना ही I ना ही II

qs.sol: प्रश्न समाज में काम के लैंगिक बँटवारे की धारणा का उदाहरण माँगता है। महिलाओं का हल से खेत न जोतना और पुरुषों का परिवार के कपड़े न धोना, दोनों उस रूढ़ धारणा के उदाहरण हैं। इसका अर्थ यह नहीं कि ऐसे काम किसी एक लिंग के लिए ही उचित हैं। बात केवल वर्णित सामाजिक अपेक्षा को पहचानने की है; इसलिए दोनों कथन लागू होते हैं।
qs.rel: Society assigning tasks by gender is a gender stereotype or the sexual division of labour. Neighbours: gender roles, glass ceiling, invisible/unpaid domestic work, patriarchy.

qs.stem: Which of the following is an example of a cultural practice that reflects patriarchal values?
qs.sol: Costume can reflect social expectations and gender roles, including patriarchal values. Architecture, technology and ecology are not the best examples in this context.
qs.rel: Patriarchal practices: male-line inheritance, dowry, son preference, restrictions on mobility and dress codes for women. Neighbours: purdah, patrilocality, honour crimes, dowry prohibition act 1961.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही नहीं है? I. लैंगिक भेदभाव प्रत्यक्ष और अप्रत्यक्ष हो सकता है। II. लैंगिक भेदभाव खुले तौर पर या दबे छुपे रूप से हो सकता है।

opts.D: ना ही I ना ही II

qs.sol: लैंगिक भेदभाव प्रत्यक्ष हो सकता है, जैसे स्पष्ट रूप से अवसर रोकना, और अप्रत्यक्ष भी हो सकता है, जैसे सामान्य दिखने वाला नियम असमान असर डाले। उसका रूप खुला और आसानी से दिखने वाला या सूक्ष्म और कम दिखाई देने वाला भी हो सकता है। इसलिए दोनों कथन भेदभाव के मान्य भेद बताते हैं। प्रश्न गलत कथन पूछता है, जबकि यहाँ कोई कथन गलत नहीं है।
qs.rel: Gender discrimination can be direct or indirect and affects both sexes, though women are mostly affected. Neighbours: structural discrimination, Article 15(3) enabling special provisions for women.

qs.stem: Which programme suggested textbook revision and gender sensitisation of educational staff?
qs.sol:
The Programme of Action under the National Policy on Education translated policy recommendations into operational steps.

Its agenda included revising learning materials and sensitising educational personnel about gender.
qs.rel: The Programme of Action (POA) 1992 under NPE 1986 recommended gender-sensitive textbooks and orientation of educational staff. Neighbours: NPE 1986 'education for women's equality', Mahila Samakhya 1988.

qs.stem: किस वर्ष के अध्ययन से पता चला है कि, पुरुष और महिलाएं अपने अन्योन्याश्रयता प्रकार में भिन्न हैं?
qs.sol: गेब्रियल और गार्डनर के 1999 के अध्ययन “Are There ‘His’ and ‘Hers’ Types of Interdependence?” में महिलाओं और पुरुषों की संबंधपरक तथा सामूहिक परस्पर निर्भरता का परीक्षण किया गया।
qs.rel: Studies of interdependence/independence show gender differences in self-construal (Markus and Kitayama 1991). Neighbours: Gilligan's ethics of care, Carol Gilligan critique of Kohlberg, gender-linked socialisation.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विकल्प ‘जेंडर’ की अवधारणा से संबंधित नहीं है?

opts.A: यह किसी व्यक्ति की जैविक विशेषताओं को संदर्भित करता है
opts.B: अलग-अलग समाजों में अलग-अलग तरीकों से निर्मित
opts.C: यह सामाजिक रूप से निर्मित भूमिकाओं और मानदंडों को संदर्भित करता है
opts.D: दैनिक जीवन में अपनाए जाने वाले सामाजिक रूप से सीखे गए व्यवहार

qs.sol:
अवधारणा

जेंडर से आशय व्यक्तियों से संबद्ध सामाजिक रूप से निर्मित भूमिकाओं, अपेक्षाओं, पहचानों और व्यवहार-प्रतिरूपों से है। ये अर्थ सीखे जाते हैं और विभिन्न संस्कृतियों तथा कालखंडों में भिन्न हो सकते हैं।

विश्लेषणात्मक दृष्टि से यह जैविक लिंग से भिन्न है, जो जैविक एवं शरीर-क्रियात्मक विशेषताओं के आधार पर व्यक्तियों का वर्गीकरण करता है।

अनुप्रयोग

जैविक विशेषताओं से संबंधित वाक्यांश जैविक लिंग का वर्णन करता है, जबकि अन्य कथन सांस्कृतिक विविधता, सामाजिक भूमिकाओं एवं मानदंडों अथवा सामाजिक रूप से सीखे गए व्यवहार का वर्णन करते हैं। अतः जैविक विशेषताओं से संबंधित कथन यहाँ प्रयुक्त अर्थ में जेंडर की अवधारणा से संबंधित नहीं है।

अंतर

जैविक विशेषताएँ शारीरिक एवं शरीर-क्रियात्मक वर्गीकरण से संबंधित …
qs.rel: Gender is a social construct (roles, behaviours) rather than a fixed biological characteristic; it varies across cultures. Neighbours: sex is biological; gender identity; gender stereotypes.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are NOT correct?

I. Gender is a socio-cultural construct.

II. Sex is systemic.
qs.sol: Two different categories are at work here. Sex is the biological category — male or female — fixed by anatomy, physiology and genetics. Gender is the socio-cultural construct a society builds on top of that category: the roles, norms, expectations and institutions it assigns to each sex. Because gender is produced and sustained through social arrangements rather than by biology, it is gender that is described as relational, hierarchical, historical, contextually specific and systemic; sex, being biological, is not. …
qs.rel: Gender is a socio-cultural construct; sex is biological, not 'systemic'. Neighbours: sex ratio vs gender gap, gender parity index (GPI), gender equity.

qs.stem: Regional bias can be mitigated in schools by one of the following, choose the correct answer from the following.
qs.sol:
Regional bias involves prejudiced interpretations of communities and their past.

Purposeful history teaching can present balanced evidence and shared heritage.

It directly addresses those prejudices.
qs.rel: Regional bias is reduced by purposive teaching of history and culture that values different regions and communities. Neighbours: national integration, multicultural education (James Banks), unity in diversity.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन लिंग संवेदनशीलता को दर्शाता है? I. कुछ संस्कृतियों में, महिलाओं को गाड़ी चलाने की अनुमति नहीं है। II. लड़के तथा लड़कियों के लिए विभिन्न शौचालय की व्यवस्था करना।

opts.D: ना ही I ना ही II

qs.sol: लिंग संवेदनशीलता का अर्थ है लड़कों और लड़कियों की अलग-अलग आवश्यकताओं और अनुभवों के प्रति जागरूक रहना और दोनों के लिए निष्पक्षता और गरिमा सुनिश्चित करने के लिए कार्य करना। लड़के और लड़कियों के लिए अलग शौचालय की व्यवस्था निजता और सुरक्षा की वास्तविक आवश्यकता पूरी करती है; ऐसे शौचालयों का अभाव लड़कियों के स्कूल छोड़ने का एक ज्ञात कारण है, इसलिए कथन II लिंग संवेदनशीलता दर्शाता है। महिलाओं को गाड़ी चलाने की अनुमति न देना लैंगिक रूढ़ियों पर आधारित भेदभावपूर्ण प्रतिबंध है, इसलिए कथन I लैंगिक पूर्वाग्रह दर्शाता है। अतः केवल II सही है।
qs.rel: Gender sensitivity means recognising and responding to gender inequalities and avoiding stereotypes. Neighbours: gender awareness, gender mainstreaming, gender-responsive budgeting, inclusive language.

qs.stem: How do classroom processes reproduce gender in school?

opts.B: Boys handling art and crafts only.
opts.C: Mixed gender teams for all projects.
opts.D: Separate seating for boys and girls.

qs.sol: Separate seating by gender can reinforce gender divisions in everyday classroom practice. Mixed and equitable participation challenges such reproduction of gender roles.
qs.rel: Separate seating, task division and unequal teacher attention reproduce gender in schools (hidden curriculum). Neighbours: teacher expectations, textbook imagery, gender-segregated sports.

qs.stem: जिन लोगों की यौन विशेषताओं में भिन्नता होती है जो सामान्य पुरुष या महिला शरीर के साथ अनुरूप नहीं होते हैं। उन्हें _____ कहा जाता है।
qs.sol: इंटरसेक्स उन जन्मजात लैंगिक विशेषताओं को कहते हैं जो पुरुष या महिला शरीर की सामान्य द्विआधारी परिभाषा में नहीं आतीं।
qs.rel: People born with variations in sex characteristics not fitting male/female norms are intersex. Neighbours: transgender (identity differs from sex assigned at birth), third gender recognised in NALSA 2014, Transgender Act 2019.

qs.stem: What term refers to the unstated norms and practices within schools that implicitly teach gender roles?
qs.sol:
Concept

In educational sociology, the curriculum experienced in a school has two layers: the formally documented one that is written down and openly taught, and an unwritten layer of values, expectations, and behavioural patterns that students absorb simply by taking part in school life. This second, unwritten layer -- transmitted through routines, teacher-student interactions, discipline patterns, and everyday practices rather than through any official document -- is called the hidden curriculum.

Application

The question describes exactly this second layer: unstated norms and practices that implicitly teach gender roles. …
qs.rel: Hidden curriculum: unstated norms, practices and values schools convey (Jackson, 1968). Neighbours: formal, informal, null curriculum (Eisner); gender role reinforcement.

qs.stem: A teacher observes that classroom interactions often result in boys dominating science discussions. What instructional adjustment can best promote equitable participation?

opts.B: Designing turn-taking protocols during group discussions.
opts.C: Assigning boys to lead science discussions in classroom.
opts.D: Grouping students by their ability level.

qs.sol: Turn-taking protocols ensure that classroom discussion time is shared fairly, so they directly promote equitable participation when one group is dominating.
qs.rel: To counter boys dominating discussions, use turn-taking protocols, mixed groups and equal participation structures. Neighbours: teacher expectation effects, wait time, gender-responsive pedagogy.

qs.stem: How can a teacher free the resources used in the classroom from gender bias?

opts.B: By giving training on gender roles
opts.D: By fixing gender quotas for leaders

qs.sol: Classroom resources become free from gender bias when the teacher reviews textbooks and learning materials for stereotypes, unequal representation and biased language. Such review helps identify and replace biased content with inclusive examples and images.
qs.rel: Free classroom resources from bias by reviewing biased textbooks and using inclusive images and examples. Neighbours: gender audit, NCERT textbook review, representation of women.

qs.stem: कु छ लड़के और लड़कियां जन्मजात अधिवृक्क अतिविकसन (कन्जेनिटल एड्रेनल ह्यपरप्लासिए) नाम की अवस्था के साथ पैदा होते हैं, जिसके कारण उनमें निम्नलिखित में से क्या होता है?

opts.A: उनके गैर-प्रभावित साथियों की तुलना में ऐन्ड्र जन का स्तर काफी अधिक है
opts.B: दू सरों की तुलना में अपनी शारीरिक बनावट के बारे में कम परवाह करना
opts.C: लड़की या लड़के जोड़ीदार के साथ खेलने से बचने के लिए; पारं परिक स्त्रैण घटनाओं के इर्द-गिर्द घूमने वाले खेल न खेलना
opts.D: लड़कियों को ऐसा व्यवहार करने के लिए दृढ़ता से प्रभावित करना जैसे कि वे लड़के हों या इसके विपरीत।

qs.sol: जन्मजात अधिवृक्क अतिविकसन से ऐन्ड्रोजन स्तर बढ़ सकता है।
qs.rel: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) can cause genetically female children to have male-typed genitalia and behaviour: a case of biological influences on gender identity. Neighbours: sex chromosomes XX/XY, Klinefelter, Turner syndromes.

qs.sol: “अंतर्विभागीयता ढाँचा” सही है, क्योंकि अंतर्विभागीयता ढाँचा जेंडर और दिव्यांगता जैसी परस्पर जुड़ी स्थितियों से उत्पन्न बाधाओं को साथ में समझता है। “मास्लो की आवश्यकताओं का पदानुक्रम” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि मास्लो का आवश्यकता पदानुक्रम सामान्य मानवीय जरूरतें बताता है, लेकिन इन पहचानों के संयुक्त प्रभाव का विश्लेषण नहीं करता।
qs.rel: Intersectionality (Kimberle Crenshaw) analyses how gender, disability, caste, class overlap to create compounded disadvantage. Neighbours: multiple marginalisation, inclusive policy, feminist theory.

qs.stem: Which statement best summarizes Indian attitudes towards political leadership and gender roles at home?

opts.A: Society equally supports women’s leadership and shared domestic responsibilities
opts.B: Society accepts women as political leaders but expects traditional domestic roles
opts.C: Society rejects women’s leadership while supporting equality within households
opts.D: Society discourages women's political participation while promoting domestic independence

qs.sol: The statement summarizes a mixed attitude: women may be accepted in political leadership, but traditional domestic roles are still expected at home.
qs.rel: Indian attitudes accept women as political leaders yet often expect traditional roles at home: a gap between public and private spheres. Neighbours: reservation for women in Panchayati Raj (73rd Amendment, 33%), women's reservation Act 2023.

qs.stem: लगभग सभी उदाहरणों में लिंग पहचान को ___ के रूप में स्वयं पहचाना जाता है

opts.A: पुरुष या महिला होने की निजी अनुभूति
opts.B: अंतर्निहित और बाहरी या पर्यावरणीय कारकों के संयोजन का परिणाम
opts.C: यह समाज के भीतर व्यवहार और उपस्थिति जैसे देखने योग्य कारकों द्वारा प्रकट होता है।
opts.D: यह व्यक्ति का अपना व्यक्तिपरक अनुभव है

qs.sol: आधिकारिक प्रश्नपत्र से संशोधित: बोर्ड के प्रीव्यू में “अंतर्निहित और बाहरी या पर्यावरणीय कारकों के संयोजन का परिणाम” चिह्नित है, पर यह संभावित प्रभाव बताता है, पहचान स्वयं नहीं। “यह व्यक्ति का अपना व्यक्तिपरक अनुभव है” लैंगिक पहचान का सबसे उपयुक्त वर्णन है। “पुरुष या महिला होने की निजी अनुभूति” इससे संबंधित किंतु सीमित है।
qs.rel: Gender identity is a person's self-identified sense of being male, female, neither or both. Neighbours: gender expression, sexual orientation, assigned sex at birth, Kohlberg's gender constancy.

qs.stem: देवदासी प्रणाली भारत के किस हिस्से में प्रचलित थी?
qs.sol: देवदासी प्रथा ऐतिहासिक रूप से दक्षिणी भारत में प्रचलित थी।
qs.rel: Devadasi system: girls dedicated to temples, prevalent in South India (Karnataka, Andhra, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra); banned in Karnataka in 1982. Neighbours: Madras Devadasis Act 1947, social reform of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Muthulakshmi Reddy.

qs.stem: प्रारंभिक बचपन में लिंग पहचान के संदर्भ में सबसे प्रभावशाली कारक कौनसा है?

opts.A: माता-पिता, परिवार के सदस्य और देखभाल करने वाले

qs.sol: माता-पिता, परिवार और देखभाल करने वाले सबसे पहले और लगातार प्रभाव डालते हैं।
qs.rel: Early gender identity is influenced chiefly by family, particularly parents, through modelling and differential treatment. Neighbours: gender constancy by 6-7 years (Kohlberg), gender schema (Bem), toys and clothing.

qs.stem: Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques(Regulation and Prevention of Misuse) Act,1994, is a constitutional guarantee that checks on:
qs.sol: The Act regulates prenatal diagnostic techniques to prevent sex selection and female foeticide.
qs.rel: PCPNDT Act 1994 prohibits sex determination and female foeticide. Neighbours: MTP Act 1971, Dowry Prohibition Act 1961, Child Marriage Restraint Act, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (2015).

qs.sol: विज्ञापन पुरुषों और महिलाओं को तयशुदा भूमिकाओं में दिखाते हैं; यह लैंगिक रूढ़ धारणा है।
qs.rel: Advertisements show men and women in stereotyped roles, reinforcing gender stereotypes. Neighbours: media socialisation, gender-sensitive media literacy, hidden curriculum.

qs.stem:
Complete the sentence with the most appropriate option from the following.

In the Devadasi system young girls are:

opts.A: Dedicated to the temples in the name of their families
opts.B: Offered to fire in name of Gods and Goddesses
opts.C: Offered to fire in the name of their families
opts.D: Dedicated to temples in the name of Gods and Goddesses

qs.sol: The Devadasi custom dedicated girls to temples in the name of deities, rather than offering them to fire.
qs.rel: In the Devadasi system young girls are dedicated to temples in the name of God, often leading to sexual exploitation. Neighbours: Basavi/Jogini in Karnataka and Andhra, legal prohibition, social reform movements.

topics.deep:
- **Sex vs gender:** sex = biological, fixed (chromosomes XX/XY, hormones), universal, nature-made; gender = socially and culturally constructed roles, behaviours and expectations that vary by time, place and culture (Ann Oakley, Simone de Beauvoir: "one is not born, but becomes a woman"). **Gender identity** = self-identified sense; **gender expression**; **sexual orientation**; intersex = variation in sex characteristics; **transgender** = identity differs from sex assigned at birth (Susan Stryker - umbrella term for identities that challenge gender norms). **Judith Butler**: gender is performative (Gender Trouble, 1990).
- **Concepts:**

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Gender equality | equal rights, opportunities, treatment |
| Gender equity | fairness; measures to compensate disadvantages |
| Gender parity | numerical equality (GPI = girls/boys ratio) |
| Gender-neutral policy | makes no distinction between genders |
| Gender-sensitive | recognises differences and responds |
| Gender mainstreaming | integrating gender perspective in all policies |
| Patriarchy | male dominance in society and family |
| Gender stereotype | fixed belief about roles (blue = boys) |
| Glass ceiling | invisible barrier to women's advancement |
| Intersectionality | overlapping disadvantages (Crenshaw) |

- **Gender socialisation:** learning gender roles from family (most influential in early childhood), school, peers, media, religion, community. Theories: **Mead's symbolic interactionism**, Cooley's looking-glass self, Bandura's social learning, **Kohlberg's gender constancy** (identity, stability, constancy by ~6-7 years), **Bem's gender schema**, Freud's identification. Agents of socialisation do not include heredity. Hidden curriculum (Jackson 1968) = unstated norms that teach gender roles (separate seating, task division, textbook imagery).
- **Sources of gender discrimination:** unequal division of labour at home, son preference, unequal education and employment opportunities, government and legal biases, customs (dowry, purdah), media advertisements, textbooks, school practices. Discrimination can be direct/indirect, institutional.
- **Demographics:** Census 2011 sex ratio **943** (options near 940); **child sex ratio (0-6) 914** (2001: 927); Kerala highest (1084), Haryana lowest in child sex ratio; female literacy about 65% vs male about 82%. Causes of decline: sex-selective abortion using amniocentesis/ultrasound, female infanticide.
- **Laws and schemes:** Equal Remuneration Act 1976, Dowry Prohibition Act 1961, **PCPNDT Act 1994**, Maternity Benefit Act 1961 (amended 2017), Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005, **POSH Act 2013** (Vishakha guidelines 1997), Transgender Persons Act 2019, NALSA v. Union of India 2014 (third gender), 73rd/74th Amendments (33% reservation), Women's Reservation Act 2023. Education: **KGBV (2004)**, NPEGEL (2003), Mahila Samakhya (1988), Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (2015), Sukanya Samriddhi, NPE 1986 "education for women's equality", Programme of Action 1992 (textbook revision, gender sensitisation of staff), National Policy for Empowerment of Women 2001.
- **Gender-fair classroom:** equal expectations, mixed-gender groups and pairs (build interpersonal skills, confidence, assertiveness), turn-taking protocols to stop male dominance in science talk, gender audit of textbooks and visuals, non-sexist language, role models, safe school environment, girl-friendly toilets, gender-sensitive career guidance.
- **Biological influences:** congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) can virilise genetic females; boys and girls have similar nutritional needs until adolescence (~7-9/puberty).
- **Devadasi system:** girls dedicated to temples, practised in South India (Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra); prohibited in Karnataka 1982 and Andhra 1988; Madras Devadasis (Prevention of Dedication) Act 1947. Other social evils: sati (banned 1829, Raja Ram Mohan Roy), child marriage (Sarda Act 1929; PCMA 2006).
- **Related diversity issues:** regional bias, caste and tribal marginalisation, minority rights (Article 30), multicultural education.

**Likely question angles:**
- Sex vs gender - which feature belongs to which.
- Gender-neutral vs gender-sensitive vs gender-aware policies.
- Census sex ratio and child sex ratio figures; highest/lowest states.
- Laws: PCPNDT, POSH, Dowry, Equal Remuneration - year and purpose.
- Agent of socialisation not valid (heredity).
- Hidden curriculum examples; who coined the term.
- Theorists: Butler, Mead, Bem, Kohlberg (gender constancy).
- KGBV, NPEGEL, Mahila Samakhya features.
- Teacher strategies to reduce gender bias.
- Meaning of intersex/transgender/third gender and laws.

topics.title: 8. Teaching Methods, Lesson Planning & Teaching-Learning Material
topics.theory:
- **Approach** (philosophy) > **method** (plan) > **technique** (device): drill is a technique. Teaching phases (Jackson): pre-active, interactive, post-active.
- **Methods and exponents:** Project - **Kilpatrick**; Heuristic - **Armstrong**; Dalton - Parkhurst; Brainstorming - **Osborn**; Socratic = question-answer; Kindergarten - Froebel; Montessori; Tutorial = small ability groups.
- **Herbartian five steps:** preparation, presentation, association, **generalisation** (formulating rules), application. 5E: engage, explore, explain, elaborate, evaluate.
- **Lesson plan:** what/whom/how; first step = learning objectives; backward design starts with desired outcomes (Wiggins and McTighe). Objectives need **observable verbs** (list, define), not 'know'.
- **Bloom's taxonomy:** remember, understand, apply, analyse, evaluate, create; Krathwohl's affective domain begins at **receiving**.
- **Micro-teaching** (Dwight Allen, 1963): practise one skill with few students; plan-teach-feedback-replan-reteach-refeed.
- **Inductive** (particular -> general; science, grammar, maths) vs **deductive** (general -> particular, top-down); discussion integrates participants' contributions.
- **Teacher-centred** (memorising, extrinsic motivation) vs **learner-centred** (interaction, intrinsic motivation, differentiated tasks); PCK coined by **Lee Shulman** (1986).
- **TLM** = Teaching Learning Material; low-cost/no-cost aids (leaves, stones); criteria: relevant, simple, durable, multi-use; Dale's cone.
- Classroom management: ability grouping may label students; boredom causes indiscipline; teacher improves physical climate; co-curricular participation must be voluntary.

qs.stem: Learning can occur:

opts.D: only from books and written material

qs.sol: “anywhere, anytime and from anyone” is correct: Learning can take place through everyday experience, interaction and varied settings at different times. “only within the classroom” fails: A classroom is one learning setting, but it is not the only one.
qs.rel: Learning is lifelong and occurs anywhere, anytime, from anyone: formal, non-formal, informal. Neighbours: Delors' four pillars, lifelong learning (UNESCO), open and distance learning, Faure Commission 1972 'Learning to Be'.

qs.stem: ________ is the full form of TLM.
qs.sol:
No official answer key was published for this paper; the answer is worked out from the question.

TLM denotes materials used to support teaching and learning.

The initials expand to Teaching, Learning and Material in that order.
qs.rel: TLM = Teaching Learning Material: charts, models, flashcards, real objects, low-cost/no-cost aids. Neighbours: TLA, Dale's Cone of Experience, criteria: relevance, durability, simplicity, safety.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is a function of a teacher?

1. Maintaining record of pupil's attendance.

2. Planning for curricular and co-curricular activities.

Choose the correct code.
qs.sol: Maintaining attendance records and planning curricular and co-curricular activities are both teacher duties.
qs.rel: Teacher functions: planning, teaching, evaluating, record-keeping, guiding, co-curricular organisation, community liaison. Neighbours: NCTE roles, teacher as facilitator, counsellor and researcher.

qs.stem: Which of the following best supports active learning in the classroom?

opts.B: Participating in group discussions and activities
opts.D: Listening to a long lecture without interaction

qs.sol: “Participating in group discussions and activities” is correct: Discussion and shared activities require learners to contribute, reason and respond to peers. “Reading a textbook silently” fails: Silent textbook reading can aid study but does not by itself provide the same interactive participation.
qs.rel: Active learning: group discussion, projects, problem solving, role-play, think-pair-share. Neighbours: Bonwell and Eison, constructivism, flipped classroom, passive rote learning contrast.

qs.stem:
Which of the following types of home-assignement can be given to the students?

1. Informational

2. Study type

Choose the correct code.
qs.sol: “Both 1 and 2” is supported: Informational and study-type assignments are both recognised forms of home assignment. By contrast, “Only 1” only 1 excludes the valid study-type assignment.
qs.rel: Home assignments may be informational, study type, practice/drill, creative and project-based. Neighbours: purposes - revision, self-study; principles - clarity, appropriateness, timely feedback.

qs.stem: Text book can be used as _______________.
qs.sol:
Note on the answer key: DSSSB published only a provisional answer key for this paper, and no final key. The provisional key marks “study of a subject”, which is the graded answer here. “reading” is also defensible, because a textbook is also used by reading it.

A textbook organizes material for systematic study of a subject. Reading is a normal way of using it, so the broad wording allows both readings. Entertainment and writing are possible activities around books but do not describe the textbook’s central instructional purpose.
qs.rel: Textbook: a standard instructional resource for study of a subject. Neighbours: NCERT textbooks, workbooks, reference books, characteristics (accuracy, graded content), NCF 2005 on reducing textbook burden.

qs.stem:
Which of the following should be the criteria for selection of resources for teaching?

1. Usefulness

2. Clarity

3. Simplicity

Use the correct code.
qs.sol: “1, 2 and 3” is supported because usefulness, clarity and simplicity all make a teaching resource effective. “Only 1 and 2” omits simplicity, although a resource must also be easy for learners to use.
qs.rel: Lesson plan components: what to teach (content/objectives), whom (learner characteristics), how (methods, TLM, evaluation). Neighbours: Herbartian five steps, Bloom's RCEM format, Gagné's events.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are the component(s) of Lesson Plan?
 I. What to teach
 II. Who to teach
 III. How to teach
qs.sol: A lesson plan must consider what to teach, who to teach and how to teach. These cover content, learner context and method.
qs.rel: Resource selection criteria: usefulness, clarity, simplicity, relevance, cost, durability, learner interest. Neighbours: low-cost/no-cost TLM, community resources, inclusive classrooms.

qs.stem: How does experiential learning in the classroom benefit students?

opts.C: It leads to cognitive, attitudinal, and behavioural changes

qs.sol: Experiential learning benefits students by fostering cognitive, attitudinal, and behavioural changes through active engagement. This approach promotes holistic development beyond simple memory retention or social limitation.
qs.rel: Experiential learning builds cognitive, attitudinal and behavioural change through doing and reflection. Neighbours: Kolb's cycle, Dewey, field trips, internships, project work.

qs.stem: What is essential for achieving equal educational opportunities in a society?
qs.sol: Equal opportunity in education depends on equality in the wider social system. “Technological advancement” can improve access, but equipment by itself cannot remove social inequality that limits educational opportunity.
qs.rel: Effective learning activities involve spontaneous involvement and appropriate challenge. Neighbours: Vygotsky's ZPD, flow, learner-centred tasks, interest and effort.

qs.stem: कौन सा शब्द लैटिन शब्द 'कॉग्नोस्क्रेरे' से व्युत्पन्न है?
qs.sol: 'Cognition' का संबंध जानने, पहचानने और समझने की मानसिक प्रक्रियाओं से है। इस शब्द का व्युत्पत्तिगत संबंध लैटिन 'cognoscere' से बताया जाता है, जिसका अर्थ जानना है। प्रश्न में छपा लैटिन रूप वर्तनी में थोड़ा अलग है, लेकिन लक्षित शब्द स्पष्ट है। पाठ्यक्रम शिक्षण-योजना है, रचनात्मकता नया विचार पैदा करने की क्षमता है और अवधारणा किसी विचार का मानसिक रूप है; इनका दिया गया शब्द-मूल समान नहीं। इसलिए व्युत्पत्ति और अर्थ दोनों को साथ देखकर संज्ञान से संबंधित अंग्रेज़ी शब्द चुनना चाहिए।
qs.rel: Textbooks give structured, graded content and a common curriculum base. Neighbours: workbooks, teacher's guide, reference books; limitations - rote learning, single view.

qs.stem:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन से लैंगिक भेदभाव के स्रोत और रूप हैं?
I. घर के अंदर श्रम का विभाजन
II. नियुक्ति, पदोन्नति, नियुक्ति
III. कानून और नियम
qs.sol: लैंगिक भेदभाव घर के भीतर असमान श्रम विभाजन, नौकरी में नियुक्ति या पदोन्नति के पक्षपात और भेदकारी कानून या नियमों से पैदा हो सकता है। ये क्रमशः परिवार, कार्यस्थल और संस्था के स्तर पर दिखते हैं। प्रश्न स्रोत और रूप दोनों पूछता है, इसलिए केवल रोजगार या कानून लेने से असमानता का एक अलग क्षेत्र छूट जाएगा। कथन I को छोड़ना घरेलू श्रम के असमान विभाजन की अनदेखी करता है, जो भेदभाव का एक स्रोत है। केवल नौकरी के फैसले घरेलू और कानूनी असमानता नहीं समेटते। घर, कार्यस्थल और संस्थागत व्यवस्था तीनों भेदभाव बनाए रख सकती हैं। केवल नियम लेने से घरेलू काम और रोजगार पक्षपात छूटते हैं।
qs.rel: Micro-teaching (Dwight Allen, Stanford 1963): practising a specific teaching skill with few students in short 5-10 minutes lesson, with feedback. Neighbours: cycle - plan, teach, feedback, re-plan, re-teach, re-feed.

qs.stem: In the teaching-learning process, what is the primary function of textbooks?
qs.sol: Textbooks primarily function to provide structured content that organizes curriculum material systematically for learners. This resource supports the teaching process without replacing the teacher's role in instruction.
qs.rel: Drill is a teaching technique (not method or approach); approach = philosophy, method = overall plan, technique = classroom device. Neighbours: Anthony's model - approach, method, technique.

qs.stem:
समावेशी शिक्षा को कौन सा कारक प्रभावित करता है?

I. मूल्यांकन प्रणाली

II. शिक्षक की तैयारी

III. शिक्षार्थियों के बीच विविधता
qs.sol: समावेशी शिक्षा का उद्देश्य अक्षमता वाले और वंचित समूहों के बच्चों सहित सभी बच्चों को नियमित कक्षाओं में साथ पढ़ाना है। इसकी सफलता कई कारकों पर निर्भर करती है। हर बच्चे की एक ही तरह से परीक्षा लेने वाली कठोर मूल्यांकन प्रणाली उन शिक्षार्थियों को बाहर कर सकती है जिन्हें अनुकूलित आकलन चाहिए। शिक्षकों को विभेदित शिक्षण अपनाने और सामग्री को अनुकूल बनाने के लिए प्रशिक्षित और तैयार होना चाहिए। क्षमताओं, भाषाओं और पृष्ठभूमि में शिक्षार्थियों की विविधता यह तय करती है कि पाठ्यचर्या और सहायता की योजना कैसे बने। इसलिए तीनों कारक समावेशी शिक्षा को प्रभावित करते हैं।
qs.rel: Experiential (learning by doing) method stresses active participation. Neighbours: project method (Kilpatrick), Dewey, heuristic method (Armstrong), laboratory method.

qs.stem: बहुभाषी होने का एक प्रमुख मनोवैज्ञानिक लाभ क्या है?

opts.B: चिंतन में अनुकूलन की योग्यता में सुधार

qs.sol:
संकल्पना — बहुभाषिकता का अर्थ दो या अधिक भाषाओं का नियमित प्रयोग है। बहुभाषी वक्ता में दोनों भाषा-तंत्र एक ही समय सक्रिय रहते हैं; इसलिए किसी भी कथन को व्यक्त करने के लिए एक तंत्र का चयन करना और दूसरे को अवरुद्ध रखना आवश्यक होता है। चयन और अवरोध की यह बार-बार होने वाली प्रक्रिया मस्तिष्क के कार्यकारी-नियंत्रण तंत्र को प्रशिक्षित करती है, जो ध्यान, अवरोध तथा मानसिक विन्यासों के बीच अंतरण को नियंत्रित करता है।

अनुप्रयोग — प्रश्न बहुभाषी वक्ताओं में पाए जाने वाले मनोवैज्ञानिक अर्थात् संज्ञानात्मक लाभ के विषय में पूछता है। सुदृढ़ कार्यकारी नियंत्रण अधिक मानसिक अथवा संज्ञानात्मक लचीलेपन के रूप में प्रकट होता है; व्यक्ति नियमों, श्रेणियों, दृष्टिकोणों और कार्य की बदलती माँगों के बीच अधिक सहजता से …
qs.rel: Good TLM: multiple utility, relevant, durable, simple, attractive, inexpensive, safe. Neighbours: improvised aids, audio-visual aids classification, Dale's cone.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of a Good Teaching Learning Material? I. Material of multiple utility II. Material should have utilitarian value
qs.sol: Useful teaching and learning material can serve multiple instructional purposes and also have practical value for learners’ tasks. Multiple utility allows a teacher to reuse or adapt it across examples and activities; utilitarian value helps it connect with meaningful learning outcomes. Since both characteristics make material more effective and economical, the two statements can stand together.
qs.rel: Team spirit develops through shared goals and cooperative activity. Neighbours: cooperative learning (Johnson), jigsaw, group dynamics, leadership.

qs.stem: Which of the following best describes hyperlexia in children with autism spectrum disorders?

opts.D: Difficulty understanding and using social language despite strong decoding skills

qs.sol: Hyperlexia may involve advanced word decoding alongside difficulty with comprehension and social use of language. “Complete absence of verbal communication” does not fit: complete absence of speech is not required for this reading profile.
qs.rel: Inductive-deductive approach suits science, grammar and mathematics. Neighbours: induction (particular to general), deduction (general to particular), Aristotle vs Bacon, Socratic method.

qs.stem: How can e-classrooms be adapted for students with hearing impairments?

opts.A: By providing closed captions and sign language interpreters
opts.B: By increasing the volume of lectures

qs.sol: “By providing closed captions and sign language interpreters” gives students with hearing impairments visual access to spoken teaching and discussion. “By increasing the volume of lectures” may help some learners with residual hearing, but it does not make speech reliably accessible to all deaf or hard-of-hearing students.
qs.rel: Reflective teacher education asks trainees to reason about methods and their effects (Schon, Dewey, Kolb). Neighbours: reflective journal, Gibbs cycle, action research.

qs.stem: In which year did E. L. Thorndike develop the theory of trial and error learning?
qs.sol: “1913”: The board associates this year with Thorndike’s account in The Psychology of Learning, so the printed key is retained. “1912”: This preceding year does not identify that publication; Thorndike’s original trial-and-error experiments began earlier than any year offered here.
qs.rel: First guide in selecting learning resources: learners' interests, context and needs. Neighbours: curriculum alignment, availability, cost, inclusivity.

qs.stem:
Choose the most appropriate option.

Technology that has affected the sex ratio is:
qs.sol: Prenatal diagnostic technologies can identify fetal sex; their misuse for sex-selective decisions has affected the sex ratio.
qs.rel: Families know the child and can provide information for suitable educational support. Neighbours: parent-teacher partnership, home-school links, IEP participation.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are the special feature(s) of Kasturbha Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya?
 I. Providing residential facilities to create a free environment for learning /
 II. Providing life skill trainings
 III. Providing extra coaching for slow learners
qs.sol: Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya provides residential support, life-skill training and extra academic support/coaching for learners who need it.
qs.rel: Deductive reasoning is top-down (general to specific); inductive is bottom-up. Neighbours: hypothetico-deductive method, syllogism, scientific method steps.

qs.stem: भारत में शिक्षा का 10+2+3 पैटर्न किस वर्ष शुरू किया गया था?
qs.sol: कोठारी आयोग द्वारा सुझाया गया 10+2+3 शिक्षा पैटर्न, कुंजी के अनुसार, भारत में 1975 में शुरू किया गया।
qs.rel: Effective methods give scope for peer learning and active participation. Neighbours: cooperative learning, ZPD, collaborative learning, think-pair-share.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are the special feature(s) of Kasturbha Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya?
 I. Providing residential facilities to create a free environment for learning /
 II. Providing life skill trainings
 III. Providing extra coaching for slow learners
qs.sol: Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya provides residential support, life-skill training and extra academic support/coaching for learners who need it.
qs.rel: Quality time of parents supports child development and attachment. Neighbours: parenting styles (Baumrind: authoritative, authoritarian, permissive), Bowlby attachment.

qs.stem: David Kolb, an educational researcher, developed a ____________ reflective model.
