qs.sol: Kolb’s experiential learning cycle has four stages: concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualisation and active experimentation. “three-stage” does not fit: three stages omit a phase of Kolb's experience-reflection-concept-action cycle.
qs.rel: Teachers should build meaningful collaboration among students for shared learning. Neighbours: cooperative vs competitive learning, jigsaw, peer tutoring.

qs.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.

The latest trend in language teaching is that:

opts.A: Special emphasis is given to grammar teaching
opts.B: Grammar is taught in special periods
opts.C: Grammar is integrated with the text and taught contextually

qs.sol: Contextual language teaching integrates grammar with the text so learners see how forms work in use.
qs.rel: Brainstorming (Osborn): group generates many ideas without criticism. Neighbours: synectics, buzz sessions, role-play, case method, discussion.

qs.stem:
Which of the following are those teaching–learning materials that are prepared by teachers and students in most of the schools?
 I. Graphs
 II. Number and alphabet cards
 III. Flash cards on different themes
qs.sol: Graphs, number/alphabet cards and flash cards are common teaching-learning materials prepared by teachers and students in schools.
qs.rel: TLM prepared by teachers/students: graphs, number/alphabet cards, flashcards, charts, models. Neighbours: low-cost aids, improvisation, teaching aids classification.

qs.stem:
______ is the key process of teacher-centered approach.

I. Memorizing 

II. Recalling from memory
qs.sol: In a teacher-centered or traditional approach, the teacher controls the teaching process and students often learn by memorizing content and recalling it from memory. Therefore, both memorizing and recalling from memory are key processes in this approach.
qs.rel: Teacher-centred approach emphasises memorising and recalling; teacher is authority. Neighbours: lecture method, rote learning, behaviourist view, exam-oriented.

qs.stem: कौन सी नीति लिंग के बीच कोई अंतर नहीं करती है?
qs.sol: जो नीति लिंग के आधार पर कोई भेद नहीं करती और सभी पर एक समान नियम लागू करती है, उसे लिंग-तटस्थ नीति कहते हैं; वह लिंग को प्रासंगिक श्रेणी नहीं मानती। लिंग-जागरूक नीति लिंग से जुड़ी परिस्थितियों को स्पष्ट रूप से पहचानती है। लिंग-समानता नीति समान अवसर या परिणाम के लक्ष्य से चलती है और इसके लिए असमान प्रारम्भिक स्थितियों को पहचानकर अलग उपाय भी कर सकती है, इसलिए उसका अर्थ ‘‘कोई अंतर न करना’’ नहीं है। लिंग-विशिष्ट नीति किसी एक लिंग या अलग-अलग लिंगों के लिए अलग उपाय बनाती है। अतः ‘‘कोई अंतर नहीं करती’’ का संकेत लिंग-तटस्थ नीति की ओर है।
qs.rel: Financial resources of a school: grants, allocations, funds. Neighbours: human resources (teachers), physical resources (library, labs), time as resource, community resources.

qs.stem: A teacher designs a lesson that blends scientific inquiry, connects topics, and adapts for all abilities. Which teaching method is being applied?
qs.sol: A lesson that blends inquiry, connects topics and adapts for all abilities uses an integrated and inclusive approach.
qs.rel: TLM = Teaching Learning Materials. Neighbours: TLM Mela, NCERT Teaching Aids, Operation Blackboard (1987) provided TLM.

qs.stem: Learning is a complex process that leads to what type of growth in individuals?
qs.sol:
Learning modifies knowledge, understanding and ways of thinking through experience.

These changes principally describe mental growth in the classification asked.
qs.rel: Activity-learning materials must be relevant, contextual, related to learners' lives and reusable. Neighbours: Activity Based Learning (Tamil Nadu), NCF 2005, play-way.

qs.stem: What is the primary goal of integrating language instruction across different subject areas?

opts.A: To help students develop effective communication skills that support learning and understanding across all subjects
opts.B: To assess students' language skills only during language arts instruction
opts.C: To restrict the use of language to language arts classes and exclude language instruction from other subjects
opts.D: To focus only on grammar and vocabulary in language arts classes

qs.sol: CONCEPT: According to the principle of 'Language Across the Curriculum', language is not merely a skill confined to the language arts classroom; it is also the medium through which ideas are understood, read, written about, discussed, and expressed in every subject, including science, social studies, and mathematics. Therefore, the purpose of integrating language instruction across all subject areas is to develop communication skills in students that strengthen learning and understanding in every subject. …
qs.rel: Learner-centred approach: peer interaction, intrinsic motivation, teacher as facilitator. Neighbours: constructivism, inquiry, activity-based learning, differentiated instruction.

qs.stem: Differentiated assessments in schools are an example of what factors that promotes inclusion?
qs.sol:
Differentiated assessment changes tasks, modes or expectations to suit learners’ needs.

That changes the educational process, so it is an educational modification supporting inclusion.
qs.rel: Problem solving supports experiential learning in higher education. Neighbours: Kolb's cycle, problem-based learning, simulation, internship.

qs.stem: According to Bandura (1977) how many distinct processes are involved in observational learning?
qs.sol: Bandura identified attention, retention, reproduction and motivation as four processes in observational learning.
qs.rel: Lesson planning begins with identifying learning objectives, then content, methods and TLM, then evaluation. Neighbours: backward design (Wiggins and McTighe), Bloom's taxonomy.

qs.stem: Which of the following best describes an activity-based approach in mathematics teaching?

opts.A: Providing only lectures and demonstrations to the whole class.
opts.B: Engaging students in hands-on activities to explore concepts.
opts.C: Giving students notes to read silently without discussion.
opts.D: Asking students to memorize formulas and rules without practice.

qs.sol: Concept: An activity-based approach in teaching is a constructivist method in which students learn by directly manipulating materials, performing hands-on tasks, and discovering mathematical relationships themselves, rather than by passively receiving ready-made information from the teacher. It rests on the principle that concepts understood through direct experience and self-activity are retained and applied better than those merely told or written down. …
qs.rel: Cross-collating sources demands evaluating credibility and relevance. Neighbours: critical thinking, information literacy, primary vs secondary sources.

qs.stem: How many general teaching moves were identified by Henderson in 1963 as being essential to teach any rule?
qs.sol: Henderson’s 1963 framework identifies four general teaching moves required to teach a rule.
qs.rel: Henderson (1963) described general teaching moves for teaching a rule (e.g. 4 moves). Neighbours: Herbartian steps, Gagne's nine events, Bruner's discovery.

qs.stem: Which concept involves respecting differences among students?
qs.sol: Respecting differences among students is the core idea of diversity. Homogeneity means sameness, not respect for differences.
qs.rel: Problem-solving tasks with real-life applications are authentic, learner-centred pedagogy. Neighbours: project-based learning, case study, inquiry-based learning.

qs.stem: कौन सा शिक्षा अभियान 2009 में शुरू किया गया था?
qs.sol: राष्ट्रीय माध्यमिक शिक्षा अभियान माध्यमिक शिक्षा के लिए 2009 में शुरू किया गया था।
qs.rel: Discussion method integrates participants' contributions, builds understanding. Neighbours: panel, symposium, seminar, debate; teacher as moderator.

qs.stem:
What is the fundamental objective of conducting a diagnostic evaluation in an

educational setting?
qs.sol:
Evaluation in teaching is commonly classified into three types by purpose and timing: diagnostic, formative, and summative. Diagnostic evaluation is conducted before or during instruction to pinpoint the specific learning difficulties, gaps, or misconceptions an individual learner has in a skill or content area, so the teacher can plan targeted remedial teaching.

Applying this to the question: the objective described, identifying learning difficulties, is exactly the defining function of diagnostic evaluation, distinguishing it from evaluation types that operate at other stages of instruction. …
qs.rel: Diversity: respecting differences among students (culture, ability, language). Neighbours: multicultural education (James Banks), inclusive classroom, differentiated teaching.

qs.stem:
Which of the following precautions should be taken while working with clay?

I. Using too much water makes the clay weak, and cracks may later develop in the slabs.

II. Children should maintain cleanliness and hygiene while working with clay.
qs.sol:
Concept

Safe clay work rests on two general principles: control the material's consistency and maintain hygienic handling. Excess water makes a clay body overly soft and increases uneven shrinkage during drying, while clean hands, tools, and work areas support safe classroom practice.

Application

Statement I applies material control: too much water weakens the clay body, so a slab is more likely to crack as it dries.

Statement II applies hygienic handling: children should keep themselves, their tools, and the work area clean while using clay.

Contrast

Only I considers material consistency but leaves out hygienic classroom practice. …
qs.rel: Cooperative discipline (Linda Albert): helps students understand each other's cooperation and positive behaviour. Neighbours: Canter's assertive discipline, Kounin, Glasser's choice theory, Skinner behaviour.

qs.stem: What are the two main features of ADHD?
qs.sol: ADHD is characterised by inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity. “Hyperactivity and social withdrawal” does not fit: social withdrawal is not one of the two defining ADHD symptom domains.
qs.rel: Low-cost/no-cost materials: leaves, stones, seeds, waste materials. Neighbours: improvisation, nature study, Activity kits, science kits.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a primary goal of development policies related to disability?

opts.A: To promote public awareness and inclusion
opts.B: To restrict access to public transportation
opts.C: To increase taxation on assistive devices
opts.D: To limit educational opportunities for persons with disabilities

qs.sol: “To promote public awareness and inclusion” supports equal participation by addressing barriers and attitudes toward disability. “To restrict access to public transportation” would create another barrier to participation, contrary to that goal.
qs.rel: Planning phase of teaching includes selecting objectives, content and methods; Jackson's phases: pre-active (planning), interactive, post-active (evaluation). Neighbours: Morrison's cycle.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is a key principle in creating an inclusive school for children

with special needs?

opts.A: Keeping children with special needs in separate classrooms
opts.C: Fostering an environment where all students learn together
opts.D: Providing special services only outside of school hours

qs.sol:
Concept: Inclusive education, as defined under India's Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (Section 2(m)) and by frameworks such as UNICEF, is an education system in which children with and without disabilities are educated together in the same classrooms and schools, with teaching, curriculum, and support adapted to the full range of learner needs, rather than separating students by ability or disability status.

Application: The option describing a shared environment where all students learn together directly reflects this principle: it centers the school's design on joint participation and common instructional spaces rather than on separation by need. …
qs.rel: Using varied materials in school is multi-resource/ multi-material approach (मिश्रित सामग्री). Neighbours: improvisation, resource room, resource persons.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a nature of science?

opts.A: Science is both a body of knowledge and a process.
opts.D: Science is a global human endeavor.

qs.sol: Science is open to everyone; exclusion is not a feature of its nature.
qs.rel: Board key is disputed for this item. Revise the core definitions of the topic and use elimination.

qs.stem: एक बच्चे के लिए प्राकृतिक नियमों की अवधारणा लगभग किस उम्र तक पूरी तरह विकसित हो जाती है?
qs.sol: भौतिक जगत की बच्चों की समझ के पियाजे के विवरण में व्याख्याएँ जीववादी और कृत्रिमवादी विचारों से हटकर अवैयक्तिक प्राकृतिक कारणों की ओर बढ़ती हैं; लगभग 12 वर्ष की आयु तक, जब बच्चा औपचारिक संक्रियात्मक चिंतन के निकट पहुँचता है, प्राकृतिक नियमों की अवधारणा लगभग पूरी तरह विकसित हो जाती है।
qs.rel: Stating objectives in terms of behavioural outcomes (Mager's ABCD) makes them observable and measurable. Neighbours: Bloom's cognitive taxonomy, observable verbs (list, define, solve).

qs.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.

Reflection on reading is said to be complete only when it includes:
qs.sol: Reflection requires interpreting what was read and discussing that interpretation; analysis and discussion complete the reflective process.
qs.rel: Teachers improve physical climate by seating, lighting, ventilation, cleanliness and getting repairs done. Neighbours: psychological climate, classroom management, safe environment.

qs.stem: The step ‘Generalization’ in the Herbartian model aims at which of the following?
qs.sol:
Concept: In the Herbartian lesson sequence, generalization moves from particular examples to a principle that applies beyond those examples. Comparison or association first identifies shared features; generalization then expresses the shared rule.

Application: The prompt asks for the aim of the Generalization step. After comparing lesson examples, learners formulate a general rule that can be used in further cases. This makes ‘Formulating universal rules’ the matching activity.

Repeating the entire lesson revisits content; it does not abstract a rule from the examples.

Providing entertainment seeks engagement rather than a general principle. …
qs.rel: Herbartian steps: preparation, presentation, association (comparison), generalisation, application. Generalisation formulates universal rules/principles. Neighbours: Herbart (German), Pestalozzi influence.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a characteristic of learning process?

opts.D: Learning is the outcome of the interaction of the individual with the environment

qs.sol: Learning can transfer from one situation to another, so calling it non-transferable is incorrect.
qs.rel: Teacher in ECCE: facilitator of play and observation, planner of theme-based integrated activities. Neighbours: ICDS, NCERT ECCE framework, NEP 2020 foundational stage.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is the most crucial consideration when selecting learning

resources for an inclusive classroom?

opts.A: The resource's appeal to the majority group in the class
opts.B: The teacher's familiarity with the resource
opts.D: The resource’s ability to meet diverse learning needs and abilities

qs.sol: Concept: Inclusive education requires that learning resources be selected primarily for their capacity to accommodate the full range of learner diversity — different abilities, paces, and support needs — rather than for convenience, popularity, or budget. This is the core principle behind Universal Design for Learning (UDL): a resource is judged by whether every learner can actually access and engage with it. …
qs.rel: Resource selection for inclusion must meet diverse learning needs. Neighbours: UDL, accessible formats, differentiated materials.

qs.stem:
According to Herbert Spencer education should aim at complete development. Which principle of curriculum

development aligns with this ideology?
qs.sol:
Spencer’s aim of complete development requires preparing learners for the various activities of life.

A curriculum that includes all activities covers that breadth rather than only one organisational feature.
qs.rel: Setting an agenda first gives meetings direction; relevant to team communication. Neighbours: minutes, agenda, effective meeting norms, facilitation.

qs.sol: “Oral motor skill therapy focusing on muscle tone and control” is correct: Therapy directed at oral muscle control and movement addresses the tongue, cheek and articulation difficulties described. “Kinesiology taping with strength training” fails: Kinesiology taping and general strength training do not specifically target the coordinated oral movements needed for speech.
qs.rel: Pedagogical content knowledge links content and teaching methods to learners' needs (Shulman 1986). Neighbours: TPACK, content knowledge, pedagogical knowledge.

qs.stem: जेंडर को परिभाषित कीजिए।

opts.C: पुरुषों और महिलाओं का विभेद करने वाली सांस्कृतिक और सामाजिक रचना
opts.D: पुरुषों और महिलाओं के बीच जैविक विभेद

qs.sol:
अवधारणा: समाजशास्त्र और शिक्षाशास्त्र में लिंग (Sex) और जेंडर (Gender) के बीच एक बुनियादी अंतर किया जाता है। लिंग जन्म के समय शरीर-रचना, प्रजनन अंगों व गुणसूत्रों के आधार पर तय होने वाला जैविक तथ्य है, जबकि जेंडर वे भूमिकाएँ, व्यवहार व अपेक्षाएँ हैं जिन्हें समाज और संस्कृति गढ़ते हैं तथा जो समय, स्थान व परिस्थिति के साथ बदल सकती हैं।

अनुप्रयोग: प्रश्न में जेंडर की परिभाषा पूछी गई है। दिए गए विकल्पों में "पुरुषों और महिलाओं का विभेद करने वाली सांस्कृतिक और सामाजिक रचना" यह विकल्प उपरोक्त अवधारणा से पूर्णतः मेल खाता है, क्योंकि यह इसे सामाजिक-सांस्कृतिक निर्माण के रूप में परिभाषित करता है, न कि किसी जैविक तथ्य के रूप में।

तुलना: शेष विकल्प निम्न कारणों से जेंडर की परिभाषा नहीं दर्शाते:

"जन् …
qs.rel: Peer assessment: students give feedback on peers' work quality. Neighbours: self assessment, formative assessment, rubrics.

qs.stem: ‘Listen and draw’ is a listening activity. This activity is particularly useful for checking ______. I. object vocabulary II. prepositions III. Colours and numbers
qs.sol: In “listen and draw,” learners follow spoken instructions to place and colour objects, often in particular numbers and spatial positions. The drawing can reveal whether they recognised object names, interpreted prepositions such as “under” or “beside,” and understood colours and numbers. All three categories can therefore be assessed through the same listening activity.
qs.rel: Convergent questions have one right answer; divergent have multiple valid answers (Guilford). Neighbours: Bloom's levels, questioning skills, wait time.

qs.stem: नए (beginner) शिक्षकों के लिए पाठ योजना (lesson plan) का मुख्य कार्य क्या है?

opts.A: यह सैद्धांतिक ज्ञान की आवश्यकता को समाप्त करती है।
opts.B: यह दैनिक कार्ययोजना प्रदान करती है।
opts.C: यह विद्यार्थियों की ग्रेडिंग करने में सहायता करती है।
opts.D: यह प्रशासनिक निर्देश प्रदान करती है।

qs.sol:
पाठ योजना शिक्षण-अधिगम प्रक्रिया के लिए शिक्षक द्वारा पहले से तैयार की गई एक संरचित रूपरेखा होती है, जिसमें शिक्षण उद्देश्यों, विषय-वस्तु के प्रस्तुतीकरण के चरणों, शिक्षण विधियों-गतिविधियों और मूल्यांकन बिंदुओं को क्रमबद्ध ढंग से लिखा जाता है। यह विशेष रूप से अनुभवहीन (beginner) शिक्षकों के लिए एक व्यावहारिक कार्य-मार्गदर्शिका का काम करती है, क्योंकि उनके पास कक्षा-प्रबंधन का पूर्व अनुभव नहीं होता।

चूँकि नए शिक्षकों के पास तात्कालिक निर्णय लेने का अनुभव नहीं होता, इसलिए पाठ योजना उन्हें बताती है कि कक्षा में किस क्रम में क्या पढ़ाना है, किन गतिविधियों-साधनों का प्रयोग करना है, और समय का बँटवारा कैसे करना है — अर्थात् यह एक ठोस दैनिक कार्ययोजना प्रदान करती है, जिसे शिक्षक कक्षा में चरण-दर-चर …
qs.rel: Lesson plan for beginners provides a daily teaching roadmap and confidence. Neighbours: unit plan, year plan, Herbartian plan, micro lesson plan.

qs.stem: Proper application of content knowledge is evident when the teacher:

opts.A: gives a lot of home assignments
opts.C: transforms the subject matter in such a way that it reaches the students

qs.sol:
Concept: Effective teaching requires more than possessing subject-matter (content) knowledge alone — it requires Pedagogical Content Knowledge (PCK): the ability to transform that content, through analogies, representations, examples, and sequencing, into a form that is accessible and meaningful to learners at their level of understanding (Shulman, 1987).

Application: The stem asks which teacher behaviour demonstrates "proper application of content knowledge" in practice. The option stating that the teacher "transforms the subject matter in such a way that it reaches the students" directly describes this act of reshaping content for learner accessibility — the defining feature of PCK. …
qs.rel: Application of content knowledge: teacher transforms subject matter so students understand it. Neighbours: Shulman's PCK, content transformation, representation.

qs.stem: What role do aims and objectives play in defining a discipline's knowledge?

opts.A: They determine the entertainment value of a subject.
opts.B: They shape the kind of knowledge and methods used within the discipline.
opts.C: They are only used in classroom assessments.
opts.D: They are unrelated to how knowledge is structured.

qs.sol:
A discipline's body of knowledge is not arbitrary -- it is shaped by the discipline's own aims and objectives. These aims determine both what counts as legitimate knowledge in the field and which methods of inquiry, verification, and organization are used to build that knowledge.

In this question, the same principle is being tested: a discipline's aims and objectives set the boundaries of its subject matter and prescribe the methods used to investigate it. …
qs.rel: Differentiated instruction adapts content, process and product to student readiness. Neighbours: Tomlinson, flexible grouping, UDL, tiered tasks.

qs.stem: Emotions have some effects on the developing individual. Which of the following are those effects? I. They influence adjustment in the society. II. They work as motivators of our behaviour.
qs.sol: Emotions affect the developing individual in several ways. They influence personal and social adjustment: a child who can manage fear, anger and jealousy relates better with family, peers and teachers, while emotional disturbance can lead to maladjustment. Emotions also act as motivators of behaviour: curiosity, joy, fear and anger drive a person to approach, explore, avoid or attack. Both listed effects are therefore correct.
qs.rel: Inductive method derives rules from examples, experiences and experiments (particular to general). Neighbours: deductive method (rule first), discovery method, heuristic method.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा, जुडिथ बटलर (Judith Butler) के जेंडर प्रदर्शनात्मकता के विचार को सर्वोत्तम रूप से निरूपित करता है?

opts.A: जेंडर, जन्म के समय जैव रूप से निर्धारित हो जाता है।
opts.B: जेंडर पहचान, यौन उन्मुखता के समरूप है।
opts.C: जेंडर, हार्मोनल परिवर्तनों का परिणाम है।
opts.D: जेंडर भूमिकाएँ सामाजिक रूप से निर्मित होती हैं और क्रियाओं के माध्यम से दोहराई जाती हैं।

qs.sol:
जुडिथ बटलर का 'जेंडर प्रदर्शनात्मकता' (gender performativity) सिद्धांत यह मानता है कि जेंडर कोई स्थिर, जन्मजात या जैविक विशेषता नहीं है, बल्कि यह सामाजिक रूप से स्थापित मानदंडों के अनुसार बार-बार दोहराई जाने वाली क्रियाओं (repeated stylized acts) के माध्यम से रचा और बनाए रखा जाता है — अर्थात व्यक्ति जेंडर 'है' नहीं, बल्कि जेंडर को निरंतर 'करता' है।

इसी अवधारणा के आधार पर, दिए गए विकल्पों में वह कथन सबसे उपयुक्त है जो जेंडर भूमिकाओं को सामाजिक रूप से निर्मित बताता है और यह स्पष्ट करता है कि वे बार-बार की जाने वाली क्रियाओं के माध्यम से दोहराई जाती हैं — क्योंकि यही कथन 'सामाजिक निर्माण' और 'क्रियाओं के माध्यम से पुनरावृत्ति' दोनों तत्वों को एक साथ समाहित करता है, जो बटलर के सिद्धांत के मूल म …
qs.rel: Evaluating achievement and preparing progress reports are teacher functions, so 'neither' as 'not a function' is incorrect framing. Neighbours: teacher roles - planner, facilitator, evaluator.

qs.stem: विज्ञान, मानविकी और गणित जैसे व्यापक अध्ययन-क्षेत्रों के वर्गीकरण में निम्न में से कौन एक व्यापक क्षेत्र के बजाय गणित की विशिष्ट शाखा है?
qs.sol: मूल प्रश्न से संशोधित: “शैक्षणिक अनुशासन” में बीजगणित भी आ सकता था; प्रश्न को व्यापक अध्ययन-क्षेत्र बनाम विशिष्ट शाखा के वर्गीकरण तक सीमित किया गया है। विज्ञान, मानविकी और गणित व्यापक अध्ययन-क्षेत्र हैं। बीजगणित गणित की प्रतीक, समीकरण और संरचना संबंधी विशिष्ट शाखा है। इसलिए वही वर्गीकरण में अलग पड़ता है।
qs.rel: Co-curricular activities related to motor development: sports, drawing, dance; newspaper reading is cognitive/language. Neighbours: selection principles, voluntary participation, balanced programme.

qs.stem: Which teaching methods is Socrates an exponent of?
qs.sol: Socrates taught by asking a series of probing questions that led learners to discover answers themselves; this is the question-answer (Socratic) method.
qs.rel: Ability grouping can lead to labelling students as bright or weak (Pygmalion effect). Neighbours: heterogeneous grouping, mixed ability, Rosenthal and Jacobson.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are those medium(s) by which value education can be provided to the students?
 Statements:
 I. Skits and Dramas
 II. Morning Assembly
 III. Compulsory Subject
qs.sol: Value education can be provided through skits/dramas, morning assembly and compulsory subjects. All three are possible media.
qs.rel: Value education media: skits, drama, stories, songs, assembly, role models. Neighbours: moral education, NCF 2005 values, Kohlberg.

qs.stem: लड़के और लड़कियों की पोषण संबंधी आवश्यकताएं किस आयु तक समान होती हैं?
qs.sol: विद्यालयी पोषण के सामान्य आयु-वर्गीकरण में लड़कों और लड़कियों की पोषण संबंधी अनुशंसाएँ लगभग नौ वर्ष तक समान मानी जाती हैं। दस वर्ष के आसपास विकास की गति और शारीरिक परिवर्तन अलग होने लगते हैं, जिससे कुछ पोषक तत्वों की आवश्यकताएँ भिन्न हो सकती हैं। दिए विकल्पों में ७–९ वर्ष का आयु-वर्ग इस साझा चरण का अंतिम उपयुक्त समूह है। १०–१२ और ११–१३ वर्ष में किशोरावस्था के बदलाव शुरू हो सकते हैं। ४–५ वर्ष भी साझा आवश्यकताओं के भीतर है, लेकिन प्रश्न 'किस आयु तक' पूछता है, इसलिए अंतिम समूह चुनना चाहिए।
qs.rel: Socrates' method is question-answer (dialectic/Socratic questioning). Neighbours: Plato, maieutic method, Aristotle, inductive reasoning.

qs.stem:
Choose the best option from the following.

Text books contain information about human rights, values and social norms. Thus we can call text books as:
qs.sol:
Teaching human rights, values and social norms can shape how learners act towards other people.

The official key therefore emphasizes textbooks as tools for social change.

Note on the official key: Source of information is also a defensible literal description of the printed premise. The request for the best description lets the board prefer the broader social purpose, rather than mere factual provision.
qs.rel: Textbooks act as tools for social change by conveying rights, values and norms. Neighbours: hidden curriculum, textbook reform, constitutional values.

qs.stem: Learners with impairments are NOT a homogeneous group because:

opts.A: their impairments and needs vary in type and severity
opts.B: all impairments are treated the same way everywhere
opts.C: they all have the same background

qs.sol: Learners differ in the type and severity of impairment and in the support they need. “they all have the same background” wrongly assumes shared life circumstances and does not explain the variation in impairment and support needs.
qs.rel: Participatory social science teaching: field visits, discussions, role-play, project work. Neighbours: constructivist classroom, case method, community resources.

qs.stem: शिक्षण की प्रभावशीलता को ____ के संदर्भ में आंका जाना चाहिए।

opts.C: कक्षागृह में शिक्षण सहायक सामग्री का उपयोग
opts.D: अच्छे अंक प्राप्त करने में उम्मीदवार की दक्षता

qs.sol: प्रीव्यू कुंजी अच्छे अंक प्राप्त करने की दक्षता को मानती है। अंक अधिगम परिणाम दिखा सकते हैं, पर शिक्षण प्रभावशीलता का अपूर्ण माप हैं; विकल्प में विद्यार्थियों के बजाय “उम्मीदवार” लिखा है। अन्य मुद्रित विकल्प संसाधन या रुचि बताते हैं, उपलब्धि का मापन नहीं।
qs.rel: In PBL, authentic tasks, reflection and collaboration make learning succeed. Neighbours: Kilpatrick's project method, inquiry learning, driving question.

qs.stem: शिमला हिल्स में अपनी तरह का पहला "माध्यमिक विद्यालय में विज्ञान शिक्षण पर अखिल भारतीय संगोष्ठी" किस वर्ष आयोजित किया गया था?
qs.sol: माध्यमिक विद्यालयों में विज्ञान शिक्षण पर पहली अखिल भारतीय संगोष्ठी 1956 में तारा देवी, शिमला हिल्स में आयोजित हुई थी।
qs.rel: Role-play and brainstorming show adaptability and engagement strategies in teaching. Neighbours: motivation, varied strategies, active learning.

qs.stem: Seeing students losing interest during class, a teacher integrates role-play and brainstorming sessions into her lesson. Primarily, which facilitation technique is she using?

opts.A: Fixed lecture format and content delivery
opts.D: Individual active work and silent study periods

qs.sol:
Teaching-aptitude questions about facilitation classify a teacher's classroom behaviour into three broad categories: how content is delivered (lecture-based transmission), how learning is measured (assessment and grading), and how the teacher manages the learning process itself — adjusting method and activity in response to how students are responding, so as to sustain their attention and participation.

In this scenario, the teacher notices students losing interest — a real-time signal from the classroom — and responds by replacing passive delivery with role-play and brainstorming, both of which require students to actively participate rather than merely listen. …
qs.rel: REC kit principle: break content into small units. Neighbours: chunking, microlearning, programmed instruction (Skinner, small steps).

qs.stem: प्रतीकात्मक अंतः क्रियावाद (जॉर्ज हर्बर्ट मीड) विशेष रूप से ______ पर आधारित है।
qs.sol: प्रतीकात्मक अंतःक्रियावाद बताता है कि मानव संचार और अंतःक्रिया से साझा प्रतीकों का अर्थ बनता है।
qs.rel: Teaching effectiveness is judged by learning outcomes and student understanding, not just marks. Neighbours: competency-based approach, NEP 2020 focus on competencies.

qs.stem: किलपैट्रिक किस शिक्षण पद्धति से संबंधित है?
qs.sol: विलियम एच. किलपैट्रिक परियोजना शिक्षण विधि से संबंधित हैं।
qs.rel: William Heard Kilpatrick propagated the Project Method (Dewey's pupil, 1918). Neighbours: Dalton plan (Parkhurst), Montessori, Kindergarten (Froebel).

qs.stem:
In which of the following approach Pedagogy indicate learning by doing based on engagement of students through different activities?
I. Teacher centered approach
II. Student centered approach
qs.sol: Learning by doing and engagement through activities are features of a student-centered approach, not a teacher-centered one.
qs.rel: Learning by doing through varied activities is activity-based/experiential pedagogy. Neighbours: Dewey, Montessori, Gandhi's basic education.

qs.stem: Who first introduced the term “Pedagogical Content Knowledge”?
qs.sol:
Lee S. Shulman introduced 'Pedagogical Content Knowledge' (PCK) in 1986. It is the special knowledge a teacher needs to make a subject understandable: a blend of subject content and pedagogy.

Vygotsky (zone of proximal development), Gardner (multiple intelligences) and Tolman (latent learning, cognitive maps) are known for other ideas.

Hence the answer is Lee Shulman.
qs.rel: Lee Shulman introduced Pedagogical Content Knowledge in 1986. Neighbours: TPACK (Mishra and Koehler 2006), content knowledge, teacher knowledge base.

qs.stem: CIC stands for ___.
qs.sol: CIC expands to Classroom Interactional Competence in teaching discourse.
qs.rel: Classroom Interactional Competence (CIC): teachers' ability to use interaction to support learning (Walsh). Neighbours: IRF pattern, wait time, scaffolding.

qs.stem: What element directly follows lesson objectives in most plans?
qs.sol:
A lesson plan normally moves from intended objectives to the procedures and activities through which learners will reach them.

The sequence therefore places teaching procedures immediately after the objectives.
qs.rel: Teaching procedures follow objectives in lesson plans. Neighbours: evaluation, assignments, materials, summary.

qs.stem:
Read the Assertion (A) and Reason (R) given below and choose the correct option.

Assertion (A): When introducing the concept of volume to young children, using water and containers of different shapes is beneficial.

Reason (R): Hands-on activities help children visualize and compare how much space an object occupies.

opts.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
opts.B: A is false, but R is true
opts.C: A is true, but R is false
opts.D: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

qs.sol: Using water and differently shaped containers helps children experience and compare volume directly. Hands-on activities explain why this approach is beneficial.
qs.rel: Introducing concepts of volume etc. begins from concrete experiences. Neighbours: concrete-pictorial-abstract, Bruner's enactive-iconic-symbolic, Piaget.

qs.stem: Which of the following best represents a learner-centered approach in curriculum development?

opts.A: Preparing students mainly for social roles and productivity
opts.B: Organizing knowledge strictly into traditional subject areas
opts.C: Designing lessons based on learners’ interests and participation
opts.D: Providing fixed content with standardized evaluation

qs.sol: A learner-centered approach prioritizes student interests, needs, and active participation. This contrasts with teacher-centered models that focus on rigid subject structures or fixed content delivery.
qs.rel: Learner-centred curriculum builds on learners' interests and needs. Neighbours: child-centred education (Rousseau, Dewey, Montessori), NCF 2005.

qs.stem: What are filled with facts that students are expected to memorize?
qs.sol:
In a fact-centred classroom, the prescribed learning material organises content for study.

Text books present the curricular facts that students are expected to learn.

Notebooks and rough books instead record or practise that material.
qs.rel: Textbooks often contain facts students memorise. Neighbours: rote learning, workbooks, reference books, notes.

qs.sol:
आधिकारिक उत्तर-कुंजी पर टिप्पणी: बोर्ड की आधिकारिक उत्तर-कुंजी "लघु छड़ी (Short cane)" को सही मानती है। कोई भी मुद्रित विकल्प पूरी तरह तर्कसंगत नहीं है, क्योंकि लघु छड़ी भी दृष्टिबाधित व्यक्तियों द्वारा उपयोग की जाने वाली मान्य छड़ी है; शेष तीन भी छड़ी के प्रकार हैं। इस प्रश्न का मूल्यांकन आधिकारिक कुंजी के अनुसार "लघु छड़ी (Short cane)" से किया गया है, जैसा वास्तविक परीक्षा में हुआ।

लघु छड़ी, वलित छड़ी, इलेक्ट्रॉनिक छड़ी और दीर्घ छड़ी सभी गतिशीलता के लिए प्रयुक्त छड़ियों के प्रकार हैं। वलित छड़ी लंबी छड़ी का मोड़कर रखा जा सकने वाला रूप है।
qs.rel: Board key is disputed for this item. Revise the core definitions of the topic and use elimination.

qs.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.

Text books are as the primary source for transmitting educational content because they are considered to be:
qs.sol:
Textbooks offer organized curricular content that can be checked and used consistently.

Their role as an authoritative instructional source rests on reliability of that content.
qs.rel: Textbooks are reliable primary source for transmitting educational content. Neighbours: reference materials, supplementary readers.

qs.stem: Talking and indiscipline in the classroom is an indication of ______________.
qs.sol: Repetitive instruction may produce boredom expressed as classroom talking and disruption.
qs.rel: Talking and indiscipline often indicate boredom from repetitiveness. Neighbours: causes - unmet needs, lack of interest, teaching quality; remedies - varied methods.

qs.stem:
The teaching learning process is an integration of “who” “what” and “how”. Which of the following constitutes the 

“who” in this process?
qs.sol:
“Who” concerns the learner; “what” concerns content and “how” the method.

The learner’s cognitive level therefore describes who is being taught.
qs.rel: 'Who' in teaching-learning refers to learner: cognitive level of development, background. Neighbours: what - content, how - methods.

qs.stem:
Choose the appropriate option to complete the sentence.

A mathematics teacher needs to highlight the ______ value of mathematics to make the learning of mathematics more meaningful.
qs.sol: Showing the practical use of mathematics makes its learning meaningful in everyday contexts; this is its utilitarian value.
qs.rel: Utilitarian value of mathematics: use in daily life. Neighbours: disciplinary, cultural, aesthetic and social values; NCF 2005 mathematisation.

qs.stem: Engaging students in exploratory activities is an appropriate strategy to develop which of these attributes in them?
qs.sol: Exploratory work lets learners investigate and decide independently, strengthening self confidence.
qs.rel: Exploratory activities build confidence and curiosity. Neighbours: discovery learning (Bruner), inquiry method, heuristic method.

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT the characteristic of constructivist approach to Learning and Teaching?

opts.A: Opinion, ideas given by the students are accepted and honoured
opts.B: Focus is not on learning, but on teaching
opts.D: Students make meaning from their own experience

qs.sol: A constructivist classroom centers learners’ meaning-making from prior experience. It welcomes student ideas and supports discussion in a democratic environment. Teaching still matters, but its purpose is to create conditions for learning, not to displace learning as the focus. The claim that focus lies on teaching rather than learning therefore conflicts with the approach; the other features fit it. Respecting student ideas supports active meaning-making. Making teacher delivery the focus contradicts learner construction. Open discussion is compatible with a democratic classroom. Connecting new ideas to experience is central to the approach.
qs.rel: Constructivist approach focuses on learning, not on teaching or transmitting. Neighbours: teacher-centred approach opposite; Piaget, Vygotsky, Bruner.

qs.stem: कक्षा में शिक्षक और छात्रों के बीच संचार को क्या कहा जाता है?
qs.sol: बातचीत में भाषा का परस्पर प्रयोग होता है। कक्षा में शिक्षक और विद्यार्थियों के बीच प्रश्न, उत्तर तथा प्रतिक्रिया का प्रवाह कक्षा-प्रवचन कहलाता है; दिए गए पदों में ‘‘भाषा प्रवचन’’ उसी विचार को व्यक्त करता है। भाषा अर्जन किसी भाषा के प्रयोग की क्षमता विकसित होने की प्रक्रिया है, स्वयं बातचीत नहीं। भाषा उपकरण अभिव्यक्ति का साधन या विशेषता है। भाषा पाठ्यक्रम नियोजित विषयवस्तु, लक्ष्य और अधिगम अनुभवों का ढाँचा है। प्रश्न किसी योजना या क्षमता का नाम नहीं, बल्कि चल रहे संवाद का पद पूछता है। इसी कारण प्रवचन का अर्थ सबसे सटीक बैठता है।
qs.rel: Communication between teacher and students in class is language/interaction. Neighbours: classroom discourse, IRF pattern, dialogic teaching.

qs.stem:
Which of the following methods can be used to organise notes for interpreting an information? 

I. Flow chart 

II. Transition devices
qs.sol: A flow chart is a visual method for organizing notes because it shows sequence, relationships, and structure, which helps in interpreting information. Transition devices are linking words or phrases used mainly while writing connected text; they are not a method for organizing raw notes. Therefore, only I is correct.
qs.rel: Flow charts help organise notes; transition devices are connecting words. Neighbours: mind maps, outlines, graphic organisers.

qs.stem:
Choose the right answer from the option below.
Classroom teaching can be effective when teachers have secure knowledge of subject content, curriculum and ________.
qs.sol: Effective classroom teaching requires knowledge of how to teach the content, that is pedagogical content.
qs.rel: Effective teaching requires pedagogical content knowledge. Neighbours: Shulman, subject knowledge, classroom management.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are the characteristic(s) of Teacher Centred Approach of teaching–learning?
 I. Extrinsic modes of motivation like praise, rewards and punishment are generally used by the teachers.
 II. Emphasis is given on passive listening, reading and writing and reproducing things taught by or as directed by the teacher.
qs.sol: Teacher-centred teaching often uses extrinsic motivation and emphasizes passive listening, reading, writing and reproduction of taught material.
qs.rel: Teacher-centred approach: extrinsic motivation, teacher authority, lecture. Neighbours: learner-centred opposites.

qs.sol: पारस्परिक शिक्षण की प्रचलित रणनीतियाँ सारांश, प्रश्न, स्पष्टीकरण और पूर्वानुमान हैं; इसलिए “उत्तर देना (Answering)” स्वतंत्र रणनीति के रूप में सूची में नहीं आता। “प्रश्न करना (Questioning)” पाठ को समझने की जाँच के लिए विद्यार्थियों द्वारा प्रश्न बनाने की मान्य रणनीति है।
qs.rel: Reciprocal teaching (Palincsar and Brown): summarise, question, clarify, predict. Neighbours: cooperative reading, scaffolding, metacognition.

qs.sol: “संरचित अधिगम परिणाम प्रदान करके” सही है, क्योंकि पेशेवर संगठन मानक और अपेक्षित दक्षताएँ बताकर शिक्षक को संरचित अधिगम परिणाम तय करने में मदद कर सकते हैं। “स्कूल के सांस्कृतिक कार्यक्रमों का प्रबंधन करके” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि स्कूल के सांस्कृतिक कार्यक्रमों का प्रबंधन अनुदेशी लक्ष्यों और सीखने के परिणाम तय करने का मुख्य योगदान नहीं है।
qs.rel: Structured learning outcomes provide a professional standard framework. Neighbours: competency framework, rubrics.

qs.stem: Which scenario best illustrates effective peer tutoring in an elementary classroom setting?

opts.B: Older students mentoring younger pupils in reading comprehension
opts.C: Teachers assigning extra homework to struggling students
opts.D: Parents volunteering to assist with classroom management

qs.sol: Peer tutoring is illustrated when older or more capable students mentor younger pupils in reading comprehension. This uses peers as learning supports.
qs.rel: Peer tutoring: older students mentor younger pupils. Neighbours: cross-age tutoring, Vygotsky ZPD, cooperative learning.

qs.stem: In which of the following teaching strategies does the student acquire the knowledge himself/herself by discovering the facts himself/herself supported by the guidance of the teacher?
qs.sol: In the heuristic method learners discover facts themselves with teacher guidance.
qs.rel: Heuristic method (Armstrong): discover facts by oneself. Neighbours: discovery method (Bruner), inquiry, problem-solving.

qs.stem: Which of the following are the approaches to Learning and Teaching? I. Competency – Based Approach II. Subject – Centered Approach III. Constructivist Approach IV. Learner – Centered Approach
qs.sol: Competency-based, subject-centered, constructivist, and learner-centered are all recognized approaches to organizing learning and teaching. They emphasize different things: demonstrated abilities, subject matter, knowledge construction, and learner needs. The question asks which listed labels are approaches, not which is preferable. All four fit the broad category despite their different principles.
qs.rel: Approaches to learning and teaching: competency-based, subject-centred, learner-centred, activity-centred. Neighbours: NCF 2023, Bloom.

qs.stem: Lack of several basic necessities can create disruptions in the classroom process. Which of the following are those basic necessities? I. Secured, safe and congenial environment II. Sufficient teaching learning materials III. Good student – student and student – teacher relationships
qs.sol: Classroom processes run smoothly only when basic needs are met: a secure, safe and congenial environment, sufficient teaching-learning materials, and good student-student and student-teacher relationships. The lack of any of these leads to disruption in the classroom, so all three are basic necessities.
qs.rel: Basic necessities (water, toilets, furniture) affect classroom processes. Neighbours: RTE Act infrastructure norms, Operation Blackboard.

qs.stem: Which of the following combination(s) is/are NOT correct?
qs.sol:
Teaching aids are classified by the sense(s) through which they deliver information: audio aids use sound only, visual aids use sight only, and audio-visual aids combine sound with moving images at the same time.

Applying this test to each pairing: cassette recordings and radio broadcasts are heard, not seen, so both correctly pair with "audio aid." Graphs are seen, not heard, so pairing graphs with "visual aid" is also correct. Television broadcasts, however, carry synchronized sound together with moving pictures, so the sense-channel test places television under "audio-visual aid," not under "visual aid" alone.

Cassette – Audio aid: correct, a sound-only channel. …
qs.rel: Television is audio-visual, not merely a visual aid. Neighbours: radio - audio aid, cassette - audio aid, graphs - visual aid, Dale's cone.

qs.stem: In which of the following approach to learning and teaching, both the teacher and the students perform activities strictly confined to the prescribed contents/ textbooks in the subject being taught?
qs.sol: When both teacher and students work strictly within the prescribed content or textbook of the subject, the approach is subject-centered.
qs.rel: Subject-centred approach: teacher and students confined to textbook subject matter. Neighbours: learner-centred, activity-centred, competence-based.

qs.stem:
To make social science interesting, teacher uses several resources which act as tools for learning. ‘Map’ is one of the essential tools. Which of the following is NOT an element of the Map?

I. Direction Indicator

II. Scale of a Map

III. Title of the Map

opts.D: Neither I nor II nor III

qs.sol: A map is a scaled representation of part of the earth's surface on a flat sheet, and cartographers list certain essential elements that every map needs. These include a title saying what the map shows, a scale relating map distance to ground distance, a direction indicator such as a north arrow, a legend or key explaining the symbols, and often a grid or projection. All three items in the question are therefore standard map elements, and none of them can be called a non-element of a map.
qs.rel: Maps, globes, charts are essential resources in social science. Neighbours: timelines, models, field trips, museums.

qs.stem: Teacher prepares for the lesson with variety of resources and strategies, but with no particular learner in mind. Which of the classrooms does this describe?
qs.sol:
The preparation is general and is not tailored to a particular learner’s needs.

The paper classifies this as a common classroom rather than a specially adapted or vocational setting.
qs.rel: Preparing lessons with no particular learner in mind produces a common classroom lesson. Neighbours: differentiated instruction, learner profile.

qs.stem: भावात्मक डोमेन के वर्गीकरण के अनुसार, 'ग्राही (Receiving)' स्तर में मुख्यत: क्या शामिल होता है?

opts.B: उद्दीपकों पर ध्यान देने के लिए संवेदनशीलता और इच्छा को दर्शाना
opts.D: जीवन के एक सुसंगत दर्शन का निर्माण करना

qs.sol:
अवधारणा: क्रैथवोल, ब्लूम और मेसिया (1964) द्वारा प्रस्तावित भावात्मक डोमेन (Affective Domain) के वर्गीकरण में शैक्षिक उद्देश्यों को पाँच अनुक्रमिक स्तरों में बाँटा गया है — ग्राही (Receiving), अनुक्रिया (Responding), मूल्यांकन (Valuing), संगठन (Organization), और चरित्रीकरण (Characterization)। प्रत्येक उच्चतर स्तर भावनाओं, अभिवृत्तियों और मूल्यों के आंतरिकीकरण (internalization) की बढ़ती हुई मात्रा को दर्शाता है।

अनुप्रयोग: इस वर्गीकरण का सबसे निचला और प्रथम स्तर उद्दीपकों (stimuli) के प्रति जागरूकता तथा उन पर ध्यान देने की संवेदनशीलता और इच्छा के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है — अर्थात् शिक्षार्थी किसी परिघटना के अस्तित्व के प्रति सचेत होकर उस पर चयनात्मक ध्यान (selective attention) देने को त …
qs.rel: Krathwohl's affective domain: receiving, responding, valuing, organisation, characterisation. Receiving = awareness and willingness to attend. Neighbours: Bloom's cognitive, Simpson's psychomotor.

qs.stem: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of unit planning in the pedagogy of English language lesson development?

opts.A: To organize lessons around shared objectives.
opts.B: To focus exclusively on grammar instruction.
opts.C: To assess students only after each lesson.
opts.D: To select random activities for engagement.

qs.sol:
Concept: Unit planning is a stage of curriculum planning that sits between the yearly scheme of work and a single lesson plan. A unit plan groups a related sequence of lessons — built around a common theme, skill area, or set of instructional objectives — so that every lesson within the unit works systematically toward the same shared learning goals, giving continuity and coherent progression across several class periods.

Application: In English language pedagogy, a unit typically covers a theme, genre, or skill cluster — for instance, a sequence of lessons combining a reading text, related vocabulary, grammar-in-context, and a writing task. …
qs.rel: Unit planning organises lessons around shared objectives. Neighbours: yearly plan, lesson plan, Herbartian unit.

qs.stem: For teacher teaching a class with large strength, which of the techniques is best?
qs.sol:
CONCEPT: In a very large class, the most suitable technique must communicate the core lesson efficiently to all learners while giving them a shared record for later study. Direct whole-class delivery and organized notes provide that reach and consistency.

APPLICATION: The class has large strength, so a lecture can address the whole group at once and class notes can preserve the key points for every learner. Debate, discussion, and practicals require more coordination; self-study reduces immediate teacher guidance; group work with a lecture can add participation but is less scalable as the single best technique for this stem. …
qs.rel: Large-class teaching: lecture with class notes is most practical; group work for variety. Neighbours: peer learning, ICT, team teaching.

qs.sol: Teacher–student interactions can reveal inequities in who receives attention, participation and support. The board marks “inequities”, although this completion is awkward and the question gives no context. “equities” does not fit: equities refers to fairness or equal opportunity, not its unequal distribution.
qs.rel: Teacher-student interactions show inequities in attention and participation. Neighbours: gender bias, hidden curriculum, call patterns.

qs.stem: In PCK- Pedagogy, Content and Knowledge; Knowledge refers to:
qs.sol:
Effective subject teaching requires adapting content and methods to learners’ prior understanding and needs.

The board’s use of “Knowledge” here therefore points to knowing the students.

PCK is conventionally Pedagogical Content Knowledge; its learner component is the intended focus of this question.
qs.rel: In PCK, K refers to knowledge of students (and content/pedagogy). Neighbours: Shulman, TPACK, knowledge of learners.

qs.stem: Collaborative projects of the methods of teaching will encourage which learning?
qs.sol: Collaborative projects promote indirect learning through participation.
qs.rel: Collaborative projects encourage indirect (cooperative) learning. Neighbours: direct instruction, cooperative learning, project method.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not advised to be kept in mind while selecting activities for co-curricular activities?

opts.A: Activities should be reasonably large in number and varied
opts.B: The activities should not impose excess strain on the students
opts.C: Students must be forced to participate in all the activities.
opts.D: The activities should be in accordance with students’ interest and ability.

qs.sol: Principles for selecting co-curricular activities include: offering a reasonably large and varied range, matching activities to students' interests and abilities, and avoiding excess strain on students. Participation should be voluntary and guided; forcing every student to take part in all activities goes against these principles, so it is the point not advised.
qs.rel: Participation in co-curricular activities should be voluntary, not forced. Neighbours: selection principles - interest, aptitude, balance.

qs.stem: Learning process involves two phases, one is Preparatory phase and which of the following is the other phase?
qs.sol:
Note on the official key: Actual learning phase is the accepted answer. Real learning phase is also defensible in English because real and actual can both describe the learning itself after preparation. Its printed Hindi wording, सीखने का स्थावर चरण, means a fixed or stationary phase and does not convey the same meaning.

The preparatory phase readies the learner. The following phase involves doing the learning activity itself; final suggests completion, while formative describes development rather than this phase name.
qs.rel: Learning has preparatory phase and actual learning phase. Neighbours: learning curve, plateau, readiness.

qs.stem: Which of this is not a role of teacher?

opts.A: The teacher must be a person of high integrity and must possess high self worth.
opts.B: The teacher must have pleasing personality, in depth knowledge and professional training .
opts.C: Teacher should enact as parent of students.
opts.D: Teachers should lead a true moral life.

qs.sol: Professional teaching includes integrity, competence and ethical conduct. Acting as a student's parent is not the teacher's professional role.
qs.rel: Teacher should be a role model, not a parent substitute. Neighbours: in loco parentis, facilitator, guide, counsellor.

qs.stem: A teacher, keeping in mind the background and abilities of each learner, prepares a lesson in which learners solve problems collaboratively. Which principle of effective pedagogy is best demonstrated here?

opts.B: Relying only on the student's self-ability
opts.C: Differentiation based on multi-dimensional learning factors
opts.D: Giving special attention to environmental resources

qs.sol: Concept: Effective, learner-centered pedagogy rests on the principle of differentiated instruction: because learners differ across multiple dimensions — prior background, ability level, and pace — a teacher must adapt how a lesson is designed to those dimensions rather than deliver one fixed method to everyone. Structuring problem-solving as a collaborative task is a learner-centered strategy that can be layered onto such a differentiated design, letting learners build understanding through guided peer interaction. …
qs.rel: Differentiation using multi-dimensional learner profile with collaborative problem solving. Neighbours: Tomlinson, MI, readiness and interest.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not the guideline to enhance questioning skills among children in classroom?

opts.B: Appreciate questions that are appropriate to the development level
opts.C: Never respond in an encouraging way
opts.D: Do not stop the discussion with the right answer

qs.sol: Children ask more and better questions when the classroom feels safe and their curiosity is valued. Teachers are therefore advised to listen sensitively to what children ask, to appreciate questions suited to their stage of development, to respond warmly and encouragingly, and to keep the discussion going even after a correct answer so that further questions arise. A teacher who never responds encouragingly signals that questions are unwelcome, which discourages children from asking at all. That statement runs against every guideline for developing questioning skills.
qs.rel: Encouraging responses build questioning skills; discouraging responses harm. Neighbours: wait time, Socratic questioning, Bloom's questioning.

qs.stem:
In which of the following teaching methods the whole class is divided into different homogeneous small sections on the basis of abilities so that

teacher can remove their difficulties by giving them individual guidance?
qs.sol: “Tutorial method” is supported: Tutorial teaching divides learners into small ability groups and provides individual guidance to resolve difficulties. By contrast, “Lecture method” lecture method addresses a larger group through exposition rather than individual guidance.
qs.rel: Tutorial method: groups of homogeneous ability get individual help. Neighbours: remedial teaching, programmed instruction, group teaching.

qs.stem: बैकवर्ड डिज़ाइन (backward design) योजना में, शिक्षक ________ से शुरुआत करता है।
qs.sol:
अवधारणा: बैकवर्ड डिज़ाइन (Understanding by Design — Wiggins व McTighe द्वारा प्रतिपादित मॉडल) पाठ्यक्रम एवं इकाई-नियोजन की एक तीन-चरणीय प्रक्रिया है, जिसमें नियोजन परिणाम से आरंभ होकर गतिविधियों की ओर बढ़ता है: शिक्षक सबसे पहले यह तय करता है कि पाठ की समाप्ति पर छात्रों में कौन-सी समझ व दक्षताएँ विकसित होनी चाहिए, और उसके आधार पर ही आगे की योजना बनाई जाती है।

चरण 1 — वांछित परिणाम पहचानना: शिक्षक सबसे पहले यह निर्धारित करता है कि छात्रों को पाठ/इकाई की समाप्ति पर कौन-से ज्ञान, कौशल और समझ (वांछित अधिगम परिणाम) प्राप्त करने हैं।

चरण 2 — स्वीकार्य प्रमाण तय करना: पहचाने गए परिणामों के आधार पर यह तय किया जाता है कि उनकी प्राप्ति किन आकलन साधनों (परीक्षण, प्रदर्शन-कार्य आदि) से मापी जाएगी।

चर …
qs.rel: Backward design (Wiggins and McTighe) starts with desired learning outcomes, then assessment, then activities. Neighbours: UbD, learning objectives.

qs.stem: Which strategy is most effective for selecting and using educational resources in a lesson plan?

opts.A: Selecting resources that support diverse learning styles and needs, and ensuring they are directly aligned with the learning objectives and instructional activities.
opts.B: Using a standard set of resources for all lessons, regardless of the specific content or objectives of each lesson.
opts.C: Prioritising the use of digital resources over traditional materials without considering their effectiveness in meeting learning objectives.
opts.D: Choosing resources based solely on their availability rather than their relevance to the learning objectives and student needs.

qs.sol: Effective lesson-level resource selection follows two governing principles: alignment, where every resource must serve the lesson's stated learning objectives and the instructional activities built around them, and differentiation, where resources should accommodate the range of learning styles and needs present in the classroom, since a single format rarely reaches every learner. …
qs.rel: Select resources supporting diverse learners and objectives. Neighbours: UDL, relevance, accessibility.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से उदाहरण – शिक्षार्थी कें द्रित सामाजिक विज्ञान कक्षा की सामान्य विशेषता का कौन सा संयोजन सही है? I. जब आप कृषि में शामिल प्रक्रियाओं पर पढ़ाते हैं, तो आप उन छात्रों, जिन्होंने उन प्रक्रियाओं को देखा है, का वर्णन करने के लिए कह सकते हैं – शिक्षार्थी के अनुभवों का उपयोग करना II. यदि स्कूल स्वास्थ्य संबंधी मुद्दों पर एक वार्ता आयोजित करना चाहता है, तो स्थानीय स्वास्थ्य कार्यकर्ता को बच्चों को संबोधित करने के लिए आमंत्रित किया जा सकता है - सामुदायिक संसाधनों का उपयोग

opts.D: ना ही I ना ही II

qs.sol: शिक्षार्थी-केंद्रित सामाजिक विज्ञान कक्षा शिक्षार्थियों के अपने अनुभवों पर आधारित होती है, जैसे कृषि की प्रक्रियाएँ देख चुके बच्चों से उनका वर्णन करवाना, और वह सामुदायिक संसाधनों का उपयोग करती है, जैसे स्वास्थ्य संबंधी विषयों पर बच्चों से बात करने के लिए स्थानीय स्वास्थ्य कार्यकर्ता को बुलाना। दोनों उदाहरण अपनी विशेषताओं से सही मिलाए गए हैं।
qs.rel: Learner-centred social science: discussion, role-play, projects, field trips. Neighbours: constructivism, inquiry.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a very detailed and specific plan consisting of intended learning outcomes, description of teaching- learning strategies and activities and actual tool for assessment of the learning outcomes?
qs.sol: A lesson plan is the most detailed and specific level of instructional planning. For a single lesson it states the intended learning outcomes, describes the teaching-learning strategies and activities, and includes the actual tools for assessing those outcomes. Year and semester plans outline content over long periods, and a unit plan organises a whole unit in broader terms.
qs.rel: Lesson plan is a detailed plan with outcomes, procedures and evaluation; unit plan is broader. Neighbours: yearly plan, Herbartian steps.

qs.stem: Which one is not a part of Organisation and Integration of Learning Experiences and Content?
qs.sol: The organisation of learning experiences considers situations, interaction, and learner development; teachers’ principles are outside this listed set.
qs.rel: Organisation of learning experiences: continuity, sequence, integration (Tyler). Neighbours: Tyler's rationale, scope and balance.

qs.stem: हरबर्ट पाँच औपचारिक पदों (Herbartian five formal steps) का सही अनुक्रम निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा है?

opts.A: उद्देश्य कथन → पुनर्कथन → गृहकार्य → समीक्षा → प्रतिक्रिया

qs.sol:
हरबर्ट के पाँच औपचारिक शिक्षण पद (Herbartian Five Formal Steps), जिन्हें बाद में उनके अनुयायियों तुइस्कन ज़िलर (Tuiskon Ziller) और विल्हेम राइन (Wilhelm Rein) ने विस्तृत रूप दिया, इस सिद्धांत पर आधारित हैं कि नया ज्ञान शिक्षार्थी के पूर्व-ज्ञान (apperceptive mass) से जोड़कर ही स्थायी रूप से सीखा जाता है। इसके पाँच क्रमिक चरण हैं: तैयारी, प्रस्तुति, संबंध/तुलना, सामान्यीकरण और अनुप्रयोग।

तैयारी (Preparation) — छात्रों के पूर्व-ज्ञान की जाँच करना और नए विषय में रुचि जगाना।

प्रस्तुति (Presentation) — नई तथ्यात्मक सामग्री प्रस्तुत करना।

संबंध/तुलना (Association/Comparison) — नई सामग्री की पूर्व-ज्ञात तथ्यों से तुलना कर संबंध स्थापित करना।

सामान्यीकरण (Generalization) — तुलना किए गए तथ्यों से …
qs.rel: Herbartian five steps: preparation (prastavana), presentation, association/comparison, generalisation, application. Neighbours: Herbart (1776-1841), Ziller, apperception.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are NOT correct?

I. In case of multi-grade and multi-level situations, teaching learning materials provide vital help to the teachers for effective management of their class.

II. Teaching learning materials are needed for effective self-learning.
qs.sol: Both statements are correct. Teaching-learning materials support teachers in managing multi-grade and multi-level classrooms, and they also support effective self-learning. Since the question asks for the statement(s) that are NOT correct, neither I nor II is the answer.
qs.rel: Multi-grade teaching: one teacher teaches several grades together; TLM must be adapted. Neighbours: multi-level teaching, Mobile crèches, Rishi Valley.

qs.stem: A curriculum team is selecting a pedagogical approach to enhance inclusivity and peer interaction. Which rationale most strongly supports their choice of peer tutoring?

opts.A: It restricts student roles to observer and participant only
opts.B: It minimizes opportunities for flexible group formation
opts.C: It utilizes student strengths for academic support
opts.D: It standardizes all instructional delivery methods

qs.sol: Peer tutoring supports inclusivity by using students' strengths for academic support and peer interaction.
qs.rel: Cooperative learning uses student strengths for inclusion and peer interaction. Neighbours: jigsaw, think-pair-share, UDL.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही नहीं है?

opts.C: सृजनात्मक आकलन में, ग्रेड अधिक भार वहन नहीं करते हैं।
opts.D: एक निश्चित निर्धारित पाठ्यक्रम में छात्र के समग्र प्रदर्शन को निर्धारित करने के लिए संकलनात्मक आकलन का उपयोग किया जाता है।

qs.sol: रचनात्मक आकलन शिक्षण के दौरान चलता है और सीखने में सुधार के लिए लगातार प्रतिक्रिया देता है। वह अवलोकन, प्रश्न या छोटे कार्य जैसे अनौपचारिक रूप ले सकता है; उसे अधिक औपचारिक बताना गलत है। संकलनात्मक आकलन इकाई या पाठ्यक्रम के अंत में परिणाम देखता और समग्र प्रदर्शन आंकता है। रचनात्मक आकलन में अंक सामान्यतः कम केंद्रीय होते हैं। लगातार प्रतिक्रिया अनौपचारिक भी हो सकती है; उसे अधिक औपचारिक कहना भूमिका उलटता है। संकलनात्मक आकलन अध्ययन अवधि के बाद प्राप्त परिणाम देखता है। रचनात्मक आकलन में अंकों से अधिक सुधार योग्य प्रतिक्रिया महत्वपूर्ण होती है। निर्धारित पाठ्यक्रम की समग्र उपलब्धि संकलनात्मक निर्णय है।
qs.rel: Creative (formative) assessment is informal, not formal; the key marks it incorrect statement as 'more formal'. Neighbours: formative vs summative contrast.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

opts.A: Multi-grade Teaching is a situation where multiple teachers teache several classes at a time.
opts.B: Multi-grade teaching is seen in the developed as well as in the underdeveloped countries.
opts.C: Multi-level teaching is related with Mono-grade situation.
opts.D: Multi-grade teaching is more effective by the appropriate sitting arrangement.

qs.sol: Multi-grade teaching is a situation in which one teacher teaches pupils of two or more grades at the same time, so the statement about multiple teachers is incorrect. It occurs in developed and developing countries, benefits from suitable seating, and multi-level teaching refers to different learning levels within a single grade.
qs.rel: Multi-grade teaching: one teacher, several grades at once in the same classroom. Neighbours: multi-level, small schools, RTE norms.

qs.stem: _____ and _____ are planned and organized for improving the power of thinking.
qs.sol: Teaching and instruction are planned and organized processes used to improve learners' thinking power.
qs.rel: Teaching and instruction are planned to improve thinking. Neighbours: teaching vs instruction vs training vs conditioning (Thomas Green's activities).

qs.stem:
“If you are planning to teach the different states of India in class VI, then you need to know whether the students are well conversant in using the atlas”. This given statement is referred to which of the following phase(s) of Assessment For Learning?
 I. Formative Assessment
 II. Diagnostic Assessment
qs.sol: Checking whether students can use an atlas before teaching states of India is diagnosis of prior knowledge and readiness. It is diagnostic assessment.
qs.rel: Prior knowledge of learners must be assessed before teaching new content. Neighbours: Ausubel advance organiser, diagnostic assessment, readiness.

qs.stem: Designing differentiated learning activities is a significant aspect of which of the following approaches?
qs.sol: A child-centric approach keeps the learner's needs, abilities, interests and pace at the centre of teaching. Designing differentiated learning activities means planning different tasks or supports for different learners, so it is a significant aspect of the child-centric approach.
qs.rel: Differentiated activities belong to child-centric approach. Neighbours: Montessori, Gardner's MI.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is essential when analysing subject content in relation to

teaching objectives?

opts.C: Using one method of instruction for all students

qs.sol:
Content analysis, as part of lesson and unit planning, means examining a subject's content and organising it so it directly serves the stated teaching objectives — the material selected, the method used, and the sequence followed are all expected to trace back to what learners are meant to achieve.

Among the options offered, only aligning content with curriculum standards ties the content directly to the objectives a curriculum lays down for that subject and level, which is exactly what analysing content "in relation to teaching objectives" requires. …
qs.rel: Content analysis requires aligning with curriculum standards and objectives. Neighbours: content, objectives, learner level.

qs.sol: “केवल b सही है।” सही है, क्योंकि प्रारंभिक चरण की विषय-वस्तु बच्चों के जीवन अनुभवों और उनके सांस्कृतिक, भौगोलिक तथा सामाजिक संदर्भ से जुड़नी चाहिए। “a और b दोनों सही हैं।” गलत है, क्योंकि मध्य चरण की विषय-वस्तु को केवल परिचित और तात्कालिक परिवेश तक सीमित नहीं रखा जाता।
qs.rel: Early stage content should suit children's developmental level. Neighbours: foundational stage, play-based learning, NEP 2020.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is an example of an observable verb suitable for a behavioural

objective?
qs.sol:
A behavioural (instructional) objective, per Robert Mager's criteria, must be written using an action verb that names a directly observable and measurable student behaviour — something an outside observer can see or hear the learner do, and can count or verify. Verbs that name an internal mental or affective state (thinking, knowing, valuing) cannot be used, because no observer can directly witness a mental state occurring; it can only be guessed at indirectly.

Checking each option against this observability test:

List — names a learner physically or verbally producing a set of items; an observer can watch the list being written or spoken and count the entries. …
qs.rel: Observable verbs for objectives: list, define, identify, solve; avoid know, understand. Neighbours: Bloom's action verbs, Mager.

qs.stem: In the types of Learning resources, the term _____ denotes a partially three-dimensional, full-size replica or scale model of a landscape typically showing historical events, nature scenes or cityscapes, for purposes of education or entertainment.
qs.sol: A diorama is a partial three-dimensional scene or model used to represent landscapes, historical events, or other educational scenes.
qs.rel: Diorama is a partially three-dimensional, full-size or scale replica of a scene. Neighbours: model, mock-up, replica, specimen.

qs.stem:
In the Herbartian model of lesson planning, the 'Motivation or Preparation'

step is primarily designed to facilitate:
qs.sol:
Concept: Herbart's model of teaching arranges a lesson into a fixed sequence of formal steps, each with one specific instructional purpose. The commonly cited steps are Preparation (or Motivation), Presentation, Association, Generalisation, and Application, with many versions adding a closing Recapitulation/Evaluation step to consolidate and test what was learnt.

Application: The first step, called Preparation or Motivation, comes before any new content is taught. Its purpose is to link the upcoming topic to what learners already know and to arouse their interest, so this step is designed to facilitate prior knowledge activation. …
qs.rel: Herbartian 'preparation' activates prior knowledge and motivates. Neighbours: apperception mass, presentation, association.

qs.sol: दल शिक्षण में कई शिक्षक अपनी विशेषज्ञता, समय और सामग्री साझा करते हैं; इसलिए जब संसाधन (विशेषज्ञ शिक्षक, सामग्री) सीमित हों, तब यह सबसे उपयोगी है।
qs.rel: Team teaching: several teachers share expertise, time and material. Neighbours: co-teaching, collaborative teaching, Trump plan.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not a part of Pedagogical Content Knowledge?

opts.A: Knowledge of learners and their characteristic

qs.sol: Knowledge of learners, contexts and purposes belong to the teacher knowledge framework; a separate inventory of teachers’ competencies is not listed as one of these components.
qs.rel: PCK does not include 'knowledge of teachers' competencies'; it includes content, pedagogy, learners, curriculum. Neighbours: Shulman categories.

qs.stem: शिक्षार्थियों के संदर्भ में सामग्री से संबंधित और इसमें शामिल है:
qs.sol: टिप्पणी: मूल प्रश्न में शिक्षार्थियों के संदर्भ का उल्लेख पृष्ठभूमि-ज्ञान की ओर भी संकेत कर सकता है; पुस्तिका का अभिप्रेत उत्तर ‘पाठ्यचर्या ज्ञान’ है। इस उत्तर के अनुसार पाठ्यचर्या ज्ञान में सामग्री को शिक्षार्थियों के संदर्भ से जोड़कर व्यवस्थित करना शामिल है।
qs.rel: Material in learners' context should be relevant and accessible. Neighbours: contextualised teaching, local resources.

qs.sol: “Setting clear learning objectives” is correct: Clear objectives identify what learners should understand or do and guide activities and assessment. “Writing on the blackboard” fails: Writing on the blackboard is a teaching action chosen after the lesson goals are set.
qs.rel: Clear learning objectives guide activities and assessment. Neighbours: SMART objectives, Bloom's taxonomy, backward design.

qs.sol: “अनुदेशी उद्देश्यों की पहचान करना” से पहले स्पष्ट होता है कि विद्यार्थी को क्या सीखना है; उसी आधार पर गतिविधियाँ और आकलन तय होते हैं। “शिक्षण विधियों का चयन करना” उद्देश्यों के स्पष्ट होने के बाद किया जाता है, ताकि विधि सीखने के लक्ष्य से मेल खाए।
qs.rel: Identifying instructional objectives is the first step in instructional design. Neighbours: ADDIE model, Tyler's rationale.

qs.sol:
आधिकारिक उत्तर-कुंजी पर टिप्पणी: बोर्ड की आधिकारिक उत्तर-कुंजी "भागीदारी में कमी को संबोधित करना" को सही मानती है। कोई भी मुद्रित विकल्प पूरी तरह तर्कसंगत नहीं है, क्योंकि भागीदारी की बाधा घटाना पोजिशनिंग का वैध अंतिम लक्ष्य है; अन्य दिए गए लक्ष्य भी वैध हैं, इसलिए निषेधात्मक प्रश्न का एक स्पष्ट उत्तर नहीं है। इस प्रश्न का मूल्यांकन आधिकारिक कुंजी के अनुसार "भागीदारी में कमी को संबोधित करना" से किया गया है, जैसा वास्तविक परीक्षा में हुआ।

उचित पोजिशनिंग से बच्चे को गतिविधियों तक पहुँच और अधिक स्वतंत्रता मिलती है। आराम और भागीदारी भी इसके वैध लक्ष्य हैं।
qs.rel: Board key is disputed for this item. Revise the core definitions of the topic and use elimination.

qs.sol: An instructional plan links the content of activities to curriculum objectives and a suitable learning environment. “Activities, assessments and feedback” describes teaching processes but omits the explicit objectives and planned environment.
qs.rel: An instructional plan links activities to curriculum objectives and learning environment; assessment and feedback follow. Neighbours: ADDIE, 5E.

topics.deep:
- **Teaching vs instruction vs training vs conditioning** (Thomas Green's activities): teaching is intentional, interactive, multi-purpose; instruction gives information; training builds skills; conditioning forms habits. **Approach** = philosophy/assumptions, **method** = overall plan, **technique** = specific classroom device (Anthony). So drilling is a technique.
- **Teaching levels (Hunt/Morrison):** memory level (Herbart), understanding level (Morrison), reflective level (Hunt). **Phases (Jackson):** pre-active (planning), interactive, post-active (evaluation).
- **Methods:**

| Method | Exponent / idea |
|---|---|
| Lecture | teacher-centred, good for large classes |
| Demonstration | show-and-explain, science |
| Discussion / seminar / symposium / panel | integrates contributions of participants |
| Project method | **Kilpatrick** (Dewey's pupil); purposeful activity |
| Heuristic | **H. E. Armstrong**; learner discovers facts |
| Dalton plan | Helen Parkhurst; contract, self-pace |
| Socratic | question-answer, dialectic |
| Brainstorming | **Osborn**; group generates ideas without criticism |
| Inductive vs deductive | particular -> general vs general -> particular |
| Tutorial | small homogeneous ability groups |
| Role play, simulation, case study, field trip | experiential |
| Montessori / Kindergarten | Montessori (didactic apparatus), **Froebel** (play-way) |

- **Herbartian five steps:** preparation, presentation, association (comparison), generalisation, application. Generalisation = formulating rules. Morrison's cycle: exploration, presentation, assimilation, organisation, recitation. **5E:** engage, explore, explain, elaborate, evaluate.
- **Lesson plan:** components = what (objectives, content), whom (learner characteristics), how (methods, TLM, evaluation). First step: learning objectives; then content, teaching procedure, resources, evaluation, assignment. **Backward design** (Wiggins and McTighe): outcomes -> assessment -> activities. Unit plan organises content around shared objectives; yearly plan broader. **RCEM** (Mysore) format; Gagne's nine events.
- **Objectives:** Bloom's cognitive domain (revised 2001: remember, understand, apply, analyse, evaluate, create); **Krathwohl** affective (receiving, responding, valuing, organisation, characterisation); psychomotor (Simpson, Harrow, Dave). Mager: behavioural objectives with **observable verbs** (list, define, solve), not "know/understand".
- **Micro-teaching** (Dwight Allen, Stanford 1963): one skill, 5-10 minutes, 5-10 students; cycle plan-teach-feedback-replan-reteach-refeedback. Skills: introduction, questioning, reinforcement, stimulus variation, illustration, explaining, closure. **Team teaching** (Trump), peer tutoring (cross-age), cooperative learning (Johnson and Johnson, jigsaw, think-pair-share), reciprocal teaching (summarise, question, clarify, predict).
- **Approaches:** teacher-centred (lecture, memorising, extrinsic motivation) vs learner/child-centred (interaction, intrinsic motivation, differentiated tasks) vs subject-centred vs activity-centred vs competency-based. **Pedagogical content knowledge** (Shulman 1986); TPACK (Mishra and Koehler).
- **TLM:** teaching-learning materials; improvised, low-cost/no-cost (leaves, stones, waste); criteria - relevance, simplicity, durability, multiple utility, safety; Dale's cone of experience; models (diorama, mock-up, replica), charts, flashcards. Resource types: human, physical, financial (grants), time. Operation Blackboard 1987 gave TLM.
- **Questioning:** convergent (one right answer) vs divergent (many); wait time; encourage responses; Bloom-based questions. Textbook: structured content, primary source but not the only one; NCF 2005 "learning without burden".
- **Classroom management and discipline:** Kounin (withitness, ripple effect, overlapping), Canter (assertive discipline), Glasser (choice theory), Linda Albert (cooperative discipline), Skinner (behaviour modification), Dreikurs (democratic). Indiscipline often signals boredom; ability grouping risks labelling. Physical climate (seating, light) and psychological climate both teacher responsibilities. Multi-grade and multi-level teaching handled by activity cards and peer groups.
- **Teacher roles:** planner, facilitator, evaluator, counsellor, record keeper, researcher, community link, role model; the teacher is not a parent substitute.
- **Home assignments:** informational, study, practice, creative; should be clear, graded and followed by feedback. Co-curricular activities must be voluntary, balanced and related to interests.

**Likely question angles:**
- Match method with exponent (Kilpatrick, Armstrong, Parkhurst, Osborn).
- Order of Herbartian steps or 5E phases; what generalisation does.
- First step in lesson planning; components of a lesson plan.
- Observable vs non-observable verbs for objectives.
- Micro-teaching definition, inventor, phases.
- Approach/method/technique classification (e.g. drill, lecture, inductive).
- Features of learner-centred vs teacher-centred approach.
- Inductive vs deductive method uses (science, grammar, maths).
- Criteria for choosing TLM or low-cost aids.
- Classroom management theorists and concepts (withitness).

topics.title: 9. Language Acquisition & Language Pedagogy
topics.theory:
- **Skill order:** listening -> speaking -> reading -> writing; listening/reading receptive, speaking/writing productive. Levels of language: phonology, morphology, **syntax** (sentence structure rules), semantics, pragmatics.
- **Acquisition:** Chomsky (LAD, innate), Skinner (imitation/reinforcement), Vygotsky (social), **Krashen** (input hypothesis, affective filter); L1 acquired from environment, L2 learned.
- **Milestones:** babbling ~6 months, first word ~12 months, two-word sentences 18-24 months, vocabulary explosion 3-6 years via social interaction; reception precedes expression.
- **Bilingual** = two languages; **multilingual** = more than two; benefits: cognitive flexibility; multilingualism is part of India's heritage; translanguaging uses all languages in class.
- **LAC (Language Across the Curriculum):** all teachers are responsible for language development; Bullock Report 1975.
- **Methods:** Grammar-Translation (classical Latin/Greek; speaking least practised), Direct, Audio-lingual, **Communicative Language Teaching** (communication/interaction), TPR (Asher).
- **Grammar:** deductive (rule first) and inductive (examples first); latest trend - grammar integrated with text.
