- **Reading:** phonics builds sound-letter links; **bottom-up** (decoding) vs **top-down** (prior knowledge); skimming = gist, scanning = specific information.
- **Three-Language Formula** (NPE 1968); NEP 2020: mother tongue/home language till at least Grade 5; Article 350A; Eighth Schedule 22 languages.
- Dialogic teaching harnesses talk; role play, mime, puppets develop speaking; standard language used in media, administration, judiciary.

qs.sol: बालक सामान्यतः घर और आसपास के लोगों से संवाद करते हुए सबसे पहले मातृभाषा अर्जित करता है। भाषा अर्जन में इसे प्रथम या मूल भाषा का अर्जन कहा जाता है। यह नाम सीखने के क्रम को बताता है, भविष्य में कुल कितनी भाषाएँ आएँगी उसे नहीं। दूसरी भाषा पहले अर्जित भाषा के बाद आती है; तीसरी और चौथी भाषा के लिए उससे भी अधिक पूर्व भाषाएँ आवश्यक हैं। प्रश्न में सामान्य मातृभाषा अर्जन पूछा गया है, इसलिए आरंभिक भाषा का वर्ग लागू होता है।
qs.rel: Mother-tongue learning is first language acquisition (L1), natural and unconscious; second language is learned. Neighbours: Krashen's acquisition-learning hypothesis, NEP 2020 mother tongue till Grade 5, three-language formula.

qs.stem: वह भाषा जिससे बच्चा मुख्य रूप से शैशअवस्था से उजागर होता है, उसे ___ कहा जाता है।
qs.sol: शैशव से मुख्य रूप से सुनी और सीखी जाने वाली भाषा मातृभाषा या प्रथम भाषा है।
qs.rel: Mother tongue is the language a child is exposed to from infancy. Neighbours: first language L1, medium of instruction, home language, NEP 2020 and Article 350A.

qs.stem: Which of these is the first skill that a child learns in life?
qs.sol: Among the listed language skills, listening develops first. Infants hear voices and other sounds before they can produce words. They gradually recognise patterns in the speech around them, which supports later speaking. Reading and writing require additional symbol knowledge and are generally learned much later. The question asks for the earliest skill in life, so the developmental sequence matters: receptive oral language begins before spoken production and before literacy activities. The printed Hindi choice for the later reading-related skill uses a broader word, but that does not change the sequence.
qs.rel: Listening is the first language skill; order: listening, speaking, reading, writing (LSRW). Neighbours: receptive (listening, reading) vs productive (speaking, writing) skills.

qs.stem: The use of more than two languages is called as _______________.
qs.sol: The key quantity in the sentence is “more than two.” Multilingualism denotes the use or competence of several languages and therefore fits three or more languages. Bilingualism specifically refers to two languages. Monolingualism refers to one. The printed fourth term suggests a fixed count of four, whereas the stem covers any number above two, including three and five. In education, a multilingual classroom may draw on several languages used by its learners rather than restricting interaction to one or two. The general term for that situation is the one selected here.
qs.rel: Using more than two languages is multilingualism; two = bilingualism; one = monolingualism. Neighbours: Three-Language Formula (Kothari Commission, NPE 1968), translanguaging.

qs.stem:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन से विलंबित भाषण के कारण हैं?
I. मानसिक मंदता
II. श्रवण दोष
III. व्यवहार संबंधी विकार
qs.sol: विलंबित वाणी बौद्धिक विकास की कठिनाई, श्रवण दोष और व्यवहार या सामाजिक संचार की कठिनाई से जुड़ सकती है। कम सुनने पर बोली हुई भाषा का अनुभव घटता है; विकास संबंधी स्थितियां भाषा समझ और संवाद को प्रभावित कर सकती हैं। तीनों कारक योगदान दे सकते हैं, हालांकि किसी बच्चे का वास्तविक मूल्यांकन व्यक्तिगत परीक्षण मांगता है। कथन I को छोड़ना बौद्धिक अक्षमता की अनदेखी करता है, जो विलंबित वाणी का एक सामान्य कारण है। कथन II और III को छोड़ना श्रवण दोष और व्यवहार संबंधी विकारों की अनदेखी करता है, जो विलंबित वाणी के कारण हैं। केवल व्यवहार सूची का एकमात्र संभावित योगदानकर्ता नहीं है। तीनों श्रेणियां वाणी विकास में देरी से जुड़ सकती हैं।
qs.rel: Children acquire first language by natural exposure to environment, not formal teaching (Chomsky's LAD, Skinner's imitation). Neighbours: Krashen's input hypothesis, Vygotsky's social interaction.

qs.stem: Statistical results are:
qs.sol: A statistic computed from a single sample — a mean, proportion, or any estimator drawn through a standard estimation procedure — carries sampling variability: it will not exactly equal the population parameter in every sample. Research-methodology treats such a result's reliability by its behaviour over repeated sampling rather than in any one instance: a soundly-constructed (unbiased) estimator is one whose expected value across many samples equals the true parameter, so the result is accurate in aggregate — "on average" — even when any one sample's value departs from it. …
qs.rel: Question on aesthetic expression: music is what feelings sound like (arts and language link). Neighbours: arts integrated education, NEP 2020 art integration.

qs.stem: Which is the apex body for curriculum related matters for school education in Inda ?
qs.sol:
No official answer key was published for this paper; the answer is worked out from the question.

NCERT is the national educational research and training body responsible for guidance on school curriculum.

UGC concerns university education, whereas the other listed bodies refer to school examination boards rather than the national curriculum apex institution.
qs.rel: Language Across the Curriculum (LAC) strengthens listening, speaking, reading and writing in all subjects. Neighbours: Bullock Report (1975), NCF 2005, responsibility of all teachers.

qs.stem: In the drill and practice mode of CAL, what does the computer typically provide to the learner?

opts.B: A series of exercises with immediate feedback

qs.sol: “A series of exercises with immediate feedback” is the defining pattern of drill and practice in computer-assisted learning: learners respond repeatedly and learn from prompt correction. “Only video demonstrations” can illustrate a skill, but watching alone does not supply the repeated responses and feedback this mode requires.
qs.rel: Answering aloud uses speaking, a productive (expressive) skill. Neighbours: oral, receptive skills, fluency vs accuracy.

qs.stem: Growth term represent purely which sense of a person?
qs.sol: Growth refers to a measurable increase in bodily size, weight, height, or related physical capacity. Development is the broader term that may include cognitive, emotional, and social change. The question asks for the narrow sense associated with growth. Political and logical are unrelated categories here, while common gives no developmental domain. Common is not a specific dimension of a person's growth. Physical size and related bodily measures describe growth in the narrow sense. Political refers to public life and institutions, not bodily increase. Logical refers to reasoning, a different developmental dimension.
qs.rel: Drama as a linguistic activity needs freedom and enjoyment. Neighbours: role play, improvisation, process drama, language games.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are the major type(s) of play for a child?
 Statements:
 I. Constructive play
 II. Functional play
 III. Dramatic or pretend play
qs.sol: Constructive play, functional play and dramatic/pretend play are major types of play in child development.
qs.rel: A standard language is codified and used in media, administration, judiciary and education. Neighbours: dialect, register, lingua franca, official language (Eighth Schedule, 22 languages).

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन लैंगिक भेदभाव के बारे में सही है? I. वे सांस्कृतिक रूप से प्रभावित हैं II. वे सामाजिक रूप से निर्मित हैं

opts.D: ना ही I ना ही II

qs.sol:
अवधारणा: जेंडर से आशय स्त्री, पुरुष, लड़की या लड़का होने से जुड़ी सामाजिक रूप से आकार लेने वाली भूमिकाओं, व्यवहारों और अपेक्षाओं से है। ये अपेक्षाएँ अलग-अलग संस्कृतियों में भिन्न हो सकती हैं और समय के साथ बदल सकती हैं।

सांस्कृतिक प्रभाव साझा मान्यताओं और रीति-रिवाजों से जुड़ा है; सामाजिक निर्माण बताता है कि संबंधों और संस्थाओं के माध्यम से लोग इन अपेक्षाओं को कैसे सीखते, दोहराते और लागू करते हैं। ये परस्पर जुड़ी व्याख्याएँ हैं।

कथन I सांस्कृतिक प्रभाव से जुड़ा है। उदाहरण के लिए, कोई समुदाय कुछ खेलों या व्यवसायों को किसी विशेष लिंग से जोड़ सकता है; दूसरे समुदाय में अपेक्षाएँ भिन्न हो सकती हैं।

कथन II सामाजिक निर्माण से जुड़ा है। परिवार, विद्यालय और साथी काम बाँटने, उदाहरण देने तथा प्रोत्सा …
qs.rel: Grammar can be taught deductively (rule first) or inductively (examples first). Neighbours: Grammar-Translation, direct method, functional grammar.

qs.stem: Which of the following is a fundamental principle of curriculum development?

opts.A: Relevance to the needs of learners

qs.sol:
Concept

Curriculum development uses learner-centredness, relevance, flexibility, continuity, and connection with social life as guiding design principles. Relevance to learners means selecting content, methods, and pace in relation to learners’ developmental level, interests, and educational needs.

Application

Relevance to the needs of learners directly expresses this learner-centred design principle because it makes learner requirements a basis for curriculum decisions.

Contrast

Ignoring societal context removes community expectations and real-life conditions from curriculum planning.

Random selection of topics replaces objectives and planned sequence with chance. …
qs.rel: Multilingualism improves cognitive flexibility, adaptability of thinking, problem solving. Neighbours: Cummins' threshold hypothesis, bilingual advantage, additive bilingualism.

qs.stem: What does deafness indicate?
qs.sol: The board uses deafness for profound congenital irreversible hearing loss; clinically, deafness need not always be congenital or irreversible. “Temporary hearing loss” does not fit: temporary loss is not the lasting severe category intended here.
qs.rel: Syntax = rules governing sentence/phrase structure. Neighbours: morphology (word forms), phonology (sounds), semantics (meaning), pragmatics (use).

qs.stem:
Inductive-Deductive approach is best method for teaching -

1. Science

2. Grammar

3. Mathematics

Choose the correct code.
qs.sol: The inductive-deductive approach first builds a rule from examples and then applies it to new cases. It suits science, grammar and mathematics alike, so all three are credited.
qs.rel: Word and sentence choice depend on audience, context, purpose, register. Neighbours: sociolinguistics, formal vs informal style, Hymes' communicative competence.

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Learning?
qs.sol: Learning is usually described as a continuous, active, individual and purposeful (goal-directed) process. The learner keeps learning from experience throughout life, engages actively with what is learnt, and learns in a way and at a pace shaped by prior knowledge. Being unintentional is not one of these characteristics: standard descriptions treat learning as purposeful, directed towards goals the learner or teacher has set. Incidental learning does occur, but it is not presented as a defining characteristic of learning, so this is the trait that does not belong.
qs.rel: Linguistics is the scientific study of language. Neighbours: phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics; Saussure, Chomsky.

qs.stem:
There are various factors on which our choice of words, our selection of sentences are always dependent. Which of the following are those factors?

I. The context

II. The place where we speak

III. The theme
qs.sol: Word choice and sentence selection depend on the context, the place or setting where we speak, and the theme or subject of communication. All three factors affect appropriateness and meaning, so I, II and III are correct.
qs.rel: LAC develops language skills while studying all subjects. Neighbours: Bullock Report 1975 'A Language for Life', NCF 2005 position paper on language.

qs.stem: How has the feature of live streaming, enabled by Web 2.0 and 3.0 technologies, benefited teachers in education?

opts.A: It limits learning to only in-person classroom settings.
opts.B: It eliminates the need for audio-visual tools.
opts.C: It allows teachers to restrict access to information.
opts.D: It enables teachers to deliver and record lectures or demonstrations from remote locations.

qs.sol: Live streaming lets teachers teach or demonstrate from elsewhere and record material for later access. “It limits learning to only in-person classroom settings.” does not fit: live streaming extends teaching beyond the classroom.
qs.rel: English words like 'pedagogy' are of Greek origin ('pais' child, 'agogos' leader). Neighbours: Latin roots, etymology, loan words.

qs.stem: What does John Dewey emphasize on?

opts.A: That education should be a social process

qs.sol: Dewey treated education as a social process through experience, participation and interaction.
qs.rel: Syntax in writing means word order and sentence structure. Neighbours: grammar, punctuation, cohesion, coherence.

qs.stem: Hierarchy of human needs was proposed by _______.
qs.sol: Abraham Maslow proposed the hierarchy of human needs. “Pavlov” is associated with classical conditioning, which explains learned stimulus responses rather than a hierarchy of needs.
qs.rel: Motivation, self-confidence and attitude play a role in language acquisition (Krashen's affective filter). Neighbours: anxiety, integrative vs instrumental motivation (Gardner).

qs.stem: In which year was EDUSAT launched?
qs.sol: “2004” is supported: EDUSAT, India’s dedicated educational satellite, was launched in 2004. By contrast, “2001” 2001 predates the EDUSAT launch.
qs.rel: Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) aims at communicative competence through interaction (Hymes, Canale and Swain). Neighbours: Grammar-Translation, Direct method, Audio-lingual method.

qs.stem: David Kolb, an educational researcher, developed a ____________ reflective model.
qs.sol: Kolb’s experiential learning cycle has four stages: concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualisation and active experimentation. “three-stage” does not fit: three stages omit a phase of Kolb's experience-reflection-concept-action cycle.
qs.rel: LAC means Language Across the Curriculum. Neighbours: content and language integrated learning (CLIL), subject teachers' role.

qs.stem: अधिगम के लिए आकलन में होने वाली मुख्य प्रक्रिया कौन सी है?

opts.A: शिक्षक प्रत्येक छात्र को उनके अधिगम में सुधार करने के तरीके के बारे में प्रतिक्रिया प्रदान करता है
opts.B: छात्रों से प्रश्न करना कि वे किस स्तर पर हैं।
opts.C: छात्र जो अपने आकलन और मूल्यांकन हेतु शिक्षकों पर निर्भर रहते है।

qs.sol: अधिगम के लिए आकलन में प्रत्येक शिक्षार्थी को सुधार के लिए उपयोगी प्रतिपुष्टि दी जाती है।
qs.rel: Latest trend: grammar integrated with text and taught in context, not isolated. Neighbours: whole language, task-based learning, functional approach.

qs.stem: कौन सी जोड़ी प्रतिभागियों को पारस्परिक कौशल, आत्मविश्वास, संचार और मुखरता विकसित करने में मदद करता हैं?
qs.sol: मिश्रित लिंग की जोड़ी विभिन्न लिंगों के बीच संचार और पारस्परिक आत्मविश्वास का अभ्यास देती है।
qs.rel: Multilingualism is integral to India's linguistic heritage; classrooms are multilingual. Neighbours: NCF 2005, NEP 2020, 121 major languages (Census 2011).

qs.stem: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct? I. Materials for activity learning need to be relevant, contextual and related to real life experiences II. Textbook is an essential material for teaching and learning
qs.sol: Activity-learning materials should connect to learners’ contexts and daily experience. A textbook can also serve as a core resource for structured teaching and learning. Both printed claims are acceptable.
qs.rel: Listening is the first step in language learning. Neighbours: LSRW sequence, natural approach, comprehensible input.

qs.stem: Which of the following is an important benefit of using Indian Sign Language (ISL) or Indian Sign System (ISS) in classroom settings for school subjects?

opts.A: It is used only for social conversations, not academic content.
opts.B: It replaces all spoken and written language in schools.
opts.C: It restricts communication to non-verbal cues only.
opts.D: It helps in enhancing the conceptual understanding and participation of deaf students.

qs.sol: “It helps in enhancing the conceptual understanding and participation of deaf students.” is correct because accessible signing lets students engage with subject explanations and classroom exchange. “It is used only for social conversations, not academic content.” is too restrictive: sign language can express academic concepts as well as everyday conversation.
qs.rel: Integrating language instruction across subjects builds effective communication. Neighbours: LAC, CLIL, discourse in subjects.

qs.stem: An artist uses paper, canvas, clay, metal, paint etc. which can be moulded or transformed to create some physical or art object. Which of the following are those physical or art objects? I. Drawing II. Painting III. Sculpture IV. Design
qs.sol: Drawing, painting, sculpture, and design can all be physical or visual art outcomes made through transforming materials such as paper, clay, metal, or paint. The passage lists materials and asks for products of artistic creation. A design may be embodied on paper or another medium, so there is no reason to exclude it while retaining the other three forms.
qs.rel: Multilingual strategies (translanguaging, mother tongue support) address linguistic diversity. Neighbours: NEP 2020 mother tongue as medium, bilingual textbooks.

qs.stem: Which practice best supports experiential learning in graduate education?
qs.sol: Experiential learning is supported by active engagement with real problems. Problem solving gives learners direct experience instead of only passive reception.
qs.rel: Levels of language: phonetics/phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics. 'English' is a language not a level. Neighbours: discourse level.

qs.stem: What is the primary goal of behaviour modification?

opts.B: To increase adaptive behaviour and decrease maladaptive behaviour
opts.C: To encourage free expression of emotions
opts.D: To provide medication for behavioural issues

qs.sol: “To increase adaptive behaviour and decrease maladaptive behaviour” is correct: Behaviour modification uses learning principles to strengthen useful behaviour and reduce behaviour that interferes with functioning. “To diagnose mental disorders” fails: Diagnosing a mental disorder is an assessment task, not the principal goal of behaviour modification.
qs.rel: Reading material should be meaningful, interesting and graded. Neighbours: phonics, whole word method, look-and-say, reading readiness.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा, विकास की प्रमुख विशेषता है?

opts.A: यह किशोरावस्था के बाद रुक जाता है।
opts.B: यह एक गुणात्मक परिवर्तन होता है।
opts.C: यह सामाजिक प्रभाव से अप्रभावित रहता है।
opts.D: यह शरीर की ऊँचाई तक सीमित होता है।

qs.sol:
संकल्पना: विकासात्मक मनोविज्ञान में वृद्धि और विकास का भेद उनके द्वारा सूचित परिवर्तन के प्रकार के आधार पर किया जाता है। वृद्धि मात्रात्मक परिवर्तन है—आकार, भार, ऊँचाई अथवा संख्या में ऐसी मापनीय बढ़ोतरी, जिसे इकाइयों में व्यक्त किया जा सकता है। विकास गुणात्मक परिवर्तन है—संरचना, संगठन और कार्यशीलता में प्रगतिशील परिवर्तन, जो केवल मात्रा बढ़ाने के बजाय व्यक्ति की कार्य-क्षमता के स्वरूप को बदलता है। विकास को जीवन-पर्यंत तथा शारीरिक, संज्ञानात्मक, संवेगात्मक, सामाजिक, नैतिक और भाषायी आयामों में बहुआयामी माना जाता है; यह वंशानुक्रम और सामाजिक-सांस्कृतिक वातावरण की सतत अंतःक्रिया से निर्मित होता है।

आधार

	

वृद्धि

	

विकास




परिवर्तन की प्रकृति

	

मात्रात्मक; इकाइयों में मापनीय

	

गुणात्मक …
qs.rel: Listening is a receptive mode: comprehending oral input. Neighbours: intensive/extensive listening, top-down listening, dictation.

qs.stem: An employee who is unhappy because of ______ processes in a business can negatively affect the corporate image of the business and make it less successful.
qs.sol: Poor communication processes can create confusion, dissatisfaction and mistrust among employees. An unhappy employee can harm the organisation's image and reduce business success, so poor communication is the correct answer.
qs.rel: Language is rule-governed: word order and structure guide sentence formation. Neighbours: Chomsky's generative grammar, competence vs performance.

qs.stem: Which of the following best describes the nature of science as a discipline?

opts.A: It relies on observation and experimentation of nature.
opts.B: It cannot be tested or scientifically verified.
opts.C: It ignores facts and focuses only on imagination.
opts.D: It is based only on personal opinions and beliefs

qs.sol: Science relies on observation, experimentation, evidence and verification. It is not based only on imagination, opinion, or untestable claims.
qs.rel: Reading and writing are literacy skills (decoding/encoding written language). Neighbours: LSRW, reading readiness, emergent literacy.

qs.stem: भाषा अधिग्रहण के चरण - बच्चों की आयु का निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा संयोजन सही है? I. बड़बड़ाना - लगभग 6 महीने II एक शब्द चरण - लगभग 1 वर्ष

opts.D: ना ही I ना ही II

qs.sol: बच्चे लगभग छह महीने की आयु में बार-बार बोलने जैसी ध्वनियाँ निकालते हैं, जिसे बड़बड़ाहट कहते हैं। लगभग एक वर्ष में एक शब्द से पूरा अर्थ व्यक्त करने का चरण आता है। बच्चों में कुछ अंतर होता है, पर दोनों अनुमानित आयु भाषा अर्जन के सामान्य क्रम से मेल खाती हैं। लगभग एक वर्ष का एक-शब्द चरण भी सही है। लगभग छह महीने की बड़बड़ाहट भी सही है। दोनों अनुमानित आयु विकास क्रम से मिलती हैं। दोनों चरण देखे जाते हैं, इसलिए निषेध गलत है।
qs.rel: Language acquisition stages: cooing ~2 months, babbling ~6 months, first word ~12 months, two-word stage ~18-24 months. Neighbours: telegraphic speech, holophrases.

qs.stem: Which of the following options best describes the difference between sex and gender?

opts.A: Gender is fixed, while sex changes over time.
opts.B: Sex is biologically determined, while gender is socially constructed.
opts.C: Sex is a social role, while gender is based on anatomy.
opts.D: Sex and gender mean the same thing.

qs.sol: “Sex is biologically determined, while gender is socially constructed.” is correct: Sex generally refers to biological attributes, while gender concerns socially shaped roles and identities. “Sex is a social role, while gender is based on anatomy.” fails: The reversed formulation assigns social roles to sex and anatomy to gender, so it swaps the concepts.
qs.rel: Literature elicits spontaneity and integrated language learning in early years. Neighbours: stories, rhymes, picture books, read-aloud.

qs.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.

Reflection on reading is said to be complete only when it includes:
qs.sol: Reflection requires interpreting what was read and discussing that interpretation; analysis and discussion complete the reflective process.
qs.rel: Reflection on reading is complete when it includes analysis and discussion. Neighbours: pre-, while-, post-reading stages, comprehension levels.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is not a function of a teacher?

1. Evaluating the achievement of pupils.

2. Preparation of progress-reports.

Choose the correct code.
qs.sol: “Neither 1 nor 2” is supported because evaluating pupils and preparing progress reports are both teacher duties, so neither is excluded. “Only 1” wrongly excludes evaluation of pupil achievement, which is a normal teacher duty.
qs.rel: A six-year-old child's vocabulary averages roughly 2500-2600 words (varies by source: about 2500). Neighbours: 2-year-old 200-300 words; 5-year-old ~2000.

qs.stem: Which of following principles of learning states that ‘most recently learned are the best remembered’ ?
qs.sol:
No official answer key was published for this paper; the answer is worked out from the question.

The recency principle says recently learned material is retained most readily.

Primacy instead favours early learning, while intensity concerns the strength or vividness of an experience.
qs.rel: 'Listen and draw' checks vocabulary of objects and prepositions - listening comprehension. Neighbours: TPR (Total Physical Response by James Asher), listening tasks.

qs.stem: In the management of group-learning, which kind of grouping might lead to the labelling of few students as bright and few as weak?
qs.sol: Ability grouping can label pupils as bright or weak according to their assigned group.
qs.rel: Language ability is partly wired in our genetics (Chomsky's innateness, Language Acquisition Device). Neighbours: critical period hypothesis (Lenneberg), Pinker.

qs.stem: Language ability is partially wired in our__________.
qs.sol: “genetics” is appropriate because inherited biological factors contribute to the human capacity to acquire language, alongside experience and interaction. “practice” helps develop language skills but does not account for the partly inborn capacity described by the question.
qs.rel: Grammar-Translation Method derives from classical Latin and Greek teaching. Neighbours: Direct method, audio-lingual, CLT, emphasis on reading and translation.

qs.stem: यूनेस्को योजना मिशन के यूएसएसआर विशेषज्ञ किस वर्ष तकनीकी सहायता परियोजना पर भारत आए थे?
qs.sol: भारत में विज्ञान शिक्षा के इतिहास के अनुसार यूनेस्को योजना मिशन के यूएसएसआर विशेषज्ञ तकनीकी सहायता परियोजना पर 1963 में भारत आए थे।
qs.rel: Skimming (gist) and scanning (specific info) are reading techniques. Neighbours: intensive/extensive reading, SQ3R, speed reading.

qs.stem:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन से साहित्यिक उपकरण हैं?

I. मैटाफर

II. आयरनी

III. राइम
qs.sol: अवधारणा: साहित्यिक उपकरण वे तकनीकें हैं जिनसे लेखक भाषा में अर्थ, प्रभाव या सौंदर्य रचते हैं। रूपक समानता सुझाता है, आयरनी कथन या अपेक्षा और वास्तविकता के बीच विरोध दिखाती है, तथा राइम समान ध्वनियों की पुनरावृत्ति है। अनुप्रयोग: I में रूपक किसी वस्तु को दूसरी वस्तु के रूप में प्रस्तुत करता है; II में आयरनी अपेक्षा या कही गई बात और वास्तविक स्थिति का अंतर दिखाती है; III में राइम मिलती-जुलती ध्वनियाँ दोहराती है। तुलना: रूपक अर्थ-संबंधी तुलना, आयरनी विरोधाभास और राइम ध्वनि-पैटर्न पर केंद्रित हैं। इसलिए I, II तथा III साहित्यिक उपकरण हैं।
qs.rel: Literary devices: metaphor, irony, rhyme, simile, personification, alliteration. Neighbours: figures of speech, imagery, symbolism.

qs.stem: Which feature best describes a 'rule governed system' in the context of language?

opts.A: Language operates with structured rules for grammar and syntax.
opts.B: Language does not have any structure or authentic rules for all
opts.C: Language is naturally evolving with new rules which may change
opts.D: Language is based only on spoken words and written expressions

qs.sol: A rule-governed language system means that language works through structured rules of grammar, syntax and usage.
qs.rel: A rule-governed system operates with structured rules for grammar. Neighbours: Chomsky's universal grammar, productive rules.

qs.stem: At approximately what age do most children begin to combine two words to form simple sentences, indicating a key milestone in language development?
qs.sol: Two-word combinations typically emerge at roughly 18 to 24 months as an early language milestone. “12 months” does not fit: at twelve months many children have single words, not usual two-word combinations.
qs.rel: Children combine two words around 18-24 months (telegraphic speech). Neighbours: holophrase 12-18 months, 50-word vocabulary at ~18 months.

qs.stem: Communicative Lessons are not _______________.
qs.sol: Communicative lessons emphasize meaning in context and authentic learner interaction, rather than a primarily grammatical format.
qs.rel: Communicative lessons are contextualised, learner-centred and authentic, not grammar-drilled. Neighbours: authenticity, fluency, information gap.

qs.stem:
Choose the correct option to complete the sentence.

“Dialogic teaching and learning” that harnesses cognition in students emphasises:

opts.B: Interaction between students and the teacher
opts.D: Involving parents in the teaching process

qs.sol: Dialogic teaching develops understanding through exchange between students and teacher. Cognition is engaged by questions, responses and discussion.
qs.rel: Dialogic teaching (Robin Alexander) uses interaction between teacher and students to harness talk. Neighbours: Vygotsky, Bakhtin, Mercer.

qs.stem: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct? I. Language acquisition refers to developing competence in a language by using it in natural, communicative situations (as available while learning languages we hear in our homes and the neighbourhood). II. Language learning refers to developing competence in a language by learning it rules and vocabulary through explicit teaching in a classroom setting.
qs.sol: Acquisition develops language through natural communicative exposure and use. Classroom language learning may explicitly teach grammar rules and vocabulary. The two descriptions therefore distinguish the processes correctly.
qs.rel: Language acquisition is natural, subconscious; learning is conscious formal. Neighbours: Krashen's five hypotheses.

qs.stem: In the 'Language Across the Curriculum' approach, whose responsibility is language education considered to be at school?
qs.sol:
Concept

Language Across the Curriculum (LAC) is the pedagogical principle that language learning is embedded in every subject rather than confined to a language period. In every classroom, language is the medium through which learners listen, speak, read, write, discuss, and construct subject knowledge.

Therefore, responsibility for developing learners’ language proficiency is shared across the teaching staff: each teacher supports the language practices needed to learn that teacher’s subject. …
qs.rel: In LAC, language education is every school teacher's responsibility. Neighbours: Bullock Report, content-area literacy.

qs.stem: Which productive oral skill receives the least structured practice in the Grammar Translation Method of English teaching?
qs.sol:
Modified from the original question: both listening and speaking could be considered neglected, so “productive oral” was added to identify the intended skill.

Grammar Translation centers on reading texts, studying rules and writing translations. Learners may hear explanations, but spontaneous spoken production is rarely practiced.

Speaking is the productive oral skill; listening is receptive, while reading and writing are written skills.
qs.rel: In the Grammar Translation Method speaking gets least structured practice. Neighbours: reading and writing emphasised, mother tongue as medium.

qs.stem: Which productive oral skill receives the least structured practice in the Grammar Translation Method of English teaching?
qs.sol:
Modified from the original question: both listening and speaking could be considered neglected, so “productive oral” was added to identify the intended skill.

Grammar Translation centers on reading texts, studying rules and writing translations. Learners may hear explanations, but spontaneous spoken production is rarely practiced.

Speaking is the productive oral skill; listening is receptive, while reading and writing are written skills.
qs.rel: GTM neglects speaking; Direct method and audio-lingual stress oral work. Neighbours: Berlitz, Palmer, Lado.

qs.stem: Which strategy is most effective for assessing early language acquisition in a classroom with varied learners?

opts.A: Checking for memorization of word lists

qs.sol: For varied young learners, observing interactive role-play gives direct evidence of early language acquisition in use. Written tests or word-list memorization are less suitable.
qs.rel: Observing interactive role-play scenarios is effective for assessing early language acquisition among varied learners. Neighbours: anecdotal records, checklists.

qs.stem: भाषा की ओर देखने का निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा तरीका भाषा की प्रतिभा और उसके उपयोग को प्रतिबंधित करता है? I. भाषा केवल संचार के साधन के रूप में। II. व्याकरण और शब्दकोश के संयोजन के रूप में भाषा।

opts.D: ना ही I ना ही II

qs.sol: भाषा को केवल संदेश पहुँचाने का साधन मानना उसके विचार, पहचान, खेल और सृजन से जुड़े उपयोगों को कम कर देता है। केवल व्याकरण और शब्दकोश का मेल मानना भी संदर्भ, बदलाव और वास्तविक प्रयोग को नहीं समझाता। प्रश्न सीमित दृष्टिकोण पहचानने को कहता है। दोनों प्रस्ताव भाषा की बहुमुखी क्षमता को संकुचित करते हैं, इसलिए दोनों को चुनना तर्कसंगत है।
qs.rel: Views on language: language as resource, as right, as problem (Ruiz); language as a skill vs as a resource. Neighbours: NCF 2005 treat multilingualism as a resource.

qs.sol: पठन और पाठों पर चिंतन से भाषा की समझ तथा अभिव्यक्ति विकसित होती है।
qs.rel: Reading and reflecting on lessons develops language comprehension and expression. Neighbours: reading comprehension, reflective reading.

qs.sol: “यह स्वतःस्फूर्त संचार को प्रोत्साहित करता है और व्यावहारिक भाषा कौशल में सुधार करता है।” सही है, क्योंकि प्राकृतिक सांकेतिक भाषा में हास्य साझा करने से शिक्षार्थी अर्थ, समय और सामाजिक संदर्भ के अनुसार स्वतः संवाद करने का अभ्यास करते हैं। “यह दोहराव पर ध्यान केंद्रित करके व्याकरण संबंधी त्रुटियों की बारंबारता को कम करता है।” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि सिर्फ दोहराव से व्याकरण की त्रुटियाँ घटाने पर जोर इस गतिविधि का मुख्य व्यावहारिक भाषा लाभ नहीं बताता।
qs.rel: Spontaneous communication and practical language use are encouraged by communicative/natural approaches. Neighbours: role play, language games.

qs.stem: During the preschool years (3-6), what primarily drives the explosive vocabulary growth from hundreds to thousands of words?

opts.A: Incidental exposure through social interactions and rich language environments
opts.B: Repetitive drilling of isolated words in structured classroom settings
opts.C: Exclusive focus on reading printed materials without oral practice
opts.D: Formal grammar instruction and rote memorization techniques

qs.sol: Preschool vocabulary grows rapidly mainly through rich language environments and incidental exposure during social interaction.
qs.rel: Vocabulary explosion at 3-6 years comes from incidental exposure through social interaction. Neighbours: fast mapping, Vygotsky, language-rich environment.

qs.stem: Why is the number of words in each language often found to be lower in bilingual children compared to monolingual children?

opts.A: Because they struggle with language development
opts.B: Because they learn fewer words overall
opts.C: Because their vocabulary is divided between two languages
opts.D: Because they have limited cognitive capacity

qs.sol: Bilingual children often divide their vocabulary across two languages. A word known in one language may not have an equally used equivalent in the other language, so the count within each single language can appear lower than in monolingual children. This does not mean they know fewer words overall or have weaker cognitive ability.
qs.rel: Bilingual children's vocabulary per language is lower because it is divided between languages; total vocabulary is similar or higher. Neighbours: code-mixing, conceptual vocabulary.

qs.stem: “Readers look at the organization of the text and ideas without relating it to their prior knowledge or experience” which of the reading models does this define?
qs.sol:
The described model derives meaning from the text rather than using prior knowledge to generate expectations.

It proceeds from textual units towards understanding, which is bottom-up processing.
qs.rel: Bottom-up model: reader decodes text starting from letters/words (Gough). Neighbours: top-down (Goodman) and interactive (Rumelhart).

qs.stem: Creating supportive environment for critical and creative writing comes under which strategy for promoting active learning?
qs.sol: The activity named in the stem is critical and creative writing. A supportive setting lets learners generate ideas, test expressions, revise, and communicate an original view. Those actions directly fit creative learning as a strategy for active participation. Problem solving centres on identifying and resolving a defined problem, which is not the focus stated here. Visual-based learning would rely on pictures or other visual material. Cooperative learning is organised around peers working together, but no group structure is mentioned. The decisive clue is the learner’s production of writing and ideas, rather than a visual aid, a fixed problem, or a team task.
qs.rel: Supportive environment for critical and creative writing is creative learning. Neighbours: process writing, brainstorming, drafting, editing.

qs.stem: “Readers come with a prior knowledge and experiences and continue to read as long as the text confirms their expectations” which of the reading models does this define?
qs.sol:
The reader starts with prior knowledge and expectations rather than letter-by-letter decoding.

Those expectations guide interpretation and are checked against the text.

The board selects the top-down model for this expectation-led description.

Note on the official key: Interactive reading can also draw on prior knowledge, but combines it with bottom-up decoding. The stem does not describe that combined process.
qs.rel: Top-down model: reader uses prior knowledge and expectations (Goodman's psycholinguistic guessing game). Neighbours: schema theory, bottom-up.

qs.stem:
Choose the right answer. 

Before reading activity is important in which of these subject as it preempts the student with predictions and 

vocabulary?
qs.sol:
Note on the official key: Science is the accepted answer. Languages is also defensible because predicting a text’s content and preparing unfamiliar vocabulary are common before-reading activities in language lessons. Such preparation can also help with Mathematics and Social studies, so the stated activities do not identify a unique subject.

Before-reading activities activate prior knowledge and prepare students for a text. In scientific texts, predictions about concepts and familiarity with technical vocabulary can aid understanding.
qs.rel: Pre-reading activities like prediction are important in science and all subjects. Neighbours: KWL charts, advance organisers.

qs.stem: Which among these is the method of teaching prose (गद्यशिक्षणविधिः) in Sanskrit ?
qs.sol:
No official answer key was published for this paper; the answer is worked out from the question.

Katha-kathana is the storytelling method used for narrative prose.

Dandanvaya and Khandanvaya focus on construing verse, while Geeta-natya uses song and drama.

The prose-teaching method among these is Katha-kathana.
qs.rel: Katha-kathana vidhi (storytelling) is a method of teaching prose in Sanskrit. Neighbours: Pathya-pustaka, Bhandarkar, Direct method, Vyakhya vidhi.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements best explains the sequence of language development in typically hearing children?

opts.A: Language development begins only after age 3
opts.B: Children first speak, then understand language
opts.C: Reception of language occurs before expression

qs.sol: “Reception of language occurs before expression” is correct: Children generally understand words and messages before they can use them expressively. “Children first speak, then understand language” fails: Putting speech before understanding reverses this usual receptive to expressive sequence.
qs.rel: In typical hearing children, reception (understanding) precedes expression. Neighbours: babbling, jargon, first words.

qs.stem: In Language as a school Subject which is not Methodology of teaching ?
qs.sol: The preview marks “Function oriented” as not a teaching methodology, but functional approaches to language teaching are established. Form-focused and product-oriented approaches also exist, while “teacher oriented” describes classroom control rather than a distinct language method. The printed choices do not support a unique answer; the preview key is retained with this limitation.
qs.rel: Methodology of teaching language: learner-oriented, structure-oriented; 'function-oriented' is an approach, not as listed. Neighbours: structural, situational and notional-functional approaches.

qs.stem: A post-1950s secondary school principal must adopt a language instruction policy that promotes national integration while preserving cultural diversity. Which constitutional strategy, endorsed by subsequent educational policies, should the principal utilize?

opts.D: Compulsory instruction in Union official language

qs.sol: The principal should implement the Three-Language Formula. It balances mother tongue/regional language, Hindi or another Indian language, and English, thereby supporting national integration without erasing linguistic diversity.
qs.rel: Three-Language Formula promotes national integration while preserving linguistic diversity (NPE 1968, Kothari). Neighbours: Hindi, English, regional; NEP 2020 flexibility.

qs.sol: “आरंभिक अंतःक्रियाओं और उद्दीपनों पर अत्यधिक ध्यान दिया जाना महत्वपूर्ण हैं।” इसलिए सटीक है कि प्रारंभिक अनुभव, बातचीत और उपयुक्त उद्दीपन सोच तथा भाषा के विकास में भूमिका निभाते हैं। “आनुवंशिक वंशागति पूरी तरह से संज्ञान को निर्धारित करती है।” पर्यावरण और सीखने के योगदान को नकारता है, जबकि विकास केवल आनुवंशिकता से तय नहीं होता।
qs.rel: Early interaction and stimulation are vital for language growth. Neighbours: input, caregiver talk, critical period.

qs.stem: By using ______, as a teacher try to speak English as much of time as you can. I. mime II. puppets III. acting
qs.sol: Mime, puppets and acting all give learners visible context for a teacher’s English speech. Gesture can demonstrate meaning without constant translation, a puppet can support dialogue, and acting can model an action or situation. The question asks which aids help the teacher speak English as much as possible. Each technique can make language comprehensible, so the inclusive combination is justified.
qs.rel: Mime, puppets and acting support use of English in class. Neighbours: TPR, drama techniques, visual aids.

qs.stem: In a classroom , translanguaging may not involve which of the following ?

opts.B: comparing and being playful with different languages
opts.C: using school language compulsorily in whole part of the activity
opts.D: mixing words and expressions from different languages in the same spoken or written utterance

qs.sol: Using only the school language throughout excludes the multilingual practices described.
qs.rel: Translanguaging uses learners' full linguistic repertoire; it does not compel use of only the school language. Neighbours: Ofelia Garcia, code-switching.

qs.stem:
‘Problem related to languages’ is one of the hurdles to school-family-community partnerships.
 Which of the following actions can be taken with respect to this hurdle?
 I. Set aside a room in the school in which to provide child care during events.
 II. Have printed materials translated into home languages.
 III. Help parents set up car pools.
qs.sol: For a language-related hurdle in school-family-community partnership, the relevant action is to translate printed materials into home languages. Child care and car pools address different barriers.
qs.rel: Language barriers in school-family partnership are addressed by translators and multilingual communication. Neighbours: parental engagement, SMC.

qs.stem:
Complete the sentence with one of the options given below.
Reading can be defined as a:

opts.A: Simple comprehension process of given symbols
opts.B: Complex cognitive process of decoding symbols
opts.C: Multiple tasking process of given text
opts.D: Dual tasking process with set expectations

qs.sol:
Reading means decoding written symbols into sounds and words, and then constructing meaning from them using language knowledge, prior knowledge and inference.

Because it combines perception, memory, language and thinking, it is a complex cognitive process, not a simple one.

Hence: complex cognitive process of decoding symbols.
qs.rel: Reading is a complex cognitive process of decoding symbols. Neighbours: decoding and comprehension, Simple View of Reading.

qs.stem: What is one key benefit of multilingual education?
qs.sol:
Multilingual education refers to classroom teaching that uses more than one language, often building on a learner's mother tongue rather than replacing it. Policy frameworks such as UNESCO's guidance on multilingualism and India's National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 treat this approach as a way to value and maintain the range of languages children bring to school, alongside supporting their overall academic development.

Applying this to the item: among the four outcomes offered, the one that matches what these frameworks attribute to multilingual instruction is the outcome of keeping multiple languages actively spoken and valued in the learning environment. …
qs.rel: Multilingual education promotes cultural and linguistic diversity. Neighbours: mother tongue-based MLE, additive bilingualism.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से किस साक्षरता ने एक सामुदायिक प्रयास किया?
qs.sol: राष्ट्रीय साक्षरता मिशन ने साक्षरता के विस्तार में समुदाय की भागीदारी को केंद्र में रखा।
qs.rel: Literacy campaigns: National Literacy Mission (1988), Total Literacy Campaign (Ernakulam 1989). Neighbours: Saakshar Bharat 2009.

qs.stem:
नादविद्या जरूरी नहीं है ______।

वाक्य को पूरा करने के लिए सबसे अच्छा विकल्प चुनें।

opts.D: लगता है कि शब्द का मतलब है

qs.sol: नादविद्या अक्षर और ध्वनि के संबंध सिखाती है; शब्द का उच्चारण सीखने से उसका अर्थ जानना अनिवार्य नहीं होता।
qs.rel: Nada-vidya relates to the study of sound in Indian linguistic thought. Neighbours: varna, sphota (Bhartrihari), Panini's Ashtadhyayi.

qs.stem: “Complex cognitive process” of decoding symbols is called:
qs.sol: Reading requires decoding written symbols into language and meaning.
qs.rel: Reading = complex cognitive process of decoding symbols. Neighbours: sub-skills, phonics, fluency, comprehension.

qs.stem: “शब्दावली विकास” निम्न में से किसका एक आवश्यक घटक है?
qs.sol:
आधिकारिक उत्तर-कुंजी पर टिप्पणी: बोर्ड की आधिकारिक उत्तर-कुंजी "निर्देश पढ़ना" को सही मानती है। तर्कसंगत उत्तर "भाषा कौशल" है, क्योंकि शब्दावली पठन, श्रवण, बोलने और लेखन सहित भाषा-क्षमता का घटक है। इस प्रश्न का मूल्यांकन आधिकारिक कुंजी के अनुसार किया गया है, जैसा वास्तविक परीक्षा में हुआ।

शब्दावली लिखित निर्देश समझने में सहायता करती है, इसलिए “निर्देश पढ़ना” से उसका संबंध है। लेकिन निर्देश पढ़ना शब्दावली के उपयोग का एक प्रसंग है, वह व्यापक क्षमता नहीं जिसका शब्दावली विकास घटक हो। “भाषा कौशल” ग्रहणशील और अभिव्यक्तिपरक दोनों कार्यों में शब्दावली को समेटता है।
qs.rel: Vocabulary development is a component of reading instruction. Neighbours: word recognition, context clues, morphology.

qs.stem: Harnessing the power of talk to stimulate and extend thinking and learning in pupil is advocated by which of the teaching methods given below?
qs.sol: Dialogic teaching uses purposeful classroom talk to develop pupils’ thinking and learning.
qs.rel: Dialogic method uses talk to extend thinking (Alexander, Vygotsky). Neighbours: Socratic method, discussion, scaffolded talk.

qs.stem: Phonics approach facilitates reading because it ______ Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
qs.sol: Phonics teaches the correspondence between speech sounds and written letters, directly supporting decoding.
qs.rel: Phonics builds sound-letter relationships for decoding. Neighbours: synthetic vs analytic phonics, whole language, look-and-say.

qs.stem: समय के बजाय दूसरी भाषा में औसत उपलब्धि के संदर्भ में किस समूह का प्रदर्शन बेहतर रहता है?
qs.sol: आधिकारिक प्रश्नपत्र से संशोधित: पुस्तिका में महिला चिह्नित है, लेकिन प्रश्न सीखने की गति पूछता है जबकि उपलब्ध प्रमाण उपलब्धि मापते हैं, सीखने का समय नहीं। संशोधित प्रश्न दूसरी भाषा में औसत उपलब्धि के बारे में है; मेटा-विश्लेषण में महिला शिक्षार्थियों के पक्ष में छोटा औसत अंतर मिलता है, हर व्यक्ति के लिए नियम नहीं।
qs.rel: Second language learners and bilingual groups: studies on achievement compare groups (Cummins' threshold). Neighbours: submersion vs immersion programmes.

qs.stem: "टॉप डाउन मॉडल" और "बॉटम अप मॉडल" ______ का हिस्सा हैं।
qs.sol: टॉप डाउन और बॉटम अप मॉडल पढ़कर समझने की प्रक्रियाओं का वर्णन करते हैं।
qs.rel: Top-down and bottom-up are reading models. Neighbours: Goodman, Gough, interactive models.

qs.stem: दिए गए विषयों में से किसमें प्रत्येक वाक्य को कॉम्पैक्ट शैली में बहुत सारी जानकारी और न्यूनतम अनावश्यकता के साथ लिखा जाता है?
qs.sol: गणितीय भाषा प्रतीकों और सटीक कथनों से कम अनावश्यकता में अधिक जानकारी देती है।
qs.rel: Compact style of sentences characterises scientific or mathematical text. Neighbours: register, technical vocabulary.

qs.sol: मातृवाक् में स्वर, लय और अभिव्यक्ति सामान्य बातचीत की अपेक्षा अधिक अतिशयोक्तिपूर्ण होते हैं। “मंद स्वर (undertone)” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि मंद स्वर मातृवाक् के उभरे हुए स्वर-लय का वर्णन नहीं करता।
qs.rel: Mother-tongue speech to infants (motherese) has exaggerated tone, rhythm and expression. Neighbours: child-directed speech, language input.

topics.deep:
- **Skills (LSRW):** listening and reading = receptive; speaking and writing = productive. Order of acquisition: **listening -> speaking -> reading -> writing**. Levels of language: phonology/phonetics, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, discourse (a specific language like English is not a level). **Syntax** = rules governing word order and sentence structure; morphology = word formation; linguistics = scientific study of language. Language is a rule-governed, arbitrary symbolic system.
- **Theories of acquisition:**

| Theorist | Idea |
|---|---|
| Skinner | verbal behaviour, imitation and reinforcement |
| Chomsky | innate Language Acquisition Device, universal grammar; competence vs performance |
| Piaget | language follows cognition |
| Vygotsky | language from social interaction; private speech |
| Krashen | five hypotheses: acquisition-learning, monitor, natural order, **input (i+1)**, affective filter |
| Lenneberg | critical period hypothesis |
| Cummins | BICS vs CALP; threshold hypothesis; interdependence |
| Bruner | LASS (Language Acquisition Support System) |

- **Milestones:** cooing 2-3 months, **babbling ~6 months**, holophrases ~12 months (first word), 50 words and **two-word (telegraphic) stage 18-24 months**, vocabulary explosion 3-6 years (incidental exposure and interaction), about 2000-2500 words at 5-6 years; overregularisation ("runned") shows rule learning. Reception precedes expression.
- **Mother tongue and first language (L1):** acquired naturally from the environment, not by formal teaching; second language (L2) is learned; third language acquisition builds on L1/L2. **Bilingualism** = two languages, **multilingualism** = more than two. Benefits: cognitive flexibility, metalinguistic awareness, cultural understanding; bilingual children's vocabulary per language may be smaller but total concept vocabulary is similar. Subtractive vs additive bilingualism. **Translanguaging** uses the full linguistic repertoire (Ofelia Garcia).
- **Language policy:** Article 343 (Hindi official), Eighth Schedule (22 languages), Article 350A (mother-tongue instruction at primary stage), **Three-Language Formula** (Kothari Commission 1964-66, NPE 1968; NEP 2020 keeps it with flexibility), NEP 2020: home language/mother tongue as medium at least till Grade 5, preferably Grade 8. NCF 2005 treats multilingualism as a resource. Standard language is codified and used in media, administration, judiciary and education; dialect vs register vs lingua franca.
- **Language Across the Curriculum (LAC):** all teachers share responsibility for language development; Bullock Report 1975 "A Language for Life"; develops LSRW in every subject; subject-specific vocabulary and genre.
- **Methods of ELT/language teaching:**

| Method | Key features |
|---|---|
| Grammar-Translation | classical Latin/Greek based; translation, rules; **speaking least practised** |
| Direct (Berlitz) | target language only, no translation |
| Audio-lingual | habit formation, drills (Skinner, structuralism) |
| Structural-situational | Palmer, Hornby; sentence patterns in situations |
| **Communicative Language Teaching** | communicative competence (Hymes), meaning and interaction, authentic, learner-centred |
| Total Physical Response | James Asher; listening + action |
| Silent Way, Suggestopedia, CLL | Gattegno, Lozanov, Curran |
| Bilingual method | C. J. Dodson |
| Task-based, natural approach | Prabhu (Bangalore project), Krashen and Terrell |

- **Grammar teaching:** deductive (rule first) vs inductive (examples first); latest trend - grammar integrated with text in context. **Reading:** phonics (sound-letter), look-and-say/whole word, whole language; models - **bottom-up** (Gough; decoding), **top-down** (Goodman; prior knowledge and prediction), interactive (Rumelhart); skimming (gist) and scanning (specific information), intensive vs extensive reading; pre-, while-, post-reading stages; reading is a complex cognitive process of decoding symbols. **Writing:** process approach (plan, draft, revise, edit). **Listening activities:** listen and draw, dictation, TPR. Dialogic teaching (Robin Alexander) uses talk to extend thinking; role play, drama, puppets, mime support speaking.
- **Language assessment:** observation of role play, oral tests, portfolios, checklists, rubrics for LSRW.
- **Literary devices:** simile, metaphor, personification, irony, alliteration, rhyme; Sanskrit prose teaching includes katha-kathana (storytelling), vyakhya and sutra methods.

**Likely question angles:**
- Order of language skills; which are receptive/productive.
- Match theorists (Chomsky, Skinner, Krashen, Vygotsky) with their views.
- Age of babbling, first word, two-word stage.
- Method identification from description (GTM, direct, CLT, TPR).
- Bottom-up vs top-down reading definitions.
- LAC meaning, origin, responsibility of teachers.
- Three-language formula year/commission; constitutional articles on language.
- Benefits of multilingualism; BICS/CALP.
- Deductive vs inductive grammar teaching.
- Skimming vs scanning; phonics definition.

topics.title: 10. Pedagogy of Science, Maths, Social Science, EVS & Arts/Drama
topics.theory:
- **Scientific method:** sense problem -> define -> hypothesis -> experiment -> analyse -> conclude; memorising is not a step. Verified hypothesis creates new knowledge; **theory** = accepted hypothesis. Kuhn: paradigm shift; Popper: falsifiability.
- **Nature of science:** body of knowledge + process, empirical, open to all; best teaching by activities/inquiry (5E).
- **Mathematics (NCF 2005):** goal = **mathematisation of the child's mind**; aims - reasoning, brevity and precision; values - utilitarian, disciplinary, cultural. Activity/manipulative-based teaching for number concepts; maths language uses symbols (%, <, =).
- **Pre-number concepts:** matching, sorting, comparing, ordering. Maths is a hypothetico-deductive system.
- **Social science:** history, geography, civics, economics, sociology (medicine is not one). Approaches: **chronological**, regressive, concentric, topical; dramatisation, role play, maps, local literature make it participatory.
- **EVS (III-V):** six themes - family & friends, food, shelter, water, travel, things we make & do. Environmental education starts from kindergarten (cleanliness, care).
- **Arts education:** visual (painting, sculpture, clay, design) + performing arts; integration builds creativity, aesthetic sensibility, spatial ability, varied experiences; Tagore: art = creative soul's response.
- **Drama:** types - linear/scripted and **process-oriented drama**; role play = character embodiment; sources: imagination, environment, history/literature, movies; ~11 yrs can write simple scripts.
- Clay: right moisture, remove air bubbles; enhances creativity and fine motor skills.
- Local/indigenous knowledge helps community problem solving.

qs.stem: सामाजिक विज्ञान क्या है?
qs.sol: आधिकारिक प्रश्नपत्र से संशोधित: प्रीव्यू में समाजशास्त्र चिह्नित है, लेकिन भूगोल भी सामान्यतः सामाजिक विज्ञानों में शामिल है। इसलिए मुद्रित प्रश्न के दो सही विकल्प हैं।
qs.rel: Social science is the study of society and human relationships; sociology is the study of society. Neighbours: disciplines - history, geography, civics, economics, sociology.

qs.stem: Why is Social Science important in education?

opts.A: It focuses only on numbers and calculations
opts.B: It teaches us how to cook
opts.C: It helps us understand human behaviour and society
opts.D: It helps us understand natural phenomena

qs.sol: “It helps us understand human behaviour and society” is correct: Social Science studies people, institutions, relationships and life in society. “It helps us understand natural phenomena” fails: Natural phenomena are chiefly the focus of natural sciences.
qs.rel: Social science is important to understand human behaviour and society. Neighbours: aims - citizenship, critical thinking, values; NCF 2005 social science position paper.

qs.stem:
Which of the following content(s) is/are included when reporting an experiment?
 I. Apparatus used
 II. Procedure
qs.sol: CONCEPT: When a scientific experiment is written up, the report exists so that another person can understand exactly what was done and can repeat it. For that reason, a standard experiment report always documents several fixed pieces of information -- the aim/objective, the apparatus (equipment and materials) used, the procedure (the step-by-step method actually followed), the observations recorded, and the result/conclusion drawn from those observations. …
qs.rel: An experiment report includes apparatus, procedure, observations, results, conclusion. Neighbours: aim, hypothesis, precautions.

qs.sol: “भूमिका निर्वहण (Role play)” में विद्यार्थी संवाद, पात्र और अभिनय का स्वयं अभ्यास करते हैं, इसलिए नाटक को करके सीखते हैं। “स्लाइड शो (Slide show)” दृश्य जानकारी दे सकता है, पर जीवंत अभिनय और परस्पर प्रतिक्रिया का अभ्यास नहीं कराता।
qs.rel: Role play lets students enact characters and dialogues. Neighbours: simulation, dramatisation, socio-drama.

qs.stem: Which of the following is the primary benefit of classroom role-play?
qs.sol:
Role-play places learners in a simulated social or practical situation and requires them to respond within that context.

This rehearsal develops the ability to analyse and solve problems resembling real-life situations.
qs.rel: Role-play helps real-life problem solving and empathy. Neighbours: process drama, hot seating, forum theatre.

qs.stem:
People who work with visual images includes _____.
 I. Painters
 II. Sculptors
qs.sol: Painters and sculptors both work with visual images and visual-spatial expression.
qs.rel: Painters and sculptors work with visual images (visual arts). Neighbours: performing arts - dance, music, theatre; plastic arts.

qs.stem: एक समावेशी कक्षा सामान्य शिक्षा कक्षा है:

opts.A: जिसमें विकलांग/अविकलांग छात्र एक साथ सीखते हैं
opts.B: जिसमें विद्यार्थी अधिगम में भाग नहीं लेते हैं
opts.C: जिसमें छात्र व्यक्तिगत रूप से सीखते हैं

qs.sol: समावेशी कक्षा में दिव्यांग और गैर दिव्यांग छात्र सामान्य शिक्षा की एक ही व्यवस्था में साथ सीखते हैं। आवश्यकता के अनुसार शिक्षण में बदलाव करके सभी की भागीदारी सुनिश्चित की जाती है। जहाँ विद्यार्थी अधिगम में भाग ही न लें, वह उद्देश्य पूरा नहीं होता। व्यक्तिगत काम और स्वयं काम करना समावेशी कक्षा में हो सकता है, पर उनसे समावेशन की परिभाषा नहीं बनती। वे व्यवस्थाएँ यह नहीं बतातीं कि विभिन्न क्षमताओं वाले विद्यार्थी एक साथ शिक्षा पा रहे हैं या नहीं।

qs.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Learning?
qs.sol: Learning is usually described as a continuous, active, individual and purposeful (goal-directed) process. The learner keeps learning from experience throughout life, engages actively with what is learnt, and learns in a way and at a pace shaped by prior knowledge. Being unintentional is not one of these characteristics: standard descriptions treat learning as purposeful, directed towards goals the learner or teacher has set. Incidental learning does occur, but it is not presented as a defining characteristic of learning, so this is the trait that does not belong.
qs.rel: Drama and art make students better learners, with creativity and communication. Neighbours: art integrated learning, CBSE.

qs.sol:

qs.stem: What is the main characteristic of pedagogical leadership in schools?
qs.sol:
Pedagogical leadership (also called instructional leadership) is a school-leadership approach centred on improving the quality of teaching and learning, through curriculum guidance, mentoring teachers, and monitoring classroom practice, rather than through administrative authority, facility management, or budget control.

Applying this to the question: among the four listed characteristics, only "Focus on quality of teaching" describes work aimed directly at how well teachers teach and students learn, which is the defining purpose of pedagogical leadership in a school. …

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन कम दृष्टि वाले बच्चों के लिए सहायक उपकरण नहीं है?
qs.sol:
उत्तर-कुंजी पर टिप्पणी: DSSSB ने इस प्रश्नपत्र की केवल अनंतिम उत्तर-कुंजी जारी की थी, अंतिम कुंजी नहीं। अनंतिम कुंजी “स्पीच सिंथेसाइज़र” को सही मानती है। तर्कसंगत उत्तर “ब्रेल” है, क्योंकि ब्रेल मुख्यतः अंधत्व में स्पर्श से पढ़ने का साधन है, पर अल्प दृष्टि वाले विद्यार्थी को भी सहायता दे सकता है। इस प्रश्न का मूल्यांकन अनंतिम कुंजी के अनुसार किया गया है, जैसा वास्तविक परीक्षा में हुआ।

qs.stem:
Clay is a material of visual arts and crafts. What is the importance of clay?

II. It develops the fine motor skills
III. It helps in handling eye-hand co-ordination

qs.sol: Working with clay engages several aspects of child development at once. Shaping forms encourages imagination, pinching and rolling strengthen fine motor control, coordinating hands with sight supports eye hand control, and sustained making can build concentration and interest in art. Each statement describes a plausible benefit of a hands on visual arts activity. Excluding statement I ignores the open-ended creative work that clay modelling invites. Clay work can support creativity, fine movement, coordination and sustained attention. This omits the concentration and interest that extended making may develop. This leaves out eye hand coordination during shaping and manipulating clay.
qs.rel: Clay precautions: right water amount, avoid cracking, remove air bubbles (wedging). Neighbours: pinch pot, coil method, slab method.

qs.stem: Which of the following best describes the purpose of formative assessment?

opts.B: To compare students' performance with peers

opts.D: To evaluate the overall curriculum effectiveness
