qs.rel: Role play in process drama: character embodiment. Neighbours: hot seating, improvisation, tableaux.

qs.stem: Integrating drama and art into the school curriculum primarily aims to enhance students' overall development, specifically fostering their:
qs.sol:
Bloom's taxonomy identifies three domains of educational objectives: the cognitive domain (knowledge and academic understanding), the affective domain (attitudes, values, and appreciation of beauty), and the psychomotor domain (physical skills and coordination). Creative co-curricular activities such as drama and visual art are designed primarily to nurture the affective domain -- in particular, a learner's aesthetic sensibility: the capacity to perceive, appreciate, and create beauty, form, and expression.

Integrating drama and art into the school curriculum therefore targets this affective, creative dimension of a student's growth, alongside core academic learning. …
qs.rel: Mathematical language uses symbols like < {} + =. Neighbours: register of maths, notation, vocabulary.

qs.stem: How does gender intensify the experience of disability for women and men?

opts.A: By making them equally more visible in public life
opts.B: By reducing their dependence on others
opts.C: For women, it reinforces helplessness; for men, it challenges traditional masculinity
opts.D: By increasing their access to education and employment

qs.sol: Gender norms can compound disability: women may be stereotyped as helpless, while men may face pressure from expectations of masculinity. “By making them equally more visible in public life” does not fit: equal visibility ignores different gender stereotypes and barriers.
qs.rel: Drama and art enhance aesthetic sensibility. Neighbours: emotional development, creativity.

qs.stem: What is the most strongly recommended approach for teaching students with ASD?
qs.sol: Visual aids provide predictable, concrete support for many students with autism spectrum disorder. “Verbal instructions” alone can be fleeting and less concrete, while visual supports make tasks and sequences easier to follow.
qs.rel: Instructional material linking listening, language and cognition emerges from observation of auditory-verbal sessions. Neighbours: auditory-verbal therapy.

qs.stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है? I. एक समूह में एक इकाई के रूप में व्यक्तिगत आवश्यकता को महत्व देकर गुणवत्तापूर्ण शिक्षा प्रदान करने के विचार को समावेशी शिक्षा कहा जाता है। II. समावेश बच्चों में आंतरिक शक्ति निर्मित करना और आत्मविश्वास बढ़ाना है।

opts.D: ना ही I ना ही II

qs.sol: समावेशी शिक्षा समूह में पढ़ाते समय प्रत्येक बच्चे की अलग आवश्यकता को महत्त्व देती है। उसका लक्ष्य केवल एक कमरे में सबको बैठाना नहीं, बल्कि आत्मविश्वास और सहभागिता बढ़ाना भी है। साझा सीखने के वातावरण में व्यक्तिगत सहायता और बच्चों की आंतरिक शक्ति दोनों आवश्यक हैं। इस कारण दिए गए दोनों कथन समावेशन के उद्देश्य को सही तरह व्यक्त करते हैं।
qs.rel: Drama and art provide varied experiences for diverse learners. Neighbours: multiple intelligences, differentiated instruction.

qs.sol: “To develop instructional material linking listening, language and cognition” follows from studying model plans and observing individual auditory-verbal sessions: educators can see how these goals are taught together. “To focus solely on the academic performance of students” is too narrow because the sessions also address listening and language development.
qs.rel: Instructional material for auditory-verbal therapy links listening, language and cognition. Neighbours: model lesson plans.

qs.stem:
For students with diverse learning styles, integrating drama and art in education

primarily offers:
qs.sol:
Concept: Differentiated instruction theory holds that learners process information through different modalities — visual, auditory, kinesthetic, and reading/writing — so a single teaching method reaches only some students well.

Application: Drama asks students to move, speak, and embody roles, while art asks them to see, create, and represent ideas visually. Together they open up multiple sensory and expressive channels within the same lesson, so a learner who struggles with a purely verbal explanation can instead act it out or draw it — this is what "varied experiences" means here. …
qs.rel: Art integration offers varied experiences for diverse learning styles. Neighbours: Gardner's MI, VARK.

qs.stem: Scientific method follows a process. Identify which of the following is not part of a scientific process.
qs.sol:
The scientific method follows these steps: identify the problem, review and observe, form a hypothesis, gather data or experiment, analyse, and draw a conclusion.

Identifying the problem, gathering data and hypothesising are all part of it.

Magnifying (exaggerating) the problem is not a step, so it is the answer.
qs.rel: 'Magnify the problem' is not a scientific step; scientific steps: identify problem, hypothesis, experiment, analyse, conclude. Neighbours: Dewey.

qs.stem: Which cognitive ability involving the perception of shapes, depth and perspective can be developed by integrating visual arts in education?
qs.sol:
Modified from the official paper: The unqualified stem also allowed colour, physical and aesthetic development; it now asks specifically about reasoning with shapes, depth and perspective.

Drawing and sculpture require learners to judge proportions, depth, orientation and the arrangement of forms. Repeated practice strengthens spatial reasoning.

Colour recognition, motor development and aesthetic appreciation can also benefit from art, but they do not name the specified cognitive ability.
qs.rel: Visual arts develop spatial abilities (shapes, depth, perspective). Neighbours: Gardner's spatial intelligence, drawing.

qs.stem:
At the elementary level, how does awareness of regional arts and crafts help?

I. To recognise and promote traditional and contemporary art and art pieces.

II. To sensitise the children about the pluralistic cultural legacy of India – awareness of local crafts.
qs.sol: At the elementary level, awareness of regional arts and crafts helps children recognise and value traditional as well as contemporary art. It also sensitises them to India's pluralistic cultural heritage through local crafts. Hence, both I and II are correct.
qs.rel: Regional arts and crafts awareness promotes tradition and cultural identity. Neighbours: heritage education, NCF 2005, art education.

qs.stem:
If a teacher is teaching the topic 'Forts' to students, the teacher can perform introductory activities by making documentation cards indicating which of the following?

Statements:

I. Name of historical buildings.

II. Drawing of unique architectural features of the building such as pillars/domes etc.
qs.sol: CONCEPT: An introductory 'documentation card' activity is a pre-reading pedagogical tool used to orient students to a new topic before deeper study. A well-designed documentation card combines two complementary kinds of information: nominal/identification data (names, labels — what the subject is called) and descriptive/visual data (features, forms, structural elements — what the subject looks like). Combining both gives students a fuller entry point into the concept than either alone, because identification without visual detail stays abstract, and visual detail without identification stays disconnected from real examples. …
qs.rel: Introductory activities for 'Forts': documentation, maps, discussion. Neighbours: field visits, heritage education.

qs.stem: Which of the following suggestions cannot help you make teaching-learning process participatory in social science?

opts.A: Teach students how to cooperate with each other
opts.B: Link the school to the community at large
opts.C: Create a classroom that excludes group workspaces where resources are shared
opts.D: Arrange debate/discussions on emerging social issues such as dowry, population growth etc

qs.sol: Participatory teaching of social science, as recommended in NCF 2005, treats learners as active constructors of knowledge. It relies on cooperation among students, discussion of real social issues, and links between school and community so that classroom learning connects with lived experience. Shared group workspaces, where learners pool resources and work together on projects, are central to this approach. A classroom designed to exclude such group spaces pushes learners back into isolated, teacher-centred work and defeats the aim of participation.
qs.rel: A classroom that excludes group work cannot help participatory teaching. Neighbours: cooperative learning, discussion method, projects.

qs.stem:
Which of the following is/are the instructional objective(s) of mathematics?
 Statements:
 I. To apply addition of two digit numbers in solving problems of daily life.
 II. To apply formula of direct variable to solve simple problems of day to day life.
qs.sol: Applying two-digit addition to daily-life problems and using direct-variation formulas in day-to-day problems are both instructional objectives of mathematics.
qs.rel: Instructional objectives: apply addition of two-digit numbers, develop skills. Neighbours: Bloom's cognitive categories.

qs.stem: At which age a student can able to expand scenarios into simple dramatic scripts?
qs.sol:
Expanding a scenario into a script requires arranging events, assigning roles and writing dialogue that connects the events.

These tasks combine narrative organisation with the ability to consider characters’ viewpoints, skills that develop through later childhood and school practice.

Age 11 fits this later-childhood interpretation of independently expanding a scenario into a simple script.

Note on the official key: the paper marks 11. No curriculum framework or assessment standard is named, so this is the stated educational expectation rather than a universal minimum age; the exact boundary cannot be derived from the stem alone.
qs.rel: Around 11 years: students can expand scenarios into simple dramatic scripts. Neighbours: stages of drama development.

qs.stem:
Knowledge acquired through observation and experiences, verified scientifically via

systematic inquiry and experimentation, is best described as what?
qs.sol:
Concept: Epistemology classifies knowledge by its source and the way it is validated. Four classic sources are recognised: revelation (a truth disclosed by a divine or sacred source and accepted through faith), intuition (an immediate, non-inferential insight reached without inquiry), authority (a claim accepted because a trusted person, text, or institution asserts it), and empirical knowledge (derived from direct observation and experience, and confirmed through systematic, repeatable experimentation).

Application: The stem describes knowledge that is acquired through observation and experience and verified scientifically through systematic inquiry and experimentation. …
qs.rel: Empirical knowledge is based on observation and experiments. Neighbours: rationalism, authority, intuition.

qs.stem: ________ अधिगम या विद्वतापूर्ण जांच की एक शाखा है जो छात्रों (अध्ययन का कार्यक्रम) के लिए विशेष रूप से स्नातक और स्नातकोत्तर स्तरों में एक संरचना प्रदान करती है।
qs.sol: विद्यार्जन विषय विद्वत अध्ययन के क्षेत्र को संगठित करता है।
qs.rel: Pedagogy is the discipline of teaching-learning and scholarly inquiry into it. Neighbours: andragogy (adult learning, Knowles), heutagogy, didactics.

qs.sol: विज्ञान, सामाजिक विज्ञान और गणित के पाठ, निर्देश और उत्तर समझने के लिए पढ़ना और लिखना विशेष रूप से जरूरी हैं, इसलिए “पढ़ना और लिखना” सही है। “सुनना और बोलना” उपयोगी हैं, लेकिन लिखित विषय-वस्तु के अध्ययन और अभिव्यक्ति की अपेक्षित जोड़ी नहीं हैं।
qs.rel: Subject texts in science/maths/social science need reading comprehension strategies. Neighbours: LAC, content-area reading.

qs.stem: Which approach is best suited for promoting conceptual understanding of numbers among primary school students?

opts.A: Teaching numbers primarily through theoretical worksheets assigned for homework
opts.B: Teaching numbers primarily through hands-on materials (manipulatives) and real-life examples in lessons
opts.C: Teaching numbers primarily through the definitions stated in the textbook
opts.D: Teaching numbers primarily through repeated recitation of multiplication tables

qs.sol:
Concept: Young learners build genuine conceptual understanding of numbers when abstract ideas are first grounded in concrete, hands-on experience with physical objects and situations drawn from real life, before or alongside symbolic representation. This concrete-to-abstract progression helps a child construct the relationships between numbers rather than only memorising symbols or rules.

Application: Among the given options, using hands-on materials and real-life examples in lessons lets a student physically handle quantities and see numbers embedded in familiar situations, gradually linking these concrete experiences to the abstract number concept being taught. …
qs.rel: Hands-on materials promote conceptual understanding of number at primary level. Neighbours: Dienes, abacus, number line.

qs.stem: Which approach is best suited for promoting conceptual understanding of numbers among primary school students?

opts.A: Teaching numbers primarily through theoretical worksheets assigned for homework
opts.B: Teaching numbers primarily through hands-on materials (manipulatives) and real-life examples in lessons
opts.C: Teaching numbers primarily through the definitions stated in the textbook
opts.D: Teaching numbers primarily through repeated recitation of multiplication tables

qs.sol:
Concept: Young learners build genuine conceptual understanding of numbers when abstract ideas are first grounded in concrete, hands-on experience with physical objects and situations drawn from real life, before or alongside symbolic representation. This concrete-to-abstract progression helps a child construct the relationships between numbers rather than only memorising symbols or rules.

Application: Among the given options, using hands-on materials and real-life examples in lessons lets a student physically handle quantities and see numbers embedded in familiar situations, gradually linking these concrete experiences to the abstract number concept being taught. …
qs.rel: Concrete-to-abstract teaching with manipulatives builds number sense. Neighbours: Bruner's enactive, iconic, symbolic modes.

qs.sol: विज्ञान, सामाजिक विज्ञान और गणित के पाठ, निर्देश और उत्तर समझने के लिए पढ़ना और लिखना विशेष रूप से जरूरी हैं, इसलिए “पढ़ना और लिखना” सही है। “सुनना और बोलना” उपयोगी हैं, लेकिन लिखित विषय-वस्तु के अध्ययन और अभिव्यक्ति की अपेक्षित जोड़ी नहीं हैं।
qs.rel: Science, social science and maths texts require comprehension and language skills. Neighbours: LAC.

qs.stem: Integrating music in lessons enhances:
qs.sol:
Cross-curricular integration pairs a classroom activity with the specific cognitive-skill domain it most directly reinforces.

Music is built from countable, repeating rhythmic patterns and literal duration ratios -- for example, a half note equals two quarter notes. So musical activities give direct, hands-on practice in counting, ratio/proportion, and pattern recognition, the core sub-skills of mathematical ability. Classroom research finds music-integrated lessons measurably improve students' pattern recognition and mathematical performance.

Scientific skills are built through experimentation and hypothesis-testing activities, not rhythmic pattern work. …
qs.rel: Music integration enhances mathematical abilities (patterns, rhythm). Neighbours: Mozart effect claims, arts integration.

qs.stem:
Choose the best answer from the following.

Incorporating art in lessons leads to better comprehension and memory because it is:
qs.sol:
Art engages sight, movement and other senses during learning.

This sensory engagement creates additional cues for understanding and recall.
qs.rel: Art in lessons aids comprehension and memory via sensory learning. Neighbours: multisensory learning, dual coding.

qs.stem: Reading local literature helps a social science teacher to:

opts.A: contextualise the topic in classroom teaching

qs.sol:
Concept

Contextualisation (localisation) in pedagogy means linking a classroom topic to resources and experiences drawn from learners' own environment, so that an abstract syllabus idea becomes concrete and meaningful. Region-specific stories, folklore, and local writing are one such resource a teacher can draw on to build this link.

Application

When a social science teacher reads local literature, they gather region-specific examples, events, and social practices that can be woven directly into the lesson. …
qs.rel: Local literature helps contextualise topics in social science. Neighbours: local history, community resources.

qs.stem: The significance of an event lies in the context of its time of occurrence and the content is organised and studied as such in which of the following approaches?
qs.sol:
Concept: History/social-science content can be sequenced for teaching in several named ways. The Chronological approach organises and studies content strictly in the order of its time of occurrence, so an event's significance is understood in the context of the period in which it happened.

Application: The stem's criterion — significance tied to the time of occurrence, with content organised and studied in that order — is exactly the defining feature of the Chronological approach.

Spiral approach: the same theme is revisited at increasing levels of complexity across grade/class levels, not sequenced by when events occurred. …
qs.rel: Chronological approach organises events by time of occurrence. Neighbours: regressive, topical, psychological approaches.

qs.stem: What are the types of drama?

opts.B: Linear Drama method, Process oriented Drama
opts.D: Dance through Drama, Character in Drama

qs.sol:
Note on the answer key: DSSSB published only a provisional answer key for this paper, and no final key. The provisional key marks “Linear Drama method, Process oriented Drama”, which is the graded answer here. “Story drama, Music Drama” is also defensible, because story drama and music drama are also recognized forms of drama.

Linear and process oriented drama name two approaches used in educational drama. The Hindi stem asks how many types there are, while the English asks what the types are; neither establishes an exhaustive taxonomy. Story and music drama are also recognized forms, so the classification is broad.
qs.rel: Types of drama: linear (scripted) drama and process-oriented drama. Neighbours: story drama, improvisation.

qs.stem: Which of the following is not an importance of social science?

opts.A: Proves scientific experiments in social contexts.
opts.D: Provides equitable solutions for marginalised groups.

qs.sol: Social science helps understand human behaviour, is interdisciplinary, and can support equitable solutions. Proving scientific experiments in social contexts is not a core importance of social science.
qs.rel: Social science teaches humanities, not proving scientific experiments. Neighbours: importance - citizenship, awareness, values.

qs.stem: A curriculum committee is revising science teaching to better reflect evolving pedagogy. Which change best aligns with contemporary pedagogical practices?

opts.A: Restricting experiments to standardized procedures in manuals
opts.B: Including inquiry-based exploration and encouraging students’ reasoning
opts.C: Focusing only on strict discipline and traditional instruction
opts.D: Making teaching independent of students’ developmental patterns

qs.sol: Contemporary pedagogy in science encourages students to explore, ask questions, form explanations, and reason from evidence. Inquiry-based exploration makes learners active participants rather than passive followers of fixed procedures. Therefore, including inquiry and encouraging students’ reasoning is the best change.
qs.rel: Contemporary science pedagogy includes inquiry-based exploration. Neighbours: 5E model, constructivist, NCF 2005.

qs.stem: A teacher in a secondary school wants to help students understand the significance of economic activities in society. She decides to design an interdisciplinary project that connects economic systems with cultural diversity and political processes. Which approach best reflects the scope of social studies as described in the context?

opts.A: Integrating multiple themes to promote civic engagement.
opts.B: Focusing solely on economic theories for research.
opts.D: Teaching economic activities in isolation from other areas.

qs.sol: The project connects economic systems with culture and political processes. This interdisciplinary integration promotes civic understanding and engagement, matching the scope of social studies.
qs.rel: Integrating multiple themes promotes understanding of interconnected economic activities. Neighbours: thematic approach.

qs.stem: Dramatization is one of the teaching-learning strategy used by teachers in a social sciences class. Which of the following statement is correct? I. The drama on “Krishna, the child” will have more action and special effects. II. The drama on “Chatrapati Shivaji” will have more emphasis on words.
qs.sol: Dramatization can change its emphasis to suit the story and learners. A childhood episode about Krishna may rely on action and visual effects, while a historical portrayal of Chhatrapati Shivaji may use dialogue and words to convey decisions and character. Both statements describe plausible instructional staging choices. The Shivaji drama can also emphasize dialogue. The childhood Krishna drama can also use action and effects. The two suggested emphases suit their different narratives. Neither staging choice is inherently wrong.
qs.rel: Dramatisation is a teaching-learning strategy in social science; both statements concerning engagement are true. Neighbours: role play, simulation.

qs.stem: A teacher wants to design a project linking the themes 'Shelter' and 'Water' for her primary EVS class. Which approach best aligns with the curriculum's goals?
qs.sol: Linking Shelter and Water is best done by studying how water affects shelters, because it directly connects both themes in one inquiry.
qs.rel: Integrated EVS project: study how water affects shelters. Neighbours: thematic integrated approach, NCF 2005.

qs.sol: The board associates climate and environment with physical context. “Climate” can also mean the social-psychological atmosphere, making the wording ambiguous. “social-psychological context” does not fit: social-psychological context concerns relationships and atmosphere; the wording ‘climate’ makes this a plausible alternative.
qs.rel: Climate and environment in EVS includes physical and social-psychological aspects. Neighbours: environment definition, school climate.

qs.stem: A which stage the child should be engaged in learning principles of science through familiar experiences, working with hands to design simple technological units and modules (e.g. designing and making a working model of a windmill to lift weights) and continuing to learn more on environment and health through activities and surveys?
qs.sol: “Upper-primary stage”: At the upper-primary stage, familiar experiences and hands-on models introduce scientific principles. “Primary stage”: The primary stage usually uses simpler exploration rather than this level of principle-based model building.
qs.rel: Upper-primary stage: learn science principles through familiar experiences and hands-on work. Neighbours: NCF 2005 science stages.

qs.stem: ‘When we study history, then we study the history of many other social science subjects like economic history, political history, history of psychology etc’. This statement given above shows that social science subjects are ______ in nature. I. independent II. interdisciplinary III. interrelated
qs.sol: Studying history through economic history, political history and similar areas shows that social-science subjects are interdisciplinary and interrelated.
qs.rel: History links with other social sciences; correlation approach. Neighbours: interdisciplinary, thematic approach.

qs.stem: “आंतरिक अंग, त्रिविमीय ज्यामितीय आकृतियों को मॉडलों के साथ सबसे अच्छी तरह समझा जाता है।” एक समावेशी कक्षा बनाने के लिए एक शिक्षक विभिन्न अधिगम सामग्री का उपयोग करता है। दिया गया कथन निम्नलिखित में से किस अधिगम सामग्री का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है?

opts.B: वास्तविक वस्तुओं के रूप में सामरिक सामग्री
opts.C: चित्रों या तस्वीरों के रूप में दृश्य सामग्री

qs.sol: आंतरिक अंग या त्रिविमीय आकृति का मॉडल हाथ से छूकर उसकी बनावट समझने में सहायता करता है। समावेशी कक्षा में यह विशेष रूप से उन विद्यार्थियों के लिए उपयोगी हो सकता है जो केवल चित्र देखकर आकार नहीं समझ पाते। प्रश्न में वास्तविक वस्तु के रूप में मॉडल का उल्लेख है। आसपास का वातावरण, समतल तस्वीर या डिजिटल उपकरण उस विशिष्ट स्पर्श आधारित सामग्री का वर्णन नहीं करते।
qs.rel: Models help in learning internal organs and 3D geometrical shapes. Neighbours: TLM, concrete aids.

qs.stem: विज्ञान और व्यक्तिगत ज्ञान के अधिकांश पहलुओं की तरह, कौन सा ज्ञान अनुभव या अनुभवजन्य साक्ष्य पर निर्भर है?
qs.sol: पश्च अनुभवजन्य ज्ञान अनुभव से प्राप्त होता है।
qs.rel: Science and personal knowledge are tacit/empirical types of knowledge. Neighbours: tacit knowledge (Polanyi).

qs.sol: “अन्य वस्तुओं के सापेक्ष समष्टि (space) में अपनी स्थिति जानने की प्रक्रिया” सही है, क्योंकि अभिविन्यास का अर्थ परिवेश की वस्तुओं और स्थानों के सापेक्ष अपनी स्थिति तथा दिशा पहचानना है। “यात्रा के लिए GPS डिवाइसों का उपयोग” उपयुक्त नहीं है, क्योंकि जीपीएस यात्रा में मदद करने वाला साधन हो सकता है, पर उसका उपयोग अभिविन्यास की परिभाषा नहीं है।
qs.rel: Spatial sense: position relative to other objects. Neighbours: geometry, spatial reasoning, Van Hiele levels.

qs.stem: Which activity best helps students understand that units must be consistent when measuring length, area, and volume?

opts.A: Estimating objects by visual comparison without using units
opts.B: Measuring objects with different informal units each time
opts.C: Measuring objects using metres, square metres, and cubic metres
opts.D: Recording object measurements but omitting the unit names

qs.sol: Consistent units help students compare measurements correctly. Metres, square metres and cubic metres match length, area and volume respectively.
qs.rel: Measuring with metres, square metres, cubic metres teaches consistent units. Neighbours: standard vs non-standard units.

qs.stem:
Choose the best suited response from the following.

One of the objectives of teaching mathematics that is unique to this subject is it develops:
qs.sol:
Mathematical notation condenses relations into short, exact expressions.

This distinctive objective is brevity and precision in expression; the other abilities develop in several subjects too.
qs.rel: Brevity and precision in expression are objectives unique to mathematics. Neighbours: logical thinking, abstraction, accuracy.

qs.stem: Which of the following statement is false about certain phenomena in plants?

opts.A: Photosynthesis adds Oxygen to the atmosphere
opts.B: Upward growth of plant shoots is seen in Negative Geotropism
opts.C: Upward growth of plant roots is seen in positive Geotropism
opts.D: Respiration adds CO2 to the atmosphere

qs.sol: Positive geotropism means growth toward gravity, so roots normally grow downward. Therefore, the statement “Upward growth of plant roots is seen in positive Geotropism” is false.
qs.rel: Plant roots show positive geotropism (downward); stems show negative geotropism. Neighbours: phototropism, hydrotropism.

qs.stem: Which of the following statement(s) is/are not correct about ‘Facilitation’ in art education? I. Helping the child by giving free access to handling musical instruments with a caution for care. II. Providing lot of art material for helping the child to choose and pick and innovate.
qs.sol:
Facilitation gives learners access to materials while guiding safe care.

It also offers choices so they can explore and innovate.

Both statements describe facilitation, so neither is incorrect.
qs.rel: Facilitation in art education means guiding without imposing. Neighbours: free expression, child art (Lowenfeld).

qs.stem: During a unit on scientific inquiry, students make repeated observations of plants bending towards light and propose that all plants exhibit this behaviour. Which core process of scientific reasoning are they applying?
qs.sol: Students are moving from repeated specific observations to a general principle. This is inductive reasoning.
qs.rel: Repeated observations leading to a general rule is inductive reasoning. Neighbours: deductive reasoning, hypothesis.

qs.stem: Science fundamentally requires:

opts.A: A set of systematic rules of procedure

qs.sol: Scientific inquiry relies on systematic procedures for observation and testing.
qs.rel: Science requires systematic rules of procedure (scientific method). Neighbours: observation, hypothesis, experimentation.

qs.stem: “Mathematics is a system of logical processes and conclusions are derived from certain fundamental assumptions”. Which of the following best describes this feature of mathematics, as stated by Mario Pieri?
qs.sol: Axioms or hypotheses are starting assumptions, and logical deductions lead from them to theorems. That is a hypothetico-deductive structure.
qs.rel: Mathematics is a hypothetico-deductive system. Neighbours: axioms, proofs, Euclid.

qs.stem: More concepts per sentence and paragraph than any other are found in text of which of these subjects?
qs.sol: Mathematics texts compress definitions, symbols, relationships and deductions into short statements, giving a particularly high concept density.
qs.rel: Mathematics texts have the highest concept density per sentence. Neighbours: reading difficulty, technical vocabulary.

qs.stem: Teacher has come prepared with colours, brush, easel and old magazines. Which form of art would she probably incorporate into the lesson?
qs.sol: Colours, brushes and an easel are used for painting; magazine images can be used in collage. Both are forms of visual art.
qs.rel: Colours, brush, easel and magazines indicate visual art (painting/collage). Neighbours: performing, literary arts.

qs.stem: Which of the following is known as an accepted hypothesis?
qs.sol: A hypothesis that has been repeatedly tested and supported by evidence becomes an accepted explanation, called a theory.
qs.rel: A theory is an accepted hypothesis. Neighbours: law, fact, hypothesis hierarchy.

qs.stem: Who out of the following in his book “Structure of Science” defines Paradigm shift as a scientific revolution?
qs.sol: Thomas Kuhn, in The Structure of Scientific Revolutions (1962), described a scientific revolution as a paradigm shift.
qs.rel: Thomas Kuhn (Structure of Scientific Revolutions, 1962) defined paradigm shift. Neighbours: Popper, normal science.

qs.stem: Studying about health, environment, Natural hazards comes under:
qs.sol: In the school curriculum, topics such as health, the environment and natural hazards are studied under general science, which covers the human body, living things and natural phenomena.

qs.stem: The basis for problem-solving strategies for local communities can be obtained through:

qs.rel: Local or indigenous knowledge helps local community problem solving. Neighbours: community resources.

qs.stem: Does the environmental education included from kindergarten. How?

opts.A: Yes, By way of teaching about Cleanliness, Animals, Plants Wastage Etc.
opts.C: Depends on the teacher who teaches

qs.stem: Activities like climbing trees, plucking fruits, jumping, drama etc were part of educational programmes in educational institutions established by which of the following philosophers?

qs.stem: One of the key recommendations by National Council of Teachers of Mathematics’ Curriculum and Evaluation Standards for School Mathematics (1989) is that instruction in elementary school mathematics should

opts.C: Stick to approaches that have been followed by our ancestors
opts.D: shift from a teacher-directed approach to those in which students are actively involved in searching for patterns and experimenting with their own conjectures.

qs.rel: NCTM Standards recommend shifting from teacher-directed approach to active student engagement. Neighbours: problem solving, communication.

qs.stem: Quality and relations are studied under which type of concepts?

qs.rel: Concept of aspects: quality and relations. Neighbours: concept types - object, aspects, event.

qs.stem:
“Art is the response of man’s creative soul to the call of the real”

qs.rel: Rabindranath Tagore's view of art as creative soul's response. Neighbours: Visva-Bharati, Gitanjali.

qs.stem: The study of phenomena that can be physically, sensed, observed and counted is:
qs.sol: Science investigates observable and measurable phenomena.
qs.rel: Science studies phenomena that can be sensed, observed and counted. Neighbours: social science studies society.

qs.sol: सूत्रों और समीकरणों की भाषा गणित शिक्षण का केंद्रीय भाग है।

qs.sol: Reading an equation aloud and discussing its meaning models how to read and comprehend mathematical language.

qs.stem:
Choose the best option from the following.

A unique feature of including art in education is that it develops in children the ability to:
qs.sol: Art uses visual, musical and other symbols for expression, developing symbolic communication.

qs.stem:

Experimentation can be defined as:

qs.stem: तर्क के आधार पर निर्णय लेना किस नाम से जाना जाता है?
qs.sol: गहन या आलोचनात्मक सोच निर्णय से पहले तर्क और साक्ष्य का मूल्यांकन करती है।

qs.stem: तकनीकी शब्द क्या होता है, जब हमारे ध्यान एक कार्य से दूसरे कार्य में स्वचालित रूप से स्थानांतरित होते हैं, उदाहरण के लिए पुस्तक पढ़ने के बीच में बातचीत सुनना?
qs.sol: जानबूझकर निर्णय के बिना स्वतः ध्यान बदलना अनैच्छिक ध्यान है। केंद्रित, विभाजित और वितरित ध्यान आवंटन की अलग अवस्थाएँ हैं।
qs.rel: A technical term/shift of attention is attention-related. Neighbours: selective attention, span.

qs.sol: “मानव समाज और सामाजिक संबंधों का एक व्यवस्थित अध्ययन” सामाजिक विज्ञान के समाज, संस्थाओं और मानवीय संबंधों के अध्ययन को समेटता है। “केवल आर्थिक मुद्दों पर फोकस करने वाली विज्ञान की एक शाखा” अर्थशास्त्र को पूरे सामाजिक विज्ञान के बराबर कर देता है और अन्य सामाजिक विषयों को छोड़ देता है।
